name: Yancey
description:
Meet Yancey!  She is about 2 years old and we believe her to be sweet lab/ hound and possibly a beagle mix.  We rescued her from a high kill shelter in TN and is now in our adoption center in Brewster waiting for her forever home.  

Yancey is such a smart girl and loves all people, and is an active girl.   She would love to run by your side, go hiking, play fetch in the yard or cuddle up next to you and be perfectly happy.   She loves her treats and toys but is still learning how to share her things so an experienced adopter is preferred.  She would do amazing in a home who can give her exercise and enjoy spending time with her.

If they are listed on Petfinder, they are still available. We do not go on a first come first serve basis, but on best fit for the family and most importantly, the puppy.  We are taking our best guess on breed and size when fully grown, based on the puppy's physical appearance.    

Yancey is up to date on her vaccinations, micro-chipped and spayed.

To apply to foster or adopt Yancey please visit snarrnortheast.org

name: Luke
description:
Luke's story is pretty incredible, we rescued him from a high kill shelter in Brooklyn, NY after he was found wounded, with scars and malnourished in a train yard. How he got there is unknown; he's pretty much the epitome of a Sarah McLaughlin commercial.  Political and sports commentator Keith Olbermann took a special interest in Luke and paid for a full medical and behavioral work up at a top notch Veterinary clinic in Manhattan, NY.  All results show Luke is pretty healthy considering everything he has been through.  He arrived to us in mid-June and despite his fear and timidness, he's coming out of his shell.  He has learned to sit, is potty trained and walks very politely on a leash. Luke is particular about his person and does prefer females, he has a hard time with males but can acclimate over time. Just know once he picks you , he is your Velcro dog for life.

Luke will need a very special and committed adopter. He had a rough beginning in life and he is still recovering, Luke has the doggy version of PTSD.  Due to this it takes him some time to warm up to new people.  Luke will need a patient person who is willing to continue to work with him to build his confidence and bond with humans.  Luke's past is unknown, it appears he has suffered trauma possibly from both the hands of humans and/or other dogs, but with love and patience he is a gem for the person who is willing to take the time to grow with Luke.  He is fearful of other dogs but could possibly adapt with the proper training and introductions.  Luke would benefit from a quiet household, with adults only; he is low energy and is most content just being with his person.  Luke is able to remain in his crate for hours in the comfort of his own home if he knows his person is nearby.  He is best suited to a home without children, loud noises or other dogs.  Luke has met one cat and appeared to have a healthy, non-predatory interest.

Luke will need slow introductions to meet new people; he does best when given space to come around on his own.  Luke will need a strong, confident leader and an experienced handler who will continue to focus on behavior training.  Luke is great on leash, a well behaved car obsessed passenger; and Luke's cuddles and kisses are extra special. He is approximately 5 years old and weighs 53 pounds.   Luke responds well to nicknames such as \"Lukey-baby, Sugar Monster and Mr. Handsome,\"  you should see his beautiful purple, gray coat! Despite a rough beginning in an unfair and cruel world, Luke has the potential to make someone an amazing pet and is a gentle soul looking for comfort and a place to call his home.

name: Nugget
description:
Animal Profile: Nugget is an adorable chihuahua/dachshund mix who is an absolute gem of a pup! Originally rescued from a high kill shelter in CA, Nugget is now thriving in his Seattle-area foster home. His foster mom can't say enough good things about this little guy; from couch and bed snuggles to romping in the yard with his canine buddy, Nugget is a loving, affectionate, and sweet little guy. He loves treats, belly rubs, sun bathing, and any stuffed toy he can play tug-of-war with! He has done great around older kids and adults, walks great on leash, and does well in his crate. Nugget would love a canine buddy in his forever home, so he can continue to have a buddy to play chase with and snuggle up to during the day.

Seattle Foster Update:

Latest update: Oh my goodness.....I can't believe no one has snapped up this loveable little guy. He likes taking walks, playing with toys, cuddling, and hanging with my 10-year-old nephew. Nugget thinks cats are pretty cool and that any treat shaped like a stick is the only kind of \"real\" treat there is. Also......discovered a new talent over the past week. Little Nugget likes to \"sing!\" Cant wait to see what other new talents this little guy has! Third update: I just love this little guy! Toys and playing are now on the daily docket! He also has gotten to interact with a few older kids. He really enjoys the attention, belly rubs, and giving kisses. Second update: This little guy has come along way in 3 weeks. He hasn't had an accident in the house in 2 weeks, he knows \"sit\" and \"come,\" and he's working on learning other commands. He's started playing with toys, and is learning to play with other dogs. He does well on a leash and likes going to pet friendly stores and meeting other people. He does better with a playmate around, rather than being alone. First update: Nugget started off very shy and timid but quickly became the life of the party. He is a happy and inquisitive little pup. He gets along well with smaller dogs and is still getting used to seeing larger dogs in the neighborhood. He's good on a leash, loves going on walks, and doesn't mind his crate. And ... a big plus ... he gets along with the cats in our house. He has some separation anxiety, but it's getting better with each separation. Nugget loves to cuddle and is a real sweetie!

Adoption Info:
Adoption fee is $475, which includes spay/neuter, current rabies/DAPPV/bordetella vaccinations, microchip, health certificate, and heartworm test. All adoption fees are donations to a Washington non-profit corporation and all donations go to benefit the animals in our rescue.

Apply online at www.DogGoneSeattle.org

Animal History: Nugget was picked up as a stray and brought to Moreno Valley Animal Shelter. He was rescued in advance of the 4th of July holiday and arrived in Seattle on July 7. He will be available for adoption in the Seattle area after evaluation in a foster home.

About Foster to Adopt Program:
Fosters provide a safe landing spot for dogs transitioning from the shelter environment and help prepare the dogs for adoption. You provide the love and structure, and we take care of everything else! We cover all vet care, and drive the adoption process. Average length of foster is 2-3 weeks. Fosters do get first consideration for adoption, if desired.

Apply to foster online at www.doggoneseattle.org/foster-application

name: Lucky
description:
Very good with people, but apparently not other dogs or cats.
She was rescued from a breeder in California. Food possessive; she probably didn't get enough to eat where she was previously.

name: Audrey
description: Audrey is a very affectionate dog with a tenacious spirit, working hard to overcome the effects of Valley Fever that left her with weakness and some paralysis in her hind legs. Through physical therapy and a lot of TLC, Audrey is now able to stand and walk, and she continues to make progress each day. She has a strong determination that is an inspiration to everyone who meets her. Born in 2015, Audrey came to Best Friends from a shelter in California. She is incontinent from the effects of Valley Fever and is on long-term medications. Despite what her body has been through, Audrey is strong and can pull on a leash, so she walks on a harness at the Sanctuary. She gets along with most other rambunctious, playful dogs she's met at the sanctuary, but does not do well with feline friends. With people, Audrey is affectionate, loving and goofy, and she will make a wonderful companion.

name: Marmalade
description: If there is one word to describe Marmalade, it's \"smart.? She enjoys training and loves to play fetch. Born in 2015, she came to the Sanctuary from a Best Friends Network Partner organization in California. Marmalade would enjoy an active home and would make an excellent hiking buddy. After a busy day or some good exercise, she can be a couch potato who just wants to cuddle up with you. Marmalade will guard food and her bowl and must go to a home where she'll be an only pet (she has shown aggression toward other dogs and cats in the past). In Dogtown, she is doing training to help her overcome leash reactivity toward other dogs and to reduce her food bowl guarding. She would thrive as an only pet, with a person or family who is willing to continue her training and take her on some adventures.

name: Tuco
description: Tuco is a sweet dog who loves attention. He enjoys playing with people, but he also likes to just hang out with them. Water and jolly balls are his two favorite toys. He loves these things so much that it can be difficult to pull him away from them. Born in 2015, Tuco came to Best Friends from a shelter in California. He will guard food and has shown other guarding behaviors. Tuco also has some handling issues, especially during medical checkups. He especially doesn't like having his feet or ears touched. His caregivers at the Sanctuary are working with him to decrease his food guarding and to improve his ability to be handled. Tuco has done well with all the dogs he's met at the Sanctuary and has even passed a cat test here. He has also lived with small dogs successfully before. When the weather is warm, Tuco could happily live in the Dogtown dog park pool, but he'd be even happier to go home with you.

name: Stitch
description: People are constantly falling in love with Stitch's face. They say he looks like a cute gargoyle. Born in 2011, Stitch came to Best Friends from a rescue organization in California. Although he's had previous heart surgeries, his heart murmur is still a grade five out of six. He takes prescription medication for his heart, and he gets eye drops. Stitch absolutely loves to be around people. He is cuddly, sweet and would make a great couch potato. He can wedge his compact, 60-pound body into his caregivers' laps and snuggle for as long as time allows. He does get overexcited when he's being leashed up, so he is working on being calm and not getting mouthy. He does best in calm, quiet environments and when the person leashing him is calm and follows a routine. Stitch does have a previous bite history. He's also very heat sensitive because of his heart condition and his short muzzle, so it's important that he goes for walks when it's not too hot outside. When it comes to other dogs, Stitch can be defensive when he first meets them, but he usually warms up. He'd do best in a home without cats. Stitch does well riding in a car, although he needs a boost to get in. On hotter days, instead of walks, he likes to ride on the golf cart around Dogtown, feeling the breeze in his face. Stitch is crate trained and eats his meals in a crate. Despite his medical challenges, he is friendly and easygoing with the Best Friends veterinary staff and has been great for medical handling here. If you'd enjoy having a cute little gargoyle who'll curl up with on the couch with you and stroll by your side when it's cool outside, Stitch may be your guy. Stitch has a generous sponsor who will cover a portion of his adoption costs.

name: West Coast Lily (WA)
description:
Lilly is the name, playing all day is my game! I originally come from California, but Iâm looking forward to my first Pacific Northwest winter! Foster mom says Iâll need a sweater to keep warm. I am an older gal, but I donât let that slow me down one bit. My foster mom has me up to three miles at a time, and she says that my average pace of 9 minutes a mile is pretty good! I walk with my foster mom and PRO alum Andrew every day, and still have energy left to play fetch. I am a âpocket pointerâ which means Iâm very small. I weigh in at a dainty 32 pounds. My foster mom says that I am âthe best of both worldsâ because I act like a big dog, but take up half the space! Foster mom says that I am making fantastic progress in every way, and she tells me sheâs proud of me every day!

 Lilly is a ball of energy, and a ray of sunshine. She is very playful, and loves to chew up rubber balls and spit out the remnants. She also likes sitting in the backyard looking at any little wild things that may cross her path. She has a strong prey drive, so sheâs kept leashed or tethered, but she doesnât mind that one bit. She is very strong, and loves walks and runs. Weâve got her up to three fast miles per run, and she could walk all day if you wanted to take her along! She is learning leash manners very quickly and responds well to treats. She is great in the house, and can be left unattended with no accidents or incidents, for the most part. Thunder, fireworks, and other unexplained loud booms to scare her and she can be reactive, but those issues are often few and far between. She is choosy about giving cuddles, but when sheâs in the mood, sheâs a great lap dog. She has been a true treat to have around. She is great with other dogs, very respectful of cats, and doesnât have a mean bone in her little body. She would be a great companion for someone who likes adventures as much as movie nights in, and she would go anywhere with anyone as long as she got a puppuccino for the ride!

name: Kaia Carson
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Hi, my name is Kaia, and I came all the way from California. While the west coast has all the sunshine, I wanted to see how the mid-west farmers daughters lived. All the dog volunteers at Last Hope say I am the sweetest little girl, I love to snuggle, and give tons of kisses. I love to ride in the car and go for walks and I am super good at both! I am a very strong girl and need someone equally as strong. I am a princess and love all the attention so I will need to be the only pet in the house. I also need a home that has a privacy fence in case the neighbors have pets. So if you always wished they all could be California girls and wanted one of your own, then I am your girl.....

Kaia's adoption fee is $250 and includes her spay, micro chip and current vaccinations. name: Saweetie
description: Saweetie came to us from a high kill shelter in California.  She is approximately 3 years old, and super sweet.  When Saweetie was in CA she hurt her tail by wagging it too hard and it became infected, so we had it amputated.  She has the cutest little nub tail, now - it is adorable as is she.  Saweetie is quite small - only around 45-50 lbs.  She craves affection.  Saweetie has been with our trainer for a few weeks, and walks nicely on a leash, and knows several commands.  Saweetie is crate trained.  She is a little anxious so she will need a patient adopter - she craves attention and needs to gain some confidence.  She couldn't be more sweet.  Saweetie is good with other dogs upon proper intro.

name: Terry
description:
MEET TERRY! (NO CATS) 

How adorable is this little tater tot??!! Terry came to us from Moreno Valley shelter in California and as always we will never understand how he ended up there. He is a pocket sized German Shepherd with a little bit of husky weighing in at only 52 lbs and we think he was born around 3/2015. Terry requires an adopter that is familiar with huskies and/or German Shepherds and would benefit from additional training. He is super smart and wants to please. This sweet little guy never misses a chance for ear rubs and snuggles. 

Terry is one happy dude. He loves to play with toys and is game for walks and hikes. He needs slow and proper introduction to other dogs but does like to play once he gets to know them. He is a little too interested in cats so we do suggest a home without cats. 

Terry is up-to-date on vaccines, heart worm negative, neutered, microchipped and on flea/tick/HW preventatives. Adoption fee $400 

If you are interested in Terry or any of the other JLGSR dogs, please take a minute to fill out our online adoption application at www.jettslegacy.com. Note: We do not schedule meet and greets for any of our dogs without an approved application on file.

name: Pluto
description:
PLUTO- 2 year old, male, GSD 
**Special Needs**
Like the cartoon pup, Pluto is pure FUN. This boy originally comes from California and like a true surfer boy he loves the sand and the water. He is dog friendly, house trained, crate trained and knows basic commands. He loves riding in the car and sticking his head out of the window. He's a big feller weighing in at 69lbs and has a strong personality so will need someone who knows the breed and experience handling a GSD. He has Epilepsy, diagnosed earlier this year but is managing it well with his current medications. He takes his medicine like a good boy and is down to having one seizure a month. Epilepsy in dogs is for life so his future family will need to be on top of his meds and not skip doses! Despite all of this he is full of life and would be an amazing hiking and adventure partner. If you are interested in Pluto please text Juliana at 973-903-9686.

name: Zoey & Biscuit / Biscuit & Zoey
description: Biscuit (8 year-old Pug/Beagle) and Zoey (9 year-old Chihuahua) are life-long friends coming to CAWS from a loving home in California when their mom got sick. Both pups are housebroken, crate trained, good eaters, and good with dogs. Biscuit is happy-go-lucky and loves all humans. She weighs 21 pounds, but should be around 17. Biscuit has recently been diagnosed with Cushings Disease, which requires daily medication for the rest of her life. Zoey is feisty and a little stand-offish at first, but warms up with time. She is really tiny at just 4 pounds. Zoey recently underwent a dental cleaning and is doing great. Zoey is not a fan of being picked up or held, but tolerates it. She enjoys lying next to you and being petted. Biscuit requires sleeping with her human (and FYI she does snore). These two pups are both precious and love each other very much. CAWS will consider separating them, but feel we first need to give them a chance to find their forever home together. name: Preston
description:
Animal Profile:
Preston is a young adult Poodle mix, about 15 lbs, who was rescued from a high kill shelter in California. Preston is now in a Seattle area foster home and available for adoption. He is a sweet pup who can be a little shy at first, but doesn't take long to warm up. He is enjoying playing with his canine buddies in his foster home and loves romping in the yard, and then will gladly hang out by your side. He is very people oriented, and incredibly smart and eager to learn. He is great with his basic commands - sit, wait, stay, come, down, and kennel up. In order for Preston to be his most successful self, he needs boundaries and structure in his forever home. An ideal home for him would be an adult-only home, who is ready to provide as much as structure as affection so that Preston can have clear expectations and confidently settle into his new home.

She loves her people, and it only took me about an hour to become her person, she loves kids, and she loves other dogs. She doesn't seem to have had a lot of training before but she is learning really quickly. We have started today with \"sit\" and \"leave it\" and she's is doing great. Being food motivated has helped a ton. She will work hard for a little piece of cheese. Sofia is definitely out of the puppy phase and does not chew on anything which has been great! name: Meadow - Adopted!
description:
ADOPTED! Our appreciation to all who wanted to provide this dog with a loving home. Unless otherwise requested, any adoption applications we received will be kept on file for future adoption consideration.

* Female Chinese Shar Pei mix

* Approximately 3 months old

* Approximately 16.5 pounds

* House trained

* Crate trained

* Okay with other dogs and cats

* Dog respectful children 8 and older

* Adoption fee: $525

All dogs with PUP are in private foster homes so we can provide our potential adopters the most current information available.

Raising a puppy requires a lot of work and is a commitment!

Meadow

will be an awesome addition to a family that can give her the attention, exercise, training and affection she deserves.

Due to the fact that this is a mixed breed puppy, we, nor our vets, cannot guarantee the size that your dog will be.

Health: Meadow has been spayed and microchipped. She is current on her DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies. She has been wormed, flea treated, and tested negative for heartworm.

History:

Meadow

comes from an overcrowded shelter in California. PUP was asked to help and we are so glad we did. All dogs PUP pulls from California come with health certificates, as required by Washington state. Meadow has a tiny congenital anomaly (dermoid) in her left eye. This is not uncommon and hardly visible. She has been vet checked and no action/treatment is needed.

Notes from

Meadow

's Foster Home: In the short time that Meadow has been in our home, she has proven to be a delightful, sweet and affectionate puppy. She adapted incredibly quickly from the trek up from the shelter in California.

Potty training, crate training and leash training were all accomplished within a week.

She is extremely friendly and confident and will greet any human with happiness and genuine joy. Her energy level is high, which is understandable for a puppy.

However, she does sleep quietly throughout the night in her crate. We make sure she has several walks per day to balance out her puppy exuberance.

Note: The above description reflects the behavior we have observed in the dog's foster home. Although PUP provides adopters up to the minute information on our dogs, we cannot guarantee they will behave in the same manner in a different environment with new owners.

ADOPTION: If you think you have room in your home and heart for this dog and you reside within Washington State, please go to our Adoption Information page, or copy and paste this link https://www.pupdogrescue.org/adopt.html in your browser. There you will find more information and be able to fill out an adoption application.

EVENTS: To attend our next PUP adoption event, please check out our Facebook page, or copy and paste this link https://www.facebook.com/pg/puprescue/events/?ref=page_internal in your browser.

name: Darla
description:
Animal Profile: Darla is an itty bitty 12-month-old perfectly sized 30 lb mixed breed (paperwork says Shepherd mix but we think Staffy terrier and several other breeds) who we just saved from a kill shelter. She joined us in Seattle on Aug. 23 and our volunteer transporter says \"Darla is sweet as they come. She has super soft body language and will definitely shine with a dog buddy. She has a submissive personality, walks on leash, is gentle and will be amazing with kids.\" Darla is settling in well to her foster home and does great with the resident dog in the home. She is very smart, food motivated, and eager to please making her a dream to train. She does like to play chase and wrestle, so she would need a sturdy, playful doggy companion if she goes to a home with another dog. She is great in her crate and is doing well with her potty training. She does well being left alone during the work day, but she really loves being with her people and would thrive in a take-your-dog-to-work situation, or as an in-home office buddy. Her leash walking skills are improving daily, and she loves to see the world! Darla has some puppy energy when she comes out of the crate and loves to have a little romp in the yard, but she settles down quickly and is just as happy to snuggle on the couch or the dog bed and take a long nap. She likes to chew on bones and play with toys and balls. She is an overall easygoing and happy-go-lucky girl, and she would be a wonderful first dog. She is an amazing girl who will make one lucky family very happy! We will share more information as we get to know her in foster care.

name: Farley
description:
* Male German Shepard dog mix

* Approximately 8.5 years old

* Approximately 62 pounds

* House trained

* Crate trained

* Okay with other dogs, not sure
about cats

* Not observed with children

* Adoption fee: $225

All dogs with PUP are in private foster homes so we can provide our potential adopters the most current information available.

Health: Farley has been neutered and microchipped. He is current on his DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies. He has been wormed, flea treated, and tested negative for heartworm. He takes medication for hyperthyroidism and arthritis.

History: Farley comes from an overcrowded shelter in California. PUP was asked to help and we are so glad we did. All dogs PUP pulls from California come with health certificates, as required by Washington state.

Notes from Farley's Foster Home: Farley is a sweet, gentle, loveable lug and such an easy guy to have in our home. When he came into rescue it appeared he had not had an easy life and wasn't well cared for at all. He's ready for, and so deserving of, lots of love and care in his retirement years. In his foster home Farley has been living with 4 other senior dogs, all between 7 - 22 lbs. and does very well with them though he'd be OK as an only dog also. He is pretty low energy but does follow you from room to room and sometimes gallops around in anticipation of mealtimes or going for a walk. He bonds with his people, wanting to be wherever they are. Farley likes to lean in for pets and then gently nuzzle your hand for more. He deserves to be an indoor dog (we're guessing he didn't have much of that prior to PUP) and have a soft bed and lots of positive human contact. He is housetrained on a schedule and crate trained. Farley is not a frequent barker, we've only heard him bark a few times. He has a few fatty tumors and some arthritis but still loves to go for walks exploring the neighborhood. Farley is a little timid meeting new dogs. Being timid, we do not recommend dog parks where some humans aren't monitoring their dogs. He has not been observed around children but may do OK with older kids that respect his age and space. He is a senior boy and would do best in a quieter home. Farley takes twice daily thyro tabs for hyperthyroidism and rimadyl once a day for his arthritis. They are both easily administered. He has a gorgeous soft coat that stays that way with regular bathing, which he enjoys. Farley is amazingly loyal and devoted to his people and is the best companion you could ask for!\

Health: Scooter Pie has been spayed, microchipped and received a dental. She is current on her DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies. She has been wormed and flea treated, and tested negative for heartworm.

History: Scooter Pie comes from an overcrowded shelter in California. PUP was asked to help and we are so glad we did. All dogs PUP pulls from California come with health certificates, as required by Washington state.

Notes from Scooter Pie's Foster Home:
Scooter Pie is a sweet, sweet girl who wants to snuggle every time you sit down. She is fully house broken and will go to the back door when she wants out. Sometimes she wants to go out, just to be out as she LOVES the warm sunshine. Scooter has been here for 2 years now while her hip injury healed. She does have mostly good days but sometimes her hip will start to bother her, and she'll start doing a lot of licking. She is helped through these times with Gabapentin. The Vet says she can take this every day and it is just part of her normal daily routine. It alleviates her discomfort.

Scooter is a serious burrower. She loves a bigger crate with lots of blankets for her to nest in and to cover up in. She will often go into her crate to sleep during the day. Yes, that's her under the pink blanket.

Scooter needs daily exercise to keep her from being bored and to build muscles that will help protect her hip. Scooter is incredibly intelligent, so she gets bored easily. I think Scooter Pie would benefit greatly from the very inexpensive training classes PUP offers in Issaquah and I think she's capable of learning amazing things. She is one of the sweetest, most attentive, loving (and smartest) dogs I've had the honor of fostering.

name: Gisella
description:
Animal Profile: Gisella is a young at heart but old soul purebred female Doberman who we just rescued from a high kill shelter in California. Our volunteer says she seems younger than her age estimate and that she has lots of energy and is a pretty fearless girl!

Note: Upon arrival and inspection of her teeth and eyes we believe she is closer to 3 years old, although she has clearly lived outdoors. We will be having an age estimate conducted by our veterinarian and update her profile accordingly.

Seattle Foster Updates:

I would describe her as more of a cuddle bug who wants to snuggle and binge watch tv. She loves helping out in the kitchen - she is excited to taste-test fruits and veggies; she patiently waits her turn to get a taste. She loves to play with her 1.5 yo chow/lab brother, he has taught her to wrestle and chase. She gets along with the 3 resident female dobies. I have found her cuddled up in puppy beds with each one of them at various times and she often joins in when they all decide to chase the boy dog. She can be a little on the shy side and depending on her mood she can be a bit of a wallflower with other dogs. She has no problem warming up to human visitors and letting them know they should be petting her, or she might show-off her wrestling skills with her foster brother when visitors are around. Being a dobie, she likes to know where her people are, so she will checkup on us if we are in a different room.

Adoption Info:
Adoption fee is $450, which includes spay/neuter, current rabies/DAPPV/bordetella vaccinations, microchip, health certificate, and heartworm test. All adoption fees are donations to a Washington non-profit corporation and all donations go to benefit the animals in our rescue.

Apply online at www.DogGoneSeattle.org

Animal History: Gisella was picked up as a stray in San Bernadino and brought to a high kill shelter. We rescued her and she will be arriving to Seattle on Sunday Aug 11th and will be available for adoption in the Seattle Area after evaluation in a foster home.

About Foster to Adopt Program:
Fosters provide a safe landing spot for dogs transitioning from the shelter environment and help prepare the dogs for adoption. You provide the love and structure, and we take care of everything else! We cover all vet care, and drive the adoption process. Average length of foster is 2-3 weeks. Fosters do get first consideration for adoption, if desired.

Apply to foster online at www.doggoneseattle.org/foster-application

name: Peaches
description:
You MUST visit www.save-a-mutt.org/herodogs to fill out an application and get pre-approved before meeting any Save-A-Mutt puppies. We are a foster based rescue, there is no facility to visit. Thank You!

---

Meet Peaches. She was brought up from California pregnant. After her puppies were born, they started becoming sick and dying. We ran tests and discovered they had distemper. Peaches lost all her puppies - but even though she tested positive for distemper, she has never shown any symptoms.

She stayed in quarantine/foster for over 4 months and is now ready to look for a forever home!

Her foster home says:  She loves my two granddaughters a lot. She is very sweet. She does get bored and chews on things she isn't suppose to. Her first day, she escaped once out the front door but did not leave our yard and it was really easy getting her back in even with 4 kids on skateboards cruising down the road. She did not chase after them at all. She plays a lot with our dog so that wears them both out. Not one potty accident in the house. 

Peaches sleeps in the crate at night and when I leave the house. I believe she has some separation anxiety but she is getting more relaxed having me out of her sight. She is a Velcro dog and will follow you everywhere. She really is the sweetest pup.  She loves people and is so sweet with my two granddaughters. Shelby came by with the girls and one of her friends showed up and Peaches was so sweet with her. Stood by her and was very gentle.  Peaches is a high energy dog, who will LOVE walks and another playful dog.\" 

A meet and greet will be necessary. She currently lives with another dog, but is particular. Because she is showing some intermittent separation anxiety - we think someone who is home more often or has experience with it would be good for her. 

You may want to call your veterinarian to discuss the possible health implications of a dog that may have had distemper. 

Here is a link for more information: http://maddieslifesavingacademy.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/Distemper-Handout-for-Fosters-and-Adopters.pdf

---

Save-A-Mutt requires a training contract and deposit on all our large and/or dominant breed dogs. You pick a trainer in your area, and upon completion of a 6+ week training class, we will refund the deposit. 

Adoptions take place typically in Stanwood. 

Peaches is spayed, microchipped and fully vaccinated. She goes home with a goody bag including collar/leash, toys, chews, Kong, and more. You will receive all medical records, microchip transfer form and other paperwork. 

Many rescue dogs need patience when transitioning to a new home. Our foster homes try to socialize each dog with other dogs, cats, kids and even livestock. We have made recommendations on their best home placement based on our foster home information.

Adoption fee is $150 + $100 refundable training deposit. 
Save-A-Mutt is a registered 501c3.

Please note, we have approximately a 300 mile adoption radius - Portland OR area and Vancouver BC is the farthest north. We donât ship dogs, once approved you must pick them up in Snohomish County, WA.

name: Baby
description:
Baby is a petite 3 year old black and tan Chi mix. Her last few weeks have been difficult with lots of adjustments. And this brave little girl is taking it on and ready to find her forever home! She needed to have her tail amputated and was wearing a medical collar for a few weeks. And then she was transport from an overcrowded California shelter to us in hopes of finding a forever home. Wow! A lot for an 8 lb pup! Baby is a friendly and fun loving pup who just wants to get her new life started! Baby enjoys the company of other small dogs, taking walks, and being held by the ones she loves.  Baby is a bit possessive of her people and appreciates just one person giving her attention at a time.  She is a bit of a \"primadonna\". Please come and meet Baby soon! She would be happy to meet you! Her DOB is 6/22/16 and she weighs 8.5 lbs.

Dog adoption fee is $239. This includes the spay or neuter surgery, age appropriate current vaccines (distemper and rabies), microchip, and preventative flea treatment.

 Please stop by to see our adoptable dogs between 1pm-5pm Tuesday-Friday and 12pm-3pm on Saturdays. You are also welcome to contact us via email at emanimalhosp@aol.com. We hope to see you soon!
 These are rescue dogs, and we do not have any further information regarding behavior, training or past experiences.
 For the safety of the dogs, we need to verify residency for all adopters. Renters, please bring a copy of the lease showing that you are allowed to own a dog. Homeowners, please bring a copy of a mortgage statement proving you own your own home. We also require a copy of a utility bill with your name and address for all adopters. We encourage you to meet the pet you are applying for before submitting the application. Your application will not be approved until after you meet the pet. If you would like to print and fill out the application to bring with you to our shelter, visit our website at http://sunnyskysshelter.org/page9.html. *PLEASE NOTE - EMAILED APPLICATIONS WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED.*

description:

Although she is a bit shy this sweet pup will take a treat gently, sit sweetly when asked, wag her tail with some kind words, and appreciates being held. name: Berlin
description:
Animal Profile: Berlin is a handsome and smart 3-year-old Shepherd mix who joined our rescue from California and is now in a Seattle-area foster home. Berlin knows all his basic obedience like sit, down, shake, come, heel and kennel up, is house trained and crate trained. He is friendly with most dogs he's properly introduced to, but he's not a dog-park dog. He can be nervous when meeting new dogs so he requires a slow introduction with confident handlers. Berlin would be happy as an only dog or with a confident alpha dog companion. He is submissive, eager to please and incredibly snuggly once he is comfortable. He will thrive with a dog-savvy leader with previous dog experience, and preferably someone with Shepherd experience. He'd love to find a home with a yard where he can run and be free as that's where he is happiest. Berlin will make a great partner for hiking, jogging or long walks followed by snuggles on the couch. He's the sweetest boy with the best smile!

name: Brigid
description:
KID-FRIENDLY SWEETIE.

Animal Profile: Brigid is a 4- to 5-year-old female Boxer/Pit/German Shepherd mix (we had her DNA done) who was rescued in California. She is our rescue's longest resident and we're still looking for the right fur-ever home for her. She loves all people and is amazing with even very young children. She doesn't bat an eye at crazy antics or rough handling by toddlers, and is not mouthy whatsoever. All she wants in life is to be next to her people. Snuggling and following you around are her favorite activities. Brigid is crate trained and can be left crated for 8 hours without issue in a secure crate. She's house trained and knows sit, down and \"kennel up.\" She's not mouthy or food/toy possessive, and she takes treats gently. Brigid is anxious and reactive in the outside world, and needs slow introductions to dogs she doesn't know. She is leash reactive except when managed by an experienced handler, and will never be a dog-park dog. But she loves playing and cuddling with dogs of all genders and sizes in her own pack and will be fine living with other dogs after a slow introduction. (She needs to understand they are part of her pack before she accepts them.) Brigid doesn't need or want to go for walks for exercise but she does need a secure fenced yard to go potty. Bonus skill: She is treadmill trained!

Brigid's Story: Brigid was a stray in San Bernardino and ended up at high-kill shelter. She was put on the euthanasia list when she came down with kennel cough, so we rescued her in September 2016! She was not spayed due to her upper respiratory infection and when she arrived we quickly saw she was very pregnant! After giving birth she ended up with a very serious infection that required separating her from pups so she could get the veterinary care she needed. She had to have her mammary gland removed and was in intensive medical care for some time. This was likely traumatic for her and may explain some of her separation anxiety and excited/reactive behavior around other dogs. Since then, Brigid had an injury which required surgery (TPLO) and has since recovered. She has also had an extensive board and train so she is well trained. We are eager to find Brigid a wonderful home she can call her own. She has been through a lot so she will need a patient, loving and supportive family.

Adoption Info: Brigid's adoption fee of $150 includes her spay, all vaccinations (Rabies, DPPV, Bordetella) deworming, microchipping and transport from California to Seattle. Brigid's adoption will also include a home training session for her new adopters. Brigid's actual rescue costs are close to $10,000 so any donations to her care are greatly appreciated.

About Foster to Adopt Program:
Fosters provide a safe landing spot for dogs transitioning from the shelter environment and help prepare the dogs for adoption. You provide the love and structure, and we take care of everything else! We cover all vet care, and drive the adoption process. Average length of foster is 2-3 weeks. Fosters do get first consideration for adoption, if desired.

Apply to foster online at www.doggoneseattle.org/foster-application

name: Tami a Rat terrier-Jack Russell mix
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Tami

Tami is a sweet if shy Rat Terrier-Jack Russell mix.

Tami loves attention and laps. She loves her daily walks and will jump in the car to go with you on an adventure for a walk on the beach or a nice park.

We are seeking a quieter home for her without children and with small dog savvy folks, who have the time to give her. Perhaps a work from home person, or retired. Tami will also do well with another small breed, dog-friendly dog. Tami is currently in a foster home where she has had a professional trainer work with her to help her through her fears. She has become more self-confident and is a happy little girl.

If you have patience and love to spare, and want a sweet girl who will warm up with trust and love and be a loyal BFF, this is your girl

Healthy dogs: As a rescue saving dogs from starvation, Neglect and Emaciation, RPR focus's on feeding each rescued animal the healthiest dog food made of Human Grade ingredients to help them recover from their stress and starvation. We share this with our adopters and encourage them to keep their new pet on the same foods for optimal health and a long life.

Adoption Fees

Adoption fee is 495.00. This covers transport from California to Washington, to the rescue facility, adoption and medical such as certain vaccines, worming, parasite, and flea/tick control, health certificate and wellness exam, microchip and any extra medical attention a dog may require such as dental, anal gland expression, emergency medical care. Also, we don't receive any grants so we rely solely on adoption fees and donations to fund all of our rescue efforts. Finally, we take on \"Special Needs\" dogs with high vet costs and pay for their procedures with 'leftover' funds from adoption fees for healthier dogs.

A dopting a Dog requires a lot of work and is a commitment! Tami will be an awesome addition to a family that can give him the attention, exercise, training, and affection he deserves.

OUR REQUIREMENTS FOR ADOPTION:

1) These dogs are not livestock dogs. They must be family pets that are allowed inside the home.

2) We give preference to applicants with prior small breed knowledge/ experiences.

3) Secure visible fencing required.

Health: Tami has been fixed, microchipped, current on DHPP, Bordetella, and Rabies. she has been wormed and flea treated, tested negative for heartworm.

History: Tami was pregnant and out of time at the shelter, Rompin Paws Rescue was asked to help and we are so glad we did. All dogs RPR pulls from California come with health certificates, as required by Washington State Law.

Adoption: If you think you have room in your home and heart for Tami, please go to our website: http://rompinpawsrescue.rescuegroups.org/

There you will find more information and be able to fill out an adoption application.

About Rompin Paws Rescue

Rompin Paws Rescue is a licensed, non-profit organization working towards our 501C3, specializing in rescuing moms to be, moms with puppies, puppies without moms and other Death Row dogs. We are located in Western Washington State. Our passion is to bring people and pets together.

Come Meet Our Pets...
We have a home based operation on Acreage in Arlington and Our dogs are placed in foster homes around the greater Seattle/I-5 Corridor North to Arlington area where they receive socialization and training while they await adoption.

Our Adoption Process...
Since we have a small facility on gated acreage, we are unable to stay open to anyone who wishes to come visit. To facilitate successful adoptions we ask interested people and families to fill out an application for the dog or dogs they may be interested in. We screen the applications and then speak with the interested party by phone. If it looks like a good match can be made, we pre-approve the applicant and set an appointment for a meet and greet with the dogs at out facility or with the fosters who have the dogs in their care. we continue the interview in person and make sure the dog and family are a good fit. http://rompinpawsrescue.rescuegroups.org/

description:

He is in need of a loving home that has no other pets and would be willing to put in the time and effort to rehabilitate him, as he is aggressive towards other dogs (the name is fitting, but wasnât intended that way). description:

description:

Max is a wire-haired terrier mail about two years old Sweet boy. Has not been around cats, gets along with most other dogs.  However, if large dogs want to boss him, he tries to boss them back.  Absolutely loves kids, likes to run and play.  Very treat motivated. Needs a fenced yard

PS:  He is house trained

name: Charlotte
description: This gorgeous girl is Charlotte, a 5 year old, mature, Tree Walker Coonhound.  After retiring from her demanding hunting job in rural West Virginia, Charlotte is happy to kick back and relax in the Virginia Country side.  She has learned to appreciate the finer things in life like a warm fluffy bed, a full belly, and lots of fun walks.  Since her arrival, Charlotte has learned to walk beautifully on a leash.  She enjoys going on walks so much that we would prefer to adopt her to a family that would enjoy taking her for frequent, long walks. Charlotte is still new to indoor life and may need some guidance when she first goes to a new home. However, with time, patience and love we know Charlotte would make a wonderful companion for any family.

name: Cali
description:
Cali regularly sees her vet and is up to date on all health requirements including rabies and heartworm testing. She receives heartworm and flea preventative every month. Cali does have hypothyroidism which is regulated by taking daily ThyroTabs. We have not had any other health issues with her. She does well with adults and other dogs. She is boarded regularly when we travel and she always receives good report cards. She does not do well with children. I have also included photos of her. 48 lbs



My name is Melanie Dreher and I am in a difficult situation with my dog Cali. Cali, is an 8 year old spayed shepherd/hound mix that we adopted from the humane society of Charlotte when she was 8 weeks old. When Cali was around 4 years old we started having behavioral issues with her starting with her nipping a friend that jumped down and scared her. Cali has always been slightly wary around bones/food. We immediately contacted Dog Wizard of Charlotte and enrolled Cali in a behavioral training program. She went with the trainer for 2 weeks and did really well. Cali has made great improvements and does well when we board her at pet paradise. She always receives positive report cards towards staff and other dogs.  Since then we have had a child. We have always been careful about their interactions together, constant supervision, no food or toys around her. We had a very scary incident last night where Cali growled at our 3 year old and tried to bite her after our daughter attempted to pet her back. We are heartbroken and donât know what to do. I received this email from a rescue friend in hopes for some advice.  Thank you for the time to review this email.

name: Rowdy
description:
I am a beautiful boy with a heavy multi colored coat . My sister Muffin is here with me but has a short coat.  Maybe I take after my mother who is a Chow Chow and Muffin takes after our Daddy who is unknown but must be colored like me.

 We both lacked cartilage in our joints when we were born, probably due to our mother not having the proper nutrition when she was pregnant with us. But we are so much better now because our rescue mama has found medicine and a new food with things that we need and we can both run now without hurting our knees. We are able to go on walks but not jog. 

We are considered Senior dogs because on August 31st 2019 we will be 8 years old. But I act like I'm still a puppy.  My mama says the reason we have not been adopted is because we act afraid of people we don't know. I can't help it, I still remember being born under a strange house in the dirt and a man coming and taking two of my sisters away. One must have died because we were only 3 weeks old and he brought the other one back (Muffin). That is when my rescue mamas came and got my entire litter, my mother, and another dog that \"hung around\" with us.

If you might think of adopting me, you would have to give me time to get to know you. Then I would become your \"Sweetie Boo\" like my mama calls me! If you think you would like to give me a chance, email my mama at sunsetanimalrescue@yahoo.com and ask for a SAR questionnaire. Complete and email back. Be sure to tell the references that they will be calling so they will be expecting the call. After talking with your references and learning your history with animals, your will come and meet me. And we will decide if we click. We are located in Winnsboro, SC which is 27 miles from Columbia, SC and 70 miles from Charlotte, NC. I am waiting for my forever home still.

name: Jacob
description: Jacob is a quiet little dude who loves to be with people. He doesn't ask for much, happy, not a barker and enjoys being either inside with his person, or outside walking. His overbite makes him very endearing. These sweeties were all pulled from P.R. where he's been in foster care until able to get a flight to the mainland. (if he does bark it may be in Spanish) and are looking for a forever home where they can love on a family to call their own. The faster we can find forever homes for these sweeties, the more Winnies Legacy Rescue can save. Please please share this posting so we can network to make a difference in their life. If you'd like to adopt, in the adoption fee, we make zero profit. It covers pull fee from the shelter, transportation to our Charlotte, VT location, vetting, paperwork to get them across state lines, shots, deworming, food and more. (Please do not fill out an application if you're not able to come to Charlotte, VT to adopt) You can also help by liking, following and sharing our f.b. page Winnies Legacy Canine Rescue. Email WinniesLegacy@gmavt.net for application or our web site has a link to it and then emailed to us.

name: LOUIE
description:
BENNY & LOUIE -m/n, MiniaturePincscher/ChihuahuaX..dob: ~June 17, 2019

Rescued after being found in a box on someone's front porch when she went out to enjoy her morning coffee.

This wasn't the 1st time, and it wouldn't be the last time, either....2 weeks later, H4S gets another call from her about a tiny adult Chihuahua who had also been abandoned-she thinks she may have seen a young couple with a backpack with this last pup about an hour before it showed up on her porch. She waited 2 days before calling me, hoping they would reappear and inquire about the dog.

H4S CARes to the rescue!

Benny & Louie's tails look like they had been docked at a young age with scissors, & they had no hair on their paws,

indicating that they had been living in a dirty cage for a quite a while. But now, they are happy, healthy, loved, well-fed and wanting to snuggle up against your neck; these boys are a real joy. Gentle and definitely want to please.

They will be ready to be an integral part of your pack on SAT/SEPT 28th, after recovering from their neuter/micro-chip surgeries. However, because of their size and breedX, H4S will not be accepting application where there will be children under the age of 10yo living in the home.

We are seeking an older couple, early retiree or work-from-home person who will be able to house train this pup with regular outside visits for proper daily exercise and potty breaks. Not just someone wanting a fur-kid to come home to after 9>10hrs at work & time spent commuting. These guys deserve a quality life of joy and companionship in exchange for their devotion.

These pups are in & will remain in foster care until their fur-ever home has been approved.

Transport is available to:

DC/MD/DE/NJ=$125 & $140>Jericho(LongIsland), RyeNY, JohnstonRI, ManchesterNH & BurlingtonVT every Saturday
via HAPPY DOGS OR LIFESAVERS Rescued Pet Transports

& $140 to Buffalo/Rochester/Syracuse 2X/mo via SAVE THEM ALL & LIFESAVERS commercial rescued pet transport services.

More pix and videos & testing with cats available upon request.

READY TO SHARE LOVE & LIFE's ADVENTURES with delivery/pick-up date on or after SATURDAY/SEPT 28th.

A secured fenced-in back yard is a PLUS! Commitment to daily walks 2X every day is required for the applicant to be approved. NO TETHERING/TIE-OUTS or ELECTRIC fences will be accepted.

Adoption fee: $350 OR $650/both (comes with all medical paperwork from day #1 with Howlin4Spirit, includes vet surgical notes), neutered(scheduled for SEPT 19th), micro-chipped, utd on all 1st yr vaccines (Rabies, Parvo/Distemper/Lepto, Bordatella), Parasite-free & current on monthly heart worm and flea/tick prevention, new Martingale collar and matching 6' leash, Kong or Nylabone chew toy, beef knee cap bone, Rabies and current health certificate, 'SUPER PUPPY' training booklet, 'RESCUED DOGS ROCK' car magnet & 3lbs of current dry food(Tractor Supply Store's '4Health' Salmon & potato).

To apply to adopt this truly sweet young spirit(s), send us your completed(we require EMAIL ADDRESSES for your personal references) application, which is provided at: www.howlin4spirit.org/adoption-application/ to: howlin4spirit@gmail.com, at your earliest convenience.

Ria joins us from Clarke County, Alabama. This sweet girl is around 7-9 months old & weighs around 25lbs. She is spayed, UTD on all vaccines, and on heartworm/flea/tick preventative.

name: 1908-1683 Mac
description:
MAC - 11 years old, 80 pounds, house trained, very friendly, loves people, good with kids, cats & dogs, loves pizza, good on leash, severe allergies, lipoma (fatty tumor)

MAC had been with his previous family his whole 11 years. He had even traveled from Cleveland, Ohio to stay with them. It's almost tragic to think this boy had everything he knew torn away from him when he was surrendered to us at the Virginia Beach Animal Care and Adoption Center. You'd think a family who traveled so far with their boy would not give him up but whatever the reason, I cannot imagine it was an easy one to make. Moving on...I found Mac to be friendly and easy to handle although when I took too long to get him harnessed or give him a treat, he let me know by barking. Rude! But super cute! lol Mac's family supported my finding by telling us how wonderful he was with everyone from young children to adults to cats and even other dogs. He's an amiable boy who wants to just be at your side, outside walking and enjoying the fresh air or lying next to you at night. Mac is awesome. He is a bit older and we're told (and you can see) a decent size lipoma on his side/chest. A lipoma is basically a fatty tumor which doesn't have to be removed unless it seems to be hurting the dog. With Mac, his lipoma doesn't seem to get in the way at all. He is a good walker and had a blast in the yard! He still has lots of energy to expend but we need to be aware he may not walk as far or run as fast as some of his younger counterparts. Mac does have severe allergies so please be aware that this may mean there is an extra financial obligation to keep his allergies in check. Mac is a great boy who seems like he would be an easy fit into most homes. Please bring your resident dog in to meet him if you have one. Please bring your kids in to meet him! Let's find this senior a home so he doesn't have to live in a shelter cage. Mac is waiting in our large dog adoption kennel and his id number is 1908-1683. WE are located at 341 S Birdneck Road in Virginia Beach and are open daily except for Tuesdays. Thanks for considering adoption!

name: STEELE
description:
Steele (aka The Miracle Dog) arrived to NY in April 2019 from Cobb County Georgia. 
He had been hit by a car and surrendered by his former owner to a local shelter where he languished in pain and requiring extensive veterinarian care ( he received the utmost of care while he was at the shelter) 
He has a huge fan club of Guardian Angels and sponsors who got him shipped up to New York where he went into emergency surgery several times to save his life. 
He is now FULLY recovered and through out all his medicals and specialty care he remained ever so sweet and gentle. 
Basically it was touch and go for a while and we did not know if he was going to survive....so yes he is the Miracle Dog!!!
So tens of thousand dollars in veterinary bills later he is now up for adoption!

name: Josie
description: Josie is very excited about life and wants nothing more than to be with people. This friendly girl is always happy to make new friends and learn new things. Josie is like the Energizer bunny, so she'll need a very active home with a person or family who is up for lots of training and enrichment. She does calm down nicely in quiet environments and is very easygoing on car rides. Born in 2015, Josie came to Best Friends from a humane society in Colorado after she was seized from a dog fighting situation. She has a tick-borne illness that causes her to have very low blood platelets. Because of this condition, Josie must be extra careful to avoid any potentially harmful situations. She also lives alone at the Sanctuary and will need to be the only dog in a home, since her condition can be transmitted to other dogs. Although Josie has a heart murmur that needs to be checked regularly, it does not require medication at this time. At Dogtown, Josie is working on impulse control and staying calm when her caregivers enter her room or put on her harness.

name: Jacko
description: Rescued from a property during a dog fight bust in Colorado, Jacko came to Best Friends from a humane society. At Dogtown he is affectionately called 'Jack Jack.' He adores his toys and treats them like his babies, carrying them around and sleeping with them on his bed. Jacko is playful with new dogs once he has gotten to know them, but he also enjoys sunbathing outside with his roommate at Dogtown. Because of his past, Jacko can be nervous meeting new people, especially if he is meeting them for the first time in a small space. He is more confident meeting people outside in an open space and during a walk. Since walks, treats and toys are some of his favorite things, he will trust new people more quickly if they offer him one of these things. He does take treats nicely, and he is eager to learn new things when treats are the reward. Once he is friends with you, Jacko will run right up to you and stop directly in front of your feet to ask for pets and scratches. He can be a very quiet dog and does not 'talk' very much, unless other dogs are 'talking,' too. He is usually a slow walker, but he loves to run when he feels up to it. Recently, Jacko learned to use a ramp to get into a car. He loves lying down and relaxing in the car and is an excellent passenger. Jacko needs a person or family who will show him that it's OK to trust new people. He'll need extra time to meet new people, especially visitors to a home. When he is comfortable, Jacko is truly a clown. He will play bow at people and flash his adorable smile.

name: Ryder
description: Ryder is your guy! He is approximately 2 years old and a Golden Retriever/Border Collie/Heeler mix-best guess. He is a beautiful strawberry blond and has a long lean body with a docked tail. He loves being part of a pack and gets along well with other dogs. He was found as a stray from the Ute reservation in Cortez, NM, and is so glad he caught his freedom ride to Colorado. This smart goofy guy rides well in the car and hopes to become your favorite adventure buddy. He can be a little reserved at first, but once he becomes comfortable, he is affectionate and enjoys shadowing your every move. Ryder is housebroken and does well in his crate, although he prefers to be outside or free roam in the house. He is learning how to live in a house and once he masters his leash skills, he will make an awesome running buddy. Ryder is UTD on shots, neutered, and microchipped. He will do best with an active home, and someone that will be willing to continue his training. He would love a home with a companion dog, and older kids would suit him fine.Ryder is being fostered in Littleton. Want to meet Ryder and fall in love? Apply to adopt at rezdawgrescue.org

name: Abe
description:
Big and handsome, friendly and well behaved -- Abe has it all! Heâs about 3.5 years old and a bit hefty at his current food-loving 86 pounds. Abe comes to us from a rescue partner in Arkansas who scooped him up as a shelter stray in the nick of time. 

Abe has been soaking up a lot of loving and giving loads in return in his foster homes both in Arkansas and now here with us.  Heâs house trained, crate trained, knows some basic commands and is pretty good on leash walks.  Abe gets along well with other dogs, but itâs people he loves the most.  By your side is his favorite place.  His attitude towards cats?  âMeh, kinda boring,â he wags.

Abe made his home with his rescuer in Arkansas while he was being treated for heartworms, an issue seen with many dogs in that part of the country.  âOnce I got the ok from the vet that Iâd recovered from my treatment, I was first in line to hop on the transport van to Colorado . . . and here I am!â woofs our boy.  To keep him healthy, Abeâs family needs to commit to having him on heartworm preventative year round.  Helping him lose a few pounds would be welcome, too!

A pleasantly active big handsome love who loves being loved on, Abe woofs: âCome on over real soon, bring cookies, and letâs get acquainted. I know weâre gonna be BFFâs in no time and then weâll head home together forever!â

description:

name: Minnie
description:
Minnie came all the way from Texas to find a great home in Colorado. She is a tiny owner surrendered terrier mix weighing in at about 8 pounds. We think that she is about 10 years old, but she's quite frisky and nimble. When she came into rescue her skin was in terrible shape. We don't know whether it was the result of a bad diet, a serious flea allergy, or a bacterial infection. She lost a lot of the hair on her body. While her skin is clear now, we donât know if her fur will grow back or if she will stay nekked!  She really doesn't seem to care, and she is not scratchy. She enjoys being with her foster siblings in their fenced-in backyard, and would probably prefer a home with a canine companion.

Minnie is spayed, she is up to date on her vaccinations (rabies, distemper and kennel cough), vet checked, heartworm tested negative and on preventative while in rescue, and microchipped. She also had a dental while in rescue. If you would like to meet Minnie, go to www.cominischnauzerrescue.com and complete the on-line adoption application. We suggest that you print a copy of the application before you hit the \"submit\" button, just in case! We will give you a call to set up a time to bring little Minnie for a visit.

name: Boots
description:
This Boots is made for adopting

And that's just what you'll do

One of these days this Boots

Is gonna walk on home with you

name: Daisy  - adventure girl! Zoomie enthusiast!
description:
Hi! I'm Daisy! I'm a gorgeous Blue Heeler who is loving life in the Colorado mountains.

I'm 3 years old and weigh about 45 pounds. I'm house-trained, crate-trained and spayed. These days I'm all big smiles!

I'm always ready for adventure when out and about, but also love snuggling up on the couch with my people and relaxing. 

I love tossing around my fluffy duck toy, chewing on big bones and Kongs, and snoozing in the patches of sun around the house. I walk nicely on a leash (unless there are bunnies - but hey, who can resist bunnies!) and get good zoomies when I'm running around the yard. 

My foster mom says I'm the total package: able to keep up on adventures, trustworthy, snuggly, and adjusting very well. She says I'm super smart, eager to work, and really athletic. She thinks I'd love agility, treibball and freestyle! I've tried barn hunt, which is really fun, too! My ideal home would be one that's committed to giving me plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and positive training. 

I am trustworthy alone at home for reasonable amounts of time while my foster mom works, and sometimes she even takes me to the office with her, where I love getting attention from all her coworkers. Did I mention how much I love my people? It's not necessary for you to have another dog in your home, as I can go either way - both with other dogs and just on my own with you! Like many heelers, I can be dog-selective, though. Look, you don't like everyone you meet, do you? So introductions to other dogs must be done with knowledgeable supervision. I do go to daycare twice a week and everyone there LOVES me, but in big playgroups, I get a little worked up. Oh, and because of that bunny prey-drive thing, I probably wouldn't be the best fit for a home with small dogs unless you're willing to do very careful introductions.

Unfortunately, I didn't get the best start in life. I was found running around in rural Texas with a bullet wound in my hip! Can you believe someone would do that to such a pretty girl? My foster people think I was probably just doing what my breed is meant to do: chase cows! Isn't it fun to see them run and hear them go \"mooooooo!\" when you nip at them?? I was just trying to live my best life... 

So speaking of herding, I am really good at it. Like, amazing. I was born this way! So when we're out walking and a runner or bike or car passes us, I want to herd them... really badly... like really, really badly... My foster mom doesn't like this; she says I send her to the chiropractor every week because when I try to herd these moving things, I lunge to the end of my leash and bark and don't let up until they go away! (Don't worry, though, I watch carefully to see if they're coming back!) It's super fun, I don't know why she doesn't like it. Anyway, my people are teaching me to \"leave it,\" which is boring, but sometimes it's worth it for my paycheck - chicken!!! In the meantime, I don't go for walks in busy places with lots of bikes, like Marshall Mesa or Boulder Creek Path. My foster mom says I might be able to some day, with lots and lots of training and some maturity. Gosh, what do I need, a Ph-freaking-D??? (Yes, says mom.) She also says that giving me enough exercise is a delicate balance of just enough, but not too much so that I'm completely overstimulated, and things that tire out my brain, not just my body.

I'm also terrible on car rides. Usually, getting in the car means we're going somewhere awesome (a new place to hike, or maybe doggie daycare!!!), and I get so excited that I bark my head off and squeal (I have the most beautiful voice, if I do say so myself, and sometimes it's nice just to hear it!)... And sometimes I get frustrated and bark when we pass those pesky bikes. Come on, Mom! Just let me at 'em... I'm better if I can't see out of the car, though, so if you can crate me in the back of your SUV, I'm okay.

So you might be catching on to the fact that my first couple of years were a little rough. No one really taught me self control or how to channel my energy and instincts, so I just let my freak flag fly, and they sent me to the pound! Luckily, SDR took me in, fixed me up, treated my heartworm (whatever that is; all I know is that I feel MUCH better these days) and sent me on my way to my forever home. My ideal home would be in a quieter neighborhood (preferably rural - I'm a country girl from Texas at heart, after all) with people who are committed to lovingly helping me learn how to function better in the busy Colorado lifestyle. It would also be great to have a big yard with a tall wooden fence, too. If I can't see those bikes going by, then I won't try to chase them, and maybe I'll finally relax a little! (If you live in an apartment/condo or a busy area, please don't apply for Daisy unless you have plenty of heeler and/or dog training experience.)

Did I mention I like to snuggle? If snuggling was a Nobel Prize category, I would probably win it every year (and spend the money on bones). As for the other stuff, it makes my people really happy when I work hard at it, and I live to please my people, so I guess I'll keep at it.

Check out my very own video above made by Summit Dog's extraordinary videographers/editors, Molly Steele and Maddie Steele!

For more info and/or to apply to adopt me, go to https://www.summitdogrescue.org/meet-daisy.html

Since he is not neutered yet, this is the new owner's responsibility once he reaches 6 to 9 months of age. 

The benefit of our organization is that you get to meet the puppy before you commit to adopting! We want perfect matches and happy families!

name: Amelia
description:
AGE: 6 years

WEIGHT: 15 lbs

COAT: Medium Wirehaired 

Amelia is a lively girl that came to us from our local animal control. She was heartworm positive and is undergoing treatment to be a healthy and happy girl. She likes attention and rides really well in the car. She walks well on a leash and likes to run around with her doggy friends in the yard. She is crate trained and very rarely has accidents. This girl wants a family that is lively and able to give her the love she deserves. Though she will not be on the transport to Connecticut due to her ongoing treatment, she is able to be adopted and transported at a later date. When her heartworm treatment is complete, she can be transported from Georgia to Connecticut to join her furever family. 

Her adoption fee will be the cost of transport from GA to CT and an additional adoption fee of $100.

Amelia is currently housed at our rescue location in Colbert, GA.

She will be available at the Colbert Veterinary Rescue Services adoption event held Saturday, October 5, 2019 from 9:30 am to 6:00 pm and Sunday, October 6 from 10:00 am to 2:00 pm at the Milford, CT Petco store on 1401 Boston Post Road. 

All dogs are spayed or neutered and up to date on all vaccinations. They are microchipped and heart worm negative or treated. They are currently on flea, tick and heart worm preventatives. Dogs older than 6 months are leash trained, crate trained and have been socialized with other dogs unless otherwise noted. 

See above for Amelia's adoption fee.

You can be pre-approved to adopt a dog by submitting an application now. When your application has been approved and you have done a phone interview, you will be given an appointment to meet and adopt your chosen dog on the morning of Saturday, October 5th. This means that you will have the first chance to adopt this dog at the adoption event. 

Please contact Ann Curcio at acole128@aol.com for more information about this wonderful dog or an adoption application.

PLEASE read our website's ADOPTION PROCESS PAGE prior to submitting an adoption application. www.apupspizzazzrescue.com/adoption-process 
ADOPTION APPLICATION: www.apupspizzazzrescue.com/adoption-application 

ABOUT OUR RESCUE DOGS: 
All of our sweet fur babies are being socialized daily with other dogs, adults, & most importantly, children. They are ALL in homes being cared for by people who LOVE them! All of our dogs are located in Connecticut, are spayed or neutered, up to date on vaccines, microchipped, dewormed, have had CT State health checks, & go home with a leash, collar, & packet of medical paperwork. 

BREED IDENTIFICATION:
Please understand that many rescue dogs are mixes of multiple breeds. Petfinder allows us to choose up to two breeds per dog. While the shelters and our rescue do our best in accurately identifying breeds, breed identification is not guaranteed. If there is a certain breed that you do not want, it is very important that you share this with our rescue when applying. When adopting a puppy, breed uncertainty plays a big part in the size/look of the dog as an adult. Please know that any puppy can be a wonderful dog, regardless of preconceived notions of certain breeds, but it is very important that the adopter has the dedication and patience to raise the puppy with boundaries, consistency, structure, & love. The more effort you give towards training & time you allow for exercise, your puppy will grow to be a HUGE source of UNCONDITIONAL LOVE, TOTAL LOYALTY, HAPPINESS, COMFORT & COMPANIONSHIP!

ABOUT OUR RESCUE:
We are a small rescue run by volunteers & focused on finding the right match for both our dogs & for you. If you are interested in adopting through our rescue, you first will need to complete an adoption application & be approved as a potential adopter before meeting any of our pups. No need to be intimidated by our application as it allows us to get to know you & your lifestyle. Of course, the more you can share the better! Please also note, while a fenced yard is fantastic, it is not required by our rescue, however, it may be required for a certain dog. Once adoption applicants are approved to become potential adopters, we offer private appointments where you can meet one or several dogs at the discretion of the rescue. We offer a unique & pleasant experience focused on finding the perfect match. It is extremely important to us that everyone is treated with respect & that NO ONE IS LEFT HANGING. WE WILL GET BACK TO YOU WITHIN 4 TO 5 DAYS of application submission. If there is a dog you are eager to meet, please email us before the 4-5 days! IF YOU DO NOT HEAR FROM US AT THAT POINT, PLEASE CALL US DIRECTLY at 203-241-2351 so that we can check the status of your application and move it forward immediately. We look forward to hearing from you and helping you find your new best friend!

HOME/RENTER INSURANCE:
SOME PROVIDERS HAVE VERY STRICT POLICIES REGARDING WHICH TYPE OF DOG BREEDS ARE ALLOWED UNDER THEIR COVERAGE. STATE FARM WAS SUGGESTED TO US AS THEY DO NOT PUNISH, DROP, NOR REFUSE YOU DUE TO DOG BREED SHOULD YOU RUN INTO ISSUES WITH YOUR CURRENT PROVIDER.

name: Ryder
description: Ryder is your guy! He is approximately 2 years old and a Golden Retriever/Border Collie/Heeler mix-best guess. He is a beautiful strawberry blond and has a long lean body with a docked tail. He loves being part of a pack and gets along well with other dogs. He was found as a stray from the Ute reservation in Cortez, NM, and is so glad he caught his freedom ride to Colorado. This smart goofy guy rides well in the car and hopes to become your favorite adventure buddy. He can be a little reserved at first, but once he becomes comfortable, he is affectionate and enjoys shadowing your every move. Ryder is housebroken and does well in his crate, although he prefers to be outside or free roam in the house. He is learning how to live in a house and once he masters his leash skills, he will make an awesome running buddy. Ryder is UTD on shots, neutered, and microchipped. He will do best with an active home, and someone that will be willing to continue his training. He would love a home with a companion dog, and older kids would suit him fine.Ryder is being fostered in Littleton. Want to meet Ryder and fall in love? Apply to adopt at rezdawgrescue.org

name: URGENT Leo
description: URGENT â Laid back Leo is sending out word to all humans in need of a cuddle bug âI am seeking a forever loving home to live out my golden years and I WOULD LOVE TO BE YOUR CUDDLE BUG!â.  Would you like to meet Leo?  At no fault of his own, Leo has found himself with no where to go.  He has done nothing wrong, in fact he is amazing!  He is what we call an easy keeper and he needs a home, or foster home, fairly quickly.  If you are looking for a loving, gentle, sweet, senior boy to cuddle and tool around with, Leo is your boy.  In exchange, he will cherish everything you do, quietly watch over you, join you on your errands and chill out with you any chance he gets.  He is devoted and adores his humans and will follow their lead. Do you want to meet this gentle soul and see for yourself how amazing he is?  He is located in CT.  Please send an email ASAP to RickyC68@aol.com for more information and please include your phone number so that we can contact you.

name: Leroy
description:
Oh Heeeey it's me Leroy!
I am 3 years old old and I am very affectionate and mushy and I love to play with my toys.
I have survived hard times and come out sweet on the other side. Get A Bull has been taking me weekly to see a great trainer who is helping to socialize me. I am crate-trained, neutered and vetted. We suspect Chloe is an Aussie/Kelpie Cross - two predominant breeds common to that part of Texas. Chloe is a lone star searching for a loving galaxy with good vet references and a fence.

name: Troy Bolton
description: Meet Troy Bolton, a 4-year-old Border Collie mix! He's hoping his arrival in NYC on 9/28 could be the \"Start of Something New. Troy has been having a blast at his foster home since \"Breaking Free from the Dallas shelter. This 73 lb cutie is an absolute sweetheart who loves people and gets along great with other dogs. Do you remember in kindergarten how you'd meet a kid and know nothing about them, then 10 seconds later you're playing like you're best friends because you didn't have to be anything but yourself? Cuddling with Troy is like that. \"Get'cha Head In the Game and apply to adopt Troy today at heartsandbonesrescue.com

name: Jason Mendoza
description: Meet Jason Mendoza, an 11 month old border collie mix who has no idea what's going on right now but everyone else is talking and he thinks he should too! After an illustrious career as leader of a 60 person dance crew and a failed - er pre-successful - DJ, Jason's realized that there's more to life than street dancing competitions. He's ready to chill out in his bud-hole (it's just like a hole where he and his buds can hang out) and watch some Jacksonville Jaguars games with his forever family instead. Jason is almost fully grown at 45lbs and we expect him to get just a tad bigger. He and the rest of our The Good Place crew will be heading from Dallas to a different zone of time - no, that sounds stupid - a different clock land (aka NYC) later this month! Apply to adopt this lovable goofball today at heartsandbonesrescue.com

description:

https://poshpetsrescueny.org/dog-application/
