description: Our newest camper is Suzy Bishop. A long way from Moonrise Kingdom, Suzy found herself in a Dallas shelter on the list to be put to sleep because of her mange. Luckily we gathered the troops and executed a successful rescue mission! Now this sweet lab mix is getting treated and will be headed north soon enough. To foster or adopt, apply at badassbk.com.

name: Gaten Matarazzo
description: Meet the Stranger Things cutie with the best smile, Gaten Matarazzo! This 2 year old pittie mush was been nothing but smiles since we rescued him from a shelter and Dallas. Gaten is an absolutely ah-mazing pup who loves everything and everyone, and has all the smarts of our favorite Stranger Things nerd Dustin - this boy learned sit in no time! Gaten gets along great with other dogs and loves nothing more than cuddling his 50 lb speckled bod on the couch for some Netflix and chill. Apply to adopt Gaten today at heartsandbonesrescue.com.

name: Midna
description:
Hello! My name is Midna! I am estimated to be a 11 month old female black lab mix from Dallas, Texas! The wonderful ladies of Angel of Hope Animal Rescue just knew living in a shelter wasn't the life for me, so....here I am!!!

I am loving having a back yard to run around in! I even have some foster sisters to run and play with!!!! They are so fun!!!! My favorite thing to do is romp around in the yard and then come in for a nap.
There are cats here too but I don't pay them much attention. I am more of a dog loving type of girl.

I am more reserved lady that takes a little while to warm up, but once I do, I LOVE YOU! I really love my foster moms and enjoy snuggling with them on the couch. 

I am fabulous in the kennel and great at going potty outdoors! 

I am told I will be getting a forever home soon! I can't wait to get a family of my own to warm up to! My foster mom says no one can resist my silky soft coat! I can't wait to meet you!



If you are interested in adopting Midna, please fill out an adoption application at www.aohrescue.org

name: Theon
description:
Name: Theon
Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 5 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

name: Wednesday
description:
Our stunning Wednesday enters the room like an arctic blast of cold on a hot summer night and grabs your attention! This magnificent one and a half year old, black Labrador Retriever mix came to us from a big city Animal Control facility, where she spent some time after a lackluster owners abandoned her. She was rail thin and gaunt when she entered the city shelter system, and took some time to adjust to her harsh surroundings. 

When Wednesday came to our Rescue, she was a wild child, a Black Beauty in need of some firm, loving leadership. It was painfully obvious that her owners had missed all of her social development cues, and woefully neglected her manners and leadership training. Wednesday was as precocious as her Addams Family namesake, and seemed to feel that her opinion was warranted on just about every subject.

In no time, Wednesday has developed into a canine thoroughbred, brimming with potential. An energy and personality match is key to Wednesday's happiness. She is a high energy, athletic dog who needs alot of outdoor exercise. She would gleefully keep rigorous pace with an avid runner, hiker or powerwalker, and seems to thrive in the brisk country air. No doubt about it, Wednesday needs an active adopter, but, also one who is extremely proficient in leadership and obedience training. She is not a dog for the casual or inexperienced adopter.

Wednesday largely appears to be Labrador Retriever, but we also suspect some Border Collie in her DNA. She is a lean, tall dog weighing 47 pounds, and is extremely graceful and athletic. She runs with great speed, and could be an agility champion. Wednesday has the energy and intelligence that we see in this high strung Herding breed, as well as the mischievious and impertinent tendency that sometimes occurs when Border Collies are under exercised and bored! 

As a double dose of working dog, Wednesday definitely needs a job, and she is a natural at obedience work. She knows all her basic commands, and has passed many of the Canine Good Citizenship tests. She handles beautifully on lead, and heels nicely. Wednesday still needs some polish on her stranger manners, since she may, on occasion, greet someone rudely, but motivated adopters should be able to work her through any issues by employing her well honed commands. In the right hands, Wednesday will become a fantastic, well behaved companion.

Wednesday would fare best in an adult home, with adopters experienced in handling large, active breeds. She would overwhelm toddlers and seniors. She could easily join a multi-dog home, with another active, well trained dog, but sometimes, unruly and ill mannered dogs press her buttons. We have not had her around cats, but she would most likely chase them beyond their tolerance level.

Wednesday has respectable house manners and is mostly housetrained. She will need some finetuning on her potty routine as she transitions to a new environment. Wednesday is in good health, and has been spayed. She has been vaccinated for rabies, bordatella, and DHLPPC (distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvo, parainfluenza and coronavirus). She has had the 4dx test, and is negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. She has been microchipped and dewormed, and is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm treatment.

If you are interested in Wednesday, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738.

name: Hero
description:
Our magnificent Hero needs a hero of his own. This beautiful, robust boy is a victim of circumstances. His doting owner lost her home, and desperately tried to find housing to accommodate her beloved companion, whom she had raised from a pup. Hero's Mom took up temporary residence in a local motel, until she could get her bearings, but Hero was booted out by the motel manager. After a tearful goodbye, sad Hero was left in the care of a well-respected town shelter, who pled his case to us.

Hero appears to be a handsome mix of black Labrador Retriever and Border Collie. He has the physique and color of a black Lab, and the white tuxedo markings and black speckled white socks that suggest Border Collie. At 50 pounds, Hero has a solid, muscular build, and yet is easy to handle on lead. As a combination herder and retriever, Hero loves the outdoors, and has a hardwired work ethic that needs to be channeled through exercise and obedience work. 

Hero sometimes seems unsure of his place in the world, and needs to join a home with a strong pack leader, willing to provide the structure that he needs to to thrive. Hero gives the impression of caution at first, as he sizes up strangers, but warms quickly to a gentle touch. Adopters will need to be comfortable putting boundaries between Hero and strangers: he can become overzealous in guarding his person. He would be the ideal watchdog.

Hero seems subdued and intimidated at times, in the midst of our busy foster home, and we sense that a quiet, adult home would suit him best. He is not a big fan of change, and a steady, quiet routine will serve him beautifully.  Hero would be the ideal walking or running companion for an active single or couple. He loves the outdoors, can keep a brisk pace on a hike, and longs to make a one-to-one connection with a strong human personality. Hero could easily join a multi-dog home with another well-trained, calm dog, but cats are a definite no-go.

Hero has progressed nicely in his basic obedience training. The obedience work serves him as a job he can take pride in, and he performs the commands beautifully, either for praise or treats. Obedience training is key to providing the working breeds with the purpose and focus that they need to live happily in a domestic lifestyle.

Hero has good house manners and is house trained and crate trained. Adopters should have appropriate patience, and expect to troubleshoot the occasional accident that will inevitably occur during Hero's transition to a new home. He is in excellent health, and is at an ideal lean body weight. He has been neutered, and has been vaccinated for Rabies, DA2PP (distemper, adrenovirus, parvo and parainfluenza), and Canine Flu. He has been boostered as needed, and has had the 4dx test: negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. He has been dewormed, and microchipped. If you are interested in Hero, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738 for more info.

name: Shiloh
description:
On a cold, snowy night in December of 2012, a PFPO foster family was walking their dogs when they found a sweet black pitbull with an old rope tied to her collar. It was apparent this dog had been tied out and had broken loose. The family took the dog to the shelter to give the owners a chance to claim her. No one came for her.

The family called the shelter everyday to check on her. When it became clear that no one was coming to claim the dog, they asked PFPO to accept her into the foster program. The family called the dog Shiloh.

From the moment Shiloh came to live with her foster family, they knew that she was a sweet and special girl. Shiloh was only about 8 months old and full of energy! Shiloh loved to go on walks, play in the snow, and take catnaps in the sun. Shiloh loved people, but she didnât understand other dogs. So, Shilohâs foster family worked very hard to find her the perfect home and perfect family to love her and her quirks.

Just 6 weeks after she entered her foster familyâs home, Shiloh had an adoption application from a nice retired man who lived in Delaware. After several visits and overnight stays (including an âaccidentâ on the carpet during her first meeting and eating a loaf of bread off the kitchen counter), Shilohâs foster family knew that this was Shilohâs perfect forever family. But, sometimes in life, sad things happen to good dogs.

Shiloh lived with this nice old man for 5 years until he got sick and passed away. Suddenly, Shiloh was without her perfect family. Staying true to the rescueâs promise of always taking back its own, Shiloh is now back with PFPO. She is still sweet. She is still loves adult people (and kids over 10). And, she still doesnât understand other dogs. She needs a new perfect family to love her. 

Could that be you?

Shiloh's adoption fee is $100. She is spayed UTD on vaccines, micro-chipped, heartworm negative and on heartworm/flea/tick prevention.

name: Lemon
description:
My name is Lemon, I am available for adoption through Colorado Canine Rescue (CCR) - a nonprofit dog rescue located in the Denver area. My vet and foster mom have guessed that I am around 2 years old and an American Pit Bull Terrier or \"pit bull-type dog.\" I was rescued from an overcrowded shelter in New Mexico. I will be available to adopt/go home after July 5th. I am currently completing a board and train program through High Drive Dog Company in Longmont, Colorado. Part of my adoption requirements include follow up training with High Drive (sponsored by CCR for 3 months), no other animals in the home, no children under 12, and no cities with BSL (breed specific legislation). It is preferred I am adopted to a home with a 6 foot wooden fence. These requirements are non-negotiable. Lemon would do best living with someone who has bully breed experience. Lemon weighs around 60 pounds, is crate trained, and doing well with housetraining. She can be vocal when she needs something, and is not appropriate for apartment/condo living.

Lemon had a rough start to life; being kenneled 24/7 for 2 months straight prior to arriving in Colorado was a lot of stress. Lemon has worked through a lot of reactivity issues. She actually plays well with a lot of dogs. She is NOT a candidate for dog parks. However, she is always welcome to attend supervised playgroups at High Drive (please see http://www.highdrivedogco.com/ for more details about the company). Lemon is not a coach potato. She is bold, eager to learn, and ready to take on the world. Lemon needs to be challenged physically and mentally. She is funny and affectionate. This pup may have started out as a lemon, but she is quite a peach.

If you are interested in adopting Lemon, please submit an application located on our website, www.coloradocaninerescue.org. We are asking for a $200.00 adoption donation. Lemon is spayed, up to date on vaccinations, and micro-chipped. Please note, CCR cannot guarantee the breed composition or ages of our dogs as we usually have no history prior to them entering the shelter. In addition, most dogs listed as potty trained will experience an adjustment period as they learn the routines in their new home.

We are proud to partner with the following veterinarians who offer a free first exam for your animal, exclusively for HT adopters: Caring Hands Animal Hospital, Palisades Veterinary Clinic, Sunshine Animal Hospital and Clarendon Animal Care and all VCA Animal Hospitals. Additionally, any VCA hospital will cover illnesses up to $250 at no cost to any Homeward Trails adopter. Start your new dog out on the right foot with this valuable, expert advice and guidance FREE! You can save animals like this one by becoming a foster! name: Lily
description:
Gorgeous Lily simply leaves us breathless! This gorgeous, Alpha Diva Husky mix will make Northern breed lovers weak in the knees, but she needs seasoned Husky folks willing to focus on her ongoing training, and rein in her chutzpah. 

Lily came to us last year from a Florida rescue, who asked for our help in solving some behavior quirks that they thought stemmed from some physical abuse in her former home. Lily was slow to trust stangers and very hand shy. She recoiled to human touch and seemed skittish.

Often we find that a Husky's beauty is his or her downfall. These stunning dogs attract a wide array of adopters ranging from extremely savvy, to those novices bewitched with his or her \"wolf-like\" appearance. We believe wholeheartedly that a Husky, regardless of individual temperment, requires dog handling ability that is well above average. Time and time again, we have known Huskies who have foiled the best laid intentions of their novice adopters.

At the age of four, Lily is a formidable presence. She is a Husky mix (possibly part German Shepherd), and weighs in at a very solid 60 pounds. She is tall and leggy, and extremely athletic. While Lily has a generally friendly demeanor and seems to enjoy the attentions of strangers, she also has a very well entrenched Alpha Diva vibe, and requires some serious handling chops and command presence in an adopter. 

Lily would be the ideal companion for very serious Husky folks, who are comfortable establishing rules and boundaries with Huskies, or other large breeds, so that Lily knows exactly where she stands. A loosey-goosey home structure will allow her to assert herself in ways that are not optimal for a human-canine living arrangement! 

The key to success with Lily is a sufficient amount of exercise, and ongoing obedience training to maintain leadership. She is a high-energy dog who needs a couple brisk leash walks each day and, preferably, an active outdoor lifestyle, with a Husky savvy single or couple. She would be the ideal running or walking companion, and would love to accompany her adopters on hiking or camping adventures. She loves the outdoors, and needs to be in a active home, in which she can be integrated into a lifestyle, not relegated to a backyard.

Lily would be best-suited to an only dog environment, or perhaps with one other compatible male. While Lily can be bossy and demanding in the Dog Pack, we certainly wouldn't rule out the right dog chemistry, but we would have to test this carefully at adoption. She seems to have some buddies in her canine playgroup, but then also seems to bully some dogs of lesser stature. We don't think that she would be suitable for a home with cats or small children. 

Lily has decent house manners, that will continue to improve under her adopter's patient, knowledgeable leadership. She is house trained and crate trained, although adopters should expect an accident or two during her transition to a new home. description:

name: Rose Talbot-Bassador
description:
09/10/19

I have had the pleasure of Rose Talbot being a houseguest in our home for the past 3 months; I guess I should say she is like one of my own.  She is a sweet and gentle girl who needs to trust and understand love.  She truly hangs on her bed for 95% of her day.  Her exercise consists of running from the backdoor to her bed.  She ventures out to let us know when she wants to go outside or we are late with her meal.  She loves her soft food and treats.  She still goes submissive when you reach down to pet her, but she has improved.  She provides her fur foster siblings with kisses as they come over to check on her.  I will share she would do best in a home that will give her time to adjust, earn her trust and provide a soft bed to lay in.  She really is a low maintenance dog that has captured the heart of her foster mom.  I keep telling her that the perfect family has not come yet, but one day although it will be sad they will come and finally give her her forever home, the one that will provide her with the love and attention she truly deserves.



7/1/19

So are you looking for a new best friend that is so appreciative of the little things?  Are you looking for a gentle soul that just wants a soft bed and love that she deserves?  Are you looking for a new companion that will melt your heart every time you look into her eyes?  Look no further!!!!

Meet Rose, a very gentle girl that finally is getting the love and attention that she deserves.  She has a tough life, but things are looking up for this sweet girl.  She recently made her trip north from Georgia to begin her journey to find a home she can call her own.  

Although she wears her past, she has been doing well with housetraining, gets along with her fur foster siblings, and loves belly rubs.  Unfortunately Rose needed 23 teeth removed, I believe she is feeling so much better; she loves her canned food.  She is fully recovered from all of her medical treatments and is now ready to receive applications to find her forever home.  



6/25/19
Rose has had a tough couple months.  She gave birth to her puppies but due to her poor health and theirs---all the puppies passed away.  Rose had a couple cysts/tumors removed and tested --they were benign.  Rose is now spayed and up to date on her shots.  She is feeling better and looking forward to the next chapter in her life.

3/30/19

Rose came from Long County AC in GA. She is a 6-8 yr old really cute  bassadore. She appears to be pregnant, will ask the vet to check Tuesday.  She  is heart worm positive. She looks like she has had many litters before. She is friendly and gets along good with others. 

 Rose will be Heart worm treated and spayed once  her puppies are weaned and Rose is Vet cleared

name: Jake ( courtesy post)
description:
Hello my name is Jake, 
My family adopted me almost 4 years ago in Cumberland RI. My paperwork said I was a lab/husky mix from Georgia, I wasnât quite a year old yet (according to my paperwork).
When they showed up to get me I was very shy and I smelled pretty terrible, I am surprised they brought me home. After we arrived home I was given a wonderful tubbie with warm water and oatmeal shampoo. I was nice and clean and ready to play. They took me to a soccer game ? 
I had an older brother named Joshua that was 9 years old, he loved to hug me and play with me. 
I had one accident when I was brought home, and I loved my crate. There were two cats at my new home, and they really did not interest me very much, they lived downstairs and I was the king of the upstairs living area. I could go outside whenever I wanted on my run that was in the back yard. 
I had two husky friends next door that I would talk to through the fence. 
My family brought me to two different training classes, but I was told that I needed individual training. 
Mom bought me a prong collar because I would pull her when we would go for a walk, it doesnât hurt, but it reminds me that I cannot pull my Mom when we walk. 
In April 2017 my family started taking care of a 4-month-old infant every weekend to help my momâs best friend. To this day Hunter is still my best friend, and I do not like it when he must leave on Sundayâs. He feeds me my food and gives me my favorite milk bone cookies all the time. Yum! 
My mom and dad love taking me on trips with them because I am not a big fan of the kennel. 
I have been to Dover Foxcroft Maine several times, I love it up there because I can run free. I love all the snow that they get up there and I love chasing my Mom and my brother on their bikes when they are riding down the road. I get a lot of exercise when I am in Maine. 
I have also been to the Outer Banks of North Carolina, I love the sunshine and the beach! I had my own bunk bed in the house we rented for a weekâ¦..I did very well in the truck on the way down and the stop at the hotel over night so we could rest. 
Last week I was in Old Orchard beach laying under my umbrella watching the waves.  I love to go walking and for rides in the truck, my crate and my blanket is my safe place and I have my own room.
 At night we play with my toys, my humans throw them and I run to fetch my squeekies. 
While growing up I started to display some behaviors that my family was not very happy with. I became extremely protective of my humans and I do not like it when people come to visit or strangers come up to me and try to pet me. When my older brother has friends over I have to go in my room in my crate to make sure everyone is safe. I have not bitten anybody but when my family left me over night to go to the water park our neighbor (my momâs close friend) was letting me out to pee and I refused to let her in the house to take me out.  Recently we found out that I was not a lab husky mix, I am actually a lab/chow mix, so that explains why my tongue is black and my behaviors. 
I know that my family loves me very much, they work very hard and do not always have the time to give me the exercise that I need. My older brother is slacking, and he does not let me out to pee when my Mom and Dad are not home, I hear my Mom say itâs a teen thing. They have me training with an E-collar now and Iâm doing very well with. 
My humans want me to be happy and safe and feel that I belong with a single person that has time to exercise with me. I love the kids in my family, but I donât know about other children. 
I am an excellent guard dog and I am totally house broken; my humans never have to lock the doors in the house because nobody is getting passed me. 
I am hoping to find a good home and promise to love you unconditionally like I do my Mom, but before I get into trouble she thinks it is best to see if there is a better living situation for me. I know this is breaking my Momâs heart, but she is trying to protect me. 

If interested in me please email Kimberly Larson at krlarson13@gmail.com

Heâs been on the road for we donât know how long but he certainly never forgot his manners or tricks or how to please and be a companion animal.

He has some lumps and bumps which have been biopsied and have been diagnosed as lipomas and therefore not removed as the vet felt it wasnât necessary.

He has some significant hair loss from a flea infestation which has been managed with some medicated flea baths and nextguard.  He also has bacteria on his skin that he has been given medicated baths for but nothing contagious.

Heâs had a rough time
With pneumonia and has been treated at the emergency vet with antibiotics and nebulizers.  We have repeated xrays multiple times to ensure it continues to improve and have extended courses of antibiotics to ensure he gets back to full health.

He is heartworm negative.

We have been giving him
Liquid collagen to help his skin and hair as well.

He continues to gain weight as needed and is currently at 86 lbs.

Jack does still love to play and learn.  Fetch with a ball is his favorite.

Jack would be an amazing family dog if you are looking for the total package.  He absolutely adores kids and watches over them
Wherever they go.

He comes with a reduced adoption fee as well given his age as we would like that money to go toward helping him continue to get better.

name: DG
description:
Meet DG! This little porker is just too cute. Sheâs a min pin, but missed the memo on the min part :-) We think it makes her only that more adorable and lovable! DG was an owner surrender from a very rural area of Georgia. She was neglected, living outside and being fed chocolate as a regular diet and was even more obese than she is now. We knew we had to get her out of there before she was dead. DG has been in rescue now and has gotten healthy. She has lost some weight (still has more to go!) and gotten spayed. She is a very sweet and quiet girl from what we have seen. DG seems to be good with other dogs; even excitable big dogs trying to play with her. We think she is about 10 years old. DG would love a retirement home and is anxiously awaiting her family while in her foster home in Baltimore County, MD. She is available immediately and foster or adoption applications can be found at www.snarrnortheast.org 
Her adoption fee is $250.

name: Linus
description: Born around May 2016 and arrived at TVR April 23, 2019 Linus is a very special boy who will need a patient, calm, and loving home to help him come out of his shell. He was likely not exposed too much as a young puppy; perhaps he was a stray in the early part of his life. We don't really know the root cause but for Linus the world can be a scary place. In the month that he has been in our care, he has become more confident and secure in his surroundings. He is still easily startled but is able to recover more than when he first arrived to us from Georgia. He has gone from staying in one corner, rarely moving throughout the day, to walking around, wagging his tail when he sees staff, and barking when he sees other dogs. He likes to play with the other dogs and is slowly gaining more confidence interacting with humans. In spite of his fears, he does know how to walk on leash and seems to be relatively house-trained, though accidents are likely during any new, stressful transitions. Linus would probably do best in a home with another dog who is friendly and able to show him the ropes. Because he startles so easily and could bolt out an open door in a panic, he would probably be better in a home without young children. We see so much potential in this sweet guy and with a little time and compassion, we think he could turn into a happy, loving companion. (A note about housetraining: Linus, like many rescue dogs, does seem to be housetrained but Their Voice Rescue does not guarantee that he won't have accidents or behavioral marking incidents in a new home.)

name: Lollie
description:
LOLLIE is a big, mushy, sweet 2-year-old, 55-pound, Black Labrador Retriever mix with a passel of adorable little pups.

Lollie came to us from Georgia, where she had to fend for herself as a lonely stray.  One fine day she wandered onto the property of a family who's male dog lived outside on a chain.  Lollie and the handsome stranger struck up a friendship and soon became romantically involved.  She soon gave birth to a litter, but for reasons unknown to us, the puppies did not survive.

The family, doing what they must have thought to be the right thing, allowed Lollie to stay on at their house, sharing outdoor accommodations with their dog. Before very long... well, there's no need to finish that sentence.  This time the family realized that something had to be done and had the presence of mind to get her into rescue.  So she left Georgia on a midnight train, (a rescue transport), and 12 or so hours later, arrived at the shelter of Animal Alliance.  Two days after her arrival she gave birth to her litter, the beautiful little pups are safe and sound in our care.  As of this writing, 7/18 the little ones are 4 weeks old.  In a few more weeks, the whole little family, including Momma, will be spayed/neutered, vaccinated, et cetera, and ready to take their rightful places in their new adoptive families.

If you would like to meet, foster or adopt Lollie, all you have to do is fill out our online FOSTER/ADOPTION APPLICATION, which can be found in the main menu of our website or at the bottom of this page - just copy and paste the link into your browser. 

Once we've reviewed your application, you can come and meet Lollie!  We think the two of you will hit it off!

Thank you for your interest in helping homeless animals!

***

This pet is spayed or neutered in accordance with our strict policy wherein all animals are altered prior to adoption.  This pet is dewormed, current on vaccines, and started on monthly flea/tick and preventatives.

Animal Alliance's policy is that we will adopt dogs younger than 1 year old to families with children under 9 years old. We do not adopt dogs 1 year or older to families with children under 9 years old due to the unknown history of adult dogs. 

Prior to submitting an application, please see the Animal Alliance Adoption Process for adoption details.

Animal Alliance is not a shelter where all the animals are housed in one location. Animal Alliance is a foster care network and animals are housed in many different locations. If you are interested in adopting a pet, please apply using the online application; applicants who call our phone line will hear a recorded voicemail with this identical message. We adopt many animals each week and meet prospective adopters at various locations so they can meet the animals they are interested in.

To fill out an adoption application, go to:
https://www.animalalliancenj.org/fosteradoption-application/

Cody loves attention from humans, and gets along well with his foster sister, a female Australian Cattle Dog. He has not interacted with children, so he would do best in a home with older children. He is obsessed with fetch, and loves playing with toys!

Cody would do best in a home without  larger male dogs, but he does very well with his female foster sister. Cody does not do well with cats. He walks very well on a leash, and when not in a fenced area, must be kept on a leash. He's a curious guy, so a home with a fenced yard would be the best for Cody.

name: SCHROEDER CROSS-POST PORTLAND, MAINE
description:
This handsome fella is Schroeder - a small JRT/Hound, maybe some bully breed in the mix, roughly 5 year old dog brought up from Georgia to Maine by another Maine rescue several years ago when he was a puppy, and is now finding himself in need of a new home. Although his original adoptive family has gone above and beyond with training and working with Schroederâs behaviors over the years, the living environment is just proving to be too much for him despite everyoneâs best and continued efforts to ensure he is not constantly stressed.

Schroeder is a sweet, energetic dog who really loves his people. Although he has been living with young kids for some time and does very well with âhis ownâ, he gets very stressed with the busy neighborhood kids and spooks easily, causing his behavior to worsen while on walks or trying to enjoy any outdoor time and he becomes reactive to other dogs and sometimes people. Ideally he needs a quiet, adult home with older/no children. A condo environment would not work well for him. It is possible he could coexist with another calm, confident dog, but Schroeder will need time to decompress and adjust through this transition so he should be treated as an only dog and be kept calmly separated from any other dogs in the home at least during this initial period. Cats are probably a no-go as his hound instincts send him on a chase.

We are helping to network Schroeder for a new home as we feel he deserves this second chance to find his ideal forever family, and sadly his original rescue is not willing or able to take him back and place him due to liability concerns. We realize that Schroeder is not an easy to place dog, and readily available fosters for a dog like him simply do not exist, but we feel he is a trainable, adoptable dog and he deserves the chance to find that special someone willing to put in the extra effort to provide him with a happy, calm lifestyle. With proper training, invested time and commitment, he has SO much potential and will be a great dog in the right home.

Schroederâs owners are not asking for a re-homing fee, but that his new people continue working with a positive trainer to ensure he has the resources and skills needed to manage his stressors and ensure a successful placement.

If you are interested in helping about this pocket-sized guy, please fill out an application on our website: 
www.buddyupanimalsociety.org/dog-adoption-application

Please help us share Schroeder and find him that perfect forever home he needs and deserves!

? If you have any questions please feel free to email us at info@buddyupanimalsociety.org ?

Thank you for reading about and sharing Schroeder, let's help find this boy his true forever!

name: Cola

Are you looking for the perfect new addition to your family? Well, then look no further than Cola herself. Cola is a 1.5-year-old Black Labrador Retriever mix, fully grown at about 47 pounds. She was rescued from Lyons, Georgia. She is known in her foster home as the \"ready-made-perfect-angel\". Cola is put simply - as wonderful as they come. She follows her foster mom like a shadow and is super obedient and smart. She would love a family with children to play with her. When Cola gets excited her whole body swings as she wiggles with joy - it is quite the site! She has a very happy tail as well. Cola walks very well on a leash, is crate trained, and also primarily housebroken. She gets along very well with other dogs and cats too. Cola is a happy, social, loving dog who simply cannot wait to find her people!

Cola is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

name: Precious
description: Precious came from Georgia.  She was surrendered because her owner was no longer able to care for her.  Precious did not come to us in the best of shape.  She was not spayed, did not have any vaccination history and her teeth were in need of a good dental.  She had to have 12 teeth removed.  She is 6-8 years old and 13 lbs.  She is a living doll and super affectionate.  She is feeling great and in good health.  It is so nice to see her prancing around and feeling much better.  She is now ready for her new home and anyone who gets her is very lucky to have her.  She absolutely loves to go for car rides and walks.  She is also a big cuddle-bug.  If you would like to adopt Precious please contact Peggy Stern at pmpstern@yahoo.com.

name: Hogan SCAS
description:
Hogan is a super sweet boy and a favorite of our staff and volunteers!! He seems to greet his human friends with a smile, and they can't help but smile back when they see that happy face. Hogan is a black lab/retriever mix around 3 years old that weighs about 45 lbs. He came to us from one of the worst animal shelters in the rural mountains of Georgia. A rescue person saw his picture, went to meet him there, and decided this boy needed to be saved.

Hogan's very favorite thing to do is PLAY! Perhaps that's because he came from a place where he sat alone in a run with nothing to do all day. :( But whether it be Fetch or tug of war, Hogan loves his toys! He's also been going to Agility with a volunteer friend and he does great on the course! He'll even swim when given the chance! Hogan is a smart boy and knows some basic commands like sit, stay, drop and down. He is housebroken, crate trained, and good with most dogs.

Unfortunately, Hogan was recently returned after being adopted for about 8 months because he became very protective of his home. Hogan needs a strong owner who has experience with protective/territorial dogs. Although he was very loving with his family, we feel that Hogan would do best in a home with no children because of his protectiveness. Hogan does get along with other dogs but has gotten into a few scuffles at doggie day camp.

If you'd like to meet Hogan for yourself, just fill out an application at www.ehrdogs.org and be sure to mention his name!! Hogan SCAS!!

name: Margo
description:
.Margo is a total cutie pie who is sweet as can be and the kind of dog you can't help but feel happy around because her personality is so joyful.  She is about 3 years old and weighs 50 pounds.  She has been here for a more than a year and would love a home of her own with people that would love her for the rest of her life. She was found as a lost doggie.  She is a hound with beautiful markings.  Margo is spayed, housebroken, up to date with her vaccinations, micro-chipped, and heartworm negative.  She knows the commands of sit, stay, and lay down and walks nicely on a leash.

Margo came from a high kill shelter in Georgia where.her time was almost up.  She is a high energy dog who loves to play and run around in the yard with the other dogs.  She is wonderful with people or dogs.  We don't know how she is with cats.  She has shown no aggression since coming here and only seems to have a loving, sweet nature for anyone who comes her way.  

We think she would be fine with older children but because of her energy level may accidentally knock young children down.  Margo loves to play with her toys, including balls, tugs and hard bones; which she loves to bite on.  

Because Margo is a high energy dog a fenced yard would be a must so she would be able to run around and be safe and secure.  

If u think Margo might fit in your family, please call Judi at (908) 510-8721 or send me an application for her. Just click on the Application Button and return it to Save Us Dog Rescue at fries3@aol.com

name: Layla
description:
Layla is one of the most beautiful dogs we have ever had in our rescue.  She is a female Labrador Retriever mix and is 3 1/2 years old.  She is approx 48 pounds.  Layla is spayed, housebroken, heartworm negative, up to date on her vaccinations, and micro-chipped.  She walks well on a leash and would make a good running partner. Layla knows the commands of sit and stay. she also knows how to give her paw and to down when asked. Her favorite thing to do is sit on your lap and go to sleep. Layla also loves to give kisses and cuddle. She has been here for more than two years and no one has shown much interest in her. 

Layla has come into rescue from a kill shelter in Georgia where her time was almost up.  She is doing well since coming into rescue and loves to give kisses and would love nothing more than to sit on your lap and snuggle. Her eyes are the most gorgeous color and seem to penetrate through you as she looks at you. 
She takes her treats very gently from your hand.  We believe Layla would do well with children but care should be taken with very young children who could be knocked over by accident through play.

Layla loves to play with her toys, including a ball and hard bones, which she loves to bite on.  She enjoys the company of other dogs and loves to play together with them in  the yard.  A fenced yard is a must for this dog so she would be able to run free and safely.  Layla is a high energy dog who loves to play with human or dog.

If u think she might be a match for your family, please email Save Us Dog Rescue at fries3@aol.com or call Judi at (908) 510-8721.

name: Buffy
description:
Beautiful, sweet, loving, well behaved, gorgeous Buffy.  She is a white, female, pointer/shepherd mix dog with brown spots on her ears and very pale brown spots on her fur.  She is a very unique looking dog.  Buffy is 3 and a half years old, 50 pounds, housebroken, up to date on her vaccinations, spayed, micro-chipped and heartworm negative.  She also has the most gorgeous white eye lashes. She knows how to sit and will do so when asked.  She is a little shy but loves giving and getting love. She is so sweet and loving. 

Buffy came from a kill shelter in Georgia where her time was almost up.  Since coming into rescue she has shown no aggression but only sweetness.  She is a high energy dog who loves to play with her toys, including balls and hard bones which she loves to bite on.  She takes her treats very gently.  We believe that she would be great with children, but care should be taken with  young children who could be knocked over by accident through play.  

Buffy is fine and friendly with other dogs and enjoys running around and playing with them here.  A secure fenced yard would be a must for this dog so she could run safely free.  We don't know how she is with cats.  Buffy is so loving and sweet and is so deserving of a loving home. Please give her a chance. 

If u think Buffy might be a good match for your family,  please send me an application to Save Us Dog Rescue at fries3@aol.com   Buffy is so deserving of a forever, loving home. If u would like to talk to me about her, please call Judi at (908) 510-8721.

name: Matilda
description:
Meet Matilda! (I've been calling her \"Mattie some too.)

This girl was a stray that we rescued from a shelter in Georgia. She was so sweet, we just had to get her out of that loud and scary place.

She is around a year old and weighs just under 11 pounds. The vet checked her over and said she was a healthy girl, other than fleas and we took care of that! Her best breed guess was Papillon/Terrier mix but whatever the breed is, she is a cutie!

Matilda is spayed current on all vaccines, dewormed, microchipped, heartworm negative, and on heartworm prevention. She must be kept on heartworm prevention all of her life, as all dogs should be.

She is great with most dogs and cats as long as she is slowly introduced (like with most dogs). She can think she is the boss, so some dogs may not appreciate that. Older kids I think would be fine with her, but she's not been \"kid tested\". She seems to be crate trained and we are working on housetraining. She is doing well with that.

The adoption fee is $225 to an approved home. All vet records and her collar will be given to her adopter and the time of adoption.

Here is the link to our adoption application: https://forms.gle/LtT3oVicgYDfrLpL7

The application is to be completed prior to meeting the pet(s) you are interested in adopting. Thank you for looking at our rescues in need of amazing homes!

name: Roxie
description:
Roxie
Pit bull terrier/Cocker Spaniel mix
Spayed female, two years old, 40 lbs. 
Fully vaccinated, dewormed and heartworm negative
If you love pitties and all the love they have to offer then, this is your girl! Roxie is a smart, happy girl who loves to cuddle on the sofa in the home and is also always up for a fun game of fetch in the back yard. She is quick to learn her commands and she will benefit from a dog savvy owner to keep her mentally and physically fit! Like any dog, Roxie needs structure and discipline on a daily basis and she will reward you with love and respect. Housebroken and crate trained, Roxie is a perfect lady in the home. When she was rescued from a high kill shelter in Georgia, she enjoyed playing with a number of dogs at her boarding facility and was sweet and friendly with all her cohorts. 
She still loves to play but is now more selective with her canine playmates. We believe she will flourish in a home as an only dog-yet we are open to the possibility that she may find a perfect forever home with a companionable brother to play the days away with. Roxie is an awesome companion and has a lot of love to give! If you are interested in adopting Roxie, please email littlepups2017@gmail.com or call 757-630-6181.

name: Rose
description:
Hi, my name is Rose! I am a Min Pin mix that came up to Wisconsin from Georgia. My age estimate is 7 years but it's possible that I am older than that.  I weigh 16 #.   I am the sweetest of girls and am considered special needs because I am blind.  I could also use a dental as my teeth have seen better days.  An overall exam with your vet would be best for me as it's possible I have dry eye along with the blindness.  Lubricating drops would help me immensely with that!  I will be so happy to have a lap to sleep on and a safe home to call my own.  Apply for me today!

name: Skyy
description:
Name: Skyy

Approximate Age: Approx. 2yrs old

Breed: Pit mix

Sex: Female

Special Needs: Allergies

Adoption fee: $300.00

Up to date on vaccinations/preventatives, spayed, house/crate trained, microchipped

I came to the rescue back in 2016 from a high kill shelter in Texas. The conditions werent the best to say the least and oh yeah, I was SUPER pregnant. Not a good place for a expecting mom. Thankfully, I was taken from there just in time and was able to have my puppies in a foster home. I was even thrown a huge baby shower by a ton of people who follow SNARR! I was so happy to finally have had my babies and be out of the shelter but my excitement quickly became tragedy. Not long after giving birth, almost half of my babies passed away- only 4 survived. 
Now that my remaining pups have gone to live their own liveshere I sit and wait. While I adore my foster mom, I want a home to call my own. 
Im confused on why I dont have my own home yet Im incredibly adorable and Im hands down the most wiggly tushed pocket pittie youll ever meet! I have never met a person I didnt like, however dogs.not too fond of dogs or any other furry little creatures. I blame that on my high prey drive and Im very smart when it comes down to it- I can be a pro stalker and Im lightning fast so its best that the temptation isnt there in forever home. Give me any kind of human though and its nothing but hugs (literally, I give hugs) and kisses! 
Due to having allergies, I take Benedryl and cannot eat chicken.

Transport to any approved home within the US can be provided at no additional fee
Currently Skyy is located in Lawrenceville, Georgia.


Please visit SNARRANIMALRESCUE.org to fill out an adoption application and our adoption requirements/process can also be found there!

name: Selima
description:
Name: Selima

Approximate Age: 3.5yrs

Breed: Baladi

Sex: Female

Special Needs: Paralyzed

Adoption Fee: $200

Up to date on vaccinations/preventatives. Spayed. Microchipped.

Where I come from people are very unkind to my breed and I was very close to not making it out alive. I was born in Egypt where baladis are considered trash & many people there go out of their way to hurt us. I was born with a hem vertebra and as a very young puppy; a very traumatic injury took away my ability to walk. Some awful individual shot me, rendering me paralyzed. As if that wasnt cruel enough, I was then tossed into a cemetery where I was left to die. Thankfully, not everyone in Egypt is cruel. I was noticed by a person visiting a loved one at the cemetery & was brought to a local rescue for medical care. 
I however was one of the lucky ones. After seeing pictures of how hurt I was, SNARR took me and flew me to the USA to get medical treatment. That was in June 2015. The bullet was removed from my spine and because of the extent of my injuries, my back legs needed to be removed. 
Today, I am a new dog. Even though I dont have any legs, I can cruise around the house just as fast as my four legged siblings. My foster mom has tried to keep diapers on me, but I dont like them so Im not wearing them. I finally trained her, so she just expresses me now & lets me be a naked baby. 
I love playtime with my other siblings, playing dress up for the holidays, snuggling with my foster mom and racing around the house like a maniac. 
There are some things though that make me nervous. Children can be too rambunctious and fast, men can be too big and their voice scares me. My wheelchair? I hate it and would rather be on the ground moving myself. Ive never been around a cat before so Im not sure how I would do with them; I guess they do have the luxury of being able to jump if they want to get away from me though. My ideal home would be with a woman or if there happens to be a man with a soft manner and a ton of patience.

*Transport can be arranged to any approved adopter within the US at no additional charge.
Currently Selima is located in Lawrenceville, Georgia.

Please visit SNARRANIMALRESCUE.org to fill out an adoption application and our adoption requirements/process can also be found there!

name: Kaydo
description:
***Kaydo is currently located in Glenwood, GA but is scheduled to attend our Sept 13-15 adoption event at Rosedale Mills (Pennington, NJ.***

Kaydo came to our rescue as an owner surrender, being among the 19 dogs and puppies that SoCo was asked to find new homes for after their owner was served with an eviction notice. Kaydo was one of his former owner's \"favorites\" and once you spend a little time with him, you'll see why the owner felt that way!

Despite obviously having a hard life, Kaydo remains a very people friendly dog. He also is friendly to most other dogs, especially the females, despite having been attacked by a pack of dogs sometime prior to coming to our rescue. In that attack, Kaydo not only suffered having his left ear ripped in two, his right ear was bitten completely off. His hearing seems fine but his ears will require regular cleanings.

The scars that show on Kaydo's body do not define who he is, you won't find too many dogs as affectionate and loyal as Kaydo. He can be very calm at times, others he just wants to play!

Kaydo has lived and enjoys being both indoors and outdoors. We're not sure how well house trained he is so any potential adopters must be willing to provide additional training, if needed. Kaydo has been fully vetted, kept on his monthly preventatives and recently completed his heartworm treatments.

To apply for the adoption of Kaydo, please submit an application at socorescue.com

name: Louise
description:
Here is our sweet girl, Lady Louise!

Buddy Up pulled Louise from Harris County shelter in Houston, Tx with a severe injury to her right eye, nearly 100% proptosis (popping out), which was suspected to be the result of blunt force trauma or injury from another dog. It also appeared to be an injury that she had been suffering with for some time. We don't know the exact details of the trauma Louise experienced, but we do know that she can be a bit overly excited around other dogs, so we need a foster/adoptive home for her either as the only pet, or possibly with another dog similar to her size and energy level that will tolerate her excited energy well as she continues her training. 

Although she is a very sweet girl with all people, she will not be placed in a home with young children due to her her size and energy - she can be a bit clumsy too! Louise is a very excited, bouncy girl and enjoys meeting new people. She is an incredibly sweet, velvety soft pup and everyone that spends times with her cannot help but fall in love. Ideally a mellow adult home able to provide moderate activity to keep her busy and continue training would be perfect for her! No cats for this girl. She is already spayed and up to date on all of her vaccines. 

Louise is an absolute love with everyone she meets and is highly trainable. She is a very smart girl willing and wanting to please, she loves spending time learning new tricks and cuddling up on the couch with company.

Louise is here in Maine and awaiting her forever home. Please email us and send in an application if you can provide a home for this lovely lady! 

Adoption Application: www.buddyupanimalsociety.org/dog-adoption-application

Please email us for additional information: info@buddyupanimalsociety.org

name: Lilly (PA)
description:
Hi, my name is Lil, or as my foster parents call me Lilly Lou. I grew up living in a home in North Carolina but after one of my people passed away the other got really sick and could no longer care for me. I was dropped off at a crowded shelter in the mountains of North Carolina. I wasnât really a big fan of being in the shelter and that is when Pointer Rescue Org showed up and I left with my foster parents. I had a long road trip from North Carolina to Harrisburg, Pennsylvania where Iâm now learning about lots of new things and am excited to find my new forever home. I am a very happy girl that LOVES to be around people and snuggle them on the couch. Every person I have seen I have wanted to meet. The same goes for dogs of all sizes. I enjoy soft, comfortable dog beds where I can get some sun but donât really like laying outside in the hot sun. Iâm not too sure about a lot of dog toys but I really like the soft, fuzzy ones that I can chew on. I get along with the other dog in the house but Iâm not a big fan of playing rough. Just laying around and being close to each other is ok with me. My foster parents tell me I walk well on a leash and donât pull and if I do I know to slow down to let them catch up. I know how to sit, especially if you have some yummy treats for me and will come when called. I LOVE Food and Treats and love to be in the kitchen anytime there is food being cooked. I was told Iâm not the best sous chef but Iâm probably the cutest one. I do like to check out whatâs on the kitchen counter but if you tell me Off I will sadly get off the counter. I enjoy going for walks and hiking but so far I donât like going into any water but I do enjoy a good mud bath. In my dream home I would be the only dog or have a brother or sister that is just as relaxed as me. Iâm a good sleeper and will gladly sleep all night in my kennel unless there is a thunder storm. Iâm not sure about those and if we have one I like to be under the covers in bed with my foster family. If you are looking for a relaxed, sweet southern girl, look no further!

Lil is a white English Pointer with some tan spots. She is around 6-7 years old, up to date on all of her shots (none due until July of 2020), spayed, microchipped, and tested negative for heartworms. She is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm preventative and has been strategically dewormed. She does well with ear cleanings and brushing but needs some coaxing to get a bath and would do best with a groomer or vet trimming her nails.
Interested in fostering? Fill out our volunteer application here: http:// www.pointerrescue.org/ helpus.html

Can't foster right now, but want to help?
Consider sponsoring a dog by making a donation to help with vetting costs. PRO is 501c3 non-profit and is fully funded by donations, your tax-deductible gift would be greatly appreciated!

You see, when I first came; I wasn't sure who I could trust. I mean who was this lady? They kept calling her my foster mom and they told me to trust her!?! My siblings taught me quickly; she's ok. I now lay by her feet when she sits down and I know if I go over to say hi, she will give me a good scratch and or a snuggle. She isn't so bad after all.

If your looking for a well behaved guy to give belly rubs, hangout, snuggle or go on adventures, then I'm your guy!

name: Conan
description: Although he often has a stoic look on his face, Conan absolutely loves people and wants to sit in your lap. Originally rescued from Hurricane Harvey in Houston, Texas, Conan went to two other rescue organizations before coming to Best Friends for help with various medical needs. Conan really needed help getting his allergies under control, and with a lot of hard work and structure, he's finally on the upswing. He is very food motivated and ready to learn new tricks or practice nose work, a fun search and scenting sport. He does tend to shred toys and eat them, so hard toys and chews are best for him. He is crate trained, so he is fine with hanging out in a crate when he is unattended or for nap time. Born in 2009, Conan really likes playing with dogs at the Sanctuary! His food allergies are currently being managed with a prescription diet, which he enjoys, and an occasional bath.

name: Willow a Special girl!
description:
Willow is a great dog that deserves a forever home after a very rough start.   When she went to the vet to be spayed, they discovered a foreign object in her body.  We were all shocked and our hearts hurt for Willow,   Despite what happened to her, she LOVES people.  She has a good heart and will make a great companion to accompany her person wherever life takes them.
 
Willow is a very friendly girl who loves attention from her foster family.  She prefers the company of people and would be a great only dog.  She rides calmly in the car, sleeps quietly in her kennel at night and walks well on a leash.
  
Willow loves to play fetch.  She will play non-stop to the point of exhaustion of either herself or your arm.  She can even catch the ball after one bounce!  We think she could be a great Frisbee dog!

Willow is a lovely Australian shepherd mix that is about a two years old.  She has a shiny black coat with brown outlines.  She weighs about 45 pounds.   She is spayed, micro-chipped and up to date on vaccines,   She is located in Houston, TX and will come to her new home on professional transport,   For an app, please email rhondabarron@earthlink.net

description:
Ed is one big hunk of love!!  Poor Ed was left in the back yard while his family just drove away. Can you imagine what he thought!    He was taken to the local pound, pulled by our rescue and placed in a foster home. 

Big Ed is a kind, fantastic, loving boy and is very much loved by his new foster family!   He lives with his foster mom and her three 11 year old triplets so bring on the kiddos.   He's crate and house trained and loves the children!   They all love hanging out together as you can see from the pics!   

Ed is a Ridgeback mix and is 3 years old and weighs 90 lbs.   He is neutered, micro-chipped and up to date on vaccines.   He did test heartworm positive, has completed his treatment.   This big guy has a lot of love to offer and needs a family to return that love and give him his forever home never to be left behind again. If you feel like you could be that family please contact Freedom Street Rescue at rhondabarron@earthlink.net for an app.   Ed is located in Houston, TX and will come to his new home on professional ground transport.

name: Jason
description:
Jason was found in a local park that is a known dumping ground in Houston, TX. He was injured and limping.  Animal Control was called and he was taken to the City Pound - and that's where his luck changed! We were contacted and happily took Jason into our rescue.  He was treated at the vet and is now happy and healthy! Currently, he is in a kennel and the staff raves about how friendly he is with everyone! He greets you with a full body WIGGLE and he loves to Cuddle too!

He likes to please people and listens extremely well! He comes when called and if he gets a little bit rowdy during play he calms quickly when asked. He is extremely motivated by praise and is very smart! We think he may have some border collie in him! He does have energy and would love a forever home that could provide him with daily walks or runs or has a nice-sized yard for him to play. He is dog friendly but can be a bit exuberant so probably best with older kids and larger/medium size dogs. No cats please. He is adventurous, loves snacks and is treat motivated which means he'll be a star pupil for training! He loves car rides, taking walks, is very loyal, protective and loving. 

Jason is a young GSD/border collie mix (we think, but can't be sure!) and is neutered, micro-chipped and up to date on vaccines. He is about a year old and weighs 75 lbs. description:

After her activities, she is calm and ready to listen to music, take a nap or play with her toys and of course a special treat. 

She will do well in a home with calm, well behaved dogs and even an indoor only cat that is comfortable with dogs...no small children because of her size. Dolly would also be fine as an only dog as long as she has her person to snuggle with at the end of the day and to love her. An experienced dog owner who enjoys outdoor activities, has a fenced yard and time to spend with her would be ideal for Dolly. She will be a loyal and protective companion. 

Dolly completed a two week boot camp with one of Houston's premier dog behaviorists, Maurice Gassiott at Gray Wolf Canine Rehabilitation. He found her to be smart, well behaved and a good pack member.

Dolly is a Boxer/Plott Hound/American Staffordshire Terrier mix. She is 4 years old, weighs 53 lbs, is spayed, heartworm negative and up to date on vaccinations. description: Smokey is shy with people, but he loves walks and food so that is the key to his heart. description: Sosa is a sensitive sweetheart. He's also a fun, active dog who loves toys, water, walks and car rides. He can be a little quirky, and his caregivers say he is like a wiggly cat in a dog's body, but that's what makes him so endearing. Born in 2013, Sundance came to the Sanctuary from a Best Friends Network Partner in Indiana. He guards food and is not comfortable with strangers entering his room or yard. He does better meeting them outside of his area first. At Dogtown, Sundance is doing great with going to his 'place' to wait for his food and with trading his bowls to reduce food guarding. He does not enjoy a lot of handling, especially by new people. He will accept occasional pets but prefers to just do a happy dance around you. He is also difficult for medical handling. He has become comfortable enough with day-to-day handling that he can be harnessed for walks, and he is working on muzzle training for upcoming vet appointments. When it comes to other dogs, Sundance can be picky and seems to prefer females. If you're looking for a dog who dances to his own beat, Sundance would love to meet you.

name: Jax
description:
PLEASE READ THE COMPLETE BIO ON JAX BEFORE APPLYING

Jax is almost ready for adoption!

Jax is a Shih Tzu that came from a true Puppy Mill in Indiana then sold here through a Mall Petstore.  It was recently discovered that he had a liver-shunt and required surgery to repair it.  Jax will need to stay on a low-protein diet or special prescription diet food specific for the liver (please do your homework, the food is not cheap, fortunately heâs a little dog and therefore only eats about a cup a day) he will need to stay on this food for the remainder of his life which should be at least 15 more years.  

Information on liver Shunts:  Congenital portosystemic shunts (AKA liver shunts) are relatively common birth defects in pets where the blood vessels in the abdomen develop abnormally and instead of funneling blood from the intestines through the liver, the blood is able to bypass the liver and enters the systemic circulation. This abnormal blood flow prevents the liver from doing its job of processing the blood â eliminating medications, waste products, and toxins, breaking down nutrients from food, and regulating the bodyâs energy balance.  

You will also need to pay attention to the treats you also give Jax:  some better treat options for dogs with shunts include meat-free dog biscuits, human snacks such as animal crackers and breakfast cereal, or non-toxic fruits and vegetables.
Jax is making up for lost time from being a sick puppy for the last few months before his surgery, but now he is acting like a normal puppy again.  Given he came from a puppy mill, he was clearly not handled/loved on so if you are looking for a companion to sit in your lap..Jax is not the dog for you!  Jax will only go to a home that currently has another small dog of similar size and still on the younger side to play with him and help him learn what is it to be a love pet to us humans. Jax is looking for a home that has the time to invest is proper training and social skills. He is working currently working on leash training and to go potty outdoors.  Jax is crate trained and will use a pad indoors.  Please note:  Jax is not 100% housebroken.  Jax is heartworm negative, neutered and is up to date on vaccinations. Jax has a microchip that will be transferred to the adopter upon completion of the adoption process.  
Jax will only be adopted out locally at this time!!

The adoption fee Jax is $ 300.00.

Scooter is a serious burrower. She loves a bigger crate with lots of blankets for her to nest in and to cover up in. She will often go into her crate to sleep during the day. Yes, that's her under the pink blanket.

Scooter needs daily exercise to keep her from being bored and to build muscles that will help protect her hip. Scooter is incredibly intelligent, so she gets bored easily. name: Jacko
description: Rescued from a property during a dog fight bust in Colorado, Jacko came to Best Friends from a humane society. At Dogtown he is affectionately called 'Jack Jack.' He adores his toys and treats them like his babies, carrying them around and sleeping with them on his bed. Jacko is playful with new dogs once he has gotten to know them, but he also enjoys sunbathing outside with his roommate at Dogtown. Because of his past, Jacko can be nervous meeting new people, especially if he is meeting them for the first time in a small space. He is more confident meeting people outside in an open space and during a walk. Since walks, treats and toys are some of his favorite things, he will trust new people more quickly if they offer him one of these things. He does take treats nicely, and he is eager to learn new things when treats are the reward. Once he is friends with you, Jacko will run right up to you and stop directly in front of your feet to ask for pets and scratches. He can be a very quiet dog and does not 'talk' very much, unless other dogs are 'talking,' too. He is usually a slow walker, but he loves to run when he feels up to it. Recently, Jacko learned to use a ramp to get into a car. He loves lying down and relaxing in the car and is an excellent passenger. Jacko needs a person or family who will show him that it's OK to trust new people. He'll need extra time to meet new people, especially visitors to a home. When he is comfortable, Jacko is truly a clown. He will play bow at people and flash his adorable smile.

name: Bizzie
description:
Age: 4-5 Years (as of 9/6/18)
Weight: 62.7 (as of 9/6/18)

This dog has been spayed/neutered, is up to date on shots, on heartworm preventative and is microchipped.

Bizzie is loving and very sweet!
She's one of those dogs who epitomizes canine forgiveness - you'll see this when you read her backstory. Fortunately for Bizzie, her future's looking ever so bright! We're thinking she's a blend of Chow Chow and Shepherd probably born sometime in 2014 or 2015. She has been fine with adult dogs and puppies; she has not been introduced to cats. She's been great with all adults, and though she has not lived with children, we think she would be okay with older, dog-respectful kids. House training and crate training are in the works, and she seems to do fine on leash. A dog who has lived on a chain for years, like Bizzie did, can have a tendency towards guard dog behaviors and though she has not shown any of these tendencies, her adopters will likely need to work with a professional trainer to help her accept strangers and work through any fears she might exhibit.

Bizzie loves to run and play with other dogs, people and toys! She rides well in the car while crated, she's very calm. Though a fenced yard would be great to get in some running and playing, daily leash walks for business, exercise and fun will work just as well to keep her happy and healthy. And to keep that canine mind sharp, think puzzle toys and games. Bizzie really just wants to find a forever home where she'll be loved and cared for. Could that be your home? Fill out an application today and her people will get right back to you!

Bizzie's Backstory: Bizzie truly deserves a wonderful life. Her first 3-4 years were very hard. She was from the south side of Jackson, Mississippi, and was tied out on a 6-foot chain to be used as a guard dog. Her shelter was limited to a carport, no matter what the temperature or weather was like. She often did not have food nor water, except when a neighbor was contacted for dog food. After that, the neighbor often checked on her and would feed her and give her water. We know that Bizzie had at least one litter of puppies that a rescue took, but Bizzie was left behind. However the rescue did provide a spay for her. Bizzie's friend finally convinced her owner to relinquish her. When the vet checked Bizzie, she did have heartworm, which has been treated and she is now clear. At first, this pretty girl was scared when anyone approached her with a leash - maybe she was afraid she would be tied out again. Of course, we know that this will never again be the case!

Medical Note: This dog has been treated for heartworm disease with melarsomine injections. Once treatment is completed and the dog tests negative for microfilaria, the dog will be cleared to resume normal activity and able to be adopted. Untreated heartworm disease can cause lasting damage to the heart, lungs and arteries, and can affect the dog's health and quality of life even after the parasites are gone, possibly presenting as medical complications and/or new conditions in the future. This dog showed no symptoms of heartworm disease before or during treatment. A good resource for more information on heartworm disease is: https://www.heartwormsociety.org/pet-owner-resources/ heartworm-basics. Please check with your vet if you should have any questions or concerns about this condition, and discuss any concerns you may have with your SOS Adoption Counselor.

name: Onyx
description:
Onyx is a shy little black terrier mix who came from rural Kansas loving home. She and her sister Pearl were 2 year old left-overs to a backyard breeder, but to us they are sweet little girls learning to be house dogs and developing their self confidence. They are learning that people can be nice and bring treats and toys and give belly rubs. name: Hank
description:
WE ARE NOT A SHELTER. WE ARE A NO-KILL 501-C-3 NON-PROFIT RESCUE: To see an animal, you must fill out an application first and then once approved, we can set up for you to meet the animal you are interested in.

Here is the Dog Application that you can copy and paste into a browser: https://fs17.formsite.com/waverlypetrescue/form028182466/index.html

Hank was a stray and his time was up in a kill shelter in Kansas. A WPR volunteer was adopting a dog from this shelter in Kansas, and decided to take Hank too so that he would not be put down the next day. They knew Hank could be a WPR dog. They just couldn't leave him knowing he would be put down. So Hank is now a Waverly Pet Rescue dog. He is living in a foster home. He is up to date on shots, tested heartworm negative, and neutered.

Hank is about 3 years old as of May 2019. We have had him for a couple of weeks now and he is doing well! He has not been around cats or children yet.

5/17/19: So we picked up Hank last night.  He is such a sweet boy, but very timid.  Unsure of everything.  But, he has already made great improvements in the 24 hours we have had him.  It will just take some time to make him understand that he is in a safe place and everything is okay.  I think he will be a great dog.  He is very loving.  No aggression at all.  He is eating good too.  And getting along great with our dog.  In fact, I think it helped having our dog.  She kind of shows him the ropes sometimes.  He has done great with the kennel as well, and so far seems as though he is housebroke.

5/26/19: My daughter is interning at a vet clinic this summer so she showed some pictures of Hank to another employee and they think that he is a boxer/pit bull mix.  When I googled brindle boxer pit mix I got some pictures that do look a lot like Hank.  He unofficially weighs 52 lbs.  We weighed him here at home.  Here are a few words of how I would describe Hank.  Hank is a sweet boy and loves everyone.  He's shy with new experiences but with patience he comes around.  Gets along great with other dogs.  Likes to go for walks.  Housebroke.  He goes in his kennel great at night, but not so much in the morning for the day.  He has been destructive with cushions and blankets in his kennel during the day, but outside of his kennel he's pretty good.  He really likes being around people and seems to be so happy.  He's a pretty cool dog overall.  

6/18/19 UPDATE: I had him briefly around a 3 yr old child and he did fine. Was a little startled by the childâs quick movements but I think children a little older would understand better. I can play with his feet and tail and he doesnât care. I lay on him when we snuggle and play and he loves it.  He has never shown any aggression at all. I think he would probably do just fine with the kids.  He loves attention. 

8/2/19 UPDATE: Hank is doing great!  He just recently learned how to shake.  He is so eager to please.  I no longer have any problems getting him to go into his kennel in the morning.  I get a small treat out and most of the time he heads to his kennel without me even telling him to.  Otherwise, I just tell him to go \"kennel up\" and away he goes.  He then sits in his kennel waiting while I gather toys and bones to put in his kennel with him.  He loves going on walks on a leash, and enjoys playing in our little dog baby pool.  He is not a barker.  About the only time he barks is sometimes when he is playing with our dog.  He prefers back scratches over belly rubs.  Hank is a happy sweet fun dog who just wants to be loved. Hank weighs about 54 pounds now!

Will someone please adopt Hank and give him a forever home? $175.00 adoption fee.
