name: Jaco
description:
Meet Jaco!  He's a 10 month old purebred German Shorthaired Pointer puppy.  He's a lovely all liver male with a docked tail.  This boy joined our rescue from an overflowing shelter in Kansas.  He is bouncy, full of energy, and will do well with breed experienced owners ready for a high energy GSP.  

From his foster:  \"He is doing awesome so far.  He is SUPER sweet with us, and is even more velcro'd to me than Huck (figure that might lessen as he gets more settled in?) He shows absolutely NO sign of food or toy aggression. He has \"Sit\" for treats down about 80% already, has had zero bathroom accidents.  Being outside during the fireworks caused him no more that a turned head and perked ears too!  \"Down\" is a big struggle though - he's very gentle when he rears up and falls into you so that's not a big deal, but refraining from checking out cabinets may take some dog whisperer type training... haha  He's a super sweet dog, and while at almost a year old he's definitely still a puppy, he heeds verbal correction quickly. He shows a lot of intelligence and is learning commands really well. Plus, when he is carrying on with our other dogs and starts 'getting mouthy', he sounds like Chewbacca.
We are trying to get good video of the Chewbacca thing - it's really funny to hear him doing it.  His coat is super silky and he has a very expressive face - there's no doubt when he's happy, unhappy, tired, inquisitive, excited, or just generally in a goofy-guy mood.  There's more I forgot... He sits and will also shake for treats.  At feeding time when we put his bowl on the counter to fill it he automatically goes to the other end of the room and sits and waits for us to tell him to come eat.  We about have him good to go on fetch with a tennis ball too, meaning sitting and waiting for you to throw it and then dropping the ball right to you when he brings it back.\

description: Foster update: Bull is a total sweetheart. He is calm, gentle and affectionate. He doesn't have an angry bone in his body. He is low maintenance and is happiest resting at home and getting cuddles. He loves to pick a comfy spot and fall asleep. Every so often, he wakes up, chews on his toys, then goes back to his spot with the toy still in his mouth. He loves belly rubs and asks for them as much as he can. Often by flopping his body onto yours. Bull is fully house-trained and hasn't had any accidents. Bull is a goofball. In addition to his goofy expressions, he also has some very special moves. Amongst his favorites, he loves to lay on the sofa with his head hanging off the side, so much so that he ends up sliding onto the floor, with his hind legs still stretched out on the edge of the sofa. Another signature move is what we call the Bull-dozer. Bull nuzzles his smushy head into your lap, succumbing to the heavenly pets, his butt still high up in the air, until he can no longer keep himself up and flops his 55-pound body onto you, dozing off into doggy dreamland. At home, Bull is the perfect chilled out pup. Outdoors, he is still getting used to the scary NYC noises. He gets frightened by the loud sounds and by all of the commotion, but to be fair, so do I! He doesn't pull on the leash but we are still working on walking straight - he likes to run into you from time to time, mostly because he's busy observing his surroundings. He is great with other dogs and other people, and is friendly to everyone he meets. Bull is so gentle, he needs a bit of love and encouragement to have his doggy side come out more. He's slowly learning how to play fetch and tug of war, and play with other dogs. I'm sure he'll be a pro in no time. Bull is a total smush and would do well in a calm and loving household, where he can relax and get lots of cuddles. He is such a gentleman and can't wait to make his forever family very happy! description:
This is Pike from the \"mountain\" litter.  He was born on May 11, 2019 at his foster's home.  His mother Shasta was saved from a high-kill Kentucky shelter so Pike and his siblings would have had an uncertain fate had we not gotten her out in the nick of time!  

Pike is a mixed breed and and is the \"big\" brother of the litter he currently weighs around 25# and will likely be 50-65# when he grows up.  He is a typical puppy full of energy and liveliness.  He enjoys playing with other dogs as well as cats and kittens.  He recalls to his name and he likes to play with toys.  He enjoys playing in water and chasing frogs.  

Pike's  is a busy boy and will need a family that can keep up with him!

When thinking about adopting a puppy please consider how it will change your life. You must have a home environment in which the puppy will not be home alone more than 4 hours a day total. You must be committed to learning how to and training your puppy. Puppies need to be socialized with other dogs so that they know how to behave when they encounter other dogs.  

Puppies need a lot of love and attention and cannot be crated as a convenience for you. Puppies should never be crated more than a total of 7 hours within a 24 hour period. You may have to take them out in the middle of the night. Puppies must be taken out on a regular schedule..sun, rain, Sleet or snow.  They require lots of play time and exercise.  

You may have to clean up messes. Puppies like to chew..it is how they explore their world so your family will need to be diligent about keeping things that you don't want chewed up put away. Having a puppy is a wonderful experience if you are prepared. If you are ready to experience the joys of adding a puppy to your family visit our website goldenhuggs.org for more information about adoption.

GHR ONLY ADOPTS TO ADULTS OVER THE AGE OF 25 AND PUPPIES TO  PEOPLE WHO HAVE TIME FOR THEM. WE DO NOT ADOPT TO FAMILIES WITH CHILDREN UNDER THE AGE OF 5.

It doesn't matter where the pups are from; it only matters where they live the rest of their lives. If you are interested in adopting, please complete an application at www.goldenhuggs.org, this is the first step in the process. The adoption fee  includes spay or neuter, shots  age appropriate and transportation to the New England drop off points. For more information, please contact  info@goldenhuggs.org.

Hi my name is Duke.  I'm about 2 years old and under 15 pounds.  I'm originally from Kentucky where I lived with two other dogs until our owner couldn't afford to care for us any more.  I've been in my foster home since Jan. 2019.   As you can see from my pictures, I love to be on a lap, it  doesn't matter whose, as long as I can be close to someone.  I am really a people dog.   I have quite the personality.  I'm a lover, a snuggler, a kisser, a hoarder of toys/bones, a thief of toys/bones from the other dogs and a bit of a napoleon.  I'm not a fan of big dogs....there's that napoleon complex, or submissive dogs because I like to be the big cheese.  If another dog puts me in my place when I try to be bossy, I will typically be their friend unless toys are involved and then I'm going to steal them.  My foster mom noticed my back legs would sometimes kick out, like they slipped out of the socket.  The doctor examined me and noticed I didn't have knee sockets in my back legs. name: Dexter
description:
DEXTER:

Hello all, my nameâs DEXTER. I am a mid-size ~45 lbs Hound mixed with lots and lots of love!  I came to LaMancha from Kentucky after living outside all my life (9 whole years!) on a chain tied to box! Just remember, nowadays, just like humans, we can take a decade off our age . . . and I feel great! I have the perfect energy, and Iâm not ready to settle down, unless of course, you are! It has been an easy transition for me from living outside tied up all my life to having freedom. Love is like the wind; you canât see it but you can feel it, and the LaMancha volunteers have done wonders for my soul.

name: Farro
description:
Hi, my name is Farro! I'm originally from Lexington Ky, my two sisters, brother and I were born the weekend of the Kentucky derby. Everyone just thinks I'm super cute because of my unique coat...AND they're right! Momma is a Rat or Fox Terrier and I never met my daddy but I think I take after momma's side of the family because everything about me from my gorgeous fur and my long supermodel legs to my \"working dog\" personality just screams terrier. (Wirehair Fox Terrier I think if I could trace my ancestry) I am a calm personality most of the time but I can hold my own with my bossy sisters. I'm bigger than my sisters at 10 pounds, but I have an athlete's build. I love, treats and laying in your lap to get petted but I love the outdoors too. I have so much to do and see every day that I don't have much time for lying around napping! I love to explore! I love TOYS, other dogs, kids and getting attention from EVERYONE! My diva sisters are usually hogging all the attention but I shoulder them out of the way when I've had enough of waiting for my turn. I live with a Mastiff, Boxer/Pit, Shih-Poo and my two sisters and I can take them all on! I am only 17 weeks old but I'm mature for my age. I'm good in my crate and keep it pretty clean. Since I'm not a baby anymore I'm in school learning some basic obedience (sit, down and here) and walking on a harness and leash. Cheese is my favorite food mostly because I only get it when I'm in school. I am looking for a place of my own where I can explore with friends, get a job and see some of the worlds. I'm all recovered from my surgery and ready to move out to my own place. Do you think a fun-loving, hard-working, studious and an adventurous roommate is your pace? If so apply to meet me!

name: Aretha
description:
Beautiful Aretha has the stunning markings of a Catahoula Leopard Dog, gorgeous amber eyes, and undeniable charisma. Sheâs just 2 years old (est. birthdate 4/17) and weighs a healthy 60 pounds. 

Aretha has travelled a long, rough road. She came to STAF from an overcrowded, high-kill county shelter in Kentucky. Upon arrival, we discovered that she had a microchip registered in Tennessee. We reached out to her family of record, who told us that theyâd given her away and did not want her back. To add insult to injury (literally!) a paw injury required Aretha to spend five weeks on restricted exercise and in an e-collar. 

Aretha likes rubs and pets as much as the next dog, but she is happiest with vigorous exercise and hard workouts. The Catahoula in her needs a purpose in life â¦ retrieving tennis balls, brisk walks and running are her favorites.  She also shows great potential on agility courses. If there is a doggy-version of a triathlon, weâve no doubt Aretha would rock that, too. Sufficiently exercised, she is a undemanding, affectionate girl. 

Thanks to a weekly training class and special attention from The Pet Spot trainers (thank you, Eric & Lee!), Aretha has a great obedience-foundation and is happy to work for treats and praise. And speaking of praise, hereâs some from Arethaâs favorite volunteer and standing Thursday-night training date: âAretha is one of the smartest dogs I have been around. She is very trainable, and would be a great Frisbee dog. Properly presented, Aretha will accept new tasks and training very well. I keep treats in my pocket, and Aretha will paw at my pocket asking for a treat. Her vision is incredible, and she can spot people, dogs, birds at amazing distances. Aretha will bond quickly with her new family. I think in a day or two, with some play and treats and pets, she will be a great dog for an active lifestyle family.â

name: Rebecca
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.
SBF (single brindle female) seeking long term commitment. No fakers. I like long walks or snuggling by the

TV

. I'm very laid back. I have 4 grown offspring that are all out of the house. I came here from Kentucky in April 2019. I have had some obstacles to overcome and conquered every one like a true Southern belle.

If you'd like to be interviewed for possible acceptance, please fill out an application.

Note from foster family;

This girl has been a dream foster. Rebekah ( we call her Lexi, short for Lexington, Kentucky) is potty trained, she is an amazing walker, she's a talker. I mean like a 16 year old girl who's really going to try to get her way. She's not much of a player. Meaning that playing fetch or toys with people just not her thing. But, if you say \"walk\" or even make her think there's going to be a walk in her near feature she loses it. Never seen a dog so excited to go on walks. Walks are very important for Lexi. Please consider if you already have a life style that includes or the ability to walk at least 2 times a day. We do about .5 -2 miles each walk 2-3 times a day. She has become accustomed to hanging out at our cabin. Lexi is my only foster I have EVER let off leash. I know I might get in trouble with NDLB because I'm sure this is not allowed but we did this with extreme caution and only after we had her for about 3 months. She pretty much just lays in the sun, eats grass and moves to a shady spot when she gets warm. She loves chasing bugs and the occasional critter so we still keep a close eye on her. Someone really loved this dog once; I sure wish I had her whole story.

Her only behavior that concerns me is I'm pretty sure she's an escape artist. Might be how she ended up in this situation. I think she would do best in a laid back household as she take time to warm up to new people.

Lexi kennels without a problem, even when we first got her. She has been with us for a long time now, we don't kennel her anymore.

She does really well with other dogs but too much peopleing can be stressful for her. She lets you know when she needs a break from a crowd of people.

description:

DOB: 6/17/17
Weight: 43.8 Pounds
Adoption Fee: $350

Hi there my name is Mousey but my foster family calls me Libby! My foster parents say I'm the sweetest but they really hope I will learn to trust others too so others can see just how sweet I am. They say if you take one look at my piercing eyes you can see into my soul. I came to Minnesota from Kentucky and was in a shelter for some time and I was so scared I would spend my days hiding under a pile of blankets. I didn't find comfort in any humans until my foster parents, I have learned to trust them but I am still working on my trust in strangers. My foster parents say that a dog savvy owner will be very beneficial to help instill confidence in me and continue to work on my training. When I see new people I bark and growl and I can look really mean but I'm doing it because I'm scared. It would be best for me to be in a home that doesn't have a lot of visitors and to have a bit of space outside because I have a hard time having fun outside when I'm making sure the neighbors are staying put. I stay in the crate during the day and I keep my crate clean and I'm going potty on a schedule!

I love going on walks and my interaction with all dogs has been great. I really look to other dogs to know that everything is okay. My new home should have confident dog already in the home so I can continue my socialization training through them. Once we get over our initial meeting, I will love you more than you can imagine. I am a great cuddle buddy; I do great in car rides and just really can't get enough love! Please fill out an application if you would like to meet me or learn more about me!

name: Annie
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.
Adopt me!

*Annie needs a foster home, would love another dog that is her size or medium sized to play with!*

Annie is a 3-5year old (1 vet said 5, another vet said 3-5 and the most recent vet guessed her to be 3), 50-55 lb Walker Coonhound. She was rescued from a Kentucky pound, where it looked like she had been neglected by a previous owner as she was very underweight. Annie is now in great health and waiting for her forever home in Minnesota. She is a very sweet affectionate dog, good with other dogs (loves to play) and people. Annie would love an adoptive home with a fenced in yard so she can move and explore and sniff to her heart's content. Hounds are fun dogs to take to fenced in dog parks, their love of discovery and activity is a great way to help you get out there and have some fun in nature too! Annie is house trained (although the first week in a new place may have a few accidents) and crate trained, is very treat motivated which makes training fun and is very loving to her people.

Annie has some anxiety, and she is comforted in her crate. In her foster home, the crate is available to her with the door open when people are home, and closed when they leave.

She'd make a nice family dog, or a companion for a single person or couple who would be able to take her out for walks, and wants a buddy to cuddle with at home. Annie is a little bit skittish, she's jumpy when she hears loud sudden noises.

She would love to join an active family who can take her out on walks a lot, dog parks, obedience training, things to keep her stimulated. If she gets bored, she will pace throughout the house looking for something to do.

She seems to be especially nervous around large bald men (maybe her previous owner was a large bald man and didn't treat her so nice). Sometimes when a new person comes in the door she'll get nervous and howl and pace, but she calms down after you let her know the person is ok or take her to another room where she feels safe.

We haven't tested Annie with cats yet.

She loves to give hugs :) Tiny kids may be too much for her (because she gets startled easily), but she's been good with the older kids (6, 7 and 12) in her foster home.

name: Riley
description:
Howdy! My name is Riley. I'm originally from Kentucky where my life was not-so-good. I was homeless, emaciated, covered in ticks and could barely stand with all four on the ground. Lucky for me a local rescue took me in, gave me a place to rest my weary bones and now I am healthy and ready for my furever home.

I arrived in New Jersey, seeking a new and better life. Despite my ruff life, I am a happy-go-lucky pooch and love everyone I meet, kids and adults. I also love other dogs and would enjoy a home with a fur brother or sister. I weigh a solid 65 pounds, love to swim and enjoy toys, too. I'm not a high energy dog and don't require much, other than a lot of hugs and kisses. Won't you give me a home?

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wxyE1bpQLgs

name: Eddie
description:
Eddie came to us from a hoarding situation in Kentucky at approximately one year of age.  He is a dear little creature, approx. 9 lbs, who has been in a most wonderful foster home since his arrival where he thrives on the companionship of the other little dogs in the home and special humans whom he has come to trust.  Lack of socialization while in his first home has taken its toll and Eddie is timid when he meets new people or is put into a new situation, but once he knows his human, he will respond to kindness and loves treats!!!
Eddie's new home should have a fenced in area so he can relieve himself, a quiet environment (adult only home), and frequent human contact.  Another small dog who would become his best friend would be great.  
Eddie is crate trained and very clean in the home if kept on a good schedule. At present, he uses a dog door to enter his fenced in yard.
For an online application, please email the Pet the Pet Program at reverence@ottcmail.com.  Our process requires an approved application which is followed by a telephone interview, a home visit (applicants should reside within a 50 mile radius of Corning, New York or in the Rochester area, and a veterinarian reference.
Eddie's adoption fee is $250;.  He is healthy, neutered, current on vaccines, and is on a monthly heartworm, flea and tick preventative.

name: Vector
description: Vector came to us from a shelter in Kentucky. He spent some time in a foster home and is now available for adoption. Vector will do best with a patient family who understands he is nervous and is still learning how to be a confident boy. He is shy and unsure when meeting people. He does warm up and will snuggle with his people. He does well with other dogs both high and low energy and comes out of his shell when he is with them. He also had a cat in his foster home that he did well with. He's a smart loving boy who is learning sit and learned how to go outside to potty in his foster home with the help of his foster parents and doggy foster siblings. He will need to learn to walk on a leash, as his low confidence has prevented him from mastering it just yet.

name: Peachy
description: Peachy came to us very pregnant from a high kill facility in southern Kentucky. She has since weaned her puppies and is looking for a home of her own. Peachy is the sweetest girl, loves car rides, cuddles, and being with her person. For more information on this girl please contact us.

name: Cordelia
description: This lovely lady is Cordelia! She came all the way from a shelter in Kentucky to find her forever home. She is a super sweet and loving girl. She loves cuddling up to you for snuggles and will give you kisses in return. She would make a loyal friend because she just wants to be close to you. We don't know much about her past so would need to meet any potential \"dog siblings\" before going home with them. She may also need some basic training skills once in a new home. She is such a sweet and gentle girl that she would make a great addition to almost any home! If you think Cordelia would be the perfect fit for you, come on in, fill out an application, and spend some time with her!

name: Tria
description:
Meet Tria ??
She is a 1 year old Pug/ Beagle Mix. Tria came to us from a shelter in Kentucky. She is such a sweet heart! She is a little shy, but she is slowly coming out of her shell. She gets along with other dogs. Tria is scheduled to be spayed and she is up to date on her vaccinations. Her adoption fee is $150.

name: Betty
description: This beautiful lady is Betty! She came all the way from a shelter in Kentucky to find her forever home! She is a sweet, energetic, playful girl that really loves people! She loves going out on walks or runs in the dog park and playing with toys! We don't know much about her past, so she would need to meet any potential \"dog siblings\" before going home with them and may end up needing to be the only dog in the home. She is a sweet girl and loves to get snuggled and give kisses and has a great personality. She may need some basic training skills once in a new home but should pick up on that very quickly. If you think Betty would be the perfect dog for you, come on in, fill out an application, and spend some time with her!

name: Molly
description: This adorable girl is Molly. She came all the way from a shelter in Kentucky to find her forever home. When she first got here she was nervous and timid but after some time spent with her she has come out of her shell! She is a very gentle and sweet dog with a playful side too! She will zoom around being silly, but also likes to snuggle up close to you. We don't know much about her past so we do recommend she meet any potential \"dog siblings\" before going home with them and she may need some basic training skills once in a new home. She is a very sweet dog that would do well with just about anyone. If you think Molly would be a great addition to your home, come on in, fill out an application, and spend some time with her!

name: Oli
description: This little cutie is Oli. He came all the way from a shelter in Kentucky to find his forever home. Oli came to us very frightened and unsure. When he first meets people he can be a little timid but once he is comfortable and feels safe, he really comes out of his shell. He will crawl all over you, giving kisses, and enjoying snuggles. He will need a person/family willing to give him the patience he needs and the love he deserves to help him gain some confidence and trust. Then, he will be an amazing lap dog, snuggle buddy, and companion. If you think you would be the perfect match for Oli, come on in, fill out an application, and spend some time with this little guy!

name: Andes - video!
description:
This is Andes from the \"mountain\" litter.  He was born on May 11, 2019 at his foster's home.  His mother Shasta was saved from a high-kill Kentucky shelter so Andes and his siblings would have had an uncertain fate had we not gotten her out in the nick of time!  

Andes is a mixed breed and currently weighs around 18# and will likely be 45-55# when he grows up.  He is a typical puppy full of energy and liveliness.  He enjoys playing with other dogs as well as cats and kittens.  He recalls to his name and he likes to play with toys.  He is a busy boy and will need a family that can keep up with him.

When thinking about adopting a puppy please consider how it will change your life. You must have a home environment in which the puppy will not be home alone more than 4 hours a day total. You must be committed to learning how to and training your puppy. Puppies need to be socialized with other dogs so that they know how to behave when they encounter other dogs.  

Puppies need a lot of love and attention and cannot be crated as a convenience for you. Puppies should never be crated more than a total of 7 hours within a 24 hour period. You may have to take them out in the middle of the night. Puppies must be taken out on a regular schedule..sun, rain, Sleet or snow.  They require lots of play time and exercise.  

You may have to clean up messes. Puppies like to chew..it is how they explore their world so your family will need to be diligent about keeping things that you don't want chewed up put away. Having a puppy is a wonderful experience if you are prepared. If you are ready to experience the joys of adding a puppy to your family visit our website goldenhuggs.org for more information about adoption.

name: Neevah
description:
Hi! My name is Neevah. Bet you didnât know that MVPC specializes in seniors? I was âDivaâ in a different life, and at roughly 14 years old, I was unceremoniously dumped at a highly overpopulated shelter in Atlanta, GA. MVPC has special fosters specifically for small dogs, so I got to make my way to Ohio. From there, I was named âNeevah,â because change is good since the âDivaâ people abandoned me, but since I am blind, they wanted me to hear my similar name to acclimate! After a lengthy vet visit, it was determined I have awful teeth, am almost completely blind from cataracts and have a grade 5/6 heart murmur. My foster mom started me on medicine and though she thought I would be a hospice foster, it is obvious I have time left. Having time left means there very well may be a special family (other than my foster family) out there who will dote on me and spoil me rotten.  I am also SUCH a good girl.

I require soft food, since my teeth cannot be cleaned/pulled. My heart murmur is severe, so anesthesia is a huge risk. I am on two medicines daily. 

Furosemide 12.5mg every 12 hours
Enalapril 2.5mg once a day

You will need to contact your vet to check the costs, but I will need these for life! 

I do VERY well getting around. Blindness doesnât slow me down and I figure things out VERY quickly. I am gentle with everyone, am still housebroken and sleep in my bed soundly at night. I love to be held and snuggled.

I am a doll (so says my foster mom) and she knows there could be a family out there who is willing to make me a member of their family. No worries, even if I stay here for the rest of my life, I am very loved and spoiled. But I know my foster mom can save the next senior if an awesome family finds me. So I am puttimg myself out there just in case.

I am a sweet girl who loves everyone, dogs, cats and people alike.  I am smart, stubborn and squishy, a great combination! Oh, and I love kids. name: Snape
description:
Baby Snape was dumped in the woods with her litter mates at 6 weeks old. Who does this stuff??? Terrible! These are very lucky puppies. The woods is a very dangerous place for babies without their mother.  So, the first example of their luck started with two EMTs who discovered him and his siblings, have been loving them and will take care of him and all eight of them until they are 12 weeks old. These EMTs truly knew how to care for them!  At 12 weeks they will have had their second vet visit including age appropriate shots/treatment which means they will be safe to travel from KY to NJ arriving September 15.  He will not be housebroken at that time. He and his siblings are sweet, curious, playful and very ready to attach to a loving person or family.  Some specs on their current weight will help determine adult weight, as for now they are small. The weight range for a medium sized adult dog is 26 to 60 pounds.  On 8/22 at 9 weeks old Jeanie was 11 pounds, Snape (male) 15.6 pounds, and Hermione 12.8 pounds.  It will be hard to predict their exact weights when full grown since we do not know either of the parents personally.  But their vet made some breed predictions. The rule for estimating weight is when it comes to medium and larger breeds, take their weight at 14 weeks and double it. Then add half of the original weight. (For instance, if your puppy weighs 25 pounds at 14 weeks, double this to 50 and then add 12.5 for an estimated adult weight of 62.5 pounds).  So, they wonât be small dogs.  Some may be medium, or some large dog. When they arrive at 12 weeks old they will of course be a little bigger than they are now but still little babies in need of love.  If you are looking for an elegant, fun, super good luck beagle/treeing walker coonhound please apply to adopt Snape by visiting our website www.peace4paws.org

Once she's comfortable with the other dogs - she's fine. She has had basic training, has perfect manners & walks very well on a leash. name: Zoe
description:
AARF only adopts in Richmond, Virginia and the surrounding area. 

My name is Zoe and here is my Curriculum Vitae for consideration by my foster family.

Age: 1 1/2

Background: I was a scrawny newborn puppy and brought to the pound with my mother and left there. I was kind of sickly with mange. The day AARF came to pick me up, my former owners said they wanted me back. At 5 weeks, AARF won and my foster family took me in. With careful monitoring by AARF and the vet, I am in excellent health.

Education: I taught my foster family many things. I loved everyone and everything to the point I became an obnoxious brat. I passed puppy socialization at 2 Speak Dog. My fosters didn't understand what play was-l am spirited and fast and boxy but it's different from fighting. I need to be monitored around other dogs but I am much calmer as Iâve grown older. My best friend is a Great Dane named Stella. Some timid dogs may call me a pest but they don't understand. Cats may not understand me either.

Passions: I love, love, love toys and peanut butter. I can only handle indestructible Kong type toys. I also love my crate. lt is my safe haven and when l get too rambunctious. My foster tells me to go to the crate. lt is a special place for me to deep breathe and relax. I am content there.

Outdoors: I love walks, runs, the car, and fresh air but l am not an outdoor dog. I only want to be outside when you are with me. I am completely housebroken and love to travel. ln fact, l just came back from a driving trip to KY. lt was fun and I had no problems. I am not allowed to go off leash. When I am on a leash, it is with a gentle leader. I have been conditioned to not object to wearing it but it itches my muzzle and I slither like a snake. Without it, I pull like a workhorse. I think I am helping like pulling a wagon for the grandchildren.
References: Furnished upon request.


For more information, contact  aarfva@hotmail.com .

He would make an awesome therapy dog or Emotional Support Animal.  He can be an only dog or be matched with a mild mannered female.

name: PADDYWAK in Southern CA
description:
Paddywak came to us from a high kill shelter in L.A.  He seemed so very small and compliant, not especially reactive for an 11 year old boy.  He had never been nuetered and his breath could knock you over from bad teeth long uncared for.  My thought was perhaps he couldn't see well and was deaf because of lack of response.  He sat without complaint in my lap for the 45 minute trip home.  When he was placed in the home among the greeting family of yorkies he seemed ready to do his job which seemed to be mounting any willing volunteers.  There were none and he was quickly rebuffed and soon avoided.  Paddywak had to learn a new way of life.  From his reaction to things this little boy had never been talked, loved or played with by a human and apparently was only bred to reproduce.  Housetraining was a puzzle to him and affection quite foreign.
Today this little boy is a new \"person\".  He has had all his shots, neutered and fresh breath.  His teeth cleaning really meant removing rotted teeth that didn't even bleed.....there was only infection left in the gums.  He is healing, happy and attached at the lap.  Sit down and he becomes part of you, move to the next room and he is by your feet.  Bedtime is the best time because then he is snuggled up next to you in bed.  Life has never been so good !  He is cautious with strangers but always gentle.  When the others bark at imagined bad mailmen and other dangers Paddywak joins in but nothing comes out.  Wherever he lived before they made sure he didn't complain so they had him debarked. Little guy, big love now.  He is ready for his best home ever ! Adoption donation $250 includes microchip. Adoption applications can be submitted at www.ytnr.com  You must be willing to go to Paddywak's foster home in California to adopt him.

** Coming to Rhode Island and will be at the PetSmart- Warwick adoption event on  Saturday September 28th!! 
1276 Bald Hill Rd  (RTE 2)  Warwick RI ** 11 am to 3 pm  In order to be pre-approved, please send in an application. 
http://littlerhodyrescue.com/adoption-application/

We process applications as they arrive. The first approved applicant will be called and the pup taken off of Petfinder. We do not have the man/ woman power to all all other applicants to advise them. 
IF there s another dog that you are interested in as well, please list at the top of the application and we will enter your application for that pup if the first choice has been adopted. 

THANK YOU !!! You are giving a first rate dog a second chance....By adopting! 
 

~~~~~
Casper is a 6mo old Great Pyr and possibly Border Collie mix.  Casper and his siblings were dumped 2months ago in a rural area.  They wandered up to a family's mobile home.  The family begged for help as they were full of ticks and underweight.  Come to find out Casper was in the final process of fighting parvo but sweet Wendy was just getting sick.   

Both puppies are fighters and battled it out like champs and are healthy as horses now!!!!!
  Shame on the humans that dumped these sweet souls!  Now they are Fat and Sassy (thanks to their wonderful foster mommy) and ready for forever homes !~~~~~
****

In addition to the above, all dogs must have a Certificate of Veterinary Inspection and be deemed healthy per USDA law in order to travel. Once they have been certified they are then transported via USDA transport services only, which is required by law. 

Keep in mind that we also offer a two week return policy for the return of a healthy dog that includes a full refund. We want to make sure that the adoption is a perfect fit for both you and the dog.

If you would like more information about adopting please select \"More About Little Rhody Rescue\" where you will also find our online application if you'd like to proceed with the adoption process. Thank you!

name: Mozart
description:
Meet Mozart. This handsome senior Poodle mix was just saved from an LA animal shelter and is looking for a loving family to live out his golden years. He is incredibly sweet, loves to nap, and cuddle on your lap. We named him Mozart because we believe he lost his hearing, and his previous owner didn't take very good care of his teeth, so he will enjoy a soft foods diet from here on out! While he's slowed down a bit, other than the hearing loss and removal of his teeth, he is in great shape and has a lot of living to do! We are happy to report that he doesn't have any heart issues that are common in seniors. We think he would make an amazing companion to any family! He adores other dogs but is also very comfortable being the only dog in the home. 


Mutt Scouts is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit dog rescue dedicated to helping homeless, abused, and abandoned dogs. We are committed to providing proper socialization, training, and medical care for each animal we save, no matter the cost. 

Please visit our website for more information about our organization:
https://www.muttscouts.org/

All of our dogs are housed in private foster homes. An application is the first step and is required to schedule a meeting. Please complete application below, and include any questions in the final section. Inquiries without applications submitted will be answered as we can. Please note that we do not do out of state adoptions, and a home check and adoption fee are required.

name: Snazzy
description:
Snazzy is a 2 year old spayed female JRT mix.  She was transferred to us from an overcrowded shelter in LA after being mistreated by her owner.  Snazzy's owners were physically abusive to Snazzy and even ended up breaking her leg by throwing her.  She has healed physically and is working on healing emotionally.  Snazzy is timid with humans, and can be snappy when feeling scared, but warms up with treats and love.  She can get used to anyone but is especially nervous with men initially.  Snazzy LOVES kids and is very playful and fun with them.  She is a toy maniac and loves to play.  Snazzy is crate trained, seems to be house trained and is working on her manners.  She would benefit from a positive reinforcement training class to work on her manners and to help boost her confidence.  Snazzy is so incredibly sweet and motivated that she is eager to learn the positives of humans.  Let's help show her!

name: Hank - Available for Adoption!
description:
Hello!  I am a very handsome, red, medium size (48 lbs.), Pit Bull Mix and I am about 1 year 10 months of age.  I have a sleek long body and neck, short stature but I am healthy and strong.  My name is Hank and I am very smart, learn easily, and I am energetic and athletic. 

Iâve been neutered and received all my vaccinations in April, May and June of 2019.  I was transported and adopted to a new home in Burien on June 30, 2019 from Carson Shelter near LA where I entered as a stray on April 16, 2019.  I am now seeking a caring and forever home.  My current mom sadly needs to find me a home because she saved me sight unseen and although I am relatively small, I am too strong for her and she is small with some hand issues that make handling an exuberant dog strong boy like me challenging.  I do like to play hard and a lot!

I know my basic commands and have learned to leash walk without pulling most of the time â unless I see a rabbit!  I need a new owner who can play and walk with me a few times a day.  I love to catch frisbees, play in the water spray from the hose, fetch balls, and my stuffed toys.  I only chew my toys and Kongâs.  I get excited to meet and socialize with other dogs, but I still need training in this area.  I like to meet people and I am friendly towards most but need to continue with my socialization skills.

but acts like he is 8.

He was owner by the same family all of his life but was made to live outdoors until they moved and then he journeyed his way from Texas to Las Vegas. name: Skyy
description:
Name: Skyy

Approximate Age: Approx. 2yrs old

Breed: Pit mix

Sex: Female

Special Needs: Allergies

Adoption fee: $300.00

Up to date on vaccinations/preventatives, spayed, house/crate trained, microchipped

I came to the rescue back in 2016 from a high kill shelter in Texas. The conditions werent the best to say the least and oh yeah, I was SUPER pregnant. Not a good place for a expecting mom. Thankfully, I was taken from there just in time and was able to have my puppies in a foster home. I was even thrown a huge baby shower by a ton of people who follow SNARR! I was so happy to finally have had my babies and be out of the shelter but my excitement quickly became tragedy. Not long after giving birth, almost half of my babies passed away- only 4 survived. 
Now that my remaining pups have gone to live their own liveshere I sit and wait. While I adore my foster mom, I want a home to call my own. 
Im confused on why I dont have my own home yet Im incredibly adorable and Im hands down the most wiggly tushed pocket pittie youll ever meet! I have never met a person I didnt like, however dogs.not too fond of dogs or any other furry little creatures. I blame that on my high prey drive and Im very smart when it comes down to it- I can be a pro stalker and Im lightning fast so its best that the temptation isnt there in forever home. Give me any kind of human though and its nothing but hugs (literally, I give hugs) and kisses! 
Due to having allergies, I take Benedryl and cannot eat chicken.

Transport to any approved home within the US can be provided at no additional fee
Currently Skyy is located in Lawrenceville, Georgia.


Please visit SNARRANIMALRESCUE.org to fill out an adoption application and our adoption requirements/process can also be found there!

name: Rose Talbot-Bassador
description:
09/10/19

I have had the pleasure of Rose Talbot being a houseguest in our home for the past 3 months; I guess I should say she is like one of my own.  She is a sweet and gentle girl who needs to trust and understand love.  She truly hangs on her bed for 95% of her day.  Her exercise consists of running from the backdoor to her bed.  She ventures out to let us know when she wants to go outside or we are late with her meal.  She loves her soft food and treats.  She still goes submissive when you reach down to pet her, but she has improved.  She provides her fur foster siblings with kisses as they come over to check on her.  I will share she would do best in a home that will give her time to adjust, earn her trust and provide a soft bed to lay in.  She really is a low maintenance dog that has captured the heart of her foster mom.  I keep telling her that the perfect family has not come yet, but one day although it will be sad they will come and finally give her her forever home, the one that will provide her with the love and attention she truly deserves.



7/1/19

So are you looking for a new best friend that is so appreciative of the little things?  Are you looking for a gentle soul that just wants a soft bed and love that she deserves?  Are you looking for a new companion that will melt your heart every time you look into her eyes?  Look no further!!!!

Meet Rose, a very gentle girl that finally is getting the love and attention that she deserves.  She has a tough life, but things are looking up for this sweet girl.  She recently made her trip north from Georgia to begin her journey to find a home she can call her own.  

Although she wears her past, she has been doing well with housetraining, gets along with her fur foster siblings, and loves belly rubs.  Unfortunately Rose needed 23 teeth removed, I believe she is feeling so much better; she loves her canned food.  She is fully recovered from all of her medical treatments and is now ready to receive applications to find her forever home.  



6/25/19
Rose has had a tough couple months.  She gave birth to her puppies but due to her poor health and theirs---all the puppies passed away.  Rose had a couple cysts/tumors removed and tested --they were benign.  Rose is now spayed and up to date on her shots.  She is feeling better and looking forward to the next chapter in her life.

3/30/19

Rose came from Long County AC in GA. She is a 6-8 yr old really cute  bassadore. She appears to be pregnant, will ask the vet to check Tuesday.  She  is heart worm positive. She looks like she has had many litters before. She is friendly and gets along good with others. 

 Rose will be Heart worm treated and spayed once  her puppies are weaned and Rose is Vet cleared

name: Mocha
description:
Sweet Mocha is a 6 year old Pit Bull who has come to our rescue all the way from Long Island in New York City!! Due to overcrowded kennels in the city poor Mocha was on the list to be euthanized. She was a favorite among the volunteers at the municipal shelter and they fought hard to find safety. After reaching out to dozens of no-kill shelters they finally found The Canine Rescue of Central PA and we were happy to make room for her! 

She is appropriately named Mocha as she has a beautiful coat that looks like a cup of Mocha with some whipped cream swirled in! And she's about as sweet as a Mocha treat as well! She walks well on a leash and has a good bit of energy! But also likes to cuddle and adores being with people. She has a small prey drive and would do best in a home without children, cats or small dogs. She could likely live with medium to large sized dogs.

Mocha is spayed, up-to-date on shots and housetrained. If you are interested in meeting Mocha or would like more information please leave a voicemail at the rescue 717-232-1644 or e-mail at adopt@crcpa.org.

name: Buddha
description: Buddha is a big, goofy boy who loves to hang out with his people. He's the perfect mix of energetic and laid back. He loves to play with stuffed toys and roll around in the grass. He's also content to lay on his bed or by your feet while you are hanging out. He's a bit of a comedian and will certainly make you laugh. He's a lot of fun to cuddle and pet. He loves to go on car rides and sits nicely watching the world go by. He's crate trained, housetrained and walks nicely on a leash. Buddha was born in 2010 and came to Best Friends from a shelter in Los Angeles. He has anxiety and cannot live with other animals as he has shown aggression toward them in the past. He can be very reactive to other dogs and will bark, whine, jump or potentially try to escape to get to them. He can also be reactive towards people through a barrier like a door or fence if he does not know them. At Dogtown, Buddha is working on a training plan to help him be less reactive towards dogs. He is also working on calm greetings when people enter his space. The training plan and ongoing support would be provided to his new home. Buddha is on some prescription medications that help him be calmer. He had orthopedic surgery in 2018 and still takes medication for that. Buddha would be the perfect companion for someone who wants a single pet and who is willing to keep working on his training.

name: Domineo
description: Domineo has a lot of personality. He is a spirited, unique and somewhat independent fellow. Born in 2011, he came to Best Friends from a shelter in Los Angeles. He can be very affectionate once you're in with him, but he has a history of handling and guarding issues in a previous home, and he has bitten in the past. He has also shown aggression toward another dog, though he has had successful play dates with other dogs since coming to Best Friends, so he may simply be picky with his doggie friends. Domineo is smart and eager to work for food. In a home, he would benefit from a fenced-in yard, as he has a lot of energy. He will be happy to entertain you with his antics with one of his favorite toys, the jolly ball. But he is considered a flight risk and must be watched carefully within a secure enclosure when he's playing outside. At Dogtown, he is working on meeting people appropriately, as he tends to jump up and nip. So far, he has met several people and has done well. He can be a handful for harnessing, but that could due to his excitement in a busy environment. Domineo is looking for a person who will be committed to setting him up for success in a home. If you'd be willing to work with this high-spirited guy, he would love to meet you.

name: Winter
description: Winter came from a shelter in Los Angeles, where she was feeling very intimidated. Luckily, she trekked out to Best Friends here in Kanab, Utah, where her real personality is peeking through. She can act shy at first, but once she gets to know you with treats and a walk, she's warm and inviting. Winter does a happy wiggle dance whenever she sees her friends. Winter loves people, and if you have other dogs, that would be wonderful. She's great with them! Winter also loves her walks and loves to play in water. All Winter wants is a forever home with someone to love. Winter has a generous sponsor who will cover her adoption fee.

name: Lolita
description:
PLEASE READ ALL OF THE INFORMATION BELOW!

Lolita (Leigh) is a young small chi estimated to be 1-2 years old and weighs 6 lbs. she is a very sweet, smart, and playful girl and enjoys interacting with the other chis in her foster home. She can be timid around new people or in new situations based on her past life.

Lolita was rescued from a kill shelter in Los Angeles by a vet who cared for her for 3 months before passing her to our organization. Upon coming into our care, we discovered that Lolita had an incontinence issue which was caused by an old injury. She had previous had a fractured vertebrae which healed incorrectly she was compressing her spine.

We have brought her to a neurologist for spinal surgery and she has improved about 80%-90%. She requires a strict diet to keep her digestive tract working consistently. 

No small children based on her recent surgery and no larger active dogs that may jump on her. 

She is a super sweet girl, very smart and a great listener, very loving and just a total love. Sheâs clearly come from a bad situation in the past. She will cower or hide around new people or in new situations and needs a loving home to teach her that she is safe. She does piddle if she gets scared.

We currently adopt in the states of NY, NJ, Eastern PA, DE, and some areas in MD. We can not accept applications from other states at this time.

If you are interested in adopting this dog, please fill out our adoption application which you can find on our website at www.dutchcountryanimalrescue.org/adopt.html 

Our adoption fees are on our application.

All of our rescues are spayed/neutered, up to date on rabies and DHPP, heartworm tested, treated for worms and fleas and most are microchipped.

We are not a shelter, we are 100% volunteer public charity. All of our dogs are in foster homes until they are adopted. Since we are not a shelter, we do not receive government funding. We are a public charity that relies solely on funds through our adoption fee, fundraisers, and private donations. name: Lena - local love bug!
description:
**Please read Lena's entire profile, which includes a link to the adoption application. Thank you!** 

Lena is a large and lazy lover who had to be surrendered by her dad after he moved here from Los Angeles and just couldn't give her enough attention due to his new job.  He was devastated to give her up, but knew it was best for Lena.  We promised him we'd find her a great home!  Lena is a sweetheart of a girl who loves to chill on the couch and get butt scratches.  She's an older girl (we are guessing about 8, but really have no idea), but she can still play hard with the best of them.   Lena is a *bit* overweight but has been working hard on that with her foster and has already lost a few pounds.   She has a few to go but the change in her is already amazing!  She rides great in the car, is totally housebroken.  While her dad said she lived with a cat, Lena is a bit too interested in her foster mom's critters so would probably do best in a cat/small critter free home.  When Lena gets excited to see you (especially first thing in the morning) Lena will do a Rooroooroo!! howl/growl that is just the cutest thing ever.  She walks on a leash, but can be a strong puller, especially if she sees a critter.  Lena has wonderful Batman ears and is currently being treated for an ear infection.  Lena knows basic commands like sit, drop, come, stay, down.  We think Lena should be in an only dog household.   She plays pretty rough which seems to be too much for many dogs to handle.   It is a combination of her size and her energy level.  She is great around men and women and her dad says even kids (though again remember her size).  Lena is overall healthy, UTD on all vaccines and spayed.  This girl has many years ahead of her to love and be loved and is hoping you have a couch in your heart to share with her!!  


To adopt or learn more about Lena you must fill out an adoption application. Please note, GDRNE does not guarantee the breed of any dog or puppy unless stated that we have run DNA. All breeds listed are educated estimates. Our dogs are rescued from various situations. name: Angelo
description:
Angelo is a cute little Golden mix who came to our rescue from St Landry's Parish Shelter in Louisiana.  As a shelter that once euthanized nearly 96% of the creatures it took in, wonderful changes have been made since 2014 and there is a new mindset at the shelter.  Now, St Landry's works with many rescue groups throughout the nation to relocate a vast majority of the pets who find their way to the shelter.  Angelo is one such dog whose life has been saved!

Angelo seems to have missed out on socialization in the early phase of his life, and when he first came to our rescue, Angelo was afraid of his own shadow.  The sound of a leaf falling would make him jump and it seemed like he slept with one eye open.  Initially, he froze when he was leashed, but with a harness on he is now able to be leashed and will mosey around at his own pace.  Gradually, he will learn that a leash is a good thing and means a fun walk.  But in the meantime, an adult-only home in a quiet area with a secure and physically fenced yard is on our wish-list for Angelo.   With time and patient, this angel will come out of his shell and gain trust. 

We estimate Angelo to be about 1-2 years old, weighing about 33 lbs.  He is good with others dogs and would do well with a confident canine sibling to mentor him.  He has no history with cats.  Because his former family did not keep him on heartworm preventative, Angelo is under treatment for heartworm and can come north in October.  Angelo is up-to-date on all  vaccinations, is neutered, and micro-chipped.

Angelo is a very sweet guy who needs to feel loved and cherished.  We know he will flourish in the care of a loving adopter.   If your specialty is TLC then Angelo is the dog you needâ¦ or more precisely, who needs YOU!  

Rescued dogs come with a range of needs - from behavioral to emotional to medical.  When approved applicants adopt such dogs, they agree to continue the rehabilitation we have begun.  

If you would like to be part of Angelo's rescue story, and you have already been approved for adoption through SGRR, please contact Donna Toncic at: SunshineGoldens@gmail.com     to be considered to adopt Angelo.           

If not yet approved, please visit our website to learn more and to submit an online application:     http://sunshinegoldenrescue.com/adoption-info1.html  

Please DO NOT use the ASK ABOUT button to contact us, about this dog, as that will delay our ability to respond to your inquiry.  Please direct any questions regarding your application status to:  ajpillinger@gmail.com   

Thank you!
 
About Our Rescue 
Before being approved to adopt, all potential adopters will be required to complete our online application and participate in our pre-adoption review process. The process includes the completion of an online application, a reference from the applicants' vet, a phone interview, and a visit to the applicants' home.  The application process helps us determine what type of Golden would be best suited for the applicants' life style.  In some cases, the specific dog you are interested in may have found a home before this process is complete or further assessment may indicate that this dog is not the right match for your family.  We are frequently getting new Goldens in need of a home, so we encourage you to apply and complete the application process so that when the right dog comes along you will be ready. 

The information provided on each dog is based on the observations of our vets, volunteers, fosters, and when available, trainers. While we do our best to report any and all issues, SGRR does not make any guarantees as to the health or temperament of any dog. Dogs evolve differently in different environments and we cannot predict with any certainty how the dog you adopt will behave and adapt in your home.

SGRR Adoption Fees (subject to change)

Puppies under 6 months   $650

A contract is signed on the day of adoption.  Under the terms of the contract, all adopters are required to bring their SGRR dog to a vet within 7 business days.  All dogs receive basic veterinary care prior to adoption.  However, if an adopter's vet identifies an illness that an adopter is not willing to treat, then the dog may be returned and a full refund would be provided. 

Most of our dogs are fostered in private homes.  We do not have a facility to visit.  We are committed to our dogs before, during, and after adoption! To this end, the rescue retains an interest in each dog and our dogs can never be surrendered, re-homed, or sold. Should an adopter no longer be able to keep their SGRR dog, SGRR must be notified so that we can take the dog back into rescue and place it into another home. We reserve the right to remove a dog at any time should we find the adopter is no longer providing proper care.  Adopters agree to follow up visits as needed.

description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.New Arrival:
- DANIEL is a great Beagle mix boy who came to us from a hoarding/abuse situation in Louisiana. He is slightly taller than a standard Beagle and weighs in at 35 lbs and is about 5 years old. When DANIEL arrived we noticed his left eye was very cloudy. Our eye vet confirmed that DANIEL had glaucoma and was blind in his left eye and, unfortunately, the pressure in that eye was 75 against a normal eye pressure of 10-20 mmHg! This would result in DANIEL being in quite a lot of pain! Since DANIEL had just been neutered and treated for heartworms it would not have been prudent to perform surgery to remove the eye. So we too the opportunity to drain the fluid from the eye and administer some eye medications hoping to lower DANIEL's eye pressure. Unfortunately, after 2 weeks his pressure was still 68. While the standard solution use to be to just remove the eye in these cases, after consultation with DR Mohoric, we decided to try \"Ciliary Boy Ablation (CBA) where they injected a medication into DANIEL's eye to kill the cells that were producing the fluid that was responsible for the high pressures and high pain. Wee, I was ecstatic today when DANIEL's eye pressure was \"7\"! So DANIEL is no longer in pain and was able to keep his eye, which is much more cosmetically pleasing.
- So DANIEL is ready for adoption! He loves to gather lots of towels and blankets and make his own bed and, if possible, he would prefer it be on top of a table or in a chair.

We do our best to provide accurate information, but adopters must understand that each home is different and the dog may behave differently in a new home. Dogs are creatures of their environment and you help make the dog what it will be. Homes considering adopting a puppy must be prepared for: 1.) Flexible schedules for potty training. Puppies can only hold it for one hour per month of age (ex. a 4 month old puppy can only go 4 hours without a potty break). 2.) Crate training until the puppy is at least one year old, to prevent chewing on inappropriate things when you can't supervise. 3.) Socialization: The more positive and varying experiences as a puppy the better, both in and out of your home. 4.) Puppy behavior and life stages are equivalent to a human toddler. It takes at least a full year to have a calmer, well-adjusted dog. Patience is required and when your dog's behavior is a positive experience for you and those around you, your patience will be rewarded ten-fold for years to come. Please do not consider adopting a puppy if you have not thoroughly thought through the pros and cons of having one. So many people end up returning them after 3-5 months because they didn't realize the amount of work involved in raising a puppy. Patience, appropriate toys, socialization, and obedience training are all musts. All are time consuming, and can be expensive. All Dogs require supervision with children and obedience training. Adopters that want to have good dogs must be prepared to put the time and effort into training a dog. Any dog requires work and effort, but a well trained, well socialized dog is more than worth the effort put in to get them there.

We recommend him to go home with children 12 and up, he can be touch sensitive at first.. Do not let his age fool you this sweet, spunky dude is ready for many long walks, car rides, new adventures and snuggle time with you. If you have been searching for a low key, loving, all around great boy then come check him out. Please talk to a staff member for more information!

name: Wednesday
description:
Our stunning Wednesday enters the room like an arctic blast of cold on a hot summer night and grabs your attention! This magnificent one and a half year old, black Labrador Retriever mix came to us from a big city Animal Control facility, where she spent some time after a lackluster owners abandoned her. She was rail thin and gaunt when she entered the city shelter system, and took some time to adjust to her harsh surroundings. 

When Wednesday came to our Rescue, she was a wild child, a Black Beauty in need of some firm, loving leadership. It was painfully obvious that her owners had missed all of her social development cues, and woefully neglected her manners and leadership training. Wednesday was as precocious as her Addams Family namesake, and seemed to feel that her opinion was warranted on just about every subject.

In no time, Wednesday has developed into a canine thoroughbred, brimming with potential. An energy and personality match is key to Wednesday's happiness. She is a high energy, athletic dog who needs alot of outdoor exercise. She would gleefully keep rigorous pace with an avid runner, hiker or powerwalker, and seems to thrive in the brisk country air. No doubt about it, Wednesday needs an active adopter, but, also one who is extremely proficient in leadership and obedience training. She is not a dog for the casual or inexperienced adopter.

Wednesday largely appears to be Labrador Retriever, but we also suspect some Border Collie in her DNA. She is a lean, tall dog weighing 47 pounds, and is extremely graceful and athletic. She runs with great speed, and could be an agility champion. Wednesday has the energy and intelligence that we see in this high strung Herding breed, as well as the mischievious and impertinent tendency that sometimes occurs when Border Collies are under exercised and bored! 

As a double dose of working dog, Wednesday definitely needs a job, and she is a natural at obedience work. She knows all her basic commands, and has passed many of the Canine Good Citizenship tests. She handles beautifully on lead, and heels nicely. Wednesday still needs some polish on her stranger manners, since she may, on occasion, greet someone rudely, but motivated adopters should be able to work her through any issues by employing her well honed commands. In the right hands, Wednesday will become a fantastic, well behaved companion.

Wednesday would fare best in an adult home, with adopters experienced in handling large, active breeds. She would overwhelm toddlers and seniors. She could easily join a multi-dog home, with another active, well trained dog, but sometimes, unruly and ill mannered dogs press her buttons. We have not had her around cats, but she would most likely chase them beyond their tolerance level.

Wednesday has respectable house manners and is mostly housetrained. She will need some finetuning on her potty routine as she transitions to a new environment. Wednesday is in good health, and has been spayed. She has been vaccinated for rabies, bordatella, and DHLPPC (distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvo, parainfluenza and coronavirus). She has had the 4dx test, and is negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. She has been microchipped and dewormed, and is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm treatment.

If you are interested in Wednesday, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738.

name: Hero
description:
Our magnificent Hero needs a hero of his own. This beautiful, robust boy is a victim of circumstances. His doting owner lost her home, and desperately tried to find housing to accommodate her beloved companion, whom she had raised from a pup. Hero's Mom took up temporary residence in a local motel, until she could get her bearings, but Hero was booted out by the motel manager. After a tearful goodbye, sad Hero was left in the care of a well-respected town shelter, who pled his case to us.

Hero appears to be a handsome mix of black Labrador Retriever and Border Collie. He has the physique and color of a black Lab, and the white tuxedo markings and black speckled white socks that suggest Border Collie. At 50 pounds, Hero has a solid, muscular build, and yet is easy to handle on lead. As a combination herder and retriever, Hero loves the outdoors, and has a hardwired work ethic that needs to be channeled through exercise and obedience work. 

Hero sometimes seems unsure of his place in the world, and needs to join a home with a strong pack leader, willing to provide the structure that he needs to to thrive. Hero gives the impression of caution at first, as he sizes up strangers, but warms quickly to a gentle touch. Adopters will need to be comfortable putting boundaries between Hero and strangers: he can become overzealous in guarding his person. He would be the ideal watchdog.

Hero seems subdued and intimidated at times, in the midst of our busy foster home, and we sense that a quiet, adult home would suit him best. He is not a big fan of change, and a steady, quiet routine will serve him beautifully.  Hero would be the ideal walking or running companion for an active single or couple. He loves the outdoors, can keep a brisk pace on a hike, and longs to make a one-to-one connection with a strong human personality. Hero could easily join a multi-dog home with another well-trained, calm dog, but cats are a definite no-go.

Hero has progressed nicely in his basic obedience training. The obedience work serves him as a job he can take pride in, and he performs the commands beautifully, either for praise or treats. Obedience training is key to providing the working breeds with the purpose and focus that they need to live happily in a domestic lifestyle.

Hero has good house manners and is house trained and crate trained. Adopters should have appropriate patience, and expect to troubleshoot the occasional accident that will inevitably occur during Hero's transition to a new home. He is in excellent health, and is at an ideal lean body weight. He has been neutered, and has been vaccinated for Rabies, DA2PP (distemper, adrenovirus, parvo and parainfluenza), and Canine Flu. name: LORETTA
description: Loretta is one of four collies that was removed from a property in Maine that was overcrowded with animals. She is the biggest of the ladies that we have and has the most luxurious fluffy coat of all the ladies. All of these girls are quite worried about new people, new things, and new spaces, though Loretta seems to be the most confident of the bunch. That being said, she still came from an extreme situation and has had no exposure to a normal life for a dog, so she will need a very patient family with a quiet home to help her adjust to her new life. She'd do best with another confident but gentle dog friend to help show her the ropes. We think she'd do well with a dog-savvy cat as long as she's introduced slowly, and could do well with kids who are respectful of how nervous she will be. Because of the unique challenges that these girls will face, our staff is committed to offering plenty of pre- and post-adoption support to help each placement be as successful as possible. They are still a bit overwhelmed by all of the recent changes, so they aren't up for meeting new people just yet. If you're interested in learning more about them, please stop into our adoption center or give us a call. We'll be interviewing people regularly to help find the best match for each of these special girls.

If you would like to start the adoption our process is below:

Submit Application with two personal references and a vet reference.

If you have never had pets and do not have a vet, we will need THREE personal references.

Ensure references are people who know you and your lifestyle well.

Applicant MUST inform vet and references that someone from GaDaH will be calling.

As long as we are able to contact your vet and references, it takes just 1-3 days to process and hopefully approve applications.

If you rent we will need an approval letter for the breed of dog you are wanting to adopt from your landlord on official letterhead paper or email.

Rescue processes and hopefully approves applications.

Once approved, rescue invites applicant to come to the rescue to meet your chosen dog/s, spend time with him/her

and then hopefully take him/her home.

We do NOT hold dogs so if you are unable to come within a week or so of submitting your application the dog will still be available for adoption to other families.

For Canadian adopters, all that is needed to get them across the border into Canada is a current rabies certificate and proof of adoption, which is the adoption contract. Both of which are included in the medical file you will get when you adopt. (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/pet-travel/by-country/pettravel-canada)

Ensure ALL Fields are filled in, if something is relevant, then put n/a or something in so it recognizes an entry.

We do not recommend using a phone or ipad since these applications for some reason don't tend to come through and you will have spent a lot of time on the application for nothing as it will need to be re-done.

Once we have you approved we can schedule an appointment for you to come to meet

him/her at the rescue in Sebec, Mane and then hopefully take them home to start your new life.

I just have to work on an appointment basis as I run a boarding/day care business and the rescue and so am really busy, but by planning ahead of time I can be pretty flexible.

Carson is a young an energetic, happy-go-lucky confident young girl, she is great with the other dogs of all ages and sizes, living amongst dogs from 6 pound chihuahua's up to 120 pound German Shepherd Dogs. She is friendly and happy to greet people and will bark when she notices something she is unsure of. She is a social girl and loves to explore and when ready to rest she curls up with her friends in front of the pellet stove keeping toasty warm. She is always happy to see people and runs in with the other dogs, tail wagging. She is young and active and will need a family that can give her a good active life, suitable for his size. She is a puppy so chewing, barking / whining when left alone and needing house training are things to take into consideration. I have not seen her with children, but her demeanor and personality I have no doubt that she would be great with them and a lot of fun too. Since she is used to being around a lot of dogs, we really prefer that she be adopted to a family who either wants to adopt another puppy or dog, who already has another dog, or who can provide a lot of socialization for her with other dogs. She could be scared and lonely and will be missing her pack family. She is obviously a puppy and so expect to work with her on puppy things. She needs an active family and one that will keep her mind stimulated and challenged. Lots of hikes and adventures, training tricks, or agility, dock diving or other fun, active, stimulating activities would be perfect for this girl. As with all rescue's she needs guidance and training and we recommend families go through at least the basics of training with her themselves so that boundaries, personalities and body language can be learned from each other.We do not have cats or livestock at the rescue so we cannot say how she would be around them. Although all GaDaH dogs are very well socialized with other dogs, lots of other dogs have not had the benefit of this socialization and do not always know how to play and act with other dogs. name: MARGIE-G-AR
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
MARGIE-G was saved from the high kill shelter in Texas in early 2018. She was extremely emaciated and in rough condition, but she was so loving and affectionate. At the rescue she settled in great and it wasn't long before she was playing grandma to a female German Shepherds 3 week old pups.
MARGIE-G has a date of birth of 15 February 2009 and is fully vetted.

After being here a few months, gaining weight, starting to enjoy life and enjoying playing with other dogs, she was adopted in May 2018. Unfortunately in the middle of August 2019 I received a message that Margie-G, who had been renamed Maggie, needed to be returned as she had become extremely protective of her home and her owner.

Upon talking to her owner and just by knowing Margie's personality and of course the breed it became clear that she had been allowed to become \"alpha\" and so with being alpha comes naturally responsibility for dogs, as with humans. They must protect their family (their pack) and they must protect their home (their territory). Aggression like this doesn't happen over night and she would have taken control gradually, with growling, hackles up, barking and such - and had this been stopped and her made clear this behaviour was not needed, nor would be tolerated, there would have been no problems and she would have accepted that she was not alpha of her humans and so no need to protect her family and home. However, it wasn't stopped and it progressed to where the owner was scared of having anyone in her home and so returned her.

Since being at the rescue Margie has shown no signs of aggression or even wanting to be alpha, she has settled back in, although is still stressed and clearly missing her family life, but she is good being amongst other dogs, although not ideal for her age. She is a very sweet, loving, affectionate girl, who when allowed to come in my bedroom, will jump up on the bed and settle into a deep sleep. She will give kisses and just enjoy getting lots of love and affection.

Margie is 10 years old and with age comes health problems, she does have severe arthiritis in her hips and knee, she is on pain medications and I have some natural supplements that I am giving her to help with the joints and general health. She had been fed Alpo with her family, however, since this is an extremely low quality food we immediately switched her over to a high quality senior diet of both dry and wet food mixed together - she seems to enjoy it. She is house trained and will let me know when she wants to go out.

Considering her hips are in such bad shape she gets around great, she does jump up on the bed and climbs stairs without hesitation, however, this is not encouraged and only done when absolutely necessary, or without me knowing.

Margie really needs a quiet home and family where she can relax and enjoy her old age. The rescue is very loud and busy with lots of dogs running and playing and having fun and it can be stressful for her.

We are looking for someone who has experience with GSD / Working Breed dogs. They must be confident in being in control and not allowing the dog to think they need to be in control. As mentioned above, she became very protective and that needs to be not allowed anymore. She needs to be not only taught that it is not needed, nor acceptable behaviour, but precautions need to be taken, she needs to be either crated when people come round, put in a secure room, or have a leash and muzzle on - when dogs become protective there really is no leeway giving them opportunity. This will also show her that you are in charge and can see she is not needed. Having her under control any sign of growlng or negative behaviour can be corrected immediately and so she will learn quickly.

With the right family I do not think her protectiveness will be difficult to get under control, experience, and consistency is what is needed.
Then of course she has her arthritis so we are looking for a family that is financial stable to get her any treatment needed in the future and be strong enough now and over the next few years to be able to support her hips when she needs to go outside. Maybe a belly support will be needed, or even the possibility of a wheel-chair - all possible options that the family should be willing to consider and move forward on should it help her in the future.
At least annual x-rays and senior blood panels need to be done to keep on top of her health since she a senior girl and although she is a tough cookie, I would think she has a few more years at the most, but it is critical her health is monitored regularly. So a family that understands that and is willing to make her last few years the best ever and do what is needed, at whatever cost for her comfort.

She needs a high quality diet to suit her age, breed, any medical needs and of course ability and ease of eating. Home cooking would be PERFECT for her, but a high quality senior diet is needed.

I know there is a perfect family out there - she doesn't need LOTS of exercise, but she does need to get out and move her hips so that they don't seize up and be even more painful.

If anyone is interested in adopting her - think seriously about the commitment and her issues - it is easy to fall in love with a sad story and want to make it right - but please be sure you are able and 100% committed to her FOREVER.
