description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
LACEY-1 was saved from a high kill shelter in Texas where dogs have just 3 dogs to be saved and transported to the rescue in Sebec, Maine. LACEY-1 is spayed, core vaccines, rabies, heartworm & tick disease tested negative, de-wormed, heart worm and tick disease tested negative, monthly preventatives and micro-chipped. She has an estimated date of birth of 19 June 2017 and at the time of rescue in the middle of June 2019, weighed around 43.00 pounds. She is listed as an Pit Bull Mix. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

LACEY-1 was saved with her 3 puppies,Taylor, Spot & Holister who have been adopted and although she is doing great, she was sad and looked for them for several days after they had been adopted.

LACEY-1 is a great girl, she is fun, full of life, happy, playful, active, loving, affectionate, boisterous and a good all round girl. When she first got here with her pups she was a little apprehensive, but soon settled and took on the role of surrogate mum to some other pups that was here.

As the pups got adopted she did start to get a little anxious looking for them and whining, however, since she was living with lots of other dogs she soon was able to be distracted with play and fun with them and so she adapted and is now as happy as can be.

When I took Lacey for her spay surgery she rode like a queen in the car and was friendly and affectionate to the vet staff. She will bark at strangers coming in, but she is in a high energy environment and dogs tend to feed of each others energy. She doesn't bark excessively and will stop when told to do so.

She is a young girl and so an active lifestyle would definitely be of benefit to her. She needs a family that is familiar with the breed and understands that there is a lot of negativity towards pit-bulls and many places unfortunately do not allow the breed and people are of course quick to judge and condemn them. So we are looking for a Pro-Pit-Bull family.



She would be a great family pet, she is so much fun, so loving and gentle. She is always friendly and happy to see me or the volunteers that come occasionally come over.

He does use the dog door to go outside but he is not going to know to let you know he wants to go out - so we cannot say he is fully house-trained.

TILLY is spayed, core vaccines, rabies, de-wormed, heartworm tested negative and micro-chipped. She has an estimated date of birth of 18 April 2010 and weighs around 14.20 pounds. She has been listed as a Cairn Terrier Fox Terrier Mix. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, so it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

At the beginning of June 2018, Tilly was adopted and went to start her new life. Unfortunately in the middle of March 2019 I received an email from the family saying that she would need to be returned to the rescue. The problems the family had was that Tilly had started to get protective of her chair, and her home, she would bark and growl at people coming into the home. The family took her to the vet who recommended a training program and then anxiety medications. Tilly's negative behaviour continued and the family again reached out to the vet wanting her taken off the medication as there had been no significant improvement, the vet, even knowing that the rescue would take her back offered euthanasia as an option. Tilly had not bitten anyone and she had not a recent physical exam or blood panel done to rule out any medical issues for her personality change. Thankfully the family brought her back to the rescue.

When TILLY first got back to the rescue I noticed how over-weight she was. I put her in the bedroom which is off the main living area where there is a gate installed so she could come out of her crate and get to know the dogs and start to decompress slowly. She was at first growly with me which I tolerated for the first day back, on day two I shouted at her, pointing and telling her \"no, this behaviour was not acceptable\". I sat on the floor and within minutes she came belly-crawling over and turned over next to me to let me scratch her belly. That has been the extent of her aggression.

After a few days I let her out into the main living area with the 20 other dogs of all ages and sizes and she was a little over-whelmed, she had places she could go to have her own space which she did do mostly for the first week. She was very needy in that she would want to jump up on my knee and followed me around, which was to be expected since that was what she was used to with her family and also I am sure she wanted to be near me for a bit of security. I didn't allow this as it is important to know that she is not going to dictate the rules, that she is a member of the family, but is not in charge. At the time of writing this Tilly has been back at the rescue for 2 weeks and she has been doing great, she has growled at the other dogs, but only for them to get out of her space, she instigated play with one of the smaller dogs and is definitely coming out of her shell and getting a lot more confidence in walking around.

The rescue has had her to the vet to have blood drawn and a full CBC
and 27 Chemistry panel including testing for thyroid issues so that we can rule out hypothyroidism, some symptoms are weight gain and sudden aggression. Her extensive blood and chemistry panel came back good with nothing of any concern. She had a vets appointment on 9th April and had an examination that went well and it was agreed from the information and medical assessment that this is more of a behaviour issue and she just needs a family that will not let her get away with things, which will encourage negative behaviour. We think it was more that she was allowed to become \"alpha\" of the home and family, which led to her being territorial and consequently aggressive. The good thing is that there are no medical issues that we need to worry about.

TILLY is going to need a family that understands that she has exhibited negative behaviour and is confident and comfortable in giving a negative consequence to a negative behaviour, like you would do with children or any human for that matter. Her family said she absolutely loved going for walks and car rides and was a really happy go lucky girl although a little timid at times and they truly was heartbroken how things developed but did the right thing in bringing her back since they was not able to deal with her behaviour.

Rescue Bio before TILLY was returned.
TILLY doens't act 8 years old, she is pretty active, very playful, she is great with other dogs, but not too bothered in playing with them all the time, she likes to follow me around and will get a silly mood and spin around when I go over to feed and clean. She has a mischievous streak in she was trying to pull the to the other side of the fence she was on and started pulling it apart. She loves to have mad dashes and spins around in her crazy moments.

We do not have cats or livestock at the rescue, so we cannot comment on how she would respond or act with or around them.

A volunteer brought her young granddaughter over and she was great with her, initially she was a little bit shy, but soon warmed up and very loving and wanting to get lots of attention.

TILLY does use the dog door to go out to do her business. I do not know if she would let you know she needs to go out since she has 24/7 access to the outside, so it is important to note she will most likely need some training.

She is going to need a family that is used to small dogs. Someone who understand that he will need training and guidance and learns that humans are in charge so that he doesn't get too much of a handful. A somewhat active family who can give him the lifestyle that she needs. Going on road trips, to new places, hikes and adventures and letting her explore the sights, smells and sounds the world has to offer will be to his and your benefit. 

We do not recommend dog parks for several weeks, if not months, it is so very important for families and dogs to form a strong bond and get to know each other before exposing them to the potential dangers of dog parks. Although all GaDaH dogs are very well socialized with other dogs, lots of other dogs have not had the benefit of this socialization and do not always know how to play and act with other dogs. You also do not know the control the other families have over their dogs and you should always have a good recall for your adopted dog before going to dog parks.

name: CHIP-L
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
CHIP-L was saved from a high kill shelter in Texas with his 3 buddies, all feral and had been scheduled to be killed the day we saved them. CHIP-L is neutered, core vaccines, rabies, heartworm and tick disease tested negative, monthly preventatives and microchipped. He has an estimated date of birth of 20 April 2016 and at the time of rescue in May 2018 weighed around 11 pounds.

CHIP, PRINCE, MILO & PIXIE were all saved together. When I had informed the shelter I would take them into rescue, they informed me they were scheduled to be killed that day because they were feral. I had committed to them and so I couldn't back out.

When they got here I let them with the other dogs and just left them to it as I think it is important for dogs to decompress and figure out what has happened to them the last week, being picked up by animal control, taken to a large city kill shelter, having surgery and all the vetting then on a transport up to the rescue for 3 days, then getting here - it is so much for them all in such a short time.

CHIP has come a very long way and will come and sit next to me, he will let me scratch his head, belly, he will play although he does \"mouth\" when playing. He gets very excited when playing and is a very sweet boy. I let him build his confidence on his own and come up to me when he felt ready. At first it was taking treats and then this slowly progressed to me scratching his chest and ears, then eventually his belly. He is truly desperate for affection and he wants nothing more than to cuddle up on my lap. At times he has sneaked on the chair next to me and gone to sleep, however, he will not let me pick up he will run off, but then immediately come back.

As you can see in the video he does want to play, but he does \"mouth\" when playing and at times can put a bit too much pressure, he is not biting he just doesn't know he is playing too hard, but I gently correct him, telling him no and he does stop. This will take time, but the fact he has come so far on his own, in his own time, I believe with the right family he has huge potential.

CHIP needs a family that understands he is going to need time to figure things out again and do things at his own pace. He isn't going to be jumping on your lap snuggling up straight away, he isn't going to let you pick him up or take him for walks for a considerable time so a fenced in yard is an absolute must. With time, love and patience everything can come, being with a family that has time to spend with him, teaching him things and helping him gain trust will enable him to develop the confidence and trust he needs.

We do not recommend children more because of his mouthing little hard and also children are not as patient in allowing him to progress at his own pace.

CHIP truly is a very sweet boy, he enjoys the other dogs, he enjoys sitting on the back of the sofa watching the squirrels and birds at the feeding stations. He loves to get attention and deserves the best family and forever home.

We do not have cats or livestock at the rescue so cannot comment on how he would be around or with them.

They have an estimated date of birth of 30 January 2019 and are listed as Dachshund mix . We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely. They are bonded and so we intend to adopt them together and the adoption fee is $1,000.

We do not have cats or livestock at the rescue so are unable to comment how any dog is or will be around them. 

MINNIE and MICKEY are a fun loving pair, they are very bonded and although play with the other dogs, always end up playing together and sleeping cuddled up together. They are great with the other dogs and love to run and charge around. They are extremely affectionate and love being up on the chair or sofa snuggling.

As with all dogs they will need basic and advanced training so that they can learn their families rules, boundaries and expectations. They are very responsive and I feel that they will be easy and fun to train and will be eager to please. They are gentle pups and I think would make great family dogs.

They are puppies and so there is a lot of work involved and although they are small they can still be very mischievous and will soon be teething.

Canadian adopters need to know that customs charge 15% taxes when entering into Canada. This fee is not negotiable and is used to cover the rescue costs of pulling, vetting, health certificate, transport from Texas to Maine, monthly preventatives, supplements, food and anything else that is needed.

There are also lots of hotels, motels, pet friendly accommodations and wonderful camp-sites for the more adventurous families and what a great way to get to know your new best friend. name: SCHROEDER CROSS-POST PORTLAND, MAINE
description:
This handsome fella is Schroeder - a small JRT/Hound, maybe some bully breed in the mix, roughly 5 year old dog brought up from Georgia to Maine by another Maine rescue several years ago when he was a puppy, and is now finding himself in need of a new home. Although his original adoptive family has gone above and beyond with training and working with Schroederâs behaviors over the years, the living environment is just proving to be too much for him despite everyoneâs best and continued efforts to ensure he is not constantly stressed.

Schroeder is a sweet, energetic dog who really loves his people. Although he has been living with young kids for some time and does very well with âhis ownâ, he gets very stressed with the busy neighborhood kids and spooks easily, causing his behavior to worsen while on walks or trying to enjoy any outdoor time and he becomes reactive to other dogs and sometimes people. Ideally he needs a quiet, adult home with older/no children. A condo environment would not work well for him. It is possible he could coexist with another calm, confident dog, but Schroeder will need time to decompress and adjust through this transition so he should be treated as an only dog and be kept calmly separated from any other dogs in the home at least during this initial period. Cats are probably a no-go as his hound instincts send him on a chase.

We are helping to network Schroeder for a new home as we feel he deserves this second chance to find his ideal forever family, and sadly his original rescue is not willing or able to take him back and place him due to liability concerns. We realize that Schroeder is not an easy to place dog, and readily available fosters for a dog like him simply do not exist, but we feel he is a trainable, adoptable dog and he deserves the chance to find that special someone willing to put in the extra effort to provide him with a happy, calm lifestyle. With proper training, invested time and commitment, he has SO much potential and will be a great dog in the right home.

Schroederâs owners are not asking for a re-homing fee, but that his new people continue working with a positive trainer to ensure he has the resources and skills needed to manage his stressors and ensure a successful placement.

If you are interested in helping about this pocket-sized guy, please fill out an application on our website: 
www.buddyupanimalsociety.org/dog-adoption-application

Please help us share Schroeder and find him that perfect forever home he needs and deserves!

? If you have any questions please feel free to email us at info@buddyupanimalsociety.org ?

Thank you for reading about and sharing Schroeder, let's help find this boy his true forever!

name: Fizz
description:
ALL OF OUR DOGS ARE IN PRIVATE FOSTER HOMES IN LOUISIANA AND/OR MAINE (or partnering humane society in Louisiana). BECAUSE WE DON'T WORK OUT OF A FACILITY, WE ARE NOT OPEN TO THE PUBLIC. THE FIRST STEP IN ADOPTING A DOG IS COMPLETION AND APPROVAL OF AN APPLICATION.  

PLEASE VISIT OUR WEBSITE AT www.puppyloveme.org TO COMPLETE AN APPLICATION AND FOR MORE INFORMATION ABOUT OUR RESCUE  WE APPRECIATE YOUR TAX DEDUCTIBLE DONATION TO ASSIST IN OUR RESCUE MISSION.

Our all inclusive adoption fee is $395.  Our dogs are fully vetted, including age appropriate vaccines and spay/neutering. The dogs are transported via a licensed carrier from Louisiana to Maine monthly.  Sorry, we do not adopt to families with children under the age of 6, or, in some instances, older depending on the breed, characteristics and/or behavior of the dog.



Fluffy, sweet Fizz is 6 months old and weighs 42 pounds.  We are guessing he is a border collie/lab mix, but by all means take a guess of your own.  Fizz is a playful young man that loves toys and exploring his surroundings.  He gets along with other dogs and loves people.  He would love an active, outdoorsy family that will dote on him.  Could this be your summer buddy?

name: BRUNO
description:
Meet Bruno! Bruno is a beautiful shepherd mix that found his way to the home of a doggy foster in the freezing cold. Despite attempts to find his doggy parents, no one claimed this handsome boy. Bruno is a large boy at 102 lbs and is a very young adult at about 1 to 1 1/2 yrs old. He may still have some growing to do! Bruno is still learning manners of not to jump on people when he is excited and he does best with walks using a harness or he will end up walking you. He has not learned how strong he is but he is a very sweet boy and has no intent to hurt anyone. Due to his size, he would do best in a home without small children he could trample unintentionally. Bruno loves to try to lie in your lap when sitting down, he will cover your whole face in doggy kisses and he adores riding in cars. Bruno gets along with other dogs but due to his size, other dogs seem to be intimidated by him. He is indifferent to cats. Pays them no attention. He is working on housebreaking and as long as he is taken out within a reasonable time, does wonderfully. Bruno would need the fence in the yard of his new parents to be 6 feet. He easily hops over a 4 foot fence and then goes exploring. If there are items like a dog house at the edge of a 6 foot fence, this smart baby will use that as a step to get out and go exploring! If you are interested in snapping up this diamond of a dog, put in your application now! He will be neutered, microchipped and up to date on all shots and can be homed anywhere on the east coast from TN up to Maine.

ADOPTION FEE REQUIRED. Contact ccrtennessee@gmail.com.

name: Squirt
description:
Meet Squirt! 
This 3 year old Staffordshire Terrier mix is about as handsome as they come! Squirt came from a Manhattan animal shelter where he was at risk due to overcrowding, so we made some room for him here. He loves attention and to be scratched all down his back. He can be a bit timid of new people at first, but once he knows you wonât hurt him he is your best friend! At 70lbs (should be more like 60lbs) heâs a strong guy and because of this he will need someone who can handle walking him until he is fully leash trained (which he is doing fantastic at, heâs a fast learner)! I, his foster mom, am 4â11â and can still handle walking him when he pulls. Also because of his strength we are not recommending a home with small children but would be fine with older ones (10+). He is great with other dogs and very polite with them. Unsure about cats or small animals but can cat test upon request. Being a city boy he is not used to having a fenced in yard but wow he sure does love them!

Interested in Squirt? Send us an email at Babushkasanimalrescue@gmail.com for an application.

name: Drama
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Fill out an Adoption Application
Drama is a sweet, super soft, silly old girl who will steal our heart and make you laugh at her playful antics. She is super easy to live with, very adaptable and well mannered and lives to please you. She does however snore like a chain saw. She loves nothing better than to sit and doze near you, hangout on the back porch or go for short walks. She's a nine year's young 83 pond Mastiff mix. She hails from Manhattan so loud noises don't faze her and she is well trained and socialized. She is looking for a home where people will dote on her, play with her and make her golden years special.Likes: Chicken, scratches and being near her people. She loves to bring you a toy to play tug of war, but she can be quite enthusiastic and sometimes get a little over excited. She loves sticks and balls and likes to lay outside and chew on something.
Dislikes: She hates to disappoint and worries if she thinks you are upset with her.
Personality: Very sweet, easy going, silly and playful with great manners.
Temperament: Very trusting and let you handle her just about everywhere but she has some arthritis in her back end and is cautious about being touched there. She will follow her people everywhere, but sits on the closest dog bed or rug rather than right on top of you. She is a sweet and adaptable girl who just wants lots of love.
Energy level: low but she does like to play inside or out for very short periods.
Favorite activity: Sleeping, getting attention, sitting outside, finding a good stick, rolling on a dog bed on her back, mouth opened making silly happy noises.
Good with: Other dogs and people. She always has a tail wag for other dogs and will bark a few times when people come to the door but goes in for scratches as soon as you greet them. She likes cats a lot but can be overenthusiastic - she does take cues to back off from cats well.
Housetrained - Yes
Crate trained - No She doesn't seem to have ever been in a crate and not interested in going in, but is very good left alone in the house. She doesn't chew or get into the trash
Medical issues - She is nine and has some stiffness in her rear end but she is able to do stairs ok now, however a home with no more than a few stairs would be best as she gets older. She is little so does like to get up on a bed, but needs help. She does seem to be slightly cross eyed at times, but she can see fine other than perhaps having some depth perception issues occasionally.
She deserves a home where people can make a fuss over her and play gently for very short periods between naps. Older children if any would therefore be best. She is happiest when she can doze on a bed near you as you go about your business. Few if any stairs would be best as she enters her golden years.

Fostered in Norristown, PA.

Our rescue policy requires the following:

Adopters must have their primary residence in one of the following states: Pennsylvania, Ohio, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, West Virginia, Virginia, and parts of North Carolina.
Applications for giant breed dogs must be submitted by the property owner.
Homes with children under 6 years of age will not be approved for adoption.
Homes with children should have a fenced yard.
Pets currently in the applicant's home must have a history of appropriate veterinary care. Veterinary records will be checked.
All references must be checked before any visitation of the dog is permitted at the foster home.
All family members must be present during the home visit to the applicant's home.
Any dog(s) in the applicant's home must have an introductory meeting with the rescue dog being considered, before any adoption can be completed.

For additional information please review our FAQs or contact: mastiffstomutts@gmail.com

name: Pinto
description:
Meet the Bean siblings! Navy and Pinto are 2-month-old Labrador Retriever mixes anxiously awaiting their forever homes here in New Jersey. They were originally rescued from Marion County, South Carolina and are very lucky to be alive. At the moment, they weigh all of about 7 pounds, however, they will likely be medium-large sized dogs once fully grown. Their foster moms say, \"These two pups are definitely the life of the party! They love to run and jump on each other playing. They are definitely attention lovers.\" They are working very hard on their leash, crate, and house training skills. In no time, these smart pooches will be masters of all three!

Pinto is neutered, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

name: Wednesday
description:
Our stunning Wednesday enters the room like an arctic blast of cold on a hot summer night and grabs your attention! This magnificent one and a half year old, black Labrador Retriever mix came to us from a big city Animal Control facility, where she spent some time after a lackluster owners abandoned her. She was rail thin and gaunt when she entered the city shelter system, and took some time to adjust to her harsh surroundings. 

When Wednesday came to our Rescue, she was a wild child, a Black Beauty in need of some firm, loving leadership. It was painfully obvious that her owners had missed all of her social development cues, and woefully neglected her manners and leadership training. Wednesday was as precocious as her Addams Family namesake, and seemed to feel that her opinion was warranted on just about every subject.

In no time, Wednesday has developed into a canine thoroughbred, brimming with potential. An energy and personality match is key to Wednesday's happiness. She is a high energy, athletic dog who needs alot of outdoor exercise. She would gleefully keep rigorous pace with an avid runner, hiker or powerwalker, and seems to thrive in the brisk country air. No doubt about it, Wednesday needs an active adopter, but, also one who is extremely proficient in leadership and obedience training. She is not a dog for the casual or inexperienced adopter.

Wednesday largely appears to be Labrador Retriever, but we also suspect some Border Collie in her DNA. She is a lean, tall dog weighing 47 pounds, and is extremely graceful and athletic. She runs with great speed, and could be an agility champion. Wednesday has the energy and intelligence that we see in this high strung Herding breed, as well as the mischievious and impertinent tendency that sometimes occurs when Border Collies are under exercised and bored! 

As a double dose of working dog, Wednesday definitely needs a job, and she is a natural at obedience work. She knows all her basic commands, and has passed many of the Canine Good Citizenship tests. She handles beautifully on lead, and heels nicely. Wednesday still needs some polish on her stranger manners, since she may, on occasion, greet someone rudely, but motivated adopters should be able to work her through any issues by employing her well honed commands. In the right hands, Wednesday will become a fantastic, well behaved companion.

Wednesday would fare best in an adult home, with adopters experienced in handling large, active breeds. She would overwhelm toddlers and seniors. She could easily join a multi-dog home, with another active, well trained dog, but sometimes, unruly and ill mannered dogs press her buttons. We have not had her around cats, but she would most likely chase them beyond their tolerance level.

Wednesday has respectable house manners and is mostly housetrained. She will need some finetuning on her potty routine as she transitions to a new environment. Wednesday is in good health, and has been spayed. She has been vaccinated for rabies, bordatella, and DHLPPC (distemper, hepatitis, leptospirosis, parvo, parainfluenza and coronavirus). She has had the 4dx test, and is negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. She has been microchipped and dewormed, and is on monthly flea/tick and heartworm treatment.

If you are interested in Wednesday, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738.

name: Hero
description:
Our magnificent Hero needs a hero of his own. This beautiful, robust boy is a victim of circumstances. His doting owner lost her home, and desperately tried to find housing to accommodate her beloved companion, whom she had raised from a pup. Hero's Mom took up temporary residence in a local motel, until she could get her bearings, but Hero was booted out by the motel manager. After a tearful goodbye, sad Hero was left in the care of a well-respected town shelter, who pled his case to us.

Hero appears to be a handsome mix of black Labrador Retriever and Border Collie. He has the physique and color of a black Lab, and the white tuxedo markings and black speckled white socks that suggest Border Collie. At 50 pounds, Hero has a solid, muscular build, and yet is easy to handle on lead. As a combination herder and retriever, Hero loves the outdoors, and has a hardwired work ethic that needs to be channeled through exercise and obedience work. 

Hero sometimes seems unsure of his place in the world, and needs to join a home with a strong pack leader, willing to provide the structure that he needs to to thrive. Hero gives the impression of caution at first, as he sizes up strangers, but warms quickly to a gentle touch. Adopters will need to be comfortable putting boundaries between Hero and strangers: he can become overzealous in guarding his person. He would be the ideal watchdog.

Hero seems subdued and intimidated at times, in the midst of our busy foster home, and we sense that a quiet, adult home would suit him best. He is not a big fan of change, and a steady, quiet routine will serve him beautifully.  Hero would be the ideal walking or running companion for an active single or couple. He loves the outdoors, can keep a brisk pace on a hike, and longs to make a one-to-one connection with a strong human personality. Hero could easily join a multi-dog home with another well-trained, calm dog, but cats are a definite no-go.

Hero has progressed nicely in his basic obedience training. The obedience work serves him as a job he can take pride in, and he performs the commands beautifully, either for praise or treats. Obedience training is key to providing the working breeds with the purpose and focus that they need to live happily in a domestic lifestyle.

Hero has good house manners and is house trained and crate trained. Adopters should have appropriate patience, and expect to troubleshoot the occasional accident that will inevitably occur during Hero's transition to a new home. He is in excellent health, and is at an ideal lean body weight. He has been neutered, and has been vaccinated for Rabies, DA2PP (distemper, adrenovirus, parvo and parainfluenza), and Canine Flu. He has been boostered as needed, and has had the 4dx test: negative for heartworm, lyme, earlichia and anaplasmosis. He has been dewormed, and microchipped. If you are interested in Hero, please write to Denise@eskiesonline.com or call Denise at 860-908-9738 for more info.

name: Princess

name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home. 

If you are interested in adopting or fostering Winter, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Gracie #3
description:
Gracie #3 is an almost 2-year-old spayed black female lab. She weighs 44 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Gracie is a happy but shy girl, who loves adorably once she trusts you, but will take a bit of time and some caution to earn that trust. She absolutely loves other dogs, and has never met one she doesn't like. For this girl, the more dogs in her world, the better. If you are giving affection to another dog, her curiosity will get the better of her and she'll almost immediately come up to investigate. She can be a bit hand shy, even once she trusts you, so just needs humans that will go slow and understand to give her time. When she's in her element, she is silly, rolling on the grass, spinning around and zooming as fast as she can to play \"tag\" with the other dogs. And she's REALLY fast. She enjoys napping on the couch, and will allow herself to be a pillow for the other dogs. She also likes to sleep in bed with her humans and is incredibly silly in the mornings as she considers the bed a safe zone - she'll roll on her back and beg for belly rubs and play bitey-face. She especially loves when the other dogs join in the fun. She's excellent in the crate, and foster mom has spied her sleeping in the crate belly up while she's at work. Gracie prefers to eat alone, and will quickly eat her meals in her crate, or in a separate room, but is nervous eating in front of humans, unless it's people food that you are sharing with her (which she loves!). Her leash skills are pretty good, but she would prefer walking on quiet streets and not on a busy road. Gracie is a shy dog, and is always going to be a bit shy. She warms up to new people, but prefers them in small groups and not making a lot of noise, please. She's not the dog for you if you have rambunctious teenagers (or adults), throw parties often, or if you're looking for a dog to take everywhere with you. She started her life sheltered in a pen, and didn't get the socialization with humans she should have at an early age, so they make her a bit nervous. She's incredibly sweet and loving, and will reward you with her sweet, happy, silly self if you give her love, patience and understanding.

Kayla is a happy chocolate girl who likes belly rubs and running in the yard. She has been a loving and attentive mommy to multiple litters of puppies and now she is ready to take her turn in the spotlight. Sheâs a friendly girl with lots of energy who would do best with a family that will give her plenty of playtime outside, long walks, and lots of love. Kayla is good with dogs, but not cats and approved for kids 10 and up. Kayla is from a rural area and has not been exposed to traffic, noise, or groups of people. If dogs are overwhelmed by their environment, they can exhibit behaviors like excessive barking. To avoid this, for now we are limiting placement to stand alone single-family homes or townhomes in a suburban neighborhood or rural area. As we learn more from the dog's time spent in foster, we will evaluate if placement can be expanded to include a more urban environment and send out an update. 

Foster family reports: Kayla has a vivacious, energetic personality. After spending much of her life outdoors, she is excited to be in her foster home. Her tail has not stopped wagging! She thinks she's a lap dog and would crawl in your lap with the slightest encouragement. She introduced herself to the resident lab with play bows and ran zoomies with him. She is friendly without being either dominant or submissive. Kayla had no problem navigating the hardwood floors. She can zoom up and down stairs. She likes watching TV, especially animal shows and Litter Robot advertisements, which bring her to her feet everytime. (Must be the cat!) She also enjoys watching squirrels outside. This former breeder girl had a litter quite recently and still has enlarged mammaries. She weighs 80 lbs but should weigh ~75. She shows interest in meeting children (approved age 10+). Kayla rode well in the car and walks nicely in an Easy Walk harness. She loved her first walk in the park. Although she came from a rural area, she does not seem bothered by traffic or loud noises. Kayla is food motivated, which should help with refreshing commands. Kayla is settling nicely into her foster home. She was a little over-amped when she first arrived but now she is able to settle in the house. She enjoys playing with the resident lab, and in fact, she is usually the initiator of play! She likes taking walks around the neighborhood, and we discovered that she is a retriever. Kayla did not appear to know her name or any commands, so we are working to teach her basic commands and leash skills. She walks pretty well with an EZ-Walk harness, doesn't pull, but will sniff a lot if you let her. She needs to be tethered in the car until she knows her commands or she will be in the driver's lap. She is not crated when we leave the house and she does not disturb anything. Kayla is super loving and affectionate. She has all the most desirable lab traits! She is a velcro dog to foster mom, but seems to do most of her lab leans on the men she meets. She has met the neighbors and their dogs and impressed them with her friendliness and beauty. Other dogs really like her, so she appears to share good vibes! We don't know yet whether she likes water. Her background continues to mystify us. She was photographed at intake living on a chain, but she also knows her way around a house, is interested in human food and would like to get up on the furniture (although not allowed by her current foster). Kayla is quite energetic for her age and will need regular walks and/or active time in the yard. Since she doesn't bark, navigates stairs easily and can be exercised on leash, Kayla is now approved for townhouses on a case-by-case basis.

description:

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.  

If you are interested in adopting or fostering this dog, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption.

~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00

description:
Pokie is a 9-year-old neutered male chocolate lab. Pokie weighs 61 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Pokie is an exceptionally loving, sweet boy that adores all people and his toys. This silly boy has a toy on him at all times - so much so that we've had to teach him to check his toy at the door before he goes outside. Pokie has exceptional house manners. He is fully house trained and has full run of the house while we're out. He also loves going for rides in the car. Pokie is quiet and only lets out an occasional bark when there's someone at the door. Pokie is partially blind due to complications from diabetes, but he does see shadows and gets around just fine. He loves running around the yard and playing ball (he listens for the bounce and is quite good at locating it). His diabetes is well controlled with two injections a day that are quite easy to do. Pokie's other passion is food and he equates getting his insulin with a biscuit, so he eagerly sits in anticipation of getting his injection and treat. He would do well as an only dog or have a laid back doggy companion. No kitties. Pokie has so much love to give his forever family. He is such a sweet gentleman, LOVES people, toys and catching some rays. Pokie is mostly blind due to diabetes, but runs full speed around the house. He has excellent house manners and is a complete sweetheart. Pokie would do great as an only dog or with another super laid back companion. 

Foster family reports: Pokie is a wonderful companion. He loves to play with people and is getting along with the pack. Pokie adores everyone he meets and is very affectionate. Pokie loves to play ball (he tracks very well with his hearing). He is perfect in the house - he has never had an accident or gotten into anything he shouldnât. His thyroid and diabetes management have remained very stable. He would probably do best with a quiet doggy sibling or on his own.

description:
Maddie is our little Miss Cutie Patootie! She is a short and stocky malamute girl with so much personality. She is guaranteed to make you smile every day with her paw up for high fives and zoomies. Maddie was born October 2011. She is easy and independent. She is called a little miss spit fire, because she is a tough little cookie! She is sassy and all malamute. She enjoys being in her crate and doesn't make a peep. Or hanging outside watching everyone and everything. She also enjoys hiking and just loves the outdoors! She is also happy just laying around on her doggy bed and just being in the same room as you. Don't let that adorable teddy bear look fool you, she isn't a cuddler and prefers her space, EXCEPT when salmon treats are involved. She will come right up to you, give you high fives and show so much excitement for treat time! Just give her space and time to get to know you. She had a very rough life and is hesitant to trust people. Despite this, she sits nicely to put her collar on before going on a walk. She also rides well in car but generally speaking, Maddie doesn't just do things willingly, which is why positive training works well for her. KronchUSA salmon treats really help us encourage Maddie to make good choices. She likes to protest a little bit just enough so she feels like she had a choice.  

She will roll over for belly rubs and come up to you for some love but when shes had enough she will leave and go about her business. She was potty trained at one time but will need a refresher. She does not like other dogs but can be around them. If given the chance she will let other dogs know she is boss and that's why we recommend her as being the only dog in the home. When you are out on a walk she won't get upset seeing another dog as long as they are behaving. She isn't dog aggressive but won't back down from a challenge either. 

In May 2017, Maddie had ACL surgery on her right knee and is doing well. Of note, she was debarked as a pup so she doesn't have her 'woowoo' but don't let that stop you from giving this girl her second chance. She needs a home with Northern Breed experience. She has a strict limited ingredient diet --- salmon only protein and fat. Typical malamute she cannot be around small dogs or pets including cats.

description:
Born in August 2014, Bucky has a great sense of humor and is full of personality.  He would love to be your hiking companion followed by a picnic with a chicken sandwich. He LOVES car rides and visiting the nearby pet stores where all the goodies are. Bucky is a very social Malamute/Husky mix and would love a family of his own. He is a free spirit who responds beautifully to pawsitive communication. He enjoys chasing and burying balls (especially squeaky balls) and really enjoys going out on hikes exploring. He has separation anxiety and would do best in a home with a stay at home human. He is an amazing boy with high predatory behavior that can spot any critter or find deer. With cheerful redirection, he will give up the chase to stay with his human.

Bucky is always ready for an adventure but we believe he is trying to find his furever home. Bucky will behave so well, then out of the blue it's like he has to celebrate being good and will surprise you with the fastest zoomies!  However, this is far and few these days. He enjoys just being where you are & hanging out. He has been receiving positive training and has learned to redirect his excitement by sitting for a treat and sitting so the car door opens for an adventure. Most recently he is learning to relax, which he enjoys with chicken sandwich bite size rewards. Bucky looks like a very tall Siberian Husky. Bucky would benefit from pawsitive reinforcement training classes and someone with a good sense of humor. Bucky just wants to have fun, so learning how to communicate being consistent & calm works great for Bucky, especially with a soft yummy treat. 

With so much to give, he definitely will make someone happy once he settles in and knows he's loved. He prefers to be the only pet in the home...who doesn't like to be the star of the show?!?!  We recommend reading, Positive Perspectives 2 - Know your Dog Train your Dog by Pat Miller.  This book will open your eyes from a dogs perspective & help you communicate & train in a pawsitive manner.  To know Bucky is to love Bucky. He is such a sweet boy who is searching for his furever home & hooman. Those who meet Bucky can't believe that he hasn't been adopted.

If dogs are overwhelmed by their environment, they can exhibit behaviors like excessive barking. To avoid this, for now we are limiting placement to stand alone single family homes in a suburban neighborhood or rural area. As we learn more from the dog's time spent in foster, we will evaluate if placement can be expanded. 

Foster family reports: Update We know that Marley is not her real name so we're trying different names. Right now we're calling her Penny, so we'll see. A couple more facts about Marley/Penny. We're not sure how she got to be so large but she's the most food-unmotivated lab! She may or may not eat her breakfast and she's really not into fruits or veggies. Her thyroid has been tested and is fine. We've never had a pup take treats so gently. We're used to the \"you may lose your fingers\" type of lab. Marley/Penny will go to the door if she needs to do her business. She would like a family who's willing to take the time with her to help her feel comfortable and loved. She'd also like a couple walks a day to help her build up her stamina and lose some of those pesky pounds. She recently visited with a friend for a weekend sleepover and met two very dog-savvy cats. She initially appeared to want to play with them but that was more effort than she wanted to expend and she laid back down. Marley/Penny found the toy basket, and although she is not a huge player or retriever, she periodically picks up a tennis ball and brings it to you or gnaws on one of the many bones all over the house. description:

Ginger is a sweet, smart, gentle lady who enjoys snuggling, swimming, and going for walks. This pretty brown-eyed girl has good manners in the house, sleeps all night in a cozy dog bed, knows multiple commands, and walks well on a leash. Sheâs pretty close to perfect! Ginger is a fun, active girl who doesnât need much and is ready to find a family that has room for a laid-back love bug in their lives. Sheâs generally fine to be left alone for about 6 hours, but she needs a home where she won't be alone for a long work day. There are just a few things Ginger canât do in her golden years - like stairs. Sheâs okay on a few, but a whole flight is too much for her. She also needs help getting into a car. name: Theon
description:
Name: Theon
Suspected Breed: Husky/Lab mix
Approximate Age: 7 weeks (as of 9/12/19)
Approximate Weight: 5 lbs
Personality: playful, social puppy	
Observations with Dogs: good
Observations with Cats: good
Observations with Kids: not yet tested
Currently Living at: SC foster home, but coming to DC 9/21/19
 
Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.
BE A FOSTER:

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift. 

To learn more about sponsorship, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/donate/

 Diane von Furstenberg is a beagle mix girls who is about 5 years old and 27 lbs. Just look at those melting chocolate eyes and smooth long ears - talk about easy on the eyes.

These no puppy zones include all pet stores, dog parks, and for apartment dwellers, areas used by other dogs. These requirements are strictly for the puppys medical safety and longevity.

Flannery is 2 years old and weighs about 30 lbs with a look and a personality like a min-pin. She is an energetic, busy girl who LOVES to go for lots of walks and would likely even be a nice running buddy. She is smart and curious and will thrive on challenges. She just completed an Intro to Agility class and was a SUPERSTAR! With more training, she could be a serious competitor. She has mastered the tunnel, A-frame, hoop, and can jump anything you put in front of her. She has also been introduced to the teeter and the dog walk. Flannery will fetch anything - balls, frisbees, toys, even rocks!

Her funny personality, keeps us all chuckling. She loves to play with toys and when no one is available to play with, she will just toss toys to herself! Flannery is also a first-class snuggler and a Phillies fan.

Like her namesake, Flannery is a spunky southern girl. She will need an adopter who has some dog experience. That steller brain of hers could easily take over the show. description:

Breed: Lab/Shepard mix

She would do best with a patient adopter in a calm home, where she can have the space to come out of her shell. She is worth it, trust us! Because she is so shy with humans, she would be happiest in a home with another dog to help build her confidence. She needs a bit of stable living to learn that not all humans mean to bring her harm or neglect. She is good with other dogs and cats. 

Like most shelter dogs, Carmen may need a refresher on housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

This beautiful gal is affectionate, loyal, and loving. Bella is basically an oversized lap dog at home, and loves being close to her humans. She has come a long way since we rescued her. Initially fearful and dog-reactive, this girl attended training classes with her amazing foster and has learned how to be polite and confident, all with just some positive reinforcement and consistency. She's smart and eager to please, which makes her highly trainable.


From her foster: Meet Bella! She is a beautiful, loyal girl that loves to run and is just a bundle of energy. She wants to please her \"people\" and has done really well with training as she is extremely food motivated. Although she has energy, she can be gentle when need be with the proper commands, but overall would make a great companion for an equally energetic family! She tends to get overwhelmed in large social gatherings (such as adoption events) and it is recommended for potential adopters to meet her in her foster environment, where she is comfortable and happy and can best show her true colors.

Bella will need an adopter who is committed to giving her lots of exercise, as well as continuing with her training. We recommend another training class for her with her adopter since it is about training the human as much as it is about training the dog! A class also has the benefit of building a closer bond between dog and human. We want to ensure her forever family continues to reinforce the positive behaviors so she can remain a confident and well-adjusted pup.

This gal has been overlooked for so long because of her reactivity towards other dogs, and she wonders if anyone will give the \"new Bella\" a real chance at a loving forever home. She has worked hard for it, and she deserves nothing less.

When the shelter asked us to save this sweet senior, how could we say no? Just look at her adorable frosted face? How does a dog like this end up in the shelter, we wonder? This dog deserves better and we will make sure she gets it.

Del clearly wasn't afforded many comforts in her previous life. She didn't know what the TV was in her new foster home, and stairs are also new to her. name: The Hobbit
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8481

 Meet The Hobbit - known fondly to her foster family as Lady Arwen or Lady for short. She is a 45-50 pound, one year old, beagle/spaniel/lab mix is our best guess. She has gorgeous creamy coloring and luxurious fur - hard to keep your hand out of it. And she doesn't mind the gentle petting and attention at all. She has her nose to the ground all the time - perhaps a nod to her beagle heritage? And she has long silky fur that one might associate with a spaniel. She is so gentle and sweet, and has done beautifully with children, other dogs and car rides. Each day we see more of her exquisite personality shining through. She's very loving and sweet. She's also smart and loves to cuddle. She's been really great with our 2 year old and our 12 year old twins, but our 7 year old is a little too rambunctious for her.

More about this darling girl:
- She is house trained in her foster home, and has visited homes of family members and remembered her house manners there as well.
- She is crate trained, and knows that her crate is her personal den and uses it at time to get some downtime, to relax and unwind. She is a smart girl understanding her personal space.
- She is working on improving her leash skills. She likely never walked on a leash before coming to her foster home, and she likes to pull. With training she is improving and to become really adept and walk on a loose leash, her adoptive family will need to continue the training process.
- She may be shy when meeting new people, but she has impeccable manners - not a jumper
- She is learning her house manners - she likes being on the couch which is fine in her foster home, but she may have to be trained otherwise in her adoptive home. She is very agile and has jumped up to get food from the table. She is learning quickly that is is not acceptable in her foster home. 
- She is generally quiet. She will alert at random times but it's few and far between.
- She is learning to trust humans more thoroughly and quickly, and her fosters are consciously socializing her to help her build confidence. She would rather people kneel down to pet her instead of looming over her. She gets nervous if someone comes up behind her too quickly and can startle if she is bumped into by accident. I think she needs more work on trusting humans in general. She shows no reactivity or aggression, but retreats to her crate if she feels overwhelmed. 
- She loves to run around in the backyard. She loves to play with other dogs. She seems to be a moderate energy dog and she is still trying to figure out how it all works inside a home.
- She loves to play with other dogs.
- She has not been exposed to cats, but her foster thinks she could do well with a confident cat. She's tried to go after squirrels on walks and birds get her attention.
- She will do best with a patient adoptive home where they can continue to show her that humans are a good thing and being apart of a family is where it's at. Possibly someone with another confident dog to help her to continue to gain confidence in a home.

This dog tested positive for Anaplasmosis before arriving to the rescue. Anaplasmosis is a very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Anaplasmosis is not contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get this disease is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

name: Bella
description:
Meet sweet, playful Bella who is a petite 32lbs and 1 year old!  She is currently being fostered in Tennessee and available for adoption and transport to most northern states upon a confirmed adoption. Her adoption fee is $275 and is inclusive of ALL transportation and vetting costs.  Bella is spayed, microchipped, current on vaccines, heartworm negative and has recently been given the 6 month Proheart heartworm preventative.  Read on for more info on this loving and special girl!

Bella is a very loving dog.  She will curl up next to you, enjoys sleeping next to foster mom, she is SMART and has responded well to training which is still a work in progress. She was brought into our rescue mid August when her family had some tragic circumstances and due to no fault of their own had to surrender her.  She had been adopted by them just a couple of months before, from a city animal shelter after living as a stray on the streets of Memphis.  She is clearly a survivor! While the shelter had put her at 2-3 years old, our vet said she is actually in the region of 11-12 months.   Putting the pieces together, we believe she was likely born as a stray and survived on the streets for the first part of her life, as so many dogs in Memphis do, before finding herself in the shelter.   Obviously, she had no \"training\" or experience of living in a home.  She came a long way with her first family but didn't have a lot of socialization with other pets because she was an only dog and didn't go out much.  She's now in a foster home where she is exposed to other dogs and cats (she is NOT a fan of cats) and is actually doing well with the dogs in the foster home.  She LOVES going to doggy daycare.  That being said, she has been somewhat selective at daycare. She passed all their tests and is doing really well, however she does better with dogs bigger than herself.  She's not aggressive, but does try to be alpha with smaller dogs, and can be barky and reactive if another dog shows alpha behavior toward her.  For that reason, we think Bella will do best if she is an only dog or if there are other dogs in the home, it must be with someone who feels confident they can work with introductions and integrations.  We have tested Bella with kids 10 and above, and she has been absolutely great with them.

Bella would love a forever home where she can show you how loyal and smart she is! Please donât hesitate to reach out with any questions.

It was not just Raven's looks, but also physically how she walked and moved. Raven does have arthritis, and has been having regular acupuncture appointments to help with her condition. His person will have to be supportive and understanding, patient and willing to do whatever it takes to help him, they have to be strong because he cannot take that role, he needs a leader and someone he can trust to get through this fear. He's a Texas gem and he's got a second chance at life up here in Minnesota. This little guy will make someone so happy because he's such a funny guy once he trusts you and his heart is huge for love. Plus he's my favorite color black which never shows on your dress clothes and then to top it off he's got Doberman markings the black and tan so he's super cute and his ears stand up oh my gosh!!!

Buckwheat does need a home with another dog present and a fenced in yard

name: Delta
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.
Name: DELTA
DOB: 03/07/2017
Weight: 46
Adoption Fee: $125

I was born in Oklahoma but I claim Minnesota as my home. That's where my luck turned-around and I was truly rescued. A group of people in Minnesota finally convinced me... I would never be given-up on again. On a
cold day in December, the day after a lonely Christmas in a cage, I experienced the luckiest day of my life.

See... I had a really bad first year of life. No one really knows what happened to me. And I have no way to share it with them... although they can see my psychological scars periodically. They healed my physical ailments more easily. Well, 'easily' is probably not the best word, because I was very ill and it took many rounds of different medicines and several months to get my body healthy. I was a pretty sick puppy with worms and bacteria and parasites and wounds. I had all the ailments that a puppy growing up unloved and not cared for would have. I was given pills and shots, had blood drawn, and given more pills and shots. My body eventually healed, but only on the outside. My psychological ailments took longer.

In
my first year, I spent more than 100+ days in confinement in various cages at more than one facility. Through a series of good fortune I left Oklahoma and was transported to Minnesota. But months before my first birthday, even in Minnesota, my luck almost ran out. I was just days away from being euthanized. See... even
though I had been rescued and physically healed, I never made it to the \"adoption floor\" because I was too scared. I would shake uncontrollably and cower constantly. People tried to build my confidence and gave me lots of treats and spent hours teaching me things like... responding to my new name and how to sit. But regardless of their concern and best efforts, the metal cages, loud noises, strange faces and barking dogs kept me so unbelievably scared. And so I was labeled, \"rescue only\". Then two days before my 'down date' (my scheduled final day alive) a stranger came to my cage, picked me up, took me to a cold vehicle, wrapped me in a green blanket, took me home, put a goofy red dog coat on me, and held me for days while I adjusted to my new quieter surroundings. That was the luckiest day of my life.

A group of people saw passed my scared exterior and just wanted to give me a chance. Who
knew that it would take me more than 20 months of waiting to find my forever home. But, regardless of the passing months, the rescue people still haven't given up on me. I've gotten lots of love, snuggles, patience, treats, foster brothers and sisters and an annoying cat to bug me (ugh!). They taught me that houses are pretty awesome, and that doorways, stairs and ceiling fans aren't scary afterall. They've given me more training, and even surgery to help me with my eye lids (my eye lashes were turned inward and scratching my eyeballs -- ouch!). Nothing has made them give up on me.
They truly love me. And
trust me, ha, I
have really given them a run for their money. I still have some separation anxiety (which is understandable given what my first year was like), so I've chewed on a few dog beds, couch pillows, bedroom blankets, and more than a few pairs of shoes whenever I've been left alone. I am a work in progress and getting better every day, and I want to find my forever home. I am full of playful energy and lot going for runs and bike rides. I love car rides and long strolls on the... river. Kids are the only ones that still terrify me, so it's best that I not be around them.

I want to find my people (or person) that will be patient with me and understand what I've overcome so far. I want them to see the unfailing, unconditional love I have to give in return... because I have so much to be thankful for.

That's the story of my luckiest day... and my journey isn't over. If you want to meet me, drop my rescue people a line. And I'll see you soon. Oh please excuse if I'm a little cautious at first sight --- new places still make me a little nervous.

Oh, and also... I do need a side-kick brother or sister to help me adjust to new things. (But sorry, no little dogs cuz they just seem to bug me. )

Thanks for reading,

Delta

(P.S. My foster mom is going to ugly cry on the day I leave, so be prepared for that! No seriously... like really, please bring the Kleenex! No joke.)

description:
Knox is not just another pretty face! He is a 4 year old double merle Catahoula Hound from Mississippi.  He is an amazing energetic smart boy who happens to be deaf. His deafness requires some special accommodations, but it doesn't hold him back from being a great companion and an active dog.  In fact, he is a better watch dog than his hearing foster brother using his other senses. Knox feels vibrations from cars, footsteps, & doors opening and smells his favorite people before they even enter the room. He knows the mail carrier is coming when the truck is still a block away! He will bark to alert you but settles down when he knows all is well.

Knox, like most deaf dogs, would do best in a household where someone is home most of the day and with a canine companion to keep him company. He loves to look out the windows or better yet hang out in a fenced in yard-in the sun anytime of year.  Knox walks well on a leash, loves car rides, and is house trained, and has used a doggie door, but does not do well in a crate.

 Knox LOVES other dog and LOVES kids - he enjoys playing  & cuddling with both. He doesn't have an aggressive bone in his body but he is a Catahoula Hound, with a bit too much prey drive, so a home without cats or other small animals is best. 

Knox has learned some sign language and would benefit from continued training. The ideal  home will have someone who can spend time with him working on reinforcing his training and taking him for long hikes and walks to burn off all of that Catahoula Hound energy. 

It takes a  bit to earn his trust but when you do, his love and loyalty are an amazing thing! Knox has been in foster care for over 3 years and is so deserving of a family of his own!  Please consider opening your home and more importantly, your heart to this gorgeous boy!

description:

Bizzie is loving and very sweet!
She's one of those dogs who epitomizes canine forgiveness - you'll see this when you read her backstory. Fortunately for Bizzie, her future's looking ever so bright! We're thinking she's a blend of Chow Chow and Shepherd probably born sometime in 2014 or 2015. She has been fine with adult dogs and puppies; she has not been introduced to cats. She's been great with all adults, and though she has not lived with children, we think she would be okay with older, dog-respectful kids. House training and crate training are in the works, and she seems to do fine on leash. A dog who has lived on a chain for years, like Bizzie did, can have a tendency towards guard dog behaviors and though she has not shown any of these tendencies, her adopters will likely need to work with a professional trainer to help her accept strangers and work through any fears she might exhibit.

Bizzie loves to run and play with other dogs, people and toys! She rides well in the car while crated, she's very calm. Though a fenced yard would be great to get in some running and playing, daily leash walks for business, exercise and fun will work just as well to keep her happy and healthy. And to keep that canine mind sharp, think puzzle toys and games. Bizzie really just wants to find a forever home where she'll be loved and cared for. Could that be your home? Fill out an application today and her people will get right back to you!

Bizzie's Backstory: Bizzie truly deserves a wonderful life. Her first 3-4 years were very hard. She was from the south side of Jackson, Mississippi, and was tied out on a 6-foot chain to be used as a guard dog. Her shelter was limited to a carport, no matter what the temperature or weather was like. She often did not have food nor water, except when a neighbor was contacted for dog food. After that, the neighbor often checked on her and would feed her and give her water. We know that Bizzie had at least one litter of puppies that a rescue took, but Bizzie was left behind. However the rescue did provide a spay for her. Bizzie's friend finally convinced her owner to relinquish her. When the vet checked Bizzie, she did have heartworm, which has been treated and she is now clear. At first, this pretty girl was scared when anyone approached her with a leash - maybe she was afraid she would be tied out again. Of course, we know that this will never again be the case!

Medical Note: This dog has been treated for heartworm disease with melarsomine injections. Once treatment is completed and the dog tests negative for microfilaria, the dog will be cleared to resume normal activity and able to be adopted. Untreated heartworm disease can cause lasting damage to the heart, lungs and arteries, and can affect the dog's health and quality of life even after the parasites are gone, possibly presenting as medical complications and/or new conditions in the future. This dog showed no symptoms of heartworm disease before or during treatment. A good resource for more information on heartworm disease is: https://www.heartwormsociety.org/pet-owner-resources/ heartworm-basics. Please check with your vet if you should have any questions or concerns about this condition, and discuss any concerns you may have with your SOS Adoption Counselor.

description:

name: Bailey
description: Hi! My nameâs Bailey and Iâm a 2-year-old neutered male Chihuahua Mix. I came to Lucy Mackenzie with a bunch of my buddies from Mississippi earlier this summer. I was adopted soon after arriving, but things didnât work out as well as we had hoped. The good news is that we all learned a lot about what I need in my new home. My continued obedience training is going to be very important. Some people think that smaller dogs can get away with things just because weâre small, but thatâs not true. Boundaries and rules are really helpful and will go a long way towards my happiness. We also learned that young children confuse me quite a bit. Iâve met people of all ages here at the shelter, but in my home, it would be best if I lived with older, dog-savvy children only. I really like being around people, and will do pretty much anything to be near them. Iâve been known to climb up and over my kennel door here at the shelter, which is why I shouldnât be trusted in a fenced in area left to my own devices. I will probably find a way out. The good news is that I love going for walks and playtime, especially with my favorite toy balls, so I promise you that weâll always have a good time. If youâre looking for a new canine companion that will surely bring lots of love and joy to your life, stop in and meet me today!

description:
Our sweet Raven has patiently been waiting her turn to come from Mississippi! She is roughly a 12yr old Pomeranian mix and weighs in around 24 pounds.

She may be missing a few teeth and have to be on thyroid medicine for the rest of her days but she sure is feeling better and is no longer in pain!
She is a very good girl at the groomer's, after so many years of neglect she enjoys the pampering! Raven is good with other dogs, but not sure how she is with cats since her foster home doesn't have any. Due to her age, she would do best in a home with NO smaller children, older responsible kids would be fine though! She loves to cuddle up on the couch and snooze while the humans watch TV. Raven's bedtime routine consists of sleeping on the bed with her foster parents as she is so deserving of.
Our adorable princess is already spayed, up to date on vaccines, current on preventatives and microchipped. She is looking to spend the rest of her life with a family that will truly adore her and give her the great life she obviously missed out on all these years

Gumbo has been here since April and during that time we have found that being an only pet in the house is a good idea for him. Due to his handsome strong build and jumpiness, we recommend children 13+. He is a great boy who just wants to please his family. Could he be the perfect addition to your family?

The shelter environment is much different than your home, so expect the unexpected. We do our best to help find the right pet for you, but your new dog may act differently on your turf than he/she did on ours.
