name: Ajax
description:
How I arrived to Northwoods: I came to NHS to find my furever home because where I lived there just wasn't enough room for all my energy, and there were small dogs I liked to chase.

I am originally from Missouri. I know a lot of commands like: sit, stay, lay down, shake, high five,  and hugs ( I will jump up you for this one).
I also know a couple of hunting commands like seek( use this one for things to eat only please). I also know Find it- if i have the smell of the item i will track and find it.
I am a natural born hunter and love to hunt. I need a little training and I will be a good hunter. Tho I am a little scared of loud noises right now.
I lived with 4 children and loved them immensely-  sometimes I would even sleep with one of them. I do forget sometimes I have grown larger and would accidently bump into them. I also love stuffed animals- they are so fun to chew! I also love to play fetch and love my exercise and just running! Sometimes if I don't get enough exercise I can be a little naughty tho and do things I am not supposed to do,.

I am kennel trained and will go willingly but I don't like it for long periods of time. I get sad and bored and will start to bark. I do need a wire kennel- I will chew right thru  the others. 

My favorite chew toys are Antlers, they keep me entertained for hours! I also love water so if my bowl isn't full I will drink from a toilet- I just don't know why people don't try it!
 I am a very loyal and loving dog. I loved my friend the Beagle but dogs smaller than that get on my nerves and I really don't like playing with them. They look like prey to me so please keep them away from me or I may treat them like a snack.


Good with kids: Yes
Good with cats:No
Good with dogs:lived with Beagle and loved him, but DO NOT LIKE smaller dogs at all.

All the dogs at Northwoods Humane Society have had a basic exam by a tech. They have been microchipped, tested for Heartworm (if over 6 months of age), had at least their first distemper combo vaccination (2nd if here longer), dewormed with a general dewormer, and had a flea and tick treatment applied if applicable. All the dogs will be spayed or neutered before they are adopted to their new permanent homes. name: Foster Homes Needed
description:
Every minute matters when it comes to rescuing a Shih Tzu. We may get a short notice that someone needs to surrender their dog or a puppy mill dog needs a temporary home. We can't help if we don't have families willing to foster, and we are always in need of more foster homes!

If you live in the Minneapolis/Saint Paul, Rockford or Chicago, IL areas and want to help save lives, please complete either our online Foster Sign-Up or download a word version here:

http://www.northstarshihtzurescue.org/foster/

(please note: neither dog pictured are available to foster or adopt, both are in their forever homes)

NorthStar Shih Tzu Rescue exists to benefit both Shih Tzu and Shih Tzu blend dogs and the people of our community. We operate as a no-kill rescue that provides rescue and adoption services, and meaningful outreach programs in order to advance the welfare of these companion animals, to serve and educate our community, and to make a positive, loving impact on the lives of both.

NorthStar, located in Excelsior, MN, actively works to rescue Shih Tzu and Shih Tzu blend dogs from dangerous environments and shelters with the ultimate goal of placing them in loving, permanent, adoptive homes. We rescue unwanted, abandoned, and abused dogs. We have them vaccinated, micro-chipped, spayed or neutered, provide other medical care, and rehabilitate them in carefully selected foster homes.

We also serve as a resource to our community and all pet owners by providing education and information on the benefits of adopting an animal in need as well as responsible pet ownership, including the importance of spay/neuter, good nutrition, and positive behavior training. We strive to increase public awareness about companion animal overpopulation, commercial breeders, and to offer solutions to end the killing of adoptable animals.

We work in alliance with local animal shelters, pounds, other rescue groups, and humane society organizations to ensure these animals are not forgotten.

name: Diane von Furstenberg
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8549

 Diane von Furstenberg is a beagle mix girls who is about 5 years old and 27 lbs. Just look at those melting chocolate eyes and smooth long ears - talk about easy on the eyes. 

Diane, who is is fondly called Jolene by her foster family, is a pretty low-key dog. She is timid around new people and will need an adopter who understands that she's going to take some time to warm up. This is all so new to her, and we don't know her background, so perhaps she hasn't had a loving home before. She is very playful with the other dog in her foster home, and this is when we see her fun, quirky side come out. Her foster family is working on slowly socializing her, and helping her to build confidence so her true personality can shine. She is working on her house-training, and does well in a crate - no accidents there, and she is a quiet sleeper. And she walks well on a leash. She is just the sweetest little thing, and we will update her profile as she comes out of her shell more.

This dog tested positive for Ehrlichia and Anaplasmosis before arriving to the rescue. These are very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Neither is contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get either is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

description:

Hi, I'm Dorian's Buttercup! OPH helped evacuate me from a partner shelter in Hurricane Dorian's path and now I'm safe with OPH and looking for a home! 

I'm a female pup, about 6 months old, 38 pounds and appear to be perhaps a Hound/Shepherd mix. My family says I am the PERFECT size since I sit right in the middle of my small and larger siblings.

My three favorite things so far since coming to my foster family have been belly rubs, squeaky toys and the abundance of other dogs to befriend. I am very good with getting to know other dogs and making sure we are on the same page and boy do I love to play if they let me! I have been around large dogs and small and just love them all. If I feel overwhelmed in any way I lay down and let them sniff me but I do not react as I know they are just getting to know me too! 

I have been practicing walking on the leash and with the guidance of some of my foster siblings I am picking it up quickly!! I really enjoy walking and sniffing all around these new place. I would absolutely LOVE to find a forever family that loves walking as much as me. Did I mention I LOVE belly rubs too? My foster family says I am all about the \"people loving\" and the cuddles, which I why I think I get SO many kisses from them!!

I have been given so many gold stars for my potty training skills since coming in to my foster home! I much prefer to do my business outside, which to my surprise I have been given lots of yummy treats for, so I think I will keep that up!! 

I do very well in my crate and understand it is my safe place for me to relax. I sleep well through the night and when my foster family is out of the house I stay in my crate just fine. 

**The only BIG thing missing in my world right now, is a family to call my own. I really would LOVE to find a human family of any size who would let me make them as happy as they would make me!!**

description:

name: Zekke
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8390

Look into my eyes....you will be hypnotized by my charm!

Hello, my name is Zekke! I am six months old and estimated to be a husky mix. I arrived at my foster familys house after a super fun flight all the way from NC. Have you been on a plane ride? It was sure fun.

I've been hanging out with my foster family for a few weeks now and while its fun here, I would sure like to find my forever family as well. Below are some fun things my family wants you to know about me.

- I am crate trained. Im quiet in my crate and sleep the night away and know to keep it nice and tidy with my toys. Can't ask for more than that can you?
- I have kept my crate clean and dry. (If I bark in my crate its because I have to go out)
- I appear to be housebroken but foster Mom says accidents can happen in a new environment. Don't worry, we will both be learning when I come home with you but we will both quickly know how to talk to each other. 
- Ive just about mastered this whole leash walking thing. It was brand new to me when I arrived but I like to take walks so I'm learning how to walk like a good boy mom says. I still get excited sometimes and get tangled in foster mom's legs but we are working through it.
- Im learning other fun things too. I LOVE treats so teaching me things is pretty easy. Ive mastered sit & lay down and am trying REALLY HARD on stay (that one is tough, I like to be with mom when we are outside (she hides cookies in her pockets for me, how can I resist that)) 
 - I appear to be a roll with the punches type of pup. Ive liked everyone, 2 and 4 legged that Ive met so far. 
- Foster Mom says I am one of the easiest fosters they have had. I am quiet, keep the place clean and follow the rules. I think she likes me. :)
- I would do best in a home with older kids (over 12) until I settle down a bit more. Im pretty mouthy still, just like most teenagers. I am working on keeping this under control and am getting better each day. These foster family people don't take any back talk from me about this, they are tough. Mom says my forever people will have to continue to be tough and remind me about this until I fully outgrow it.
- I would be a great hiking or running partner with a little training. Mom & I are doing a bit of running and I LOVE IT! The foster kids started school so we have been super busy and unable to hike but we have talked about it and I'm pretty sure I would like that as well. I love to be busy.
- TOYS! I have discovered TOYS and love them. I am getting pretty good with fetch (I will bring the ball back most of the time, sometimes I get distracted) and love soft toys that make noise. Foster mom told me not to destroy them and I'm doing really good with it. I really am enjoying the toy box here. I like to take one outside each time we go. Silly foster mom picks them all up and brings back inside at bedtime every night for me to start again in the morning.
- I met cats, chickens, turkeys and pigs and am happy to report that I did not bother any of them or care about them.
- two new things we have discovered this week. I like to swim and I liked being in arlington for an event. 

Do you like my new pictures? I went to an event and there was a nice guy named Drew there who took them. I think I look pretty handsome (even if it was 100 degrees that day...whew!)

Anyway, Ill be hanging out in Nokesville, VA. I am able to go home with you as soon as you are approved to adopt. My foster family says someone is going to be very lucky to have me.

name: Mia Desi Dog
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8261

Say hello to Mia, a nine-month-old, 30-pound female Desi dog (a local term for street dog) from India. Mia has quite a rescue story her mom, Furry, was living on the streets of New Delhi with Mia and her three siblings when they were very young, but their mother was unable to feed them due to illness. Mom and pups were taken into Kannan Animal Welfare, a rescue group in New Delhi, and brought back to health. Furry has already been adopted here in the US, and now Mia is the first of her puppies to come in search of a home! 

Because Mia grew up in a rescue facility, life in a home is very new for her. That being said, theres plenty about it she loves! Walks, couches, grassy open spaces, and toys (even sticks will do!), have all been big hits. When Mia is comfortable she is a funny, happy, and athletic girl whos happy to spend a few minutes wrestling or racing with the other dogs in her foster home, and then a few more minutes snuggling with her foster mom. 

Mia thrives on routine and attaches very deeply to her household members. Although she would benefit from ongoing exposure to new situations and people, she would probably be happiest in a low-key household with one or two people, who can help her develop a sense of security and confidence. Those people will find in Mia a dog who is endlessly entertaining, unbelievably charming, and absolutely devoted!

name: Will Forte
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8330

Hi! My name is Will Forte. 

Im a Beagle mix and estimated to be about 1 years old. Im a sweet boy and I currently weigh about 32 lbs. I came to OPH from a shelter in South Carolina. I love it here with my foster family and have been hanging out, getting treated for heartworms (they are yucky) and learning new tricks. I've finished my heartworm treatment (yay!) and am ready to find my forever family. 

Some things about me:
* I LOVE treats. What's that mean to you? It means that I am very trainable to tag along with you during your daily travels and can likely learn lots of fun tricks with you.
* I LOVE to play ball. Hopefully you will too. It helps get my energy out as well so we can watch TV later. 
* I LOVE to get my zoomies out outside. My foster family has told me that's where we do this and we play nice inside and try not to run too much. 
* Do you like to explore? Hey, I do too! Let's go on hikes together and explore all that's out there in Virginia and beyond. 
* AHHH...my crate. It's my quiet and calm time and I don't mind it one bit. It's a pretty great place to nap. 
* I like everyone in my foster family so I'm sure I will like you too! They have older kids and I love being around them. 
* I hope you have some toys or that we can get some. I love to play with them. Wanna go to the pet store and pick some out?
* Here's the best part, are you ready? I have not had any accidents in my foster familys house. My mom says I may need a day to adjust to your house but shes assured me that I will quickly know your routine as well and not have any accidents there too.

I'm a super happy boy, my tail is always wagging. Let's find a time for you to meet me and see what a fun little guy I can be. There are some neat video's featuring none other than me below so you can see me in action. (I'm famous you know, I have my own videos and everything)


Click here and here to see me in action with OPH! 

Click here to see me playing with a foster friend. 

I'll be here hanging out with my foster family in Oakton, VA. Ask my foster mom for directions, she will be happy to share them with you. Don't wait! I'll be snatched up soon she says.

name: Zekke
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8390

Look into my eyes....you will be hypnotized by my charm!

Hello, my name is Zekke! I am seven months old and estimated to be a husky/white shepherd mix. I arrived at my foster familys house after a super fun flight all the way from NC. Have you been on a plane ride? It was sure fun.

I've been hanging out with my foster family for a few weeks now and while its fun here, I would sure like to find my forever family as well. Below are some fun things my family wants you to know about me.

- I am crate trained. Im quiet in my crate and sleep the night away and know to keep it nice and tidy with my toys. Can't ask for more than that can you?
- I have kept my crate clean and dry. (If I bark in my crate its because I have to go out)
- I appear to be housebroken but foster Mom says accidents can happen in a new environment. Don't worry, we will both be learning when I come home with you but we will both quickly know how to talk to each other. 
- Ive just about mastered this whole leash walking thing. It was brand new to me when I arrived but I like to take walks so I'm learning how to walk like a good boy mom says. I still get excited sometimes and get tangled in foster mom's legs but we are working through it. *** UPDATE *** Zekke has this down. Has recently been out on a busy street and was perfect on the leash with his foster family and with others.
- Im learning other fun things too. I LOVE treats so teaching me things is pretty easy. Ive mastered sit & lay down and am trying REALLY HARD on stay (that one is tough, I like to be with mom when we are outside (she hides cookies in her pockets for me, how can I resist that)) 
 - I appear to be a roll with the punches type of pup. Ive liked everyone, 2 and 4 legged that Ive met so far. 
- Foster Mom says I am one of the easiest fosters they have had. I am quiet, keep the place clean and follow the rules. I think she likes me. :)
- I would do best in a home with older kids (over 12) until I settle down a bit more. Im pretty mouthy still, just like most teenagers. I am working on keeping this under control and am getting better each day. These foster family people don't take any back talk from me about this, they are tough. Mom says my forever people will have to continue to be tough and remind me about this until I fully outgrow it. *** UPDATE ***: Zekke has really gotten this under control. He has recently met children as young as 1 and did really well with them. He seems to understand they are small and to be gentle with them.
- I would be a great hiking or running partner with a little training. Mom & I are doing a bit of running and I LOVE IT! The foster kids started school so we have been super busy and unable to hike but we have talked about it and I'm pretty sure I would like that as well. I love to be busy.
- TOYS! I have discovered TOYS and love them. I am getting pretty good with fetch (I will bring the ball back most of the time, sometimes I get distracted) and love soft toys that make noise. Foster mom told me not to destroy them and I'm doing really good with it. I really am enjoying the toy box here. I like to take one outside each time we go. Silly foster mom picks them all up and brings back inside at bedtime every night for me to start again in the morning.
- I met cats, chickens, turkeys and pigs and am happy to report that I did not bother any of them or care about them.
- two new things we have discovered this week. I like to swim and I liked being in Arlington for an event. 
- I am super dog friendly. Honestly, I have not met another dog that I have not gotten along with.

Do you like my new pictures? I went to an event and there was a nice guy named Drew there who took them. I think I look pretty handsome (even if it was 100 degrees that day...whew!)

Anyway, Ill be hanging out in Nokesville, VA. I am able to go home with you as soon as you are approved to adopt. My foster family says someone is going to be very lucky to have me.

So far, I have made friends with all of the hoomans and dogs I have met, but I really like playing with other younger dogs the best!

name: The Hobbit
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8481

 Meet The Hobbit - known fondly to her foster family as Lady Arwen or Lady for short. She is a 45-50 pound, one year old, beagle/spaniel/lab mix is our best guess. She has gorgeous creamy coloring and luxurious fur - hard to keep your hand out of it. And she doesn't mind the gentle petting and attention at all. She has her nose to the ground all the time - perhaps a nod to her beagle heritage? And she has long silky fur that one might associate with a spaniel. She is so gentle and sweet, and has done beautifully with children, other dogs and car rides. Each day we see more of her exquisite personality shining through. She's very loving and sweet. She's also smart and loves to cuddle. She's been really great with our 2 year old and our 12 year old twins, but our 7 year old is a little too rambunctious for her.

More about this darling girl:
- She is house trained in her foster home, and has visited homes of family members and remembered her house manners there as well.
- She is crate trained, and knows that her crate is her personal den and uses it at time to get some downtime, to relax and unwind. She is a smart girl understanding her personal space.
- She is working on improving her leash skills. She likely never walked on a leash before coming to her foster home, and she likes to pull. With training she is improving and to become really adept and walk on a loose leash, her adoptive family will need to continue the training process.
- She may be shy when meeting new people, but she has impeccable manners - not a jumper
- She is learning her house manners - she likes being on the couch which is fine in her foster home, but she may have to be trained otherwise in her adoptive home. She is very agile and has jumped up to get food from the table. She is learning quickly that is is not acceptable in her foster home. 
- She is generally quiet. She will alert at random times but it's few and far between.
- She is learning to trust humans more thoroughly and quickly, and her fosters are consciously socializing her to help her build confidence. She would rather people kneel down to pet her instead of looming over her. She gets nervous if someone comes up behind her too quickly and can startle if she is bumped into by accident. I think she needs more work on trusting humans in general. She shows no reactivity or aggression, but retreats to her crate if she feels overwhelmed. 
- She loves to run around in the backyard. She loves to play with other dogs. She seems to be a moderate energy dog and she is still trying to figure out how it all works inside a home.
- She loves to play with other dogs.
- She has not been exposed to cats, but her foster thinks she could do well with a confident cat. She's tried to go after squirrels on walks and birds get her attention.
- She will do best with a patient adoptive home where they can continue to show her that humans are a good thing and being apart of a family is where it's at. Possibly someone with another confident dog to help her to continue to gain confidence in a home.

This dog tested positive for Anaplasmosis before arriving to the rescue. Anaplasmosis is a very common type of bacteria that infects dogs and other species and is spread by ticks. Anaplasmosis is not contagious to humans or other pets. The only way to get this disease is to be bitten by a tick that carries it. The treatment is typically 21-30 days of antibiotics. This dog started treatment upon arriving to the rescue.

Operation Paws for Homes, Inc. (OPH) rescues dogs of all breeds and ages from high-kill shelters in NC, VA, MD, and SC, reducing the numbers being euthanized. With limited resources, the shelters are forced to put down 50-90% of the animals that come in the front door. OPH provides pet adoption services to families located in VA, DC, MD, PA and neighboring states. OPH is a 501(c)(3) organization and is 100% donor funded. OPH does not operate a shelter or have a physical location. We rely on foster families who open their homes to give love and attention to each dog before finding a forever home.

LOVELY personality! Sweet, friendly, out-going, fun personality, super-loving, 'social butterfly', happy, healthy and gentle. EXCELLENT with kids! Crate trained, rides well, walks well on-leash, gets along well with all dogs and older respectful & responsible children (must be 10y+). LOVES being with her people, but can allow her 'social butterfly' to emerge if not supervised OR if she becomes bored while outdoors unsupervised/person goes out gate...she wants to be with her person! Once outside, she will go exploring...not far, but ANY distance is too far, given this sometimes crazy world we live in.

NOT a good match for older seniors.

We will be happy to send you more pix & videos, upon request.

BEWARE! SKY is an 'escape artist'...she WILL climb chain-link & welded-wire fencing(anything she can get a foothold into). Therefore, we are seeking a stay/work-at-home person/walk on leash ONLY situation OR a home with a wooden/vinyl stockade fence with buried reinforcement wire(EXPERIENCED BEAGLE PEOPLE WILL UNDERSTAND!). She just wants to be with her PEEPS!

MUST have a secured fenced-in backyard (NO ELECTRIC FENCES=these are NOT compatible for scent hounds!) OR past INSIDE beagle experience and a regular walking/running/hiking regime and be committed to an 'ON-LEASH ONLY' exercise regime. Homes with children are REQUIRED to have a vinyl/stockade fenced-in backyard...NO EXCEPTIONS!

This pup is in & will remain in foster care in Rutherfordton, NC until her fur-ever home is approved.

Transport is available via 3 Rescued Pet transport svcs and their fees are: $125 from western NC to as far N as Long Island and Vince Lombardi svc plaza/NJTnpk, and $140 to all points along the I-95 corridor as far as ManchesterNH/BurlingtonVT & Albany/RochesterNY. Stops include: DC, MD, DEL, NJTnpk, RyeNY, JohnstonRI and ManchesterNH/BurlingtonVT, Albany & RochesterNY, & Allentown and CarlislePA on I-81.

Adoption fee: $175(includes spay, micro-chip, current health certificate, parasite-free, utd on 1st yr vax(Bordatella, Rabies, Parvo-Distemper & Lepto), all medical paperwork from day#1 at Howlin4Spirit(+ past shelter's records), beef knee cap bone, KONG or Nylabone chew toy, 1/2 gallon bag current dry food(Tractor Supply Store's '4health'-salmon & potato), 2 'pet alert' wallet cards, new Martingale collar and matching 6' leash, 'RESCUED DOGS ROCK' car magnet and 'SUPER PUPPY-The Best Dog You'll Ever Have' training booklet).

To apply to adopt this lovely little sweetie, please copy and paste the application in to a new email, complete all questions(the more detailed, the better your chances of being approved), and email to: howlin4spirit@gmail.com. MAKE SURE you provide us with EMAIL ADDRESSES for your 3 personal references and let them know we will be sending them a short questionnaire within 1 business day. Also, you will need to give your vet's office permission to release your pet's medical history to us, when we call them within 1 business day.

IF you rent, you will need to provide your property manager's contact info. We will be contacting them within 1 business day.

Thank you, for reaching out to a rescued pup in need of love, respect and a warm, safe place to call 'home'. We look forward to helping you find the right pup for you, your family, environment and habits, for a life-time of snuggling, unconditional love and adventures.

name: MADIGAN WAGS -RECOVERING FROM HER  PREVIOUS LIFE
description:
8/25/19

Hi! My name is Madigan, or you can call me Maddie. People say Iâm a pocket pit. Iâm about 38 lbs and 3 years old, so I donât really fit in your pocket, but Iâm smaller than most pit bulls. 
I had a rough start before I came up to PA. The people at Wags that rescued me say that I was most likely used as a bait dog, and then I was hit by a car! Can you believe it? But, oh how my luck has changed. Iâm living in a foster home and I love it! I have toys and chews and blankets and lots of treats. I love meeting and seeing people. I wag my tail and give kisses and they pet me. Itâs a win -win!
Now Iâm looking for my forever home. I like some dogs but I would probably be best as an only dog. If you have another dog, I would need to meet them slowly as I am a little particular, but with my past, do you blame me? Iâve never lived with cats but I could get tested to see how I do with them. 
I love my toys, especially the squeaky ones. I will play with them every day. I have so much fun playing I donât realize how excited I am and I might be a little too much for young children. Teens and up should be ok. I do well on leash with a harness but if you have a fenced in yard I think I would love playing outside. 
My foster mom puts me in a crate when she goes to work. Sometimes I bark when she first leaves but I donât carry on for long. And I havenât had any accidents in the crate. Iâm pretty good around the house. I like to find shoes and chew on them but I am getting better with correction. 
If you would like to meet me, please submit an application and your processsor can get you in touch with my foster mom. Bully breed criteria applies. 


7/23/19

Madigan (Maddie) is approx. 3 yrs old, a spayed Female petite pit mix. She was brought to PA from NC recovering from a broken pelvis, a CCL repair and an infection. She has recovered well and is feeling much better and is now looking for her forever home.  Maddie is very people friendly, adults and kids. However, she appears to be dog selective. She was known to be good friends with a Pom/Peke in training but does not appear to like some dogs. 
Maddie loves to be by her person's side and is getting more playful. She likes soft toys, chewies and antlers.  She has not been cat tested, but likes to chase rabbits and squirrels on our walk. She enjoys walks and will potty on walk or in backyard. 
It is believed that Maddie is a survivor from dog fights. She has some scratches and scrapes, but they donât bother her. She thinks they add to her charm and beauty. 
Maddie is crated while her foster is at work. She will cry and bark for about 10 minutes at first but then settles down. 


5/9/19

Madigen 

Madigen is our baby girl. She is approximately 3 years old and weighs 28lbs. Madigen came to Camp Chester on crate rest due to having her CCL and her fractured pelvis repaired after being hit by a car. She has recently been cleared for active duty and has been slowly learning to play again. Madigen is housebroken, crate trained, loves kids, could care less about cats, and LOVES ALL PEOPLE. She is so tiny you may be able to rock her like a baby, which is what she likes when she watches TV with you. As with all dogs, with slow introductions she has been accepting and playing nice. She loves playing with our resident dog Elsa, who is a 8 pound princess. 

Madigen has a very busy schedule here in Camp Chester, and it has been hard to interrupt her bust schedule for an updated photo shoot so stand by for pictures. 

So what exactly is âCamp Chesterâ? 

Camp Chester OR Wags at Chester WAGs at Chester is an institutional program that pairs incarcerated individuals with dogs to work on basic obedience, house training and socialization. Specifically, all the dogs work really hard to pass our Canine Good Citizenship Test! The Canine Good Citizen Program is a two-part program that stresses responsible pet ownership for owners and basic good manners for dogs. Every dog that arrives at Camp Chester, is given individual attention based on their needs, as every need is different.

Please call Colleen @ 267-238-7892 or Susan @ 267-312-3372. To begin the adoption process please, please fill out our online application. 

Go to wagsrescue.com and click on adoption form. After you complete the application, you will be taken to PayPal so you can submit the $25.00 application fee. Thank you!

name: Chevy
description: Chevy is a young male Akita who comes to us from small shelter in NC. He is a sweet fellow. He will be neutered and vetted prior to adoption. He will be available once we learn more about him. He is currently boarded in LaGrange, NC. Apply on our website for more information.

name: Georgia Pups
description:
This litter is 12 weeks old and we have 2 boys (Remy & Francis) and 2 girls (Lilou & Stella). They came from a hoarding case in GA and are now being fostered in Charlotte, NC. They have acclimated well into their foster homes and they do not seemed phased by loud noises , new dogs or new people. They are a very confident bunch that love to play and have lots of energy! We are working on house and crate training and they are coming along. They did come in with UTI's and have intestinal worms but are on meds for those. They love to rough house and play and are very social babies!

** If interested in these babies you can email us at info@greatdanefriends.com Only homes with giant breed experience will be considered for any of our dogs 1 year and younger. We also do not adopt siblings out together **

Please contact Great Dane Friends (info@greatdanefriends.com) for more information about this pet.

*****Great Dane Friends of Ruff Love covers NC and surrounding states for adoptions. We require a fenced yard (exceptions made on a case by case basis - NO exceptions for puppies or deaf/vision impaired dogs - no invisible fencing), that stairs in the home be covered with some sort of slip resistant material to prevent injury, that all other animals in the home be up to date on vaccinations as well as spayed/neutered and that all dogs live inside as a part of the family. Our approval process consists of an application, vet and reference checks, phone interview and house check. Please email us for an application or if you have any questions.*****

name: Rowdy
description:
I am a beautiful boy with a heavy multi colored coat . My sister Muffin is here with me but has a short coat.  Maybe I take after my mother who is a Chow Chow and Muffin takes after our Daddy who is unknown but must be colored like me.

 We both lacked cartilage in our joints when we were born, probably due to our mother not having the proper nutrition when she was pregnant with us. But we are so much better now because our rescue mama has found medicine and a new food with things that we need and we can both run now without hurting our knees. We are able to go on walks but not jog. 

We are considered Senior dogs because on August 31st 2019 we will be 8 years old. But I act like I'm still a puppy.  My mama says the reason we have not been adopted is because we act afraid of people we don't know. I can't help it, I still remember being born under a strange house in the dirt and a man coming and taking two of my sisters away. One must have died because we were only 3 weeks old and he brought the other one back (Muffin). That is when my rescue mamas came and got my entire litter, my mother, and another dog that \"hung around\" with us.

If you might think of adopting me, you would have to give me time to get to know you. Then I would become your \"Sweetie Boo\" like my mama calls me! If you think you would like to give me a chance, email my mama at sunsetanimalrescue@yahoo.com and ask for a SAR questionnaire. Complete and email back. Be sure to tell the references that they will be calling so they will be expecting the call. After talking with your references and learning your history with animals, your will come and meet me. And we will decide if we click. We are located in Winnsboro, SC which is 27 miles from Columbia, SC and 70 miles from Charlotte, NC. I am waiting for my forever home still.

name: Fred Bladen
description:
Meet Fred! Fred is a 2 year old Hound mix from NC. Fred found himself as a stray and ended up at the county shelter. Eleventh Hour Rescue saw him and now he is restarting his life in NJ. He is a sweet boy who gets along with other dogs. Life on the streets was hard for Fred who had to fight for the resources to survive. As a result, he can guard his food from fear of losing it and for this reason should not be in a home with small children. BUT he is an absolutely wonderful dog who just needs some time and patience to learn that he's no longer living in a world where everything is at risk of being taken away from him. He is a doll to every single person he meets.

Fred loves his crate and completely relaxes once he is inside it. He loves other dogs but doesn't quite have all his manners so would need a dog who tolerates \"puppy like\" playing behaviors!

If you would like to meet with Fred, be sure to go to our website, EHRDOGS.ORG, and fill out an application. Don't forget to mention his name, FRED BLADEN!

name: Shyla
description:
Shyla is a very sweet young girl who loves attention and dog treats.  At first she can be shy but she quickly becomes affectionate.  She loves having a dog friend to play with, so we hope to find her a forever home with another dog,  and she's great around cats as well as children.   Shyla is crate trained. 

This sweet girl has overcome some big obstacles in her short life.  She was removed from a hoarding situation in NC,  brought to a kill shelter,  rescued by or group,  and spent many months im a foster home as a semi feral dog. She was terrified of humans, and all of her siblings were adopted long before she came around.  If you meet Shyla now,  you'll never believe this story because she's that sweet and kongs for affection.  

If you'd like to meet Shyla in her foster home i. Piscataway,  NJ,  please send an email to jerseygirlsanimalrescue@gmail.com for an adoption application.

name: Buck
description: Buck, Male, black lab/mix, 55 lbs, 1 yr old, still very much puppy. I rescued Buck from a shelter in NC.  He's up to date on his shots, neutered, and heartworm neg and on prevention. He's a very friendly boy, very smart.  He rode pretty nicely with having a seat belt harness and tether on in the car.  He gives lots of kisses. I learned that Buck has separation anxiety, I will try to use a crate to see how that goes, but he certainly can't be left alone at home, free to roam. This boy would make an AWESOME dog for someone who suffers from PTSD that needs a companion animal to take everywhere with them. He is smart, friendly, loves everyone and all dogs, he's just a great boy who needs some training, but I think he could pick things up quickly,  I'm asking $200.00 to adopt. His tail never stops wagging. Oh and he likes cats and kids too!!!!  If you'd like to adopt Buck, please email me at ess4us@ptd.net or for more info call me at 570-773-3077. THANKS for looking! He loves to go swimming, but will not retrieve!!! But he loves the water and he listens well off leash if you like to go hiking, or for walks where he can run free.

name: Tina
description:
Tina was rescued from NC just before Hurricane Florence hit - she actually made it out just one day before the storm.  She's a sweet, middle aged girl of about 4 or 5 who is slow to warm up and enjoys  human companionship.  She's medium sized and weighs about 50-55 lbs, is spayed and vaccinated,  housebroken and crate trained, although she doesn't need to be crated.   

Tina's issue is that,  sometime in her past, another dog or dogs weren't so nice to her and she is fearful.  Her defense is showing aggression towards other dogs.  She could successfully be walked on a leash in a park or neighborhood where there are other dogs,  and she walks very well on a leash,  but she will do best not having to closely interact with other dogs.  She,  therefore,  needs to be an only dog. She is a low-key, low maintenance  dog and will make her person or family very happy.  She also loves belly rubs!! 

If you'd like to meet Tina and get an application to adopt her,  please send an email to jerseygirlsanimalrescue@gmail.com.

name: Diesel
description:
Diesel is a year old Dobie/rottie mix with a heart of gold. Diesel came to us from a shelter in NC where he was picked up as a stray. He had some minor injuries, perhaps from a car. Diesel is very low key, to the point of couch potato status, but will chase and hurt small, black animals. Heâs ok with small and larger dogs but I wouldnât put him in a cat home. Diesel loves to play outside, especially chasing birdâs shadows. He will play with the other dogs in a slow motion fashion, he is funny too watch. I believe he would be good with dog savvy children.

ADOPTION FEE $150

This Doberman is available for adoption through Volunteer State Doberman Rescue.  Please visit our website at www.vsdr.org to fill out an adoption application.

name: Ace
description:
Ace is a young (born 2.18.18) neutered male Akita. He is up to date on vaccines, microchipped, on flea/heartworm prevention, house trained, leash, and crate trained.

Ace came to us from a shelter in NC where he was surrendered by his owner. That is about all we know of the beginning of his life. He is a very sweet boy who just needs some polishing on his manners. He loves people, but maybe too rambunctious for small children. We are still assessing his social skills with other dogs.

name: ELSA
description: I'm Elsa, a STUNNING dogo argentino. I'm SUPER fearful with strangers, in fact, my name came from Elsa in \"Frozen\" because at the NC animal control I was rescued from I was SO terrified that I didn't move a muscle the whole time I was there. When I know you, I'm an attention hog who LOVES a good belly rub! I'm a great leash walker, love to play with big male dogs who are active and playful...I LOVE LOVE LOVE the pool! I am VERY protective of \"my\" person, and need a VERY experienced and responsible owner with NO kids. My \"perfect\" home would be a hermit who wants ME as their only friend! description:
Kazu
Akita mix
Neutered male, fully vaccinated, heartworm negative
5 years old, 100 lbs
Meet sweet, gentle Kazu rescued from Warren County, NC! He's a 5 year old Akita mix, neutered, up-to-date on all his vaccines and heartworm negative. Kazu is about 100 lbs, gets along well with other dogs, just very docile and submissive. He's housebroken, crate trained and doesn't destroy anything even when he's left in a room by himself! Kazu is a sweetheart who is content to just rest his head on your feet.  But if you're up for a walk, he's quite good on a leash and very eager to please. He makes an outstanding companion and will be a wonderful family member. Please email littlepups2017@gmail.com or call 757-630-6181 after 5:00 p.m. weekdays if you are interested in adopting Kazu!

name: Elsa
description: I'm Elsa, a STUNNING dogo argentino. When I know you, I'm an attention hog who LOVES a good belly rub! I'm a great leash walker,  love to play with other big dogs who are active, strong, and playful...I LOVE LOVE LOVE the pool (and I HATE HATE HATE the rain!) The perfect home for me would be a very experienced ONE or TWO person adult home, I can either be an only dog, or a compatible large MALE dog is great too...AND I MUST have a yard with a 6 ft fence, and a pool-even just a plastic pool, I'm not picky! For more info, CALL (757) 432-9222.

name: Reese
description:
Reese
was due to be put down within hours of being pulled from a shelter in NC in April 2012. She was heartworm positive and very sick. She is completely healthy now and microchipped, spayed, and up-to-date on vaccinations. She is around 5 years old and about 40 lbs. She is dog reactive and would benefit from training to help her overcome her fear of other dogs. She has not been around cats, so we're not sure how she would act. Reese has been around children ages 2-17 years and does fine with them. However, we probably would not recommend a home with small children because she does have a lot of energy. She tends to jump up on people, which we are working on. She is crate and house trained. Reese needs to go a home with a family who is active because she loves to run with her foster mom. She does well on a leash. She loves to play, but also loves to cuddle. Reese is a survivor and looking for her forever family.

If you are that special, active family, please call Esther or Dallas at 757-583-8777 or e-mail rainbowanimalrescue@cox.net.

name: Chop
description:
Meet Chop! Chop is a great boy that has stolen all of our hearts here! This ray of sunshine is always happy, he loves people, and wants nothing more than a home that will love, snuggle, and play with him! He has had quite the journey to get to Sarl so he can find his furever home. If you would like to read about Chop's heartwarming journey from Florida to New Hampshire please check out the link below to read his story. You will need to copy and paste the link as a new web address. 

https://www.eagletribune.com/news/new_hampshire/saved-from-death/article_d869edbc-522b-5b80-a539-94e2433ed8a7.html

Chop loves to play and is a very energetic and enthusiastic player, so he should go with children aged 10 and up who are not easily knocked down. Chop could potentially go with children as young as 8 years old as long as the family is dog savvy and understands he may jump up and become mouthy. 
Additionally, the adopter of Chop should recognize that Chop is partially blind due to retinal atrophy and can become spooked if he can't see someone walking towards him. Usually calling his name and talking to him does the trick. Once he hears his name and your voice he will look for you. Once he finds you, watch out! He will bombard you will lots of slobbery kisses and will try to sit in your lap! :) He just has so much love to give and really needs a family to share it with.
This boy will make an amazing addition to his new family! If you would like to meet this sweet boy, come down to Salem Animal Rescue League during adoption hours! www.salemanimalrescueleague.org or contact laurelsilvia@comcast.net. Chop is currently in Salem NH.

name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home. 

If you are interested in adopting or fostering Winter, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Murry Murdoch da Tank!
description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch?

name: Lakota Mato (Bear)
description:
Lakota is a 2-year-old boy born July 2017 who came to us from a shelter where his previous owners dumped him. He was purchased as a puppy and lived most of his life outside. He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

Lakota would do best in a home with no young children. He did well when seeing other dogs on walks and we will continue to work with him and see how he does with a female companion. He is super smart and knows how to sit. He had us fooled in the beginning but he will sit now nicely when asked (a treat helps) and he will need continued positive training to be the best pup he can be.

name: Apollo the White Knight
description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature.

name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

name: Maddie \Cutie Patootie!\","Maddie is our little Miss Cutie Patootie! She is a short and stocky malamute girl with so much personality. She...
description:
Maddie is our little Miss Cutie Patootie! She is a short and stocky malamute girl with so much personality. She is guaranteed to make you smile every day with her paw up for high fives and zoomies. Maddie was born October 2011. She is easy and independent. She is called a little miss spit fire, because she is a tough little cookie! She is sassy and all malamute. She enjoys being in her crate and doesn't make a peep. Or hanging outside watching everyone and everything. She also enjoys hiking and just loves the outdoors! She is also happy just laying around on her doggy bed and just being in the same room as you. Don't let that adorable teddy bear look fool you, she isn't a cuddler and prefers her space, EXCEPT when salmon treats are involved. She will come right up to you, give you high fives and show so much excitement for treat time! Just give her space and time to get to know you. She had a very rough life and is hesitant to trust people. Despite this, she sits nicely to put her collar on before going on a walk. She also rides well in car but generally speaking, Maddie doesn't just do things willingly, which is why positive training works well for her. KronchUSA salmon treats really help us encourage Maddie to make good choices. She likes to protest a little bit just enough so she feels like she had a choice.  

She will roll over for belly rubs and come up to you for some love but when shes had enough she will leave and go about her business. She was potty trained at one time but will need a refresher. She does not like other dogs but can be around them. If given the chance she will let other dogs know she is boss and that's why we recommend her as being the only dog in the home. When you are out on a walk she won't get upset seeing another dog as long as they are behaving. She isn't dog aggressive but won't back down from a challenge either. 

In May 2017, Maddie had ACL surgery on her right knee and is doing well. Of note, she was debarked as a pup so she doesn't have her 'woowoo' but don't let that stop you from giving this girl her second chance. She needs a home with Northern Breed experience. She has a strict limited ingredient diet --- salmon only protein and fat. Typical malamute she cannot be around small dogs or pets including cats.

description:
Born in August 2014, Bucky has a great sense of humor and is full of personality.  He would love to be your hiking companion followed by a picnic with a chicken sandwich. He LOVES car rides and visiting the nearby pet stores where all the goodies are. Bucky is a very social Malamute/Husky mix and would love a family of his own. He is a free spirit who responds beautifully to pawsitive communication. He enjoys chasing and burying balls (especially squeaky balls) and really enjoys going out on hikes exploring. He has separation anxiety and would do best in a home with a stay at home human. He is an amazing boy with high predatory behavior that can spot any critter or find deer. With cheerful redirection, he will give up the chase to stay with his human.

Bucky is always ready for an adventure but we believe he is trying to find his furever home. Bucky will behave so well, then out of the blue it's like he has to celebrate being good and will surprise you with the fastest zoomies!  However, this is far and few these days. He enjoys just being where you are & hanging out. He has been receiving positive training and has learned to redirect his excitement by sitting for a treat and sitting so the car door opens for an adventure. Most recently he is learning to relax, which he enjoys with chicken sandwich bite size rewards. Bucky looks like a very tall Siberian Husky. Bucky would benefit from pawsitive reinforcement training classes and someone with a good sense of humor. Bucky just wants to have fun, so learning how to communicate being consistent & calm works great for Bucky, especially with a soft yummy treat. 

With so much to give, he definitely will make someone happy once he settles in and knows he's loved. He prefers to be the only pet in the home...who doesn't like to be the star of the show?!?!  We recommend reading, Positive Perspectives 2 - Know your Dog Train your Dog by Pat Miller.  This book will open your eyes from a dogs perspective & help you communicate & train in a pawsitive manner.  To know Bucky is to love Bucky. He is such a sweet boy who is searching for his furever home & hooman. Those who meet Bucky can't believe that he hasn't been adopted.

name: Rainier
description:
Some of the most treasured places in America are the National Parks. At MatchDog Rescue, we are celebrating these fascinating places with a transport of pups named after our phenomenal parks. Just like the National Parks, each dog is unique and beautiful, to be treasured and admired. All of our pups are waiting to be discovered by you! Come out on October 5, 2019 and find your \"furever\" friend. Your adventure awaits!!

You don't have to travel all the way to Washington State to see this handsome guy! Meet Rainier- he is a 22 pound, two year old shepherd mix with a white body that will remind you of the snow capped mountains. Shepherds are loyal, highly trainable and have caring temperaments. Rainier is a friendly and happy pup,he just might be the sweetest dog you've ever met!Shepherds are very protective of people they love- will you be one of them? Rainier is 85 percent house trained and crate trained. He will be making the long climb from Texas to New Jersey soon so, if he sounds like the guy for you, fill out an application today.

If you think you are a perfect match for Rainier, please complete an application fully: https://www.petstablished.com/adoption_form/11415/generic

Rainier has been fully vetted, is up to date on all vaccinations and on preventatives for heartworm, flea and tick. We cannot guarantee breed information. You will find the price guidelines for adoption at matchdogrescue.org and can read about the whole adoption process and what MatchDog Rescue provides with each dog.

This gorgeous MatchDog is not yet in the state of N.J. and currently in our MatchPad in the great state of Texas. This dog will be going on a three-day road trip arriving to us here in N.J. on Sat, October 5th at Marlton PetSmart. For the very best chance of securing a meet for this dog on arrival in N.J you must be available all day on this date.

If you see a pending notification on this dog and the picture changed to black and white, it means we have informed the lucky family selected as the best match for this particular dog and they have agreed to come to the transport event as the dog arrives. Eventually go to their forever home. If for any reason this plan falls through, we will change the picture back to color and revisit other applications.

name: Dexter
description: Dexter is looking for his furever home through Blue Ridge Bull Terrier Rescue! Dexter and his adorable floppy ear came into rescue from a New Jersey shelter. He was originally found as a stray and was adopted out from the shelter and, sadly, returned. He has now has been turned over to rescue so he can find his perfect furever home once and for all. Dexter is such a happy boy who is guaranteed to put a grin on your face! He has a very high energy level and is always on the move. He enjoys going for car rides, on long walks or running around a fenced yard, but most of all he LOVES to play with toys! He will play fetch or tug with his humans, but is perfectly happy entertaining himself by tossing the ball and chasing it down on his own. He lives for squeakers! Dexter is very smart and inquisitive. He knows how to sit and give his paw, and should pick up on new tricks quickly if someone were to spend the time with him; he loves cookies. Dexter also has a calm, sweet, and loving side, curling up on the couch for a good cuddle session. Due to his rambunctious energy level, kids in his home should be ages 10+. Dexter is reactive to other dogs and will need to be the only pet in his home. No dogs, cats, or critters. Dexter is a gentleman in the home; he is crate trained, housebroken, and nondestructive. He is a healthy boy who weighs in at 60lbs, is neutered, up to date on his vaccines, heartworm negative, and microchipped. He currently enjoys a grain-free diet. We have absolutely fallen in love with this guy. His floppy ear, paired with his soulful eyes will pull you in and melt your heart. If you are ready for the new love of your life to join your family, please apply here: https://www.brbtc.org/adoption-process/  Dexter is currently fostered in Hartsville, SC, but transport is available for the right home.

name: Muffin
description: Woof, woof, Muffin here! I'm originally from North Carolina but have found my way up to New Jersey just to meet you! I am an energetic girl, but am happy to take a rest break. I love people and other dogs - enjoy making new friends. My wish is your command! Come on over to St. Hubert's in Madison NJ to meet me in person, or call 973-377-2295. Primary Color: Black Secondary Color: Tan Weight: 49lbs Age: 1yrs 2mths 1wks Animal has been Spayed

name: Clyde Lonestar*
description: Clyde is a sweet guy who would love a forever home with another dog. He's good with other dogs. His best bud is Jack LoneStar. Clyde is quiet and calm. He warms up slowly to new people. Clyde recently made the trip from Texas to New Jersey, and he is loving life in his foster home! Apply to adopt CLYDE LONESTAR at www.EHRDOGS.org!

name: Lady Beaufort
description:
This Southern Belle has traveled all the way from South Carolina to find her forever home here in New Jersey. When you meet Lady it is obvious that she did at one time have a home where someone taught her the commands that she knows and how to play her favorite game of \"fetch\".

Lady has been in foster since 1/7/18. She has been a perfect houseguest, is completely house and crate trained. She goes right into her crate every morning when I leave for work and is sleeping when I get home. Lady loves her person, loves cuddling and to be pet. She is a calm dog that loves her toys and a good nap on the couch. On walks she doesn't pay attention to other dogs and walks calmly next to them when on pack walks. We do not know much about Lady's past, but she does scare easily, so she would do best in a calm household with older, respectful children, and not much traffic in and out of the house. She takes a while to warm up to new people but once she does she loves you. Lady is a very special girl that deserves a loving home of her own. She is silly, full of personality and one the sweetest dogs I've ever had the pleasure of fostering. She is so easy to love and will make a wonderful addition to the right household.

If you want to meet Lady go to EHRDOGS.ORG and submit an application. Don't forget to ask for LADY BEAUFORT - she is waiting so patiently at the kennel for someone to fall in love with her and bring her home. Could that someone be you?

name: Eliza
description: Time, patience and yummy treats is the winning combination for Eliza. Because she is shy and fearful, the best way to become her friend is to sit quietly in her room while offering her treats and letting her decide when she wants to approach you. Born in 2015, she came to Best Friends from a shelter in New Mexico. She is at her best when there are other confident, friendly dogs around to help her feel braver. When there are a lot of unfamiliar dogs and people coming and going close by, it is stressful for her. At Dogtown, Eliza is working on learning to trust through hand feeding. She is also working on leash walking, which she enjoys. Eliza is looking for a calm and understanding person or family. A quiet home with a predictable routine and other dogs who can help build her confidence would be best for her. She is considered a flight risk, so she'll need a secure space and someone who can watch over her and keep her safe while she learns about the world.

name: Fenway
description: Fenway is eager to be brave and loves to learn new things. She's shy and fearful with strangers at first but is working on her confidence. She loves water, so in the summer she sits in her baby pool for a good portion of the day. Because she also loves all things soft and fluffy, she likes to collect her blankets in one big pile to sleep on. Born in 2016, Fenway is a distemper survivor. She came to Best Friends from a shelter in New Mexico as a puppy mom. She loved playing with her puppies, and she now enjoys playing with other adult dogs. She also loves to do agility with her doggie roommate and will follow him around the agility course. She would do great in a home with another friendly dog who could help show her the ropes and help boost her confidence. Fenway is currently doing a lot of confidence and trust training at the Sanctuary. She is a willing learner, especially if you reward her with yummy treats, and she is learning that new people, walks and car rides are all good things. She has already picked up on leash walking and is learning basic training cues such as 'sit' and 'down.' Fenway would do best in a home with a person or family who understands shy dogs and can give her time to adjust and progress at her own pace. She is looking for someone who can give her a little guidance and show her that the world can be a fun and safe place.

name: Lotti
description: Lotti is one happy, energetic girl. Born in 2012, she loves running around with her toys and swimming in her pool. Lotti came to Best Friends from the animal welfare department of New Mexico. She can be a bit picky and in-your-face with her dog friends, so she'll need a home where she can either be the only dog or have a tolerant canine companion. Super smart and people-loving, Lotti is ready to learn about life in a forever home. Lotti is currently on a special diet and medication for environmental allergies. Lotti has a generous sponsor who will pay for her adoption fee.

name: Thor
description: Thor is a strikingly handsome boy with a full-body wag. He always has a smile on his face, and his silly antics often make his caregivers at the Sanctuary laugh. He is super smart and loves training. Thor will quickly show you his array of tricks he knows, including high five, down, shake, touch, and is always wanting to learn more! Born in 2009, he still has lots of life and love to give. Thor does prefer to live with female doggie friends. Thor came to Best Friends from a shelter in New Mexico. He's been working hard with Dogtown caregivers and trainers and is ready to find a home of his own.

name: Legend
description:
Meet LEGEND!!!
This handsome pup just arrived from a reservation in New Mexico, and is now searching for his forever home! Legend is a 12-week-old shepherd mix, currently fostered in Aurora, CO. name: Lemon
description:
My name is Lemon, I am available for adoption through Colorado Canine Rescue (CCR) - a nonprofit dog rescue located in the Denver area. My vet and foster mom have guessed that I am around 2 years old and an American Pit Bull Terrier or \"pit bull-type dog.\" I was rescued from an overcrowded shelter in New Mexico. I will be available to adopt/go home after July 5th. I am currently completing a board and train program through High Drive Dog Company in Longmont, Colorado. Part of my adoption requirements include follow up training with High Drive (sponsored by CCR for 3 months), no other animals in the home, no children under 12, and no cities with BSL (breed specific legislation). It is preferred I am adopted to a home with a 6 foot wooden fence. These requirements are non-negotiable. Lemon would do best living with someone who has bully breed experience. Lemon weighs around 60 pounds, is crate trained, and doing well with housetraining. She can be vocal when she needs something, and is not appropriate for apartment/condo living.

Lemon had a rough start to life; being kenneled 24/7 for 2 months straight prior to arriving in Colorado was a lot of stress. Lemon has worked through a lot of reactivity issues. She actually plays well with a lot of dogs. She is NOT a candidate for dog parks. However, she is always welcome to attend supervised playgroups at High Drive (please see http://www.highdrivedogco.com/ for more details about the company). Lemon is not a coach potato. She is bold, eager to learn, and ready to take on the world. Lemon needs to be challenged physically and mentally. She is funny and affectionate. This pup may have started out as a lemon, but she is quite a peach.

If you are interested in adopting Lemon, please submit an application located on our website, www.coloradocaninerescue.org. We are asking for a $200.00 adoption donation. Lemon is spayed, up to date on vaccinations, and micro-chipped. Please note, CCR cannot guarantee the breed composition or ages of our dogs as we usually have no history prior to them entering the shelter. In addition, most dogs listed as potty trained will experience an adjustment period as they learn the routines in their new home.

name: Winnie: medical hold (NY)
description:
Winnie is diabetic and is currently on medical hold while she gets her insulin stabilized. She is being fostered in NY state. 

What we know about Winnie:
*sweet
*loves to be with people
*prefers her space with other dogs
*housebroken
*sleeps through the night

What Winnie's foster mom has to say about Winnie:
Who's that girl with the golden waves? It's Winnie! Winnie is a beautiful terrier mix. She's about 7 years old, and she's already quite the traveler! Winnie came to BDRA from a shelter in New Mexico, and she charmed hearts all the way from New Mexico to New York!

Winnie loves her people with all that she has. Her perfect day is a day spent with her person, giving cuddles and kisses and getting belly rubs. She tries very hard to be a good girl.

Winnie wants to be with her people at all times. She'll follow you from room to room, and will lay happily at your feet or in your lap as you work or watch TV. Sometimes she follows me so closely she actually steps on my feet. She can also be timid and submissive, and if she thinks she's in your way, she will do her best to avoid you.

Winnie has late immature cataracts, but has functional vision at this time. As her vision declines, she may be a candidate for cataract surgery. She receives eye drops every 12 hours and is an angel! She also has Anisocoria, which means her pupils are two different sizes. This does not affect her now, but will need to be regularly monitored. She is housebroken and sleeps quietly through the night.

Winnie can be tolerant of the other dogs (all males) and cats (one male, one female) in her foster home and may even sleep next to one, but more often, she does not like when another dog or cat gets too close to her. She'll give a warning growl, and if the dog doesn't move away, she will lunge. It does not escalate further than that. Out of the four male dogs here, there is one dog she likes very much (a blind poodle mix).

Winnie is diabetic and came into rescue underweight. She has since gained several pounds and is even a bit overweight! As she was an untreated diabetic, her diabetes is still being regulated, and so she will remain on medical hold. 
Blind Dog Rescue Alliance has voted against the use of electric fencing effective immediately.

description:

description:
This little wild child is Sebastien! He loves getting the freedom to run and explore everything in sight! This sweet guy with his love for play can still be a bit shy to cuddling with new people but play some tug of war with him and he'll never want to leave your side! Sebastien had a long ride here from New Orleans after his old shelter got flooded from Hurricane Barry so he would love nothing more than to finally have a safe place to call home with people he can call family!

We require all members of the household to meet the new pet to ensure it's the best match for the family.

description: Cliff is a gentle, mellow giant who just wants to hang out with people and get lots of petting. He's easygoing and likes everyone he meets. Born in 2013, Cliff came to Best Friends from a shelter in New York. Never one to turn down a meandering stroll or a golf cart ride across Dogtown, Cliff truly does like to stop and smell the roses (ok, maybe sagebrush). Cliff also enjoys very sturdy toys and relishes his \"toy time\" with volunteers. He has allergies so he eats a prescription diet to control the food allergies and he takes allergy drops to help with the environmental allergies, as well as a few other medications and twice weekly baths. Cliff has had several play dates here at the sanctuary and seems to prefer female dogs. Because Cliff is a low-energy guy, he'd be the perfect dog for someone who wouldn't mind hanging out on the couch after taking a leisurely walk.

name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home.
