description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.

description:

He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature.

name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

description:
Sweet Mocha is a 6 year old Pit Bull who has come to our rescue all the way from Long Island in New York City!! Due to overcrowded kennels in the city poor Mocha was on the list to be euthanized. She was a favorite among the volunteers at the municipal shelter and they fought hard to find safety. After reaching out to dozens of no-kill shelters they finally found The Canine Rescue of Central PA and we were happy to make room for her!

description:

From his Mom:

Although he is 6 years old, Digby is still very much a young boy who has a lot of love and spunk left in him. He is a wonderful family dog and loves children, snacks, pets, and snuggles. He loves to eat and is very responsive to food as a reward for training. He does know several, tricks too!!

Sadly, like many other Pit Bulls, Digby does come with some emotional baggage. Since he was a rescue he has fear aggression issues only towards other dogs - never humans EVER - so he definitely would do great in a one-dog house unless someone has the patience to slowly introduce him into a home with another dog. We did it for 4 days at my in-law's house in Boston and by day 4 Digby was off leash and everyone was playing happily and he's lived peacefully with our Pickle dog since we got him.

Digby really is a wonderful family dog & we are hoping someone will give him a chance in a new family home. Digby is NOT with 11th Hour Rescue but we are helping his family with the rehoming process. If you would like to meet Digby or to get more info on him, please emailpalmares215@gmail.com or call Jennifer at 973 610 1201. Digby and his family are currently located in New York City.

description:

I always joke around saying her ball is her pacifier because she has it with her the majority of the day and can be found sleeping with one in her mouth.

Although she loves interacting with dogs outside of the dog park she has no interest in playing with them at the park because of her ball obsession. She also loves sleeping on the bed and loves to cuddle! She loves to curl up and be held at night and is a big fan of covers but she's also okay if you leave her on the couch.

Roo has lived with a small Chihuahua as I fostered one for a month and Roo seems to know her size with other dogs. She really wants to interact with cats as well when we pass them in the bodegas in NYC. She even knows which bodegas have them and stops and wags her tail watching and hoping they will one day come say hi. She's good with every person she's met and loves kids as well but does try to jump and give kisses when she's overly excited.

Roo is NOT with 11th Hour Rescue but we are helping her owner with the rehoming process. If you'd like to meet Roo, please contact Lauren by email at lauren.wise@compass.com or by phone at 917-699-2380 - Roo is currently located in New York City.

name: Fox
description:
Say hello to Fox - this handsome hound mix is approximately 11 years young. Fox's history is long and interesting. Once upon a time, he was part of a sprint racing sled dog team. Unfortunately, his owner passed from cancer a few years back which left Fox and several of his friends needing somewhere else to call home. Fox and his buddies made the trek from NY to NH and enjoyed being a member of our recreational touring kennel for a few years. Unfortunately and much to Fox's dismay, it was discovered that he had torn ACLs and for his safety and comfort shouldn't run too often. This newly retired sled dog is looking for a semi-active retirement home that will bring him on frequent walks and the occasional outdoor adventure. Fox gets along well with other dogs but would prefer a home without kiddos (they are a little overwhelming and make him a bit nervous). Fox is a sweet fella who would be happy to accompany you on daily errands or hang out with you on the couch enjoying the AC all summer long.


Things To Consider Before Inquiring:

- Our adoptable sleds dog are used to living in a traditional working kennel environment (ie: completely outdoors).This means that they will need to be house trained and exposed to house stimulus like stairs, cars, vacuums, wood floors, etc. Adopting an adult sled dog is similar to welcoming a puppy.

- Our adoptable sled dogs range from medium to high energy. In general they require multiple walks daily and engaging toys when inside the home. A bored/under exercised sled dog can be a destructive and anxious sled dog! 

- Our adoptable sled dogs are trained to run and are therefore in general are a high flight risk! We do require that they be on leash or within a fenced in yard at all times until proper recall training has been received. 

- While many of our adoptable sled dogs have befriended kitties in their new homes, we do not have cats at our facility to \"test\" them with. That being said, adopters are instructed to monitor all interactions with small animals as there is no telling how they may react.

name: Hermione
description:
Baby Hermione was dumped in the woods with her litter mates at 6 weeks old. Who does this stuff??? Terrible!  These are very lucky puppies. The woods is a very dangerous place for babies without their mother.  So, the first example of their luck started with two EMTs who discovered her and her siblings, have been loving them and will take care of her and her all eight of them until they are 12 weeks old. These EMTs truly knew how to care for them!  At 12 weeks they will have had their second vet visit including age appropriate shots/treatment which means they will be safe to travel from KY to NJ, arriving September 15.  She will not be housebroken at that time. She and her siblings are sweet, curious, playful and very ready to attach to a loving person or family. Some specs on their current weight will help determine adult weight, as for now they are small. The weight range for a medium sized adult dog is 26 to 60 pounds.  On 8/22 at 9 weeks old Jeanie was 11 pounds, Snape (male) 15.6 pounds, and Hermione 12.8 pounds.  It will be hard to predict their exact weights when full grown since we do not know either of the parents personally.  But their vet made some breed predictions. The rule for estimating weight is when it comes to medium and larger breeds, take their weight at 14 weeks and double it. Then add half of the original weight. (For instance, if your puppy weighs 25 pounds at 14 weeks, double this to 50 and then add 12.5 for an estimated adult weight of 62.5 pounds). They wonât be small dogs; some may be medium, or some large dogs. When they arrive at 12 weeks old they will of course be a little bigger than they are now but still little babies in need of love.  If you are looking for an elegant, fun, super good luck beagle/treeing walker coonhound please apply to adopt Hermione by visiting our website www.peace4paws.org

name: Maybe- SHY PUP
description:
Officially introducing our very special survivor Maybe!

This shy girl is still a puppy at heart, only about a year old and once she feels safe turns into a normal playful girl with her people and doggie friends!
She survived on her own on the streets of Philly for at least several months, hanging around a construction site where kind people fed her.  She was too scared to approach and had to be trapped by our new friends @ Team Louie Animal Rescue to get her to safety.  

Once in a temporary foster with someone who helped in her capture it quickly became evident she grew up with little to no human contact- she panicked on a leash or being touched and needed time and patience to learn to trust.  

We love our âferalâ project dogs at Second Chance and since coming to us her true funny personality has quickly emerged in her foster home with the help of her more confident dog friends.  She is quite the clown and loves to play with toys, wrestle, chase, and be chased by other dogs, and now even wags her tail and solicits petting from her foster mom!  While she still is scared of new people and places, she makes progress each day and we know in the right home she has so much potential.  

What does Maybeâs ideal home look like?  

A calmer adult household with just one or 2 patient people who can earn her trust and love.  At least one other playful dog her size or larger (45-50lbs) for her to play with and learn from. A securely fenced yard to ensure she never ends up on the run and fending for herself again. And someone who will love her and accept that while she may never be a social butterfly with strangers she has such a fun lovable personality if you are lucky enough to be in her inner circle of friends!

Email njwoof@cs.com to learn more about Maybe if you think maybe your home could be the right fit for her!

name: Ella
description:
This is the story of the E Litter. Their mother, Coco, was found alone, abandoned in Barnwell, South Carolina. It was clear that she had been nursing quite recently however, at the time, none of her puppies had been claimed nor found. A week after rescuing Coco, Home for Good Dog Rescue got a call stating that Coco's puppies, now known as the E Litter, had been found. They were found by a good samaritan in the insulation of a trailer, all malnourished and dehydrated. They are all very very lucky to be alive. Once this litter arrived at Home for Good's Aiken, SC property, they receive all the attention, love, and care, they so truly needed. Within no time, these pups were all nursed back to a clean bill of health and are now ready to find the forever homes they so truly deserve!

They are now about 2 months old, 10 pounds each and the cutest Labrador Retriever/Hound mixes. They are a very playful and outgoing bunch despite their rough start to life - it is clear that they are all so happy to be given a second chance! These pups love other dogs, cats, and children. They would make perfect family companions. In their foster homes, they have begun to work on their crate, leash, and house training. Now, all they need are forever families to call their own.

Ella is spayed, up-to-date on vaccinations, and microchipped.

name: Ryder
description: Ryder is your guy! He is approximately 2 years old and a Golden Retriever/Border Collie/Heeler mix-best guess. He is a beautiful strawberry blond and has a long lean body with a docked tail. He loves being part of a pack and gets along well with other dogs. He was found as a stray from the Ute reservation in Cortez, NM, and is so glad he caught his freedom ride to Colorado. This smart goofy guy rides well in the car and hopes to become your favorite adventure buddy. He can be a little reserved at first, but once he becomes comfortable, he is affectionate and enjoys shadowing your every move. Ryder is housebroken and does well in his crate, although he prefers to be outside or free roam in the house. name: Yahtzee
description: Yahtzee is a 10 year 29 pound beautiful fawn color Cocker Spaniel. CAWS pulled Yahtzee from a Valencia, NM shelter where he was found as a stray, and hitched a ride on a transport back to Utah. He arrived very sick and lethargic. Took him to the vet within a couple days and learned he had pneumonia and bad ear infections. He was placed in isolation for a few weeks to get over his illness and regain his strength. Once he was able to get out and be a part of the family pack, hes been thriving ever since. Our little man was a fighter who wanted to live and now be part of the good life! Yahtzee has had a dental with 12 extractions. He has arthritis in his back legs and hips so will be on pain medications for the rest of his life. Due to this arthritis he should be in a home with very minimal steps or none at all. Yahtzee can totally be trusted in the home when his 2 legged people arent home. He is dog door trained. He loves his 4 legged siblings, male and female, small and large. He doesnt sleep on the couch or bed, he prefers a bed on the floor. His sight isnt 100% but he sees enough to get around. His hearing might be a little less than stellar as well. He is a very nervous little man, he will pace at times and his legs shake with nervousness. Yahtzee will play with chew toys on the floor every once in a while and he loves to tear up empty paper towel and toilet paper rolls. With his big floppy ears he comes to share after hes had a drink by dragging his ears across you, so cute, well okay, really kind of not that cute, but it goes with the territory. He will need regular grooming. This precious and sweet little man is pure as they come. Now its his time to find his forever family that will show him the unconditional love he deserves! He will surely melt your heart. Due to Yahtzees nervousness he needs to go to a home with no children, or at least older. He also needs a home with a fenced yard and no stairs, or very minimal steps due to his arthritis in his back legs and hips. Yahtzee is not a barker, very occasional yap. name: Cassi
description: Amazing! Cassi and her sole surviving puppy were saved from a high kill shelter in North Carolina. She is indeed amazing in so many ways. As a lab/boxer mix she has a wonderful personality. She is good in any situation be it with other dogs, kids, walks, or rides in the car. (Okay, she does get nervous at the vet and doesnt like to have her nails clipped, but those are her only flaws).Cassi is only about a year old and displays a maturity you might not expect. She weighs around 57 pounds. She has a short coat that is a mix of brown and white. Lots of white on all four paws, a beautiful white chest, and a perfectly symmetrical face. She has those warm friendly brown eyes that let you know that she likes to be with people.She has been living in her southern foster home with three dogs and two kids. She gets along fine with her canine friends and LOVES the kids. Boxers are known for their legendary patience and gentleness with kids. Labs are known for their easy going friendliness, sweet-naturedness, and a desire to please. Cassi has inherited these wonderful traits making her a very desirable companion.Another plus is that Cassi is house, crate, and leash trained. (Of course, you know that even trained dogs may have an occasional accident as they adjust to the new family and routine). Cassi needs plenty of exercise as she is just beginning her teen years. A few walks a day, or play time with other dogs at a dog park, and free time in the back yard all will help burn off her energy. It is not to imply that she is high energy, shes not. Even when left alone at home, she has been good, but then again Cassi is one special pup. So, is Cassi the pup for you? If yes, head over to our Adoption Application and submit your application today. Her fee for adoption is $450. That includes the cost of spaying, up to date vaccinations, transport and rescue fees. A Dog Star representative will contact you within 24 hours of receiving the application. To help speed up the process, please call your vet and give them permission to speak with us. If you do not get a response within 24 hours of submitting your application, please check your spam folder.

description:
Bobby's mom has cancer and can no longer take care of him.  It's heartbreaking that at eight years old he now is finding himself homeless and looking for someone that can open their hearts to give him a home and love.

He has not been used to children so we are thinking a home that is with someone older and more quiet.  He's a little fellow and doesn't ask for much.  He's be rather independent allowing himself in and out through a doggie door.  He likes to be pet, but does not like to be picked up.  Bobby is not a happy dog.....he's very chill and has settled in to his temporary quarters very well.

This is a courtesy post for his good Samaritan who is caring for him in NC at this time.  We will accept applications through our rescue and process for his adoption.  Please note our adoption process is as follows:

Our online application is available under the link :  http://www.diamonddogsrescueinc.com/online-adoption-application.html

Please do not fill out on a mobile application as it does not allow form to be submitted.  It should be filled out and submitted on a computer.
 
When your application is received we process by reviewing all references and then setting up your conference or meeting with the foster family after those references have been checked.    Because our foster families volunteer to open their hearts and homes to our rescues, we try to lessen the amount of interference with their lives by only allowing pre-approved adopters to meet the dog and/or call the foster family to ask questions about the dog.   The pre-approval process does not obligate you and would NOT require a home visit until you have spoken with or met with the foster family to be sure the dog is right for you.   Once that occurs and you are committed to adopting our rescue, then we will schedule your home visit.  

PLEASE NOTE:  SOME DOGS MAY NOT BE AVAILABLE FOR A MEET AND GREET.  Because we are a foster based rescue, our rescues are transported to our foster families AFTER they have been vetted and are cleared for transport medically.  Although our company has headquarters in New Jersey and our second location in Mass, where they end up being fostered depends on which foster is available at that time (our pet finder site only allows us to post in New Jersey or Mass, not where dogs are fostered).   Our foster team members are located from North Carolina all the way to Southern Maine.  IF THEY ARE BEING FOSTERED OUTSIDE OF THE AREA THAT YOU COULD EASILY TRAVEL TO, we arrange for you to speak with the foster to determine if the dog is what you are expecting.  So, if the dogs are not being fostered close enough to visit prior to adoption and this is not acceptable to you, please do not fill out an application. 

In many cases our rescues are adopted directly from their vetting and quarantine and do not even get to foster.  Many families are comfortable for a direct adoption, especially with puppies or with the evaluation provided by our references and our rescue trainer.   In this case they are transported to the adopter and our adoption contract provides for a thirty day refund of your adoption fee for any reason.   The dog is returned to us if they are not working and it cannot be resolved to yours and to our satisfaction. 

From this point, with all information on the application being acceptable and the home visit satisfactory,  the applicant is approved and the adoption takes place.  Your contracts are emailed and your adoption fee will be $350 (that includes all medical and transport fees).   Once contracts are signed and your adoption fee paid,  arrangements are made to transport the dog to his/her home, whether it be from a foster or from our vet clinic.  

Beyond the thirty refund policy in our adoption contract, Diamond Dogs Rescue, Inc. offers a lifetime guarantee on all of its animals.  If for any reason an owner needs to return the adopted dog, Diamond Dogs Rescue, Inc. always welcomes the pooch's return and your contract will provide for this.

name: Mister B
description:
3 yr old Collie Blend
Neutered
UTD on Vaccines
House trained
Crate trained (he sleeps with door open) 
Can have free reign of house and doesnât chew or mess
Great with other dogs (proper intros of course)
No cats
Older respectful kid friendly
Loves to go for rides
Walks good on a leash
Knows sit/come
Very loyal dog

There was once someone who loved him.......
But now he's gone. You see, Mister B was found in his home with his deceased owner.

With no one to care, no one to step up for him....he found himself in Rockingham Shelter. Mister stayed 1 month in the shelter and he was so scared and didnât understand what was going on. After a month, with NO ONE interested in saving his life, Mister found himself on the list to be euthanized in the morning. It seemed hopeless, until Diamond Dogs Rescue saw him and learned he was left alone in this world separated from his owner by death.

When we saw the beaded collar that was lovingly hand made, still on him in the shelter it broke our hearts to think his short life would end alone in a shelter, with no one to care if he lived or died. Diamond Dogs Rescue saw the emptiness in his eyes and just HAD TO SAVE HIM!

His foster mom can tell he was close to his owner. \"If I get to far away from him he just barks and cries. This breaks my heart. Heâs only 3 yrs old but he is also heart worm positive\". So, right now he's being treated for his heart worm and will then be available to a good home. That should be around the end of September.  Help share Mister's story so we can find his family and help his broken heart heal.  You can see photos and day to day information on him on his very own Facebook page at:

name: Sammy
description:
The shelter volunteer wrote, \"I'm watching Sammy as he's playing outside and for this moment he's just a dog playing with his ball.  He doesn't know he is on todays kill list!\"  His time was up and to a large dog already around two years old who is heart worm positive that's like a death sentence down south!  The cost to treat for rescues typically has them shying away from the added expense to an already busting budget.   BUT....because someone LOVED this dog very much and took the time to message us for his life Sammy was saved!

Sammy not only had heart worm, but a couple other issues that were treated by our vet.  He's been neutered and brought current on all vaccines.  He's a big boy weighing in at around 68lbs and is a beautiful mix breed with the most expressive eyes!  Now he's completed all treatment and is ready for a home.

Play and quite a meatball without being over the top, Sammy is like a little kid on the playground.  He loves running and playing and chasing a ball.  He likes to lay on the ground and savor a belly rub and he give the best kisses of gratitude.  Sammy is good with other dogs...actually doing the belly crawl.  Because he looks like he's a dog that could hold his own, we never thought he'd be the less dominant dog.  He's sweet and easy going and enjoys being outdoors with his human.  This dog reminds us of the way life was meant to be....living every moment carefree!

name: Romeo
description:
Named by the \"village\" that helped to save him our Romeo was a total mess.  The people of the community watched him day in and day out scavenging for food, but staying distant.  He had an embedded collar and it was badly infected.  Our vet said this was one of the worst embedded collars they had seen.  This poor dog was so sick from infection that finally capturing him was a matter of him no longer having the strength to run.  But, once captured, it was as if he was thankful they had him!

Romeo has been treated and is nicely mended.  He's learning how much love and attention humans can give and he's responding in thankful kindness.  He's been fully brought Current on vaccines, neutered, microchipped and treated in preparing for a home.  Still with our vet in North Carolina he's being posted so that we can find his family and have him sent home.

Romeo is a beautiful, loving, sweet and still a bit shy....but warms up quickly to love and patience.  This is a dog that was likely in a home before being left on his own.   He's still young, maybe between 1-2 years old and so handsome.  Once his beautiful coat comes back in fully and he puts on some weight, he will be even more good looking!

Because Romeo was a stray and spent a good amount of time on his own, avoiding being captured, it is likely he will need longer than the normal dog to adjust and feel comfortable with his new home and knowing happiness.  Dogs like this learn quickly, but patience will be what's needed.  You will be rewarded three fold for time invested in this handsome boy!

description:
Bailey is a 10-12 month old American Foxhound from out North Carolina shelter partner.

description:

Extremely smart, Cloud learns quickly and is eager to please. A high-
energy girl, she requires daily exercise and stimulation. A fenced-in yard is a must.
She d

oes well with large dominant males who offer correction and leadership. She's not a fan of cats or small dogs. Cloud has a prey drive and can be dog reactive. name: Parker
description:
Meet Parker!

Parker came to us from North Carolina during the summer and we were so excited to find this awesome dog a his forever home. We quickly noticed how much fun he was and loved getting him together with a few other dogs and watch Parker run circles around them. He loves to play fetch and like a true cattle dog can easily keep up on a really nice hike or run!

We quickly adopted him out to a fantastic family that opened up their home and hearts to this beautiful boy. Once he was settled in they noticed some behaviors they needed help with so we quickly stepped in to help train Parker. After a few months of training we had to come to the tough decision that Parker was just not the right fit for this great family. While he was great with them for most of their time together, Parker is socially dominant. We believe he would be a great dog for a family without young children and who are open to learning the training we offer to make sure Parker can live the happiest life possible.

Parker is house broken, crate trained, and very dog friendly. We have prepared Parker with the training needed and now we are looking for a family to take the tools we offer to continue his journey into becoming a great doggie citizen!

For more information visit our website at adoptadog.org or to submit an application please visit: goo.gl/VEjhLX

name: Ali
description:
Hello all, Iâm Ali and I canât wait to meet you! I made my freedom ride from North Carolina in an airplane! How cool is that?! Iâm a classy, chic and elegant girl with a little bit of sass. I guess I was born with glitter in my veins! Iâm a spunky, fun and silly girl, and a big fan of cuddling! I am always labeled as fashion fabulous with my shimmering, elegant and sleekly good looks. All I need is a nice hat and some pearls to walk the red carpet along with my spunky prance. Iâm an expert too because Iâm such an easy walker. Since arriving at LaMancha, I have been showered with love. The talk around the farm is that I have become a volunteer favorite. Everyone runs up to me and says they love me. My fosters back in North Carolina say Iâm tender-hearted, a big snuggler, fun and a spunky girl too! When I heard someone say I was 7 years young, I was surprised because I definitely donât act or feel like a middle-aged girl. I feel like a puppy at heart, My age is best guessed because I was a stray. I am a good and respectful neighbor to my canine friends next door. My friends would tell you I am peachy sweet, laid-back, affectionate, flashy chic, elegant with a huge heart of gold. Iâm feeling lucky today but my luck depends on you!

A best friend is like a four-leaf clover; hard to find and lucky to have! Adopt me and I will be your BFF!!! Please, just email rescue@lamanchaanimalrescue.org. Iâll be waiting!

- 7 years young
- Pittie mix


UTD vaccinations, chipped, spayed/neutered, wormed.

name: Beau
description:
BEAU:

Hello mates, Iâm Beau. Iâm a 1-year-old Bluetick Coonhoud from North Carolina. People say to know me is to love me.  Iâm a stunning boy with the most gorgeous breath-taking tricolor hound coat.  Iâm engaging, full of life, happy-go-lucky, life-of-the-party, silly, and spunky guy!  I adore everyone I meet!  I am playful, fun, outgoing, with a sweet personality and a kind heart. I am a mannerly boy and the perfect charmer, and Iâm not afraid to flaunt it. I love to cuddle next to you and stare at you with my sweet face and puppy dog eyes asking for belly rubs and your love. . . I have never been denied yet because everyone loves me. I want to be your BFF and your lap dog!  Oh, BTW, I also have some awesome canine friends that I love to play with too.  To me, I sound like a keeper, an easy keeper in my world!  My heart is so big for my body, and I need someone to share it with. Happiness is only real when itâs shared!

âLife is a one time offer, use it well: ADOPT ME!!!â To accept my offer, email rescue@lamanchaanimalrescue.org for the best years of your life!

UTD vaccinations, chipped, spayed/neutered, wormed.

name: Kimi
description:
KIMI:

Hi friends!  Iâm Kimi and there is sunshine in my soul every day and I want to share it with you!  I am a 2-year-old petite Shepherd mix, ~ 36 lbs. Iâm from North Carolina where I lived in a shelter for the past few months until I made my journey to LaMancha. I am an awesome, gentle and pleasant girl who always wears a smile on my face. My positive energy is contagious--I spread good vibes. My shimmering, elegant black coat is gorgeous, but look deep into my warm brown eyes and stare at my beautiful big smile.  Can you feel my warm, friendly presence?  I have lots of fans. They love to walk and spend time with me because Iâm such an easy walker, and they think Iâm so cute with my dainty little prance around the farm. We have some good conversations, good laughs, and I love getting lots of cuddles and belly rubs. Then sadly, itâs time for them to leave me and go home. Well thankfully I have some great doggie roommates to keep me company when my people friends arenât around. Iâm such a social butterfly. Truthfully, Iâm a girl who has never been loved by a family and my heart is hurting for love. I soak up all positive energy and happiness.  We both deserve a life filled with happy moments, happy feelings, laughter and smiles. Do you want to join me?

Thereâs just something about dogs that makes you feel good. When you walk in the door, even if you just went to the mailbox, theyâre thrilled to see you, like youâve been gone forever! Theyâre good for the ego. That could be us!  Please send your email ASAP!  rescue@lamanchaanimalrescue.org.

Life is good but it could be a whole lot better with your SHARES!  You could find my family for me!  Thank you friends!  Kimi



UTD vaccinations, chipped, spayed/neutered, wormed.


Please email rescue@lamanchaanimalrescue.org for an application

name: Shelby
description:
Shelby came to us from North Carolina. She is about 47 pounds and is guessed to be a beagle/harrier hound mix. Shelby loves to play with the other dogs in the rescue. She does ok on a leash and is crate trained. She is working on her house training and is well on her way, so far she has not gone in her crate, but needs to learn how to tell her humans when she needs to go out.   Shelby loves hanging out in the house and is pretty much a couch potato. Shelby is guessed to be around 4 years of age. She is a sweet hound that loves the attention of people. 
Shelby is up to date on her vaccines and is micro chipped. She will be spayed before adoption. If you are interested in Shelby,  please fill out an application at www.itavar.com

name: Sissy
description:
Sissy came to us from North Carolina. She is about 35 pounds and is guessed to be a hound mix. Sissy loves to play with the other dogs in the rescue. She does ok on a leash and is crate trained. Not sure if she is totally house trained, but she is well on her way, so far she has not gone in her crate nor in the house.  She will need a fenced in yard.  Sissy is guessed to be around 4 years of age. She is a sweet little hound that loves the attention of people. She also loves to hang out in the kiddy pool when it is hot outside.
Sissy is up to date on her vaccines and is micro chipped. She will be spayed before adoption. If you are interested in Sissy please fill out an application at www.itavar.com

name: Rufus
description:
Rufus came to our rescue from a kill shelter in North Carolina with heartworms. We put him through heartworm treatment and now he is done his treatment and feeling like a healthy happy 2 year old.  Rufus had not been taught anything before we rescued him and he is work in progress and learning quickly. Rufus is being fostered in a home with dogs, cats and lots of children and a few adults. He is a happy go lucky dog that is now finally learning some structure. Rufus loves people and just wants attention. He has a lot of energy, as a 2 year old should and would love an active family. He has been known to get in the water with some coaxing. Rufus is working on his crate training (it is getting him in the crate, once in, he is fine) and he is working on his leash walking, he does like to pull, but the foster started using an easy walk on him and it has helped a lot.  He is house trained. 
Rufus is micro chipped, up to date on all of his vaccines and neutered. If you are interested in adopting Rufus please fill out an application at www.itavar.com

name: Tapestry
description:
Tapestry, aka Tappie, is a beautiful Brindle that came to us from a shelter in North Carolina. We believe she is a Mountain Cur/Catahoula/Terrier mix. She weighs about 45 pounds and is believed to be about 3 years old. Tappie went to Ventosa Kennels in North Carolina to get some training and has earned her certificate. She is looking for a home with people that have energy like she does. She would make a great jogging or running partner. Tappie is crate trained, house trained and has learned âsitâ and âdownâ.  She does well on a leash, though daily practice is a must.  Tappie loves her humans, big or small, though she is extremely picky on her dog playmates, this is why she would do best being the only dog in the house. Tapestry must have a fenced in yard because of all of her energy, so she needs a place to run to get out all of her energy.
Tapestry is spayed, micro chipped and up to date on all of her vaccines.
If you are interested in Tapestry please fill out our application which can be found on our web site www.itavar.com

name: Tim
description: This is our friend Tim he is a year old. he is an American Pit Bull Terrier and he is the most loving guy you will meet. Dont let his big face or tough exterior run you away. he is very lovable and enjoys human company. Tim is from a rescue out of North Carolina, along with a few others he was fleeing the hurricane and floods. Tim made it all the way to our facility to find his new home. if you are interested in meeting Tim ask a kennel tech to set up a meet and greet.

name: Diamond- Courtesy Listing
description: You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.COURTESY LISTINGTHIS IS NOT A BULLY PAWS DOG. She loves apples, bananas, her toys and rides in the car. She has been thru training and is quite smart.

name: Apollo Hound
description:
Handsome 'people' boyHello! My name is Apollo Hound aka Apollo, and I am a 2 year old, 55 lb foxhound mix. I am a loving and loyal dog, but I need to let you know that I am insecure. I have gained confidence with a consistent routine, and with patience and reassurance from my past foster and the awesome human heroes that have saved me and are currently looking out for me. I came from North Carolina where I was wandering the streets, and the human that saved me did not know much about my past. However, a few things about me have been figured out: I want to please and I will work hard to understand my new home and surroundings. I love to be loved and give love right back. I am insecure, but willing and wanting to trust. I learn quickly, such as sit, down, stay/wait and I am ready to learn more. New people worry me so do new buildings. I do not like going into buildings/homes I'm not familiar with. I will follow when I trust, and especially if I have a dog buddy. I tend to trust a woman more than a man. Men wearing hats scare me, but I will warm up to a man over time, especially if one of my dog buddies trusts him. I realize I keep mentioning dog buddies. I love dogs. Dogs are my buddies!! They make me feel safe and I love to play with them. I am still learning that humans know how to play - that sometimes is so weird to me! I SHOULD NEVER BE TRUSTED WITH CATS. I like walks and am learning how to play fetch. I am mostly housebroken, but I am still learning. I need a consistent routine. I do OK in crates, but I don't like crates and storms. I have been known to escape them. There is so much that I have to offer to your home and I can't wait to be a part of your family.Apollo Hound should go into an adult only home.
Apollo's adoption donation fee is $280, which includes spay/neuter, routine vetting and a microchip. You can apply for Apollo by filling out our online application, which is found on our website www.tarashouse.net or www.tarashouse.org. Please email us at info@tarashouse.net with any questions.

name: Skinner
description:
Hi everyone, my name is Skinner! I am 10 years old and I may look huge but I'm a compact 50 pounds of love! I came to the sanctuary all the way from North Carolina when a nice pilot flew me here to find a better life. I wasn't treated very well before so I'm enjoying taking my time getting to know people and being treated the way I deserve. Despite my past I am a very sweet boy who loves to go for walks and snuggle once I get to know you! I came to the sanctuary Heartworm positive but after treatment I am all clear and doing very well! 
I love to run around outside so a home with a yard is a must for me; I am truly happiest when I am outside.
Come to the sanctuary to meet me!

name: Rj
description: RJ is a sweet guy. He is 4 years old and enjoys the company of others, RJ should definitely go to a home where there are NO OTHER DOGS AT ALL. Rj came to us from a rescue out of North Carolina and is currently looking for his forever home. He loves to run and play, so he would be a perfect dog to be active with! RJ is fully vaccinated, microchipped and neutered. if he is the perfect fir for you come on in and meet with him!

name: Jake N
description: Jake is a big hound who was rescued from North Carolina last year. He had been neglected and was gravely ill, but volunteers at HART nursed him back to health. He is very loving and has such a sweet soul. He gets along well with the other dogs in his foster home and is even fine with the cats. Jake has wonderful manners: completely housebroken, walks well on a leash, doesn't beg or jump, likes to sleep in, and keeps off the furniture. He is pretty calm and quiet and doesn't even bark at the neighbor's dogs! Jake doesn't ask for much - just someone who will give him plenty of love but also set firm boundaries for him in order to set him up for success. Give this poor hound, who has suffered so much, a chance at happiness! Thank you for your interest in this HART pet! Please visit www.hart90.org/petdetail.aspx?ID=11643 to email the contact person listed for more information and how to meet Jake N, or to submit an online application. HART adopts to the local DC/VA/MD metro area only. Visit our website for more information about our adoption process.

name: Farrah
description: Farrah is a sweet girl with plenty of tail wags for everyone. She came to HART from North Carolina where she was surrendered by her owner, along with her puppies Alan and Walter, who have since been adopted. When she first arrived in the NC shelter, she was very confused by her new surroundings, but once she adjusted, she was all tail wags and wiggles! Farrah loves people and other dogs. She can come on a bit strong because she is so happy to make new friends, but she settles well. Thank you for your interest in this HART pet! name: Simba
description: Meet Simba, named after the character in the Disney movie The Lion King.  Simba means powerful warrior, and his name certainly suits him.  Simba was pulled from a high kill shelter in North Carolina on his very last day.  Simba came to us emaciated and covered with horrible scars and bite wounds.  Everywhere on his poor, frail body had either scabs, open wounds or scars.  We estimate Simba to be around two years old and is a bully breed mix.  He is a big eater, but does not show any food aggression or guarding at all, which is amazing considering he was nearly starved to death.  Simba would benefit from some training, as he was never taught leash manners.  He has not shown any aggression toward other dogs or cats, although he will sometimes growl if he feels threatened by another dog so a very careful and proper introduction to any other dogs will be necessary.  Considering everything he has been through, we do not blame Simba one bit for his concerns.  Simba has a wonderful personality - he is very energetic and LOVES toys.  He loves to carry his blanket around and play with it.  He will play with basically anything he can find.  Simba loves people and will sit still and soak up all the love and attention you are willing to give him.  Simba is house and crate-trained, up to date on all shots, heartworm negative and on heartworm, flea and tick prevention.  Simba clearly had a really rough past and although his body will always likely bear the scars, he did not let his past form his personality.  \"Scars remind us of where we have been, but they do not have to dictate where we are going.â  And this is certainly true for Simba.  Please consider opening your heart and home to this sweet boy and finding out for yourself what an amazing boy he is â you wonât regret it!

name: Karma
description: Karma was saved from North Carolina where she spent her life chained to a tree.  . She is a sweet girl that LOVES to play and be near you.  Sheâs house trained and knows basic commands.  . Karma, while perfect, needs to be an only dog.  She does not think the world is big enough for other animals.  She's very playful and silly.  Karma has a stage four heart murmur and is on custom allergy meds.  both of which are under control.    Karma is spayed, microchipped and current on her shots.

name: Emmett *Sponsored adoption fee*
description:
\"Hey hey, the name is Emmett! Thanks for visiting me online! Iâm a new arrival to Providence Animal Center from an overcrowded shelter in North Carolina. I came north to find my new forever home. My adoption day is all I can think about, please donât make me wait too long!

name: Forrest *Foster*
description:
My momma always said, âLifeÂ wasÂ like a box of chocolates. You never know what you're gonna get.â

\"Howdy there, my name is Forrest...ya know Forrest Gump! I am so happy to meet you over this internet thing! Iâm a new arrival to Providence Animal Center from an overcrowded North Carolina shelter. My Momma always said you've got to put the past behind you before you can move on. So I am ready to move from here into my new forever home.

Shortly after arriving to the center, I was whisked away to a lovely foster home. My foster mom says that I am a very friendly and handsome boy...aww shucks! I enjoy the company of my doggie foster sister, we have a lot of fun together playing and running around in their yard. RUN FORREST RUN! am estimated to be around 1 year old & 60 pounds
am crate trained
ride well in the car
am curious, love treats, seem eager to please, playful, attention-getter
would make a great running partner
LOVE to cuddle

As if all that isn't enough already, I am also the package deal - neutered, microchipped and up-to-date on vaccines. My adoption day is all I can think about, please donât make me wait too long! If you are interested in meeting me, please email a completed adoption application (https://providenceac.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Adoption-Profile.pdf) to my friend the foster coordinator: foster@providenceac.org I hope to hear from you soon!

Lots of love & slobbery kisses,

Forrest\

name: Rico *Foster*
description:
\"Rico is the name, finding my forever home is the game! I came to Providence Animal Center from North Carolina in search of my forever family. I'm a low-rider ladies man and love other dogs. While I'm very comfortable with dogs, I am still getting used to walking on the leash and socializing with people, so I am hanging out in an awesome foster home! I am estimated to be around 1 and 1/2 years old and 32 pounds.

Some might say I am the package deal:

up-to-date on vaccines
neutered
microchipped

I am a little shy at first and would prefer to live in a quiet home, no city life for me please! Do you have another pup in the home who needs a buddy? Is she cute? I would LOVE to have a doggie roommate to hang out with in my forever home. I have met some feline friends here at the center and could potentially live with a kitty roommate also.

If I sound like the guy for you, email a completed adoption application to my friend the foster coordinator (foster@providenceac.org) to set up a time to meet me in person! My paws are crossed I will get to meet you very soon! XOXO Rico\

name: Lilly (PA)
description:
Hi, my name is Lil, or as my foster parents call me Lilly Lou. I grew up living in a home in North Carolina but after one of my people passed away the other got really sick and could no longer care for me. I was dropped off at a crowded shelter in the mountains of North Carolina. I wasnât really a big fan of being in the shelter and that is when Pointer Rescue Org showed up and I left with my foster parents. I had a long road trip from North Carolina to Harrisburg, Pennsylvania where Iâm now learning about lots of new things and am excited to find my new forever home. I am a very happy girl that LOVES to be around people and snuggle them on the couch. Every person I have seen I have wanted to meet. The same goes for dogs of all sizes. I enjoy soft, comfortable dog beds where I can get some sun but donât really like laying outside in the hot sun. Iâm not too sure about a lot of dog toys but I really like the soft, fuzzy ones that I can chew on. I get along with the other dog in the house but Iâm not a big fan of playing rough. Just laying around and being close to each other is ok with me. My foster parents tell me I walk well on a leash and donât pull and if I do I know to slow down to let them catch up. I know how to sit, especially if you have some yummy treats for me and will come when called. I LOVE Food and Treats and love to be in the kitchen anytime there is food being cooked. I was told Iâm not the best sous chef but Iâm probably the cutest one. I do like to check out whatâs on the kitchen counter but if you tell me Off I will sadly get off the counter. I enjoy going for walks and hiking but so far I donât like going into any water but I do enjoy a good mud bath. description:
Timber is incredibly handsome, smart and gentle.  The shelter networked long and hard to save him because he was such a great dog.   The video on his page was the video sent with a plea to please rescue as his time was up and NO ONE stepped up. How could you not take this dog?  Not only was he sweet and gentle but he was this way with a horrible infection that had been caused by being neutered....and he was still willing to sit/lay even through the pain.

We're not so sure of this handsome boys breed....all guesses. But we are sure of his good nature.  He's fully vetted, neutered, microchipped and ready to find a family that won't abandon him again!  We have a full trainer evaluation available to be emailed to you -just ask.   Our trainer's comments were \"I LOVE THIS DOG\" and we do to!  

We also have a great program available for foster to adopt when approved.  Check out the information at:
https://www.facebook.com/notes/toni-diamond/have-you-wanted-to-adopt-but-felt-concerned-that-it-might-be-a-dog-that-didnt-fi/10157161089056634/

Our online application is available under the link located at: 
https://www.facebook.com/notes/toni-diamond/have-you-wanted-to-adopt-but-felt-concerned-that-it-might-be-a-dog-that-didnt-fi/10157161089056634/

When your application is received we process by reviewing all references and then setting up your conference or meeting with the foster family after those references have been checked. Because our foster families volunteer to open their hearts and homes to our rescues, we try to lessen the amount of interference with their lives by only allowing pre-approved adopters to meet the dog and/or call the foster family to ask questions about the dog. The pre-approval process does not obligate you and would NOT require a home visit until you have spoken with or met with the foster family to be sure the dog is right for you. Once that occurs and you are committed to adopting our rescue, then we will schedule your home visit. 

PLEASE NOTE: SOME DOGS MAY NOT BE AVAILABLE FOR A MEET AND GREET. Because we are a foster based rescue, our rescues are transported to our foster families AFTER they have been vetted and are cleared for transport medically. Although our company has headquarters in New Jersey and our second location in Mass, where they end up being fostered depends on which foster is available at that time (our pet finder site only allows us to post in New Jersey or Mass, not where dogs are fostered). Our foster team members are located from North Carolina all the way to Southern Maine. IF THEY ARE BEING FOSTERED OUTSIDE OF THE AREA THAT YOU COULD EASILY TRAVEL TO, we arrange for you to speak with the foster to determine if the dog is what you are expecting. So, if the dogs are not being fostered close enough to visit prior to adoption and this is not acceptable to you, please do not fill out an application. 

In many cases our rescues are adopted directly from their vetting and quarantine and do not even get to foster. Many families are comfortable for a direct adoption, especially with puppies or with the evaluation provided by our references and our rescue trainer. In this case they are transported to the adopter and our adoption contract provides for a thirty day refund of your adoption fee for any reason. The dog is returned to us if they are not working and it cannot be resolved to yours and to our satisfaction. 

From this point, with all information on the application being acceptable and the home visit satisfactory, the applicant is approved and the adoption takes place. Your contracts are emailed and your adoption fee will be $350 (that includes all medical and transport fees). Once contracts are signed and your adoption fee paid, arrangements are made to transport the dog to his/her home, whether it be from a foster or from our vet clinic. 

Beyond the thirty day refund policy in our adoption contract, Diamond Dogs Rescue, Inc. offers a lifetime guarantee on all of its animals. If for any reason an owner needs to return the adopted dog, Diamond Dogs Rescue, Inc. always welcomes the pooch's return and your contract will provide for this

name: Dyson
description:

How does it happen that no one has adopted them?  Consider this happens so frequently that the \"demand\" for sweet retriever puppies is far less than the puppies who find themselves in this situation.  

Our rescue had a home for one of the puppies, but our policy is to never leave any pups in a litter behind.....so our family grew by four and we absolutely adore these pups.  They began their tenure in foster as shy mistrusting pups but it did not take long for their beautiful personalities to shine.  They are happy, healthy, playful and smart babies!  Just waiting for a family to call their own!

name: Coco
description:
Surrendered to a kill shelter by owners, Coco was considered by all who knew her as a worthy save.  When our rescue was reached out to take her, we did not hesitate given her temperament evaluation.
Her birthdate is 3/9/16.
Weight is 55 pounds
HER FOSTER MOM REPORTS:
No health issues and no bad habits that I've seen so far. The shelter paperwork said no small dogs or cats with her. She hurt a small dog at her home about a year ago. The owner said it was an accident. She is curious about my cat but nothing negative so far. The cat has been keeping his distance from her. She is quiet, I've only heard her bark once at the neighbors dog. She's a laid back and loving girl to a fault. She loves people, she will lick your hand and roll over for a belly rub every chance she gets!. I dont have any info as far as children. She is very fearful of men and we're helping her through that now. She walks well on the leash. She gets along great with all our dogs here. She has basic training, house trained and is crate trained. I've let her have free run of the house all day and night and she hasn't made any mistakes. No chewing, no potty mistakes, nothing! I feed her in her crate. When taking a treat from your hand she is oh so careful like a whisper. She absolutely loves to sleep with her person. She stays in her little spot and doesn't crowd. But when you wake up, you can bet she will crawl up to you for a belly rub!

name: Pickles
description:
Pickles is a 3-year-old female spayed Carolina Dog mix who weighs about 42lbs. She has big pointy ears and loves to go hiking, jogging, and chase squirrels. She can also be a total couch potato and just sleep next to her human for hours while the TV is on. Pickles loves peanut butter, pancakes, Swiss cheese, and popcorn. She dislikes vegetables, cats, and not being allowed to catch the squirrels. 

Pickles was originally adopted 2 years ago from North Carolina and has been extremely well cared for as her previous owner is a veterinarian. She is in excellent health and she is house-trained, crate-trained, and knows a lot of commands. Pickles can be a bit nervous around new people and new large dogs and takes a little while to come out of her shell, but when she does she is a total joy! Pickles does best with slow, low-energy introductions and sometimes barks nervously at new people who come on a bit too strong. She loves to play and loves small dogs, but can get a bit defensive around large high-energy dogs at first. However, her best friend is a 90lb Great Pyrenees so she definitely can build trust with any dog as long as the introductions go smoothly!

This family is heartbroken that they must rehome Pickles, but due to health reasons of their 2 month child, they have no choice. We are looking for the right home for this special girl - probably one without cats or small children since we cannot vouch for Pickles in those environments since she hasn't had enough exposure. Dogs will be a case by case intro. Just remember she needs calm temperaments in k9 friends.

The OS has generously offered to forward all of Pickles belongings too! We have 3 crates, about 6 months worth of dog food, heartworm/flea and tick preventatives for the year, and all other supplies she would need!

name: Huckleberry (NC)
description:
My name is Huck and Iâm looking for my forever family... could it be you?

    Iâm about a big, handsome, 3 year old lemon boy, and FULL of life! I was found as a stray and saved from the Georgia shelter before coming to my foster family in North Carolina. They got me some good food and a doctor of my own, and Iâm almost ready to start the next (and best) chapter of my life! My doctor is taking care of my heart worms and I will finish treatment and be ready to go to my new family in mid-September. 

    My favorite things are food, playing with my ball in the yard, playing with my foster brothers, snacks, running in the yard, and eating. Did I mention playing and eating?!

    My ideal family would spend time running and playing with me, and maybe has a human or dog friend, too! Initially, I was evaluated as not being good with cats, but I donât pay my foster-cat-brother any attention at all. I really hate thunder storms, but my parents have some medicine that helps me not be as scared. I donât really love taking baths, but Iâm told they have to be done.

    If you think I may be the one for you, just let PRO know! My foster parents would love to get to know you!

name: Waffle Society-LOOKING FOR A HOME
description:
9/2/19
Waffles

Cat Friendly â No!
Kid Friendly â YES!
Dog Friendly â YES!
House Broken â YES 
Crate Trained â YES!
Basic Commands â Yes!

Meet Waffles! He's a 1.5 year old Plott Hound mix and has their beautiful trademark brindle coat. He was adopted back in February and was loved and loved his people but needed a more consistent and less hectic household so that he could work on his possessiveness with toys. Energetic, but gentle, he's great with kids and gets along well with other dogs. A world-renowned hunting dog by nature, you'd never know it from his kind and loving disposition. He loves to go on long walks and is very playful in the backyard. His favorite thing to do is play with his dog friends, as he gets along with all of them! He is very treat motivated and is eager to please. He walks well on a leash and while he is at Camp Chester, he will just be perfecting the training he already has.

So what exactly is âCamp Chesterâ?

Camp Chester OR Wags at Chester WAGs at Chester is an institutional program that pairs incarcerated individuals with dogs to work on basic obedience, house training and socialization. Specifically, all the dogs work really hard to pass our mock-Canine Good Citizenship Test! The Canine Good Citizen Program is a two-part program that stresses responsible pet ownership for owners and basic good manners for dogs. Every dog that arrives at Camp Chester, is given individual attention based on their needs, as every need is different.

8/25/19
Waffles is on his way to Camp Chester from some training.  He was adopted back in February and was loved and loved his people but needed a more consistent and less hectic household so that he could work on his resource guarding issues.  Waffles will be ready in about a month for his forever home with the hope that he will learn to share better.

2/2/19

Meet Waffles! He's a 1yr old Plott Hound mix and has their beautiful trademark brindle coat. Energetic, but gentle, he's great with kids and gets along well with other dogs. A world renowned hunting dog by nature, you'd never know it from his kind and loving disposition. He loves to go on long walks and is very playful in the backyard. Unlike some other hounds I know, he never jumps up on people or up on the counter to steal some delicious people food.

Rescued from an unfortunate situation in North Carolina where he and his siblings were kept outside with little to eat and drink, he has since thrived and is up from 15-20 lbs in October to around 50-55 lbs now, which is the appropriate full size for this breed.  He didn't allow the mistreatment early in his life to impact his attitude, which tells you that he really is special. He's been fully evaluated and received all the appropriate shots. Housebroken and crate trained, he should be able to adapt quickly to a new environment.

name: Joseph
description: Hey there, my name is Joseph and I'm two years old. I came from a shelter in North Carolina where there was a good chance I was going to be put to sleep because they were very crowded and I tested positive for heartworms. Lucky for me a very nice lady sent my foster mom a picture of me and she fell in love with not only me, but my name. She called the very nice lady in NC and she arranged transport to bring me to GA. Once I settled in to my foster home, mom took me and had me treated for heartworms and I'm doing really great now!!  I'm crate, house trained, a really good boy and I love following mom around the yard when we're all out there together. I also love running around the yard with my doggie friends now AND as you can see from some of my pictures, I kinda love rolling in the dirt but I do it because it gets my doggie friend's attention and they play with me!! lol I never really was like that before I came to my foster mom's house. Now I have a happy, healthy and loving life. BUT,the next thing is, as much as I love my foster mom for the dog that I've become, I would love nothing more than a family or special someone to call my own. It might take me a little bit of time to get used to another home but I will do everything to show what a good boy I am and why my foster mom loves me so much!! She always leans down to me and says \"give mama a kiss\" and she takes my muzzle gives me a kiss on it! lol I really enjoy running now and would make a wonderful companion for that special someone looking for a very handsome, great boy like me who has learned so much since I've been with my foster mom. If you are interested in me, please email my foster mom at lizziz101@bellsouth.net P.S. I really like going for rides now and mom has started taking me to Pet Smart. And I do pretty good there too:)

name: Bayne
description:
Bayne is a gorgeous 2-year-old Treeing Walker Coonhound weighing 60#. Bayne has a lot to smile about since a foster stepped up to save his life from a rural North Carolina shelter.

If you like adventure, Bayne would love to join! This energetic pup loves going on hikes and would also make a great jogging buddy! Bayne enjoys car rides and walks well on a leash.

He is dog and people friendly. Bayne has not been tested with cats, but shows no signs of a high prey drive. He is crate trained and almost housebroken.

description:
RED came to Angel's Rest Animal Sanctuary from a North Carolina shelter with large open wounds on his hind end.  His wounds have healed and he is ready for his new home!  RED does not seem to like cats and can be picky about his doggy friends.  He has separation anxiety when he is away from people but we think this may be able to be remedied with a home that has another dog or someone that works from home.

name: Pumpkin
description:
Whose bouncy, pouncy, and tons of fun, Pumpkin is! The wonderful thing about Pumpkin is she's the only one. Yup she is the only one meant just for you. Pumpkin would love to be your one and only has she is a people pleasing dog who loves all people of all ages. She has been around toddlers and older kids which she does great with both. Pumpkin is a Finnish Spitz mix with show stopping orange and red fur. At 2 year old Pumpkin is full

of energy and bounces. But she also has manners with knowing how to sit, stay, lay down, no or leave it, and walks well on her leash. Pumpkin is so smart just tell her to stay beside you while walking and she does. And already potty trained. Pumpkin loves treats and Kongs stuffed with peanut butter.

She would prefer a fenced in yard to run in because she likes her zoom zoom zoomies. Just don't tell her she isn't Tigger because she thinks her springy bounce is fun fun fun.

Pumpkin was from North Carolina as a stray. Though we not sure how long she was a stray but she loves the home life now and going on adventures.

If you think Pumpkin is the perfect match for you please send in adoption adoption application at
https://www.underhoundrailroad.org/adoption/

name: Hazel
description: Hazel is a beautiful girl of under 1.5 years.  She was rescued from a kill shelter in North Carolina.  Hazel is very loving and sweet.  She craves attention.  She is on the smaller side (60-70 lbs).  She is fine with other dogs, and would be good with children.  Hazel probably lived out doors so she will need to learn some indoor manners, but she is a pretty gentle girl, and very smart.  She walks pretty well on a leash, and is eager to please.  We just love her.  She would like an active family.

name: Rookie
description: Rookie is a beautiful dog under 1.5 years old.   He came to us from a shelter in North Carolina.  Rookie was in pretty rough shape when he was brought to the shelter, very underweight and missing some hair...but he has been quickly improving with us!  He is gaining weight, and his coat is coming back - the vet believes it was just allergies.  With a couple of medicated baths, and good food he is looking great.  This dog is absolutely stunning, and will be even handsomer when he gains another 15 lbs or so.  Rookie is super sweet with people, and craves attention.  He is a very active boy.  He has had little training and probably lived outdoors so will need to learn some manners, but he is very smart!  Rookie is good with other dogs upon proper introduction.
