Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Jon Snow is dark, mysterious and a little shy... just like his character. But when he feels comfortable around you, he loves tummy rubs and to play with his siblings!

He is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. NEW ARRIVAL!!! NEW ARRIVAL!!! NEW ARRIVAL!!! NEW ARRIVAL!!! NEW ARRIVAL!!! NEW ARRIVAL!!!
 
This little lady is mom to a litter of beautiful blue eyed pups who will soon be available for adoption. Her babies are newly weaned and she has been a great mom, but now she needs to focus on finding a forever home! She is sweet as can be and perfectly sized.

Her life clearly hasn't been easy. In addition to being pregnant and landing in a high-kill shelter, she was heartworm positive and had to undergo painful heartworm treatment after her pups were completely weaned. Heartworm is a completely preventable disease, but she lacked the care and preventative medication needed. She was treated in early August and is on the road to recovery. She does have an activity restriction for another few weeks, but she is a calm girl and has been the best patient.

She is shy at first, but warms to her humans with some time, especially if you show her affection. She would do best with a patient adopter in a calm home, where she can have the space to come out of her shell. She is worth it, trust us! Because she is so shy with humans, she would be happiest in a home with another dog to help build her confidence. She needs a bit of stable living to learn that not all humans mean to bring her harm or neglect. She is good with other dogs and cats.

Initially fearful and dog-reactive, this girl attended training classes with her amazing foster and has learned how to be polite and confident, all with just some positive reinforcement and consistency. She's smart and eager to please, which makes her highly trainable.


From her foster: Meet Bella! She is a beautiful, loyal girl that loves to run and is just a bundle of energy. She wants to please her \"people\" and has done really well with training as she is extremely food motivated. Although she has energy, she can be gentle when need be with the proper commands, but overall would make a great companion for an equally energetic family! She tends to get overwhelmed in large social gatherings (such as adoption events) and it is recommended for potential adopters to meet her in her foster environment, where she is comfortable and happy and can best show her true colors.

Bella will need an adopter who is committed to giving her lots of exercise, as well as continuing with her training. We recommend another training class for her with her adopter since it is about training the human as much as it is about training the dog! A class also has the benefit of building a closer bond between dog and human. We want to ensure her forever family continues to reinforce the positive behaviors so she can remain a confident and well-adjusted pup.

This gal has been overlooked for so long because of her reactivity towards other dogs, and she wonders if anyone will give the \"new Bella\" a real chance at a loving forever home. She has worked hard for it, and she deserves nothing less.

Her foster reports that she is crate trained and has not had any accidents in the home.

Meet majestic Gulliver! Surrendered at a SC shelter for not getting along with the resident dogs, Gulliver quickly proved that he is indeed good with most dogs... sometimes dogs just need a proper introduction. Although Gulliver passed his cat test, he is VERY interested in cats & may want to play with them. Obviously most cats wouldn't enjoy this so he may do better in a house with no cats. He does well with other dogs but he MUST have a PROPER introduction. He can only be adopted by an experienced (large breed) adopter who is willing to hire a trainer. Gulliver was not given any training in his first home so he needs a lot of work on his manners. If he were to go to a home with another dog, there should be 2 adults in the home. It is just too much for one person to handle Gulliver + another dog.

In addition to the above, we're looking for an adopter who doesn't have young children (under 12) & has a fenced (6') in yard. Please make sure you fit all of the above criteria before applying.

Gulliver is still somewhat of a puppy, but he is very treat motivated and smart, so training him should be a breeze. He already knows numerous commands after just a few days in a foster home.

Gulliver is a tad bit underweight if you can believe it, and we need to note that he is a bit of a resource guarder with food. Given his size, he needs an experienced adopter who will agree to work with a DC PAWS approved positive reinforcement trainer to address that issue and to generally teach him how to be a gentleman.

This pup is a rare rescue find (well, perhaps not THAT rare), and his previous guardian's loss can be your gain.

Please note that we anticipate A LOT of interest in this guy and we may not be able to respond to each application right away; we are an all-volunteer rescue of individuals with full time jobs and do our best to be responsive, but sometimes it can be overwhelming with popular breeds like this one. Our goal is to find a home and family that are the best fit for Gulliver, and vice versa. As such, applications will not necessarily be considered on a first come, first served basis. That being said, we anticipate a good match will be found quickly, but we always encourage applications since you never know when applications may fall through.

description:
Logan is very playful and has a outgoing personality. He enjoys being rubbed and likes to have a window to look out of. Heâs very submissive and enjoys doing whatâs asked of him especially when thereâs a treat. Logan has an auto immune disease called VKH syndrome ( https://www.marvistavet.com/vkh-syndrome.pml ) which affects the pigment of his skin and without immediate treatment can have a long term effect on the eyes and possible blindness. In terms of medical treatment,  He is currently on a steroid (prednisone) which helps suppress his immune system to stop it from attacking itself. Also on eye medication (prednisone, timolol, and dorzolamide). Pricewise the medications themselves are not costly. As of now, I havenât spent more than $70 dollars for his medications. The more costly things Iâve noticed was the actual exam fee. He has dog insurance which covers 90% of his medical expenses excluding the exam fee. Logan knows the sit, stay, lay commands. I'll ask him if he wants water or does he have to use the bathroom and heâll respond with a whine if he does. Same for food. The type of home I think that would be best suited for him is one where he can both be active and have some time to relax and receive a lot of love and just remain social, whether itâs with kids, other dogs, etc. He is house broken so he doesnât need to be crated.  

This Akita is located in Rochester, NY. If you're interested in him, please go to our website and fill out a online adoption application and we will get back to you shortly.

name: Stella
description:
Stella.Aprox. 1 year old. 55lbs. Black Mouth Cur Mix

The story of Stella:

Stella came to us when we got an urgent plea from a good Samaritan to take a dog belonging to an estranged relative. This poor pup was being kept in a back room, chained to an old broken mattress, with no food or water for an unknown period of time. Being a large, energetic puppy, she was often difficult to handle, but rather than trying to train her, Stella had been beaten when she made mistakes. She was one of the saddest and most depressing examples of neglect we had ever seen.

Saving Stella:

The most urgent issue for Stella was giving her the nutrition her body desperately needed. Although it would be tempting to give a starving dog as much food as they can eat, it was important to strictly regulated and measured her food to avoid further health complications.

Sadly, when Stella started to feel stronger and more energetic, it was clear that she had suffered more than we knew. By locking her away, her family had robbed her of many crucial life experiences and exposure milestones that every dog needs to become a confident and happy adult. Although she was safe, Stella was still a tiny, confused and scared puppy in a big powerful body. Stella did not understand that she was not meant to walk across the dinner table, she did not believe that no one was going to use her leash to beat her, she could not trust that it was ok to move away from situations that overwhelmed her. Realizing that Stella needed expert help, we were lucky enough to get her a temporary place in a boarding and training facility where Stella has made amazing progress. She is learning how to enjoy being outside, walk on a leash, be around other dogs, basic commands and impulse control. We are now searching for the perfect foster home for Stella to learn how to live in a home.

Stella in training:

Stella's trainer says, \"While we still see the occasional unwanted behavior, it's more playful and quickly squashed. She is doing well - really has the cue down for fetch and tug, and knows Mine' for not grabbing toys when I pick them up. She wears a head collar pretty well, though still with the occasional tantrum. Doing great with dog play, and chooses avoidance when she can, which is a great trait to have.\

name: Rose
description:
Rose is a puller on the leash. Handler needs to learn how to control her while walking, and she would benefit from some leash training. She gets down and pulls hard.
She's bonded with her foster mom fast! But with her previous foster (also a woman), Rose exhibited jealousy. She's an 8.5 on the alpha scale. The lower dogs stay away from her but her foster mom's alpha, Sarge, likes her.
Rose is so smart and crate trained. She was rescued with two other dogs, Phantom and Muzzy. Rose and Phantom have to be separated at all times, even when being crated. Rose has figured out how to escape her collapsible wire kennel. Her foster uses plastic hay-baling twine to secure the front and rear panels. 
All 3 recovered nicely from their immiticide treatment, are taking a long course of twice-daily Doxycycline, and have had their first monthly treatment of Interceptor Plus Blue.
Rose is a 45 lbs American Staffordshire mix, and we believe she's 2-3 years old. She is currently in Texas, but transport can be arranged to an approved adopter!

If you're interested in adopting Rose, please fill out an adoption application on our website: www.safetails.org
If you have any questions on Rose, please feel free to message us via our rescue's Facebook page!

Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Theon is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Theon will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Theon will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Theon, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Just as winter is coming, so is this scrumptious litter of Husky/Lab pups we have rescued from a backyard breeder in SC.

The breeder claimed that the mama pup wanted nothing more to do with the puppies at 6 weeks, so they were headed to the shelter... and we all know the shelter is no place for a young puppy. While our rescue partner urged the breeder to keep the puppies with the mom for at least a couple more weeks, the answer was no.

The good news is that the puppies are healthy and strong, and were already eating solid food on their own. They will have their second distemper booster shot on 9/21, and we would love to bring them up and straight into adoptive homes.

Jon Snow is dark, mysterious and a little shy... just like his character. But when he feels comfortable around you, he loves tummy rubs and to play with his siblings!

He is a young puppy and as such, needs an adopter who is home most of the day so he can continue to be properly socialized and house trained. He is a typical, playful puppy and would love an experienced adopter to get him through all the stages of puppyhood, including teething and nipping... all worth it when you get to snuggle with all that puppy sweetness! 

He is not yet fully vaccinated and will not be until a couple of weeks after he receives his third distemper booster shot, so he needs an adopter who has a dedicated yard that isn't visited by potentially unvaccinated dogs, or be kept inside in a pen until the vet indicates it is safe to bring him to public places. As he develops, he would love a forever family who will bring him to puppy training classes to teach him the basics of being a good boy! 

Like most puppies, Jon Snow will need housetraining and crate training. We ask all of DC PAWS fosters to work on both house and crate training with their foster dog.

Jon Snow will need to be neutered at the adopter's expense by the age of 8 months, on or about 3/10/20, and provide proof of the surgery to DC PAWS Rescue. 

The adoption fee for this dog is $350. If you are interested in adopting Jon Snow, please submit an adoption application at https://dcpawsrescue.org/adoption-info/adoption-application-dogs/DC PAWS Rescue does our best to provide accurate and complete information about our adoptable animals. Please note that we cannot make any guarantees about age or breed; we rely upon our rescue partners and their veterinarians to make those assessments. We also cannot make any guarantees about housebreaking and animal temperament, as animals can behave differently through transition and in different environments.

Our shelter partners provide a basic vet screening for each animal we rescue, which includes necessary vaccinations, deworming, microchipping, and spay/neuter (unless the animal is too young or otherwise deemed by the vet to not be a good candidate for surgery). Please note that this is not a comprehensive medical exam and as such, may not identify any and all medical issues, though our goal is to flag any obvious health issues through the basic vet screening. We share all medical records with adopters and flag any known issues prior to adoption finalization. 

About DC PAWS Rescue

Our rescue is an all-volunteer, foster-based dog and cat rescue in the DC area. We rescue from rural shelters in the south, as well as local DC area shelters, such as Prince Georges County, MD and BARCS in MD.

Fosters make it possible for DC PAWS to save and care for homeless, neglected and abandoned animals! To learn about fostering dogs or cats for DC PAWS Rescue, please visit: http://dcpawsrescue.org/volunteer/fostering/foster-application

BE A SPONSOR:

For any of our animals! Sponsors help us provide critical medical care, food, boarding and other support for animals facing euthanasia. Individuals who sponsor a dog or cat receive special recognition on the animal's profile. Sponsorships can also be made in honor or memory of a loved one, and you may designate to whom DC Paws Rescue should provide notice of your gift.

name: Sofia
description:
Animal Profile: Sofia is an adorable and petite 9 lb chihuahua mix who was just rescued from a high kill shelter in CA. She has the cutest smile that quickly won over our transporter! Sofia joined us in Seattle on 9/15 and we'll post more information as we get to know her.

Update from her foster:
Sofia is a sweet heart and one of the gentlest dogs i have ever had! She is trusting and wants to please. She loves her people, and it only took me about an hour to become her person, she loves kids, and she loves other dogs. She doesn't seem to have had a lot of training before but she is learning really quickly. We have started today with \"sit\" and \"leave it\" and she's is doing great. Being food motivated has helped a ton. She will work hard for a little piece of cheese. Sofia is definitely out of the puppy phase and does not chew on anything which has been great! She is great in the crate at night and is getting more and more comfortable in there during the day. But she would much rather be with you or a dog buddy while you're home. We are also working on house training and making great progress. If you are looking for a sweet buddy for yourself or a playmate for your dog, Sofia is your girl!

description:

If your looking for a well behaved guy to give belly rubs, hangout, snuggle or go on adventures, then I'm your guy!

description:
My name is Lucille Fox and I am a wonderful 1 year old female Husky and Shepherd Mix who was just saved from a high-kill shelter in
California
where no one wanted me. I am a happy dog at 40 lbs. and need a home with a fenced in yard. Take me on car rides, walks in the park and I will become your very best friend. name: Lizzy
description:
Animal Profile: Lizzy (and her sibling Lani) are 10-month-old female red Dobie mixes who were just recently rescued from a kill shelter in California. While these girls did not have the best start in life, they are in great spirits. She is a sweet and loving girl, friendly, playful and submissive with other dogs.

Seattle Foster Updates:
Lizzy

already learned her name, how to sit, how to go up stairs, and is working on other basic commands. She's still doing well with house training, crate training and some basic obedience training, like lay down and stay. She's not the best with cats, so probably in a house without any. She would do best in a home with another resident dog as she doesn't like being alone! She loves to be with people or other animals. She is extremely curious about everything.

Lizzy

likes lots and lots of exercise. Long walks, but mostly runs, 2-3X/day. Sometimes she just likes to run all over the yard or have you throw a ball. She's such a giant sweetheart and will lay down next to your feet.

Lizzy

is okay in cars and did great when we took her on a hike. After waking up in the morning, going potty and getting a good stretch, she loves to come in the house, run upstairs going into each kids bedroom to wake them up for school.

She is too interested in small animals, such as cats and squirrels, so she is looking for a home without cats.

description:
Animal Profile: Nugget is an adorable chihuahua/dachshund mix who is an absolute gem of a pup! Originally rescued from a high kill shelter in CA, Nugget is now thriving in his Seattle-area foster home. His foster mom can't say enough good things about this little guy; from couch and bed snuggles to romping in the yard with his canine buddy, Nugget is a loving, affectionate, and sweet little guy. He loves treats, belly rubs, sun bathing, and any stuffed toy he can play tug-of-war with! He has done great around older kids and adults, walks great on leash, and does well in his crate. Nugget would love a canine buddy in his forever home, so he can continue to have a buddy to play chase with and snuggle up to during the day.

Seattle Foster Update:

Latest update: Oh my goodness.....I can't believe no one has snapped up this loveable little guy. He likes taking walks, playing with toys, cuddling, and hanging with my 10-year-old nephew. Nugget thinks cats are pretty cool and that any treat shaped like a stick is the only kind of \"real\" treat there is. Also......discovered a new talent over the past week. Little Nugget likes to \"sing!\" Cant wait to see what other new talents this little guy has! Third update: I just love this little guy! Toys and playing are now on the daily docket! He also has gotten to interact with a few older kids. He really enjoys the attention, belly rubs, and giving kisses. Second update: This little guy has come along way in 3 weeks. He hasn't had an accident in the house in 2 weeks, he knows \"sit\" and \"come,\" and he's working on learning other commands. He's started playing with toys, and is learning to play with other dogs. He does well on a leash and likes going to pet friendly stores and meeting other people. He does better with a playmate around, rather than being alone. First update: Nugget started off very shy and timid but quickly became the life of the party. He is a happy and inquisitive little pup. He gets along well with smaller dogs and is still getting used to seeing larger dogs in the neighborhood. He's good on a leash, loves going on walks, and doesn't mind his crate. And ... a big plus ... he gets along with the cats in our house. He has some separation anxiety, but it's getting better with each separation. Nugget loves to cuddle and is a real sweetie!

name: KRATOS
description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.
KRATOS was saved from a high kill shelter in Texas where dogs have just 3 dogs to be saved and transported to the rescue in Sebec, Maine. KRATOS is neutered, core vaccines, rabies, heartworm and tick-disease tested negative, de-wormed, monthly preventatives and micro-chipped. He has an estimated date of birth of 24 February 2018 and at the time of rescue in the end of August 2019, weighed around 28.00 pounds. The shelter has a breed listing of Husky Mix. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

KRATOS was adopted from the shelter but returned the day after as the family didn't have time for him.

KRATOS will be arriving at the rescue on Thursday, 12th Saturday and we will update when he has been here and settled so we can give a more accurate description of his personality and mannerisms. As time permits, we will take more pictures. You are welcome to complete and submit the adoption application if you are interested in giving him a forever home.

WE ARE NOT ABLE TO COMMENT HOW HE WILL BE AROUND CATS OR LIVESTOCK.



RATOS is available for adoption for an adoption fee of US $550.

This fee is not negotiable and is used to cover the rescue costs of pulling, vetting, health certificate, transport from Texas to Maine, monthly preventatives, supplements, food, general day to day cost of running a brick and mortar rescue and anything else that is needed. Canadian adopters need to know that customs charge 15% taxes when entering into Canada.

If you feel that you have the heart and home to give this precious soul a wonderful life, please go to our website, under the APPLICATION tab, complete, then submit the APPLICATION. Our process takes around 2-4 days, and ensuring your references are aware that we will be calling, could speed up the process. Once you have been approved, we discuss any questions in regards to the dog you are wanting to adopt, then you complete and submit the contract, make payment and then we can work out the pick up / transport arrangements.

Please do NOT submit an application if you are not looking to take home a new best friend within the next few weeks.

http://www.giveadogahome-sanantonio.org

ALL Dogs are LOCATED AT THE RESCUE IN SEBEC, MAINE. We post in various states along the east coast and Canada where we have had lots of successful adoptions to enable more exposure for these beautiful saved souls. Families will need to be prepared to travel to the rescue to meet and take home their new best friend. Sebec is located just outside the towns of Dover-Foxcroft and Milo (approx 8 miles) and approx 45 miles from Bangor. There are also lots of hotels, motels, pet friendly accommodations and wonderful camp-sites for the more adventurous families and what a great way to get to know your new best friend.
Give a Dog a Home, German Shepherd Dog Rescue

187 Downs Road, Sebec, Maine, 04481

giveadogahome@live.com

All pets adopted will be spay/neutered, micro-chipped, de-wormed,heartworm tested, rabies and relevant vaccinations.

NO DOG WILL BE ADOPTED TO BE AN OUTSIDE DOG!

If you would like to start the adoption our process is below:

Submit Application with two personal references and a vet reference.

If you have never had pets and do not have a vet, we will need THREE personal references.

Ensure references are people who know you and your lifestyle well.

Applicant MUST inform vet and references that someone from GaDaH will be calling.

As long as we are able to contact your vet and references, it takes just 1-3 days to process and hopefully approve applications.

If you rent we will need an approval letter for the breed of dog you are wanting to adopt from your landlord on official letterhead paper or email.

Rescue processes and hopefully approves applications.

Once approved, rescue invites applicant to come to the rescue to meet your chosen dog/s, spend time with him/her

and then hopefully take him/her home.

We do NOT hold dogs so if you are unable to come within a week or so of submitting your application the dog will still be available for adoption to other families.

For Canadian adopters, all that is needed to get them across the border into Canada is a current rabies certificate and proof of adoption, which is the adoption contract. Both of which are included in the medical file you will get when you adopt. (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/aphis/pet-travel/by-country/pettravel-canada)

Ensure ALL Fields are filled in, if something is relevant, then put n/a or something in so it recognizes an entry.

We do not recommend using a phone or ipad since these applications for some reason don't tend to come through and you will have spent a lot of time on the application for nothing as it will need to be re-done.

Once we have you approved we can schedule an appointment for you to come to meet

him/her at the rescue in Sebec, Mane and then hopefully take them home to start your new life.

I just have to work on an appointment basis as I run a boarding/day care business and the rescue and so am really busy, but by planning ahead of time I can be pretty flexible.

description:

LOBO-1 is neutered, core vaccines, rabies, heartworm & tick disease tested negative, de-wormed, monthly preventatives and micro-chipped. He has an estimated date of birth of 5 June 2017 and at the time of rescue in the middle of June 2019, weighed around 80.00 pounds. He is listed as a Great Pyrenees. We have no way of knowing the exact breed, it is up to individuals to decide what breed they think is most likely.

When LOBO arrived at the rescue he was so skinny and depressed and wasn't interested in much. After a few days of good food he started to show more interest and to come out of his shell. After a week or so, he was a happy boy and I let him out for playtime with a young female German Shepherd. It was clear Lobo didn't know how to play and he was definitely growing into his body, legs were going all over. After a few hours with the GSD he was having the best time, running and chasing and falling over.

After a few weeks I brought Lobo over to the house to live with me and the other dogs and small dogs and he has been great - he is the perfect height for the kitchen counter, so best not to leave food out. He has got much more confident and has lots of friends of all ages and sizes.

He does use the dog door to go outside but he is not going to know to let you know he wants to go out - so we cannot say he is fully house-trained.

He does need training and a family that takes this seriously is important. Training is not just about obedience, but also about learning each other's body language and mannerisms.

description:
Please contact Jenny Cope (giveadogahome@live.com) for more information about this pet.

He has been de-wormed, micro chipped and received any necessary monthly preventatives. He has an estimated date of birth of 2 January 2018 and he weighs around 24 pounds. His mother we believe is a Belgian Shepherd and so he is most likely a Belgian Shepherd Dog Mix, we have no idea what breed the father is. We are looking for families with knowledge of experience of working breed needs to ensure they get a good balance of mental and physical exercise.

HUA-HUA is a cautious boy, but once he has gained trust and feels safe he is very affectionate and loving. He likes to climb on your knee, or snuggle up on the bed, but has always been with his siblings. He will need time to get used to new people and new places, but once trust has been gained he is a great all round boy.

He would benefit from a family who understands the importance of mental stimulation as well as physical exercise. description:
Buddy Bones is a sweet, gentle soul who has recently found his goofy and playful side.  He is still learningÂ how to be a dog and enjoys mellow days laying in the sun andÂ feeling loved, as well as going on walks.  He loves having his butt scratched and thinks he is a lap dog.

His angels in SC provided the care he needed to be able to transport him into our long term care.  His body is scarred, as is his heart, but he continues to make a miraculous recovery every day since the day he was found.

name: Sookie
description:
You can fill out an adoption application online on our official website.Sookie came to rescue from South Carolina. A good Samaritan had reported that they saw her lying in the grass on the side of her owners house, covered in fleas, and emaciated. Animal Control investigated and took her. Sookie is an 8 year old female Boxer blend. On intake, she was extremely underweight, and she has cataracts that make it difficult to see. It has been determined that she is also a diabetic, and a new family should know that she will require insulin as part of her daily care. In addition, Sookie had a small mass on her leg that was determined to be Mast Cell. She has had surgery with our vet to remove the mass and has healed wonderfully. She is now doing so great in her foster home but would really love a home to call her very own!
Her foster Mom says she is the perfect mix of couch potatoe and playmate
! Sookie is a vocal lady who definitely has her own hilarious personality to show you. When Sookie isn't curled up on your lap (Yes, ON your lap), in her bed, or on the floor next to you she is exploring her surroundings with her curious little nose or demanding your attention with her adorable little grumbles! To Sookie, there aren't too many things greater in life than cuddling with the nearest human or playing with a fun toy! Speaking of toys, Sookie loves a good game of tug-of-war or a round of squeaking her favorite squeaky toy. She also enjoys walks full of exploring and sniffing and is more than willing to accompany you on an easy hike with some more leash training.
Sookie is very tolerant of all kinds of petting, even some attention that might annoy some dogs. She does occasionally play a little rough so, supervision around the little ones is never a bad idea. She really
enjoys interacting with other dogs, especially those who want to play with her. Once introductions are done she is happy to play with her canine buddy or simply relax on the couch next to them.
Sookie has what some consider a complicated relationship with cats. She desperately wants to play with them but in true Boxer form, she doesn't seem to understand that hissing and swatting isn't playing. A kitty that loves playtime as much as her would be a dream come true to Sookie.
Sookie has made huge strides in her leash walking but, her cataracts do inhibit
her vision somewhat so unexpected objects in her path may trip her up.
In other areas she is a lady. She waits patiently (with the exception of a few grumbles) for her food and allows you to take it away with nothing worse than a pout. She is a pro at receiving her insulin and acts as if she doesn't even know you're there when administering it.
She really is the full package and any family would be VERY lucky to call her their own.
Sookie is up to date on shots and will be spayed prior to placement in her forever home. If you would like to adopt Sookie, please put your application in here: http://www.rescuedogsrocknyc.org

name: Bowie
description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8094

Im Bowie! I am estimated to be a 6-year-old Catahoula Leopard Dog mix. Im a big boy, weighing about 75 lbs and I came to OPH from South Carolina, so Im a southern gentleman. Howdy-do!

My foster mom thinks Im awesome! She says Im crate-trained, I havent had a single accident in my foster home, and I only bark when the other dogs in my foster home bark to welcome someone home. I sometimes talk and sing when my food is being prepared, because I love mealtime! I also get very excited about going out and I spring about 3 feet straight up off the ground when its time to go! I am a strong boy, so I get walked on an easy-walk harness, which works well for me. My foster mom says Im smart to avoid obstacles and not get my leash tangled around them. Yay, me!

I can get nervous and anxious around other dogs, so I would probably do best in a home as an only dog, but I think I would do well in almost any environment: apartment, townhouse, single-family home. As long as I can be part of the family and show my devotion, I will be a happy boy.

Come meet me!

Im a Beagle mix and estimated to be about 1 years old. Im a sweet boy and I currently weigh about 32 lbs. I came to OPH from a shelter in South Carolina. I love it here with my foster family and have been hanging out, getting treated for heartworms (they are yucky) and learning new tricks. I've finished my heartworm treatment (yay!) and am ready to find my forever family. 

Some things about me:
* I LOVE treats. What's that mean to you? It means that I am very trainable to tag along with you during your daily travels and can likely learn lots of fun tricks with you.
* I LOVE to play ball. Hopefully you will too. It helps get my energy out as well so we can watch TV later.

* I like everyone in my foster family so I'm sure I will like you too! They have older kids and I love being around them. 
* I hope you have some toys or that we can get some. I love to play with them. Wanna go to the pet store and pick some out?
* Here's the best part, are you ready? I have not had any accidents in my foster familys house. My mom says I may need a day to adjust to your house but shes assured me that I will quickly know your routine as well and not have any accidents there too.

I'm a super happy boy, my tail is always wagging. Let's find a time for you to meet me and see what a fun little guy I can be. There are some neat video's featuring none other than me below so you can see me in action. (I'm famous you know, I have my own videos and everything)


Click here and here to see me in action with OPH! 

Click here to see me playing with a foster friend. 

I'll be here hanging out with my foster family in Oakton, VA. Ask my foster mom for directions, she will be happy to share them with you. Don't wait! I'll be snatched up soon she says.

description:
ADOPT ME ONLINE: https://ophrescue.org/dogs8330

Hi! My name is Will Forte. 

Im a Beagle mix and estimated to be about 1 years old. Im a sweet boy and I currently weigh about 32 lbs. I came to OPH from a shelter in South Carolina. I love it here with my foster family and have been hanging out, getting treated for heartworms (they are yucky) and learning new tricks. I've finished my heartworm treatment (yay!) and am ready to find my forever family. 

Some things about me:
* I LOVE treats. What's that mean to you? It means that I am very trainable to tag along with you during your daily travels and can likely learn lots of fun tricks with you.
* I LOVE to play ball. Hopefully you will too. It helps get my energy out as well so we can watch TV later. 
* I LOVE to get my zoomies out outside. My foster family has told me that's where we do this and we play nice inside and try not to run too much. 
* Do you like to explore? Hey, I do too! Let's go on hikes together and explore all that's out there in Virginia and beyond. 
* AHHH...my crate. It's my quiet and calm time and I don't mind it one bit. It's a pretty great place to nap. 
* I like everyone in my foster family so I'm sure I will like you too! They have older kids and I love being around them. 
* I hope you have some toys or that we can get some. I love to play with them. Wanna go to the pet store and pick some out?
* Here's the best part, are you ready? I have not had any accidents in my foster familys house. My mom says I may need a day to adjust to your house but shes assured me that I will quickly know your routine as well and not have any accidents there too.

I'm a super happy boy, my tail is always wagging. Let's find a time for you to meet me and see what a fun little guy I can be. There are some neat video's featuring none other than me below so you can see me in action. (I'm famous you know, I have my own videos and everything)


Click here and here to see me in action with OPH! 

Click here to see me playing with a foster friend. 

I'll be here hanging out with my foster family in Oakton, VA. Ask my foster mom for directions, she will be happy to share them with you. Don't wait! I'll be snatched up soon she says. 

This dog tested positive for heartworm disease before arriving to the rescue. The disease was treated while in foster care. Heartworm disease is transmitted to a dog through a bite from an infected mosquito. With monthly preventatives, the disease is completely preventable. Read about heartworm disease here: Read more about heartworm disease here here

With limited resources, the shelters are forced to put down 50-90% of the animals that come in the front door. OPH provides pet adoption services to families located in VA, DC, MD, PA and neighboring states. OPH is a 501(c)(3) organization and is 100% donor funded. name: Bobby
description:
Bobby is a handsome catch who comes to our rescue from South Carolina.  When Bobby went into our care he was shut down and withdrawn.  Through time, patience and lots of love from his foster family, he has emerged a happy, friendly and playful guy.  His little nubbie tail wags, wags, wags when he greets you at the door.  Bobbyâs breed is anyoneâs guess.  He looks like he has some collie in him, and maybe a little lab.  We do not guarantee any breed mix/combo.   Bobby is approximately 5 years old, is 57 pounds and is housetrained. 

Bobby has transformed into a playful, cuddly, loving dog who is usually touching, leaning against, or curled up with you during downtime.  He loves, loves, loves the water.  Heâll play in hoses and irrigation systems, so heâs a lot of fun when youâre washing your car.  Bobby has been for a few boat rides and will get into the water freestyle when stopped at the favorite swimming hole.  He gets excited at just the sight of water and gives you no trouble when itâs bath time!  Bobby knows his basic manners and commands, and likes pleasing you and getting treats.  His favorite treat is Redi-Whip straight from the can!  He is a stuffed toy dog and will self-entertain by throwing around stuffed toys, which occasionally end up getting tossed onto countertops!  He likes to play tug-of-war and will do zoomies in the yard when heâs got a toy in his mouth.  

Bobby enjoys walks, and is great in the car.  Heâs just an all-around outdoor enthusiast, and we would love to see him adopted to people who will take him on outdoor adventures.  Bobby will need a little time readjusting to his forever home, so we are looking for a patient adopter who will commit time to training so he continues his transformation.  Bobby gets along great with other dogs and he is also great with cats.  He will actually snuggle up with his foster familyâs cat from time to time.  He would do fine as the only dog in the home or with other animals.   

Bobby has been fully vetted, is heartworm negative and is up to date on all vaccines.  He is neutered, microchipped, and on current heartworm prevention and flea prevention. Bobby does have a back leg that ever so slightly curves inwards.  The vet checked him out and said itâs fine.  It doesnât bother him at all, and it certainly doesnât hold him back from zoomies and swimming!

Precious is a fun little piglet who has adjusted beautifully to life in her busy foster home. She doesn't see well but likes to explore and is happy to make new friends. Her owner seemed to be taking good care of her, as she came to the shelter with extensive veterinary records, but for some reason she wasn't wanted anymore and was left there to die. Precious is diabetic and takes insulin twice a day, which is a difficult condition for the shelter to handle- they did not plan on being able to keep her there long, but luckily we had space and she made the long trip up from South Carolina. 
?
We've never had a pet with diabetes before and were a little nervous about keeping up with Precious' meds, but she takes her injections with no problems and the insulin is very inexpensive. All in all she has been a sweet, loving, and easy addition to our foster family, and we are so happy we were able to get her out of the shelter safely!

name: Lady Beaufort
description:
This Southern Belle has traveled all the way from South Carolina to find her forever home here in New Jersey. When you meet Lady it is obvious that she did at one time have a home where someone taught her the commands that she knows and how to play her favorite game of \"fetch\".

Lady has been in foster since 1/7/18. She has been a perfect houseguest, is completely house and crate trained. She goes right into her crate every morning when I leave for work and is sleeping when I get home. Lady loves her person, loves cuddling and to be pet. She is a calm dog that loves her toys and a good nap on the couch. On walks she doesn't pay attention to other dogs and walks calmly next to them when on pack walks. We do not know much about Lady's past, but she does scare easily, so she would do best in a calm household with older, respectful children, and not much traffic in and out of the house. She takes a while to warm up to new people but once she does she loves you. Lady is a very special girl that deserves a loving home of her own. She is silly, full of personality and one the sweetest dogs I've ever had the pleasure of fostering. She is so easy to love and will make a wonderful addition to the right household.

If you want to meet Lady go to EHRDOGS.ORG and submit an application. Don't forget to ask for LADY BEAUFORT - she is waiting so patiently at the kennel for someone to fall in love with her and bring her home. Could that someone be you?

name: Buster White
description: Buster White is BTN's longest resident.  Buster came to BTN from South Carolina where he was seized by AC as a welfare case.  Buster had no tibia and he needed his ankle fused.  We suspect he was hit by a car and left to heal on his own.  He was starving to death and heartworm positive.  We worked with VOSM and Buster is in good shape now..  Buster loves other dogs and may or may not be okay with cats.  He's gets along great with people.  Buster is BTN's poster child for happiness.  He loves life and is thrilled just to have a bed, food and somewhere warm to stay.  He's currently heartworm negative and his legs are repaired  If you can find a place for Buster White in your heart, please email me.  He's fully vetted and microchipped.

name: Geneva
description:
GENEVA AMERICAN STAFFORDSHIRE TERRIER MIX TAN (RED)  & WHITE ARRIVED 9/4/19 ~46 LBS ~ THREE-YEARS-OLD FEMALE CHIPPED 

Geneva is one of five dogs that were rescued by PAWS from South Carolina during Hurricane Dorian. These lovely dogs are sweet, loving, lively and amazing! Elmore SPCA was happy to help a total of 14 dogs find their way towards their new beginning by being able to take in five of the fourteen dogs which made the transport possible. PAWS Rescue is amazing and so is Kershaw County Humane Society for keeping the faith that these pups would find new homes! 

Geneva  is a super loving staffie! She is very loving  and she loves to be pet and loves to be around her people once she gets to know you.  She seems to like the other dogs she has met in SC and here in NY! This lovely lady was very difficult to photograph because every time we pet her she closed her eyes and tried to snuggle in closer to us She is learning loose leash walking skills, but is pretty strong and will pull when there is something of high value available, ie food or a person to pet her.  She gets super excited when she is behind a barrier or a fence and she sees other dogs and does that pitty screech but it isn't an aggressive behavior. She is a bit shy of loud noises, door ways and fast and loud traffic. Although she is a bit wary and skittish at first, she has shown no aggressive behaviors.  If anything Geneva only wants a warm lap to curl up on and a loving hand to stroke her head. 

Geneva  is a great dog who has a ton of love to give. She would benefit from having a family who will help her gain some confidence and who will take the time to help her learn that not all humans are jerks!  Geneva is a love and seems to love everyone she has met here at the shelter, 

Geneva is current on rabies, distemper and bordetella vaccinations, has tested negative for heartworm, lyme, ehrlichia and anaplasmosis, is spayed and chipped and is ready to go to her new home! Come in and meet this adorably sweet and loving dog.

name: Tater
description:
Meet Tater! This adorable little nugget was found abandoned on a property in rural Alabama with his buddy, Sparky, when he was only three months old. Thankfully, a Good Samaritan saw the pups, and brought them home to safety. This Good Samaritan is also the mom of one of our volunteers, so of course we wanted to help these adorable puppies find their way home.

We don't know if they are from the same litter or have different fathers, but they were lucky to have each other when they were out there on their own. They were a healthy weight when found, so we suspect they were not on their own for long.

Both puppies have been well cared for and initally lived in AL with 2 stay-at-home parents, multiple dogs to romp and play with, a cat, and two birds. They had regular play time with 2 teen grandkids, and were always great with the kids. Tater has a short coat, larger ears, and is the larger of the two pups. He's growing quickly and is very gentle with his doggy friends. Tater knows sit and lay down, and knows to ask to go out. He is already crate trained and well socialized with other dogs.

FOSTER UPDATE - 9/12/19

Tater arrived last week and is being fostered in Reston, VA. This adorable little nugget has really grown since our last update and arrived in N. VA just this past weekend. His brother, Sparky, was just adopted on Sunday, so now it's Tater's turn.

Tater has been living with other dogs, a cat, and two birds, and has had regular exposure to the grandkids while in Alabama. He's excellent with other dogs and would benefit from having a confident, social dog in his new home who can show him the ropes. He is a little unsure after being separated from Sparky and is adjusting to city life, so he's timid and tentative around new people. He was initially hesitant around his new foster dad, but he warmed up within two days, and once he's comfortable with you, he's a loving puppy who likes to snuggle up on the couch and nap on you. He's only been here five days, so he's still adjusting to a lot of change.

We are looking for a family who understands that Tater needs a little time and patience to settle in...as most puppies do! He's never aggressive and is still a puppy, and he just needs time to acclimate. His foster mom has been taking him to pet stores, and to get him accustomed to new people, she's had a dog walker come in the house and she introduces him to strangers . He's progressing every day and is ready to go home!

name: Felicia
description:
Instead of \"Bye Felicia\" say \"Hi Felicia!\"  Sweet, sweet, adorable Felicia.  She is a happy, goofy, playful and affectionate little girl despite horrendously cruel treatment she was subjected to in her past.  She may take a little time getting to trust you as humans were not very kind to her previously.  She has had extensive professional obedience training and is very good on a leash.  She does need to be an only dog  in a home with NO children.

Being her owner will have some challenges, but they will be well worth the effort of gaining her love and trust!  Once you have earned her trust she becomes an affectionate goofball extraordinaire!  She is so deserving of a normal pain free life.  Please help us make that a reality.

Why she is the way she is:  Felicia was rescued from a dog fighting operation in Tennessee.  She was extremely malnourished and emaciated and lived at the end of a massive, heavy chain for years.  She had a very serious tick borne blood disease called babesia at the time but she has been treated for that and is now clear of it.  Her teeth had been filed down to the roots because she was used for breeding and this prevented her from injuring the other dog.  Our vet removed the ones that were badly damaged and infected, so sometimes her tongue hangs out.  We think it just adds to her charm.

If you, or someone you know, are interested in adopting or fostering, please visit our site at www.maydaypitbullrescue.org or send us an email at info@maydaypitbullrescue.org

name: Lucy
description:
LUCY IS CURRENTLY HOME WITH HER CURRENT OWNER WHILE SHE SEARCHES FOR HER NEW HOME. If you are interested in meeting her please email brogers@mspca.org or call 617 541-5083. Please do not email the main adoption center line or phone number. 

Lucy is a 6yr old spayed female shepherd/lab mix. She is extremely affectionate and would spend all  day in your lap if you let her! She was adopted as a rescue at 2yrs old from Tennessee. She lives with two older adults at the moment but lived with a toddler for a year (when toddler was 6 months to 18 months) and was great with toddler. She also lived with a cat during this time and got along with the cat well. She does like to get up on the couch if allowed (or if not allowed :)). She responds to some commands, sit, down, come and stay, esp for a treat. She is crated at night and loves her crate. She goes on Doggie dates where she can run and be with dogs and does well off leash with dogs but does bark and pull while on leash. She is not great for walks and pulls hard and at 64lbs she can be hard to control. Her owner has a fenced in yard so she is used to being able to go outside in the yard vs. going on walks. She is good about going outside for the bathroom. Her owner is away for 3 months of the year now and and feels she can't give Lucy the home she deserves. name: Sammy - Gentle Spirit
description:
NYS Registered Rescue # RR102
NGPR dogs are in foster homes throughout the U.S., NOT Beacon, NY. View full listing, fee and online application at - www.nationalpyr.org/rescue-dogs (sorry, no phone submissions, but if you would like more information you can call 877-739-3582 or email us at renpyrgroup@yahoo.com).

Secure VISIBLE fencing is required; invisible fencing WILL NOT contain this breed.

This adorable young Pyrenees boy is Sammy. He is a wonderful dog with a gentle spirit who came to rescue terribly neglected from a farm in Tennessee. Sammy and his buddy Rasta were left on an abandoned farm to guard chickens and a donkey. There was somebody feeding them once a week if they were lucky, and he is such a sweet boy he never even killed a single chicken. Both Sammy and Rasta are very friendly dogs, just great with strangers. We know they are good with donkeys and chickens and they are fine with other dogs as well. We don't think they have met a cat yet as they are still in boarding but we suspect they will be good with everyone and everything. This tricolor gorgeous boy is certainly a sight for sore eyes and NYBC is grateful that we are able to be part of his new journey. 
He's about 3 years old and ok with properly introduced dogs. Submit your application today to make this boy your own.

name: Reggie
description: Reggie is a loyal and loving young Bull Terrier mix from Tennessee. When Reggie first arrived he was very scared of the shelter and human interaction. He quickly grew out of that when he realized we were here to help him. He is a staff favorite for not only his goofy personality but also his affectionate side. He absolutely loves toys and is very food motivated. Reggie knows sit, stay, and come but he is eager to learn new tricks! He has a lot of energy cooped up inside a kennel but he loves playing with other dogs here, which really makes him happy. He gets nervous in his kennel, so it's best you have a staff member introduce you to Reggie outdoors or in a room at the shelter. Reggie would do best in a home with older children.

name: Theon
description: Theon is an absolutely wonderful petite brindle pit bull/ mix. He was transferred from a full Tennessee animal control because he was scheduled to be euthanized due to lack of space. Theon had come to that animal control with an injury. TAPS had Theon evaluated by one of the local veterinarians. His broken femur had already healed and could cause more damage if an attempt to fix. Theon is currently in a foster home including 2 other pit bulls. He is getting lots of love and attention. Theon continues to gain muscle in his back 2 legs. He loves zoomies, chasing his foster fur-siblings, eating double bacon cheeseburgers and strawberries. Theon is learning some basic commands such as sit, on and off and leash walking. If you are interested in this boy please get your application in, applications will be screened for best fit for this sweet boy.

name: Elroy
description: Hi!  I'm Elroy!  I'm a happy-go-lucky guy who gets along with everybody!  I love walks and adventures but my passion is TOYS!!!  My belief is you can never have too many!  I like to go on hunts & gather up all I can find, then lie on a pile of them so I can squeak & chew & shake at will.  My foster mom laughs at me when I knock over all the toy bins so I can add to my stash.  She says I'm like a toddler who scatters stuff all around but she loves me anyway!  I came from a Tennessee puppy mill where I didn't have toys or people to love me so I'm making up for lost time!  I'm only two years old and like to refer to myself as \"big boned\"; I do enjoy a good meal!  Mom's been trying to keep me on a diet but I steal the other dogs' food when she's not looking.  :-)   I am a bit mischevious but I think it adds to my charm!  Don't you?  I like playing with my doggy friends & exploring in the yard but I would be happy as an only dog as well as long as there were...can you guess?...toys!!!  My adoption fee is $200; I've been (gulp) neutered, microchipped and am current on vaccinations as well as heartworm/flea preventative.  You can find an application at waldosmuttleycrew.org.  Won't you be my \"furever\" family?

name: ZEKE
description:
ZEKE came to the rescue back in September 2016 from an abuse case in Tennessee. He had some health issues to battle but he had no problem overcoming them and healing completely
He was then adopted in January 2017 to a family with younger kids. We thought it was a good match but we discovered that Zeke needs a stronger owner to keep him in line. He needs to be in a home with a schedule, that includes his walking and exercise time. Zeke loves to walk and needs to be walked to burn off a lot of his puppy energy. You have to watch him otherwise he will become the alpha of the house, and you. He is fine in his foster home because he knows Mom is the alpha and she won't let the little stinker dominate the house. Besides loving walks, he loves to sit on the couch with you, riding in the car, going and meeting new people. He is about 20lbs and 3 yrs old. He is very affectionate.

name: Sprinkles
description:
**Please read Sprinkle's entire profile, which includes a link to the adoption application. Thank you!** 

Sprinkles is a 11-month-old, 50-pound Shar-pei mix gal.

Hello! Some people call me Coco, but I like my nickname âSprinklesâ better. Let me tell you a little about myself. I am from a southern Tennessee county, where there is no animal control and strays and unwanted animals are in abundance. My mom had me and my siblings last fall at a nice ladies house. One by one my siblings were given away until only I was left. I donât know why no one wanted me, I was just as playful and loving as the others. 

So, day after day I waited for my turn. Then, suddenly one day a strange lady drove up the driveway and I was put into the back of her car. I was really nervous because I did not know what to expect. She took me to her house where I met lots of dogs and cats who made me feel at ease. The kind lady told me that I was her new foster pup and that I would never have to live outside again and that she loved me. 

She LOVED me! It was so nice to hear! I am currently working on becoming the perfect family member.   I get into my crate with no problem and I am house trained.   I love playing with the other dogs.   I haven't been around kids but my foster thinks I will do well with older kids (only because of my size).  I am learning to be the best pup I can everyday! I am looking for a fur-ever family where I can continue to learn and grow.  Could you be my fur-ever family?
 

Sprinkles will be UTD on vaccinations and spayed or neutered at the time of adoption. Due to the young age of this puppy, he/she is not housebroken or trained. All puppies require professional training to become the best family member they can be.
To adopt or learn more about Sprinkles, you must fill out an adoption application. To find the application, copy and paste this URL into your browser: WWW.GDRNE.COM/ADOPTION-APPLICATION [Adoption Fee: $425]  **  PLEASE READ: If a dog is listed, then s/he is currently available for adoption. Their information is correct to the best of our abilities and the information we have been given as of the day of posting. Please note, GDRNE does not guarantee the breed of any dog or puppy unless stated that we have run DNA. All breeds listed are educated estimates. Our dogs are rescued from various situations. It is most likely that both their parents were strays and even if not, mixes of some sort and that their grandparents were mixes as well. The dog may have some genetic material of an American Staffordshire Terrier (pit bull). The dogs are usually mixes of many breeds, making them a breed all their own - a True and adorable American MUTT. If you are interested in this dog, you must submit an application. Great Dog is not a shelter so there is no building you can visit. Our dogs live in private foster homes until adopted. To learn more about our *shelterless* rescue, adoption fees, and procedures, review the list of Frequently Asked Questions on our website at WWW.GDRNE.COM.

name: Red aka Quintero
description:
Why is Red ( Gia Quintero) smiling ??? Well because he knows heâs so close to finding a family of his own. This handsome 3 yo ( approx) boy is so sweet! He loves to run and play and acts like a big puppy. Heâs very affectionate and loving and would love a home where he gets to be active but also to snuggle with his people. Red is about 50lbs and has a gorgeous gleaming coat ! He is a friendly and sociable boy and is waiting for his family. Red could use some help on basic manners, as he still acts like a puppy. We think with proper exercise and a stable home, he will learn very quickly :-) Heâs a smart and sweet boy and eager to please. 
He is fully vetted and arriving in NY on 8/24. His adoption fee is $375 which includes his transport from Tennessee. 
Please fill out an application for this adorable boy today and come meet him at our adoption center in Brewster NY. www.snarrnortheast.org

name: Hudson
description:
Weight: 55 pounds (approx)

Personality: Hudson was rescued from a shelter in Tennessee. He was surrendered because he was an escape artist (as Huskies tend to be). He'd never met a kennel he didn't want to dig out of, however since we've taken him into Singing Dog Farm, we haven't had any issues with him escaping! However, because of his previous Houdini antics, we would recommend a very secure yard with at least 6-fee tall fencing. Hudson is house trained, and absolutely adores children. Like, really adores them. Hudson is a wonderful dog with high energy who loves to run around the yard with the \"zoomies\" and has such an affection for people. Great on a leash and rides well in cars too! A busy and active home would be great for Hudson. He does exceptionally well with children too! Don't let this boy pass you by...

name: Lemaster Steele
description:
Hi, my name is Lemaster Steele but foster mom calls me either Lemmy or Lem. She only uses my full name if I get into something that I shouldn't be messing with. I am a 2 year old border collie, boxer, lab mix from Tennessee. I am about 32 pounds and was born on July 2, 2017. I couldn't wait until July 4th for the entire world to celebrate my birthday so I came 2 days early.

When I first meet a human I may be a little quiet. When I become comfortable I will bark to let them know when a stranger comes near the house. I also will bark for a little while when my human leaves the house because I would much rather be with them than left home alone. If I have a companion dog I will feel a little more comfortable when my human leaves the house.

It wouldn't be good for me to go to a home with cats as they do not like me always chasing them around which is what I really love to do all the time.

I am very inquisitive so if you wouldn't like any edible items to disappear when you are not around, please don't leave them out within my reach.

My foster mom is teaching me the word \"Wait\" so she can open the door and go out and in before me so that I don't accidentally trip her by speeding out ahead of her. When she says the word \"Okay\" then I can join her outside or inside. I also have learned to sit and wait while my food dish is put down and then I start eating when the word \"Okay\" is said.

I am a very active little fellow so if my human lives in a house with a fenced yard to run around in, it would make me really happy.

I do occasionally enjoy just chilling on the couch with my family watching television or a video or just sleeping in bed with them. I also walk well on a leash, am house-trained, crate-trained, love chasing vermin in the yard, going on car rides and chewing on my Nylabone. I do like playing with toys but do not know how to fetch yet.

This is just a little bit about me. As you can see, I am an all around great guy who would love to find a loving family, preferably with another dog, who will welcome me into their home.

If you are intrigued by what I told you and would like to meet me, just fill out an adoption application at www.ehrdogs.org and don't forget to put my name, Lemaster Steele on it. When it is approved, it will be forwarded to my foster mom who will contact you and arrange a date and time for us to meet.

I am anxiously waiting to hear from you...

name: XP Sami or Spanky in Tennessee - URGENT!
description:
URGENT! These 2 dogs are in Tennessee but are in desperate need of rehoming separately! The owner must leave her home on July 1st and these dogs still need places to go - a number of other animals in the home have already found placement but no one will give these dogs a chance. The owner does not want to drop them off at a shelter in Tennessee, if she can avoid it.

Sami is a senior Black Lab mix who is extremely skittish but lovable. He gets along with most dogs. Over the years he has gotten along with all the animals on my parents' farm except for Spanky.

We're not sure what Spanky is mixed with. He is about 5-7 years old. He is playful and lovable. He has gotten along with his playmate Si but does not like Sami. He loves to carry his blanket with him. He is a really good farm dog - he always knows when coyotes are on the property and is great at chasing them away from their goats. He is a drooler especially when he is happy.

These dogs do NOT belong to 11th Hour Rescue but we have been asked to help network them for separate adopters. If you can help at all, please contact Jesse directly at jess85_19@hotmail.com - the animals are currently located in Tennessee. These dogs should go to separate homes as they prefer the company of other dogs to each other.

There are also 5 cats in need of placement - they are siblings, male and neutered, about 3.5 years old. There are 2 beige, 2 with grey/white stripes and one all grey stripe. All are friendly although the all grey is still a little cranky but he is coming around. They are all indoor cats, they have never been outside. They are listed on EHR's web site under XP 5 Cats in Tennessee.

name: Bojangles
description:
Bojangles is a fetching 7 month old pup and is about 55 lbs.  While we are not sure on breed, husky mix or GSD mix make our short list.  We expect he will be medium/large sized when full grown.  He is neutered, up to date on shots, micro chipped and on heart worm prevention.

We found Bojangles in a rural Louisiana shelter and he was listed as deaf and just 6 weeks old.  Luckily we had a local foster who was able to go and pull him and foster him for the first few weeks until he could make his way to TN.

Once here, we discovered that he does have some hearing ability.  He has been fostered with a dog trainer who has been working with him on both clicker, whistle and remote vibration collar training.  We don't know how his hearing will progress or digress as he gets older, so any family who adopts sweet Bo must continue working on his training.  His trainer has offered to help Bo's new family with training techniques and routines to help them get on the right track. We are working on potty training, but that is something that will need to be continued in her new home with lots of love and support.

Bo is a sweet and loving pup who is excelling in his foster home and with his training.  He is smart and eager to learn.  He is crate and leash trained.  He does well with other dogs, cats and kids and would do best with another young companion dog to play with.  To try to keep Bo as safe as possible, we are requiring a physically fenced in yard.  We also would prefer to adopt him out within a 2 hour radius of Cookeville, TN due to his special needs.

Bojangles is currently located in Tennessee and the adoption fee is $250.  Transportation may be available to out of state adopters for an additional cost depending on the area. The first step in our process is submitting the application.  We are happy to set up a meet and greet once an application has been approved. If you would like to adopt Bojangles please fill out our online adoption application at http://safehaventn.com/ .

name: Mustard
description:
Mustard was part of a pair. He came in with Brit but after an evaluation period, we found them not to be a bonded pair. Mustard is 11 years
but acts like he is 8.
. Mustard is a friendly outgoing guy who is happy and a wiggle butt. he is on the tall side. He was owner by the same family all of his life but was made to live outdoors until they moved and then he journeyed his way from Texas to Las Vegas. Now he is looking for a home to spend the rest of his life in. He does well with other dogs but is also quite independent. We just had the holistic dentist clean up his teeth.

adoption fee is $200 Adoption fees go back to and cover all of the medical for all of the dogs. All dogs are spayed/neutered, vaccinated and micro chipped upon adoption and many have received further treatment for such things as lump removal, severe ear infections, leg injuries, etc..
For more information or to submit an adoption application, please visit our website at http://www.southernnevadabeaglerescue.com . We are also on Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/SouthernNevadaBeagleRescueFoundation . Come meet and play with our available dogs at Las Vegas area dog parks. Times and locations can be found at http://www.meetup.com/beagles-207/ . Contact us or check our Facebook updates ahead of time if you are interested in meeting a particular dog. All our dogs are in foster homes so not all are available to attend all our park meetups.
Our meetup group playdates allow you to socialize your beagle with his/her own breed at dog parks with large fenced areas where the beagles can run and play off-leash. Beagle enthusiasts, come bay with us..... AROOOOOOOOOOOO!

name: Edsel
description: You know a dog is really nice when her intake exam notes call her \"very sweet\". Edsel came to Best Friends in July 2019 from Texas and has been winning hearts ever since. Edsel has done excellent with a skin treatment that has greatly improved her coat condition. She has started duty as a tour dog, and meets and greets our afternoon visitors with a smile and a wag of her tail. Edsel is much more popular than the namesake car, and will make a great addition to your home.

name: Timmy
description: Gentle, affectionate Timmy is a hugger and a leaner. He just wants to be close to people, and he is happy to do whatever you are doing, whether it's lounging, hiking, training or running. At Dogtown, he has been improving his dog skills, and he's gotten along great with pretty much everyone. Timmy was born in 2016 and came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. He can be a little nervous in new situations, and he likes to jump up and offer hugs, so he is working on his manners and on keeping all four feet on the floor when he greets people. Timmy is crate trained and does great on walks. Because he is smart and loves learning, he has been doing agility training at the Sanctuary. Sweet Timmy is searching for an active home and is sure to make a wonderful companion. Timmy has a very generous sponsor who will cover his adoption and transport costs.

name: Aiden
description: With a wagging tail and a wiggly body, Aiden greets everyone he meets like they are his best friend. He is happiest when he is with people and getting lots of love and attention. Born in 2012, Aiden came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. He is charming and enjoys snuggling, cuddling and car rides. He has a lifelong medical condition, Intervertebral Disc Disease, and needs to have limited physical activity. Leashed walks that are long are fine, but he needs to refrain from running and jumping. Aiden needs physical therapy twice a day to help with his condition that will need to continue once he is in his forever home. \"The greatest thing you'll ever learn is just to love and be loved in return,\" seems to be Aiden's motto.

name: Daniel
description: Daniel is quite an affectionate guy and will climb right into your lap. Once he gets comfortable there, you may have to lure him off with treats. He is a loving dog who bonds strongly with people. Daniel is nervous during storms. He also has some sensitivity in his hind end, so he does not like to be handled there and will give clear signs that he is uncomfortable. However, he loves pets around the head and chest. An energetic guy, Daniel enjoys walks and would do best in an active home. Because he can jump fences, he will need a secure enclosure. He would also do best in an adult-only home due to the sensitivity of his hind end and the fact that he has bitten in the past. Daniel can be picky with his doggie friends, but he can live with other respectful dogs. Born in 2017, he came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. At Dogtown, he is working on crate training and name recognition. In the right household, this sweet and sensitive guy will make a great companion.

name: Dakota
description: Dakota is sweet and curious. She is shy and nervous when meeting strangers. However, she warms up quickly when treats are involved. She likes going for walks on the trails in Dogtown with new people, if they are respectful of her shyness and don't try to pet her too much too soon. Since she is a bit fearful of new people and other dogs, she will need to meet the residents of her new home first at the Sanctuary, as well as any other dogs that presently live in the home. Born in 2017, Dakota came to the Sanctuary from a shelter in Texas. She had heartworm disease and has finished up her treatment. She is very food motivated and enjoys enrichment activities with Kong toys and snuffle mats, which help her gain confidence. With a little patience, Dakota is likely to become a braver and more confident sidekick.

name: Tennessee
description: Tennessee loves toys and people. He is playful and gets along well with other dogs. Born in 2015, Tennessee came to Best Friends from a shelter in Texas. This little pocket pitty is always trying to make his human friends laugh with his silly antics. Tennessee enjoys having dog friends and is playful and full of life. Tennessee is currently working on crate training, loose leash walking and clicker training at Dogtown. Youthful and vivacious, Tennessee can't wait to show you how much zest for life he has.

name: Montana
description: You might find Montana perched on her chair inside her room in Dogtown. It's adorable to see, and it seems like Montana loves the view from higher up. Montana is welcoming and friendly, wagging her entire body when she sees a human friend. She is playful, silly, and really enjoys attention from people. When you enter her room, Montana will get down from her chair and be ready to snuggle. Born in 2012, Montana came to Best Friends from a shelter in Texas. She had heartworm disease and just finished up her treatment. She likes to play with other dogs here at the sanctuary, but she has been known to guard things from other dogs. She hasn't shown guarding tendencies with humans, though. Montana is currently working on clicker training, which she shows off when she happily greets the Dogtown tours. Stop by and meet Montana. She just might wag her way into your heart.

name: Mauve

At Dogtown, he's getting lots of exposure to new things and new situations. As he's gained confidence, he has started seeking attention from his caregivers. Abner would love a home with a patient person or family who can help him keep building his confidence and finding his way in the world.

Some dogs were just left to roam and some dogs were kept in cages to breed.  The conditions for all were horrible and heart breaking.  Spaghetti was beyond skinny.  Her hip bones were protruding and her ribs were showing.  We knew we had to help her.  

Spaghetti made her way to CO to get the vetting she needed and the to start her second chance at life.  She was a little nervous at first, but she has really come out of her shell and started to act like a \"normal\" dog.  She gets along with the doggies in her home and is incredibly loving.  She loves to chase the toys the foster mom throws for her and after her bathes she gets a severe case of the zoomies.  More than anything she loves to snuggle. Spaghetti may not have had the best start to life, but she still has so much unconditional love to give.
