name: Elina Lonestar*
description:
Hi, my name is Elina Lonestar, but my foster mom calls me Ellie. I am a Shepherd mix about 1 year & 3 months old. I came from Texas where I lived outside all the time with several other dogs.

I'm in NJ & living with a really nice foster mom and her 8 year old female Husky mix named Tess. At least that's what my foster mom says she is, but to me she just looks more like a beige German Shephard. I love the crate that was set up for me with a bed inside and a few toys and chew bones. I like going into my crate and will do so just to get away from any hustle and bustle even though there isn't that much here in my foster home,

I like going on car rides but still don't understand why I can't constantly kiss my foster mom even if she is driving.

I am even being taught a word called \"wait\" so I can let my human go in and out of the house first. I am a little scared and get startled easily by new things but with patience and care I know I will get over this. When Tess is outside with me I am a little more comfortable as I know that I am not alone and I know that she and my foster mom would not let anything happen to me. It's just that everything is new to me. Not the fact of being outside but the fact that there really are people and dogs in this world that really do care about me.

I love the company of dogs - in fact, I love dogs so much that foster mom says I need to go to a home with at least one other dog who can help me gain confidence. But I am too active for cats so I need to go to a cat-free forever home.

I also am cautious when meeting new people so you need to go slow when you first meet me. I would be more comfortable with older children, probably 10 years or older, as the speed at which some smaller children run and act might scare me.

I walk pretty good on a leash with my foster mom (she asked me to walk easy as she and her knees are not that young anymore. I don't know what she means by that because she looks pretty young to me) who congratulates me whenever I don't pull.

I do like playing with toys but I need to get comfortable with the person playing with me or else our fetching sessions will be one sided with my owner throwing the toy, me starting toward it and then the owner having to go fetch it themselves. This not only goes for toys but for tennis balls as well. So, unless you want to go a great distance to retrieve a ball you throw, I suggest you start out throwing it close at least at first.

I also love to jump up next to my human if they are on the couch and just snuggle up. If my human allows me to I would also really like to lie close to them on their bed because it's so comforting to me to be able to sniff their scent where I will be laying. description:
Animal Profile: Barron is a handsome 4-year-old Shepherd mix from Texas who has been waiting awhile for his forever home. Barron may have some Black Mouth Cur or Malinois in his breed mix, but only a DNA test will say for sure. While we don't know his mix, we do know he is a sweet and loyal boy who will thrive in a home with structure and leadership. Barron likes other dogs but will do best as the only dog in the home. He gets along fine with cats and children but his ideal home will have no small kids. Barron is house trained but does not do well in a crate and will need a person or people who are around most of the time; he doesn't like to be left alone. He'll be happy to accompany you on car rides or to a dog-friendly workplace, though. Barron is big, beautiful, intelligent and loving and he will make the right family oh so happy.

Only dog in the home
Secure fenced yard
Dog-savvy owner
No small children
No long hours alone

Barron is neutered, up to date on vaccinations, heartworm negative and in good health.

Walks on leash: yes, but very strong and will need someone that has strength and can handle him on a leash, children would not be recommend to walk Cooper.

name: Buddy
description:
Please do not inquire or apply through Petfinder. Please apply directly with bigdogrescueproject.org/adopt. Dogs will be transported from Texas upon approved match.

Buddy is about 2 years old and is a total sweet boy. He is a typical happy-go-lucky lab who has done well with the other dogs in his foster home. It takes him a little time to get over his shyness and then he is happy as a clam!

He met a cat at the vet office and had no problems. Buddy has not met many kids at this time!

When Buddy went in for his neuter, his pre-op blood work showed that he is in kidney failure. This was obviously unexpected news, particularly given the fact that he is such a young boy. He has since started on Benazepril, which will promote healthy kidney function, and a kibble recommended for dogs with kidney issues. Benazepril is an inexpensive medication - our vet has quoted us $8 per month. While we are currently working on a plan for his future care, it is impossible to say what to expect long-term. Some dogs do not live a full life, and others do. Buddy will need to have his blood work monitored once or twice a year and at some point could need subcutaneous fluids to flush his kidneys. As long as he is eating and drinking well, with normal activity, he is considered to be stable for a dog with his condition.

Currently, Buddy is doing really well. He does consume a lot of water which is actually a good thing, per our vet. Drinking plenty of water will help him stay hydrated and keep his kidneys flushed. Because he drinks more than the average dog, he needs more frequent potty breaks but other than that, he is a normal pup. His appetite is great, he is a happy guy and he really enjoys playing with the other dogs in his foster home.

name: Baby Jade
description:
Stare deep into those baby blues, and tell us it's not love at first sight!

Baby Jade is an absolutely stunning American Staffordshire Terrier puppy that had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. Baby Jade is currently in Houston, Texas and available for transport through our rescue partners. 

This little girl has been in foster care for about 3 months and has  trained quickly. She is smart, learns quickly and has grown to become confident dog with a playful nature. She has learned to walk on a leash, crate train and house train quickly. She is very food motivated and will require a home that will work with her on basic obedience and gives her guidance. Baby Jade can be a little stubborn and her favorite activities include stealing peaches off the trees and searching for pecans in the grass. She can be a little stubborn at times and tends to run off and explore on her own, while the other dogs play. She plays in a group daily with other dogs, both male and female, ranging from young pups to adults, and does great with all of them. She loves to wrestle and roughhouse, if the other dog will allow. When another dog sets boundaries with Baby Jade by barking, growling or correcting her with a bite to the neck, she will back down and go into puppy mode by running away. Baby Jade is dog friendly and great with kids.

She is about 50lbs now and still growing. She recently had a growth spurt and is in that awkward puppy stage where she has skinny body and long, lanky legs. Baby Jade will be a large dog when fully grown, from 80-90lbs, and has an incredibly sweet temperament. She is medium to high activity, and would be an amazing companion for runs, hikes or just a nice casual stroll around the park.

Baby Jade is at an age where she needs guidance and would thrive in an environment with another assertive and more confident dog. She does well with dominant female dogs and takes correction well, however may persist in roughhousing until her human steps in to correct her as she is all about playing. This girl is a tomboy and lives for mud puddles and water- don't let her good looks fool you into thinking she is a girly girl! She is also extremely vocal and \"sings\" when she is hungry, displeased or bored, so be prepared to always have someone talking to you and letting you know how she feels! 

Baby Jade has a high prey drive towards rodents, such as squirrels, rats and possum outdoors. We have not tested Baby Jade with cats, but she is very calm and submissive. She could likely be trained to accept cats, with strict reinforcement.

Background: 
Baby Jade had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. She was found with a broken tail and infected, butchered ears from an amateur crop job at only 6 months old. She came to us as a stray, found by a Good Samaritan who saved her life after seeing a man beat and kick her on the street for approaching his dog while on a walk. He said she was vicious and tried to throw her into oncoming traffic. 

Vetting: Baby Jade has received the standard DHLPP vaccine, rabies vaccine and Bordatella vaccine. She is spayed, microchipped and heartworm negative. We recommend that all rescue dogs coming from Texas remain on heartworm preventative for 6 months after arriving in Washington, as a precaution.

name: Jedi
description:
Jedi is a very sweet, very shy, little boy we rescued from the euthanasia list from ACS San Antonio. He had little chance because of his fear in the shelter setting. HE wasn't our typical senior or hospice rescue but because he had zero interest, and was at serious risk, we just couldn't see this little guy not have another chance of a good life.
He is a small mix, probably beagle/pug or something along those lines. Perfect lap dog. His age is estimated between 5 and 6. He is very healthy, fully vetted, heart worm negative, and the perfect house pet. Ideal home for him is a calm, quiet older single or couple owners. He is very shy until he gets to know you. Zero aggression. Does fine with other low key dogs. 
Jedi is located in San Antonio Texas with the only foster and home he's known for the last couple years. He can be transported anywhere in the US, for an approved adopter, at cost to the adopter. Ideally we can find his forever home in San Antonio or a nearby location.
This one would be absolutely perfect for a mature person or couple looking for devoted love.
Interested applicants can email us about him.

name: Missy
description:
* Please apply online at www.6dogrees.com by doing so you will get a response quicker.

Meet Missy. A small 10 pound, 2-year old female Dachshund/Chihuahua mix. Her adoption fee is $475.

Missy loves dogs and enjoys spending time with her four-legged friends. She has beautiful tan smooth coat and is low-shedding. She is potty trained and crated trained.  When is comes to people, it takes time for her to warm up â but once comfortable she is a wiggly, loving, loyal friend.

Missyâs favorite pastime is playing tag in the backyard, which only comes second to snuggling deep under the covers to keep her personâs feet warm.  She is a wonderful small watchdog and alert to everything around her.  

Missy will require:
-	A patient home that is willing to work to build her trust with people.
-	A grain-free diet. This will help keep her healthy and her coat beautiful.  
-	Grooming.  Missy is a âwash and wearâ dog (very little grooming needed).
-	A fully fenced yard.  Fences help protect rescue dogs and establish boundaries.  

Missy is a rescue dog, and like all living creatures, she requires routine and stability. Please be prepared for a lifelong commitment before applying.  Ideally, dogs should be pottied every 4 to 5 hours. Dogs cannot be left alone for 8 hours per day. Home check and plan must be carefully thought out and presented at time of interview. 

Missy is fostered in North Seattle, and if interested please submit an online adoption application at www.6dogrees.com and we will review and get back to you promptly. An adoption application must be filled out for all inquiries and prior to a meet and greet. We will review and respond to applications, not all applications will necessarily be approved for a meet and greet. Home check prior to adoption approval. 

Adoption fee include: Neuter/spay, microchip, current vaccines (DA2PP, rabies, Bordetella) de-worming, flea treatment, and heart worm testing.  We also include a 15-minute training consultation with a certified behaviorist trainer and 30-day pet insurance. 

6dogrees Rescue is a small passionate Seattle based 501c3 non-profit charitable organization that focuses on saving the lives of urgent dogs on their last hours at high kill shelters  from the State of California where pet overpopulation is at epidemic levels and kill shelters are the norm. 100% of all fees collected are spent on the dogs, we âSave it forwardâ; so each time a dog is adopted we are allowed to save another. Adoption fees are non-negotiable and are in place to allow thorough care for the dogs. 

6dogrees adoptions are limited to residents of Washington State.

Hi my name is Rascal and I'm a 3 year old Chiweenie. My past is not a happy one and is one that was filled with a lot of abuse, that involved hitting and slapping me and yelling at me. I am so thankful to be given a chance to be adopted by someone who will love me and give me hugs and kisses like my foster Mom. Due to my abusive past, I don't like for someone to look me directly in my eyes while holding me as it scares me. When my foster Mom would do this, I would smile at her showing my teeth. I would not bite and have no bite history, but that's how I showed I was nervous. After a couple of months, I learned my foster Mom would never hurt me and I replaced my smiles with lots of licking and kissing my foster Mom; and now I smile with my eyes. I have never known love or how good life could be.

I'm told I'm a very good watch dog. I'm the first to hear if someone has walked up to the door and I promptly let my foster Mom know.

I love to jump, run and play and love toys. I love car rides and sit like a gentleman in my foster Mom's lap and look out the window.

I don't like to be around other dogs and I do like to harass cats. But I just tease them. If it's time to be kenneled, while I don't like it, I will be a good quiet boy and lay down to sleep. Unless I hear something outside like a knock on the door, then I might bark.

Thank you for reading my bio. I'm hoping that a nice family will adopt me and love me so I can have the life every dog deserves.

name: Teddy (formerly Summer)
description:
Teddy needs a new home!
As much as we vet all of our applicants with questions, screenings and home visits, we don't always find the right home the first time. Some people say they will make a lifetime commitment but when push comes to shove, they can't or won't follow through. This beautiful boy was returned after 8 months in what he thought was his forever home because he is protective and guards his people. He is back in Maryland and up for adoption. Only applicants with husky/chow experience or experience with these types of behaviors will be considered. If you think you are the forever person for this guy please apply today. He is so sweet - he just needs a firm handler!
The adoptive family must commit to ongoing training, visits to a behaviorist and medication if called for. This breed needs to stay busy - they love having a job and must be exercised thoroughly.

Here is Teddy's original bio from 10/2018:
Summer originally came to us in October 2018 as one of 7 dogs MMR took in via an emergency request from The Humane Society of the United States due to the devastation in Houston, Texas when thousands of animals were displaced from their homes and shelters.
He is a gorgeous blend of MUTT and it would be interesting to know what he is. Mostly we see Chow, Shepherd, Husky and Collie but it's a guess. No matter what he is, we can tell you this handsome boy is very sweet and friendly. He likes all people - big and small. We think he is about year old and he weighs in at 50 lbs. He is working on potty training and has improved immensely since in foster care but still has a way to go. He's ok on the leash, he doesn't pull much but we can tell he might make a good running partner. He also lives with some cats and although he is interested in them he doesn't seem to care about them one way or the other. Like most of us, this boy is not without his quirks. He really hates the crate and whines and gets agitated while inside. He stands down to the female dogs in the house but can be reactive to the males - we hope this will resolve itself after his neuter. Last but not least he is a little food aggressive - not necessarily with dog food but if a person has food, is preparing food or even has a wrapper or container in their hand he will try to grab it. We think with some good training he will overcome this as well but for right now we won't place him with kids under 13. He is not at all aggressive if you touch his food while he's eating, he doesn't race to move the other dogs in the house away from their bowls and he doesn't even growl if they come near while he is eating. He really is very friendly otherwise and he is looking for a home where he will get the training he needs and a human who will love him and allow him to snuggle with them. He will be available for adoption after his neuter. *Since this was written he is potty trained and crate trained. He has been living in a home with no other pets but has been fine on walks and at the dog park.
My adoption fee is $350, which covers the cost of routine vetting, rabies and distemper/parvo vaccinations, deworming, spay/neuter surgery, heartworm testing, my microchip, monthly heartworm prevention, monthly flea/tick prevention, and any transport costs if applicable. If you can't adopt me, consider sponsoring my care and being a rescue angel. Click on the DONATE button below and chip in what you can. Your donation is tax deductible and helps us save more lives!

To fill out an adoption application, go to: http://muttsmatterrescue.com/adoption_app.html
You can save animals like this one by becoming a foster home for a dog in need! Fosters are like way stations between high kill shelters and forever homes. We need fosters so that we can save dogs before they are euthanized at the shelters. If you are interested in becoming a foster, please check out our information about fostering on our website: http://www.muttsmatterrescue.com/foster_faq.html
MMR covers the vet care, food, and tools to get started. You supply the love. Fostering saves lives. Sometimes a foster home is the only thing standing between life and death. 9/16/19 8:12 PM

name: Mr T
description:
Updated 8/7/19 - Mr. T is a 10 year old Jack Russell Terrier/Beagle mix (but acts more like a 4 year old).  He can be very active or just chill out .   Mr. T was rescued from a hoarding situation in TN.  He was lucky enough, along with 19 other dogs, to find his way to PA.  Unfortunately, none of the dogs were socialized and were very shy and afraid of just about everything.  Mr. T was the most shy of them all.  After spending over a year in a shelter receiving daily personal interaction, Mr. T got the opportunity to enter the Hounds of Prison Education (HOPE) Program.  He was very afraid of all the noise and commotion in the prison and subsequently moved into a foster home at the beginning of 2018.
 
Mr. T has made significant progress being in a quiet home with his canine foster friends.  He now seeks out his foster Mom to cuddle on the couch during TV time.  He likes to go for walks and walks well on a leash, (he pulls once he knows he is headed home so he can get there as fast as possible).  Mr. T doesn't particularly like the sounds he hears on a walk in the neighborhood, such as garage doors, a car door slamming,  or strange people walking toward him.  He has gotten past most of that and now is starting to really enjoy his local walks.  His favorite activities include going for car rides and running around the dog park.
 
Mr. T is still very wary of strangers and takes time to feel comfortable with strangers.  He likes to take his time trusting and will require a ton of patience in a new home.  He is a really, really sweet boy that just needs love, patience and understanding.  He needs a person or family that will help him unpack all of the baggage he carries from his former life.  Mr. T would do best in a quiet home (no apartments) and one that has at least one resident dog.  At this point, Mr. T has not been \"cat tested,\" but that can be done before being placed in any home with felines.

Mr. T is crate trained and housebroken.

name: Tango
description:
Update 8/6/19  Tango is an adorable, adoptable cuddle bug who likes to snuggle while watching TV.  He is approximately 9 years old and weighs about 25 to 26 pounds.  He is one of the terriers saved from a hoarding situation in TN when the ASPCA went there to rescue animals during flooding.  Tango and 19 others made their way to a PA shelter.  He was one of the most shy and scared dogs of the group.  After being in the shelter for over a year, Tango moved into the Hounds of Prison (HOPE) Program where he received obedience training and given the confidence he so badly lacked.  After graduation from the program, he was placed in a foster home to continue to work on his social skills.
 
Tango has made a lot of progress living in a quiet foster home environment with 3 fur siblings.  He follows his foster Mom and wants to be with her as much as possible.  He also enjoys cuddling and sleeping beside her and enjoys car rides and exercise at the dog park.  Tango has not been \"cat tested\" at this point, but will be prior to any decision to be placed in a home with a feline.  Although Tango likes other dogs and gets along well with them, he could be an only dog.  He is more eager to spend time with his foster Mom than anyone.  However, having another dog(s) is preferable since Tango has never lived without a buddy or two.
 
Tango is now at the point where he will go up to someone who has been a frequent visitor in the home, but still shies away from new people (unless they have a special treat which he is more than glad to snag).  He also does not like a lot of commotion, so apartment living may not be the best fit for Tango (this, of course, depends on the apartment and noise in the neighborhood).  A quiet household with a person or family that has patience to spare would be best.
 
Tango is a very sweet boy who is ready to find a forever home .  He needs an understanding family who will give him space to settle in at his own pace.  Since he is very treat oriented, the fastest way to this guy's heart is through his stomach.

description:

name: Max in NH
description:
PLEASE DO NOT USE PETFINDER'S \"ASK ABOUT\" BUTTON.  We are very sorry, but those get lost in our process and are difficult for us to manage. Questions about this puppy should be directed to melissa@caninecommit.org.  Anything else may delay the process. (Submitting an application or mini-application is the only way to hold your place.)

Max is a one year old retriever mix. He's a super friendly boy who loves to play with other dogs. Max was rescued from Tupelo Lee Humane Society in Tupelo MS. He's about 45 pounds and is currently doing well with crate training. He is neutered, up to date on vaccinations, and microchipped. His adoption fee is $475. Applications and information about our adoption process is available on our website at www.caninecommit.org. Email melissa@caninecommit.org. 

PLEASE READ:
Again, questions about this dog should be directed to melissa@caninecommit.org. Not e-mailing Melissa directly may delay the process.  Thank you!

YES, ALL OF OUR DOGS ARE IN NH! Canine Commitment does not post any dogs as available until they are here, in NH, and available to meet before committing to adopt.

HOURS:  We operate out of our personal homes so appointments are required to meet our pups.

PROCESS:  www.caninecommit.org.  Click on Adoption FAQ.

OUR LOCATIONS: Canine Commitment has two licensed shelter locations (at our private residences) in the state of NH, abiding by all state and federal import and quarantine laws. We are a 501c3 not-for-profit organization run by volunteers who just want to help save some lives.

IF THE LISTED CONTACT IS MELISSA@CANINECOMMIT.ORG, that dog or puppy is at our Manchester location or being overseen by Melissa.  Melissa is only available via e-mail; the person answering the phone at our published phone number will not have up-to-date information about that dog's availability.  All visitors to Melissa's home must have submitted an application prior to scheduling an appointment.

Thank you, so much, for considering rescue.  Please remember that the reason it can be hard and can take some time and patience to adopt a dog or puppy in our area is that we do not have debilitating overpopulation and we are not euthanizing hundreds of unwanted dogs in our local shelters.  Please also remember that we are two volunteers who give up the privacy of our personal homes, along with dozens upon dozens of volunteer hours each and every week, just to help save some dogs' lives.  We do it of our own free will and do not do it for any kudos or recognition, but kindness and patience are much appreciated as we do our very best to juggle all of the demands on our time.  It takes all of us to make a difference and we appreciate you!



A NOTE ABOUT HOUSETRAINING:  We can tell you about our experience with a dog in our homes and in the fosters' homes down south (prior to arrival in NH).  Please keep in mind that we do this with a lot of pups -- dogs go directly outside when they come out of their crates and usually are not given free range in our homes without supervision.  ANY dog may need time, patience, and consistency to learn your home, your routines, and your expectations of them.  Be patient, buy a bottle of carpet cleaner just in case, and give this new relationship some time and TLC.  Most pups have been in at least three locations prior to going to your home.  They may be confused, unsure of themselves, and looking for cues ... and understanding.  They are living, feeling beings who should not be expected to be perfect instantly. (Sometimes, they are.  Bonus!)

A NOTE ABOUT LEASH WALKING:  In our homes, the pups are in fenced areas. In most cases, volunteers have walked the adult, larger dogs at some point and we have some information from them about the dog's behavior on leash.  Most often, we do not.  Our experience with them on leash is limited to transfers to/from the car, into/out of the vet's office, etc.  Some dogs behave just the way they do in group settings when they are on leash.  Other times, they do not. Do not ask too much of a new, adult dog in your home.  Give them time to adjust before introducing them to other dogs.  Introduce them slowly and with forethought (feel free to ask us for some resources -- we are happy to provide those!).

Join us on Facebook for more photos and to join our community of dog lovers!  https://www.facebook.com/caninecommitmentnewengland

name: Baxter
description:
A super sweet 5 yr old Black Lab Mix & 70 lbs of pure baby love.  This sweet boy has seen some tough times but has come through and is doing great.  He was found as a stray nearly starved and no hair on his back. He had raw sores on his neck, head and back. It was also evident by his raw neck that  he had been kept on a chain. 

With the gracious help of a rescue and foster family, Baxter has made a tremendous recovery over the past 2 months.  He is LOVING dog life~ he plays like a puppy & loves his bone and toys. He gets along with our other dogs (took slow introductions and a little time). He also gets along with cats. Mostly just curious but doesnât chase.

Baxter is still somewhat fearful of the outdoors at times. He still gets skittish and nervous when on walks but is getting better over time.  He is also nervous around unfamiliar people. He will need a patient and loving person / family to help continue with his rehab and recovery. Most of his fur has grown back and he is looking so beautiful.

He would do well with a home where someone is home during the day and he would also do better with a home that has  another furry dog companion. He is not aggressive but loves to run, play and engage in dog play. *We wouldnât recommend Baxter go to a home with small children. 

The foster family is willing to help with introductions and transition. They are located in Union County in the Charlotte area.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a 2 year old Lurcher.  Heâs looking for a family to help him be a good boy. Not good lookingâobviously he has that one covered! But Bruce struggles with food aggression.  He loves other dogs but either needs to be an only dog or he needs a family with experience managing food aggression.  Can you help Bruce be a good boy?


Bruce's adoption fee is $300, which covers their neuter and other veterinary care.  He is currently being fostered in WV.  While we prefer that adopters pick up their dogs from their foster homes, we adopt to families across the US and Canada. If you need assistance transporting your dog home, we will help make the arrangements but you will be responsible for the actual costs, which are usually $300-600.

NOTE: Please do not click the ADOPT ME button on this page. This is the best way we have found to make the best use of our time. There are a lot of people who just want to ask questions but will never adopt and unfortunately we just don't have time to chat.

description:

name: Layla (GREAT Family Dog)
description:
While this photo from her at the SC shelter that saved her, is not a good photo, Layla is a GREAT and beautiful dog. She is 3 years old and 55 lbs of love and affection and she loves to play. Layla is good with dogs and kids and cats. She is just so sweet and just another great Labby girl, in need of a forever home. A must meet, for she will steal your heart for sure. (If you do not hear back from us within about 6 hours, send us your phone number, for there might be something wrong with your email!) 
Lovable Mutts Adoption Center is a private, in home, all breed rescue/adoption facility, specializing in all ages and sizes of dogs.  We exist only on the kindness of your donations and adoptions!  We pride ourselves on being an HOLISTIC center and feed only holistic grain free foods and give daily, various, vitamins and supplements to all of our dogs. 

Our dogs are well socialized, very friendly, well mannered, affectionate, and in wonderful health. While some might be timid or shy, we work with our adopters in any way we can, to help them to work with their new family member. We give training tips and behavioral tips and even board for a very reasonable fee. Our dogs are extremely well cared for - most even know how to use a dog door by the time they leave us, know basic commands, and are crate trained!  We stand by our pups/dogs, and give 10 days for a refund and almost always take our dogs back at any age of their lives (can sometimes depend on the dog)! 

Lovable Mutts Adoption Center has an application screening process.  All applicants are asked to provide vet references, personal references, and a home visit.  We pride ourselves in matching up the right dog with the right home.  Sometimes this happens quickly and sometimes it might take awhile.  We hope you understand and are willing to wait for the perfect pup for your situation. We reserve the right to turn applicants down and to change our mind about a suitable match, for we are only concerned about what is best for our dogs.  Also note that we arrange our visiting hours around your schedule, as this is a private, in home facility.  We respond to all inquiries promptly, so if you have any trouble sending us an email, or have not heard back from us within 24 hours, please, CONTACT US AGAIN and check your spam!  (We all know how emails can be at times!)

Our dogs are spayed or neutered (if old enough), up to date on vaccines, wormed, heartworm tested, and free of fleas and ticks.  We temperament test our  dogs and they are all suitable for many family situations. Our dogs are well mannered,  and are in our family/home situation at this time (not kept in kennels or crates), and are worked with daily.  All of our dogs do well with other dogs and many do well with cats, and we can cat test. Adoption donations vary with age, breed, vetting, and training of the dog, and range from $250 to $500. This donation helps to pay for shots, de-wormings, spays, neuters, flea protection, heartworm/Lyme testing, treatments, and other vetting/issues that might be needed, for dogs in our care.  (We do not tend to place puppies or small dogs with kids under 6 and reserve the right to match who WE feel would be the best homes for our dogs.)  
Please, come adopt one of our Lovable Mutts - you will be so glad you did!

(IF YOU DO NOT GET A REPLY EMAIL WITHIN 24 HOURS, CHECK YOUR SPAM BOX - WE REPLY EVERY FEW HOURS TO EMAILS)

name: Pita
description: Pita was saved from a horrible high kill gas shelter in Utah. He is about a year old male that is very sweet and cuddly. He will be flying to Maine for foster within the next month. If you would like to fill out an application, please go to www.underhoundrailroad.org.

name: Yahtzee
description: Yahtzee is a 10 year 29 pound beautiful fawn color Cocker Spaniel. CAWS pulled Yahtzee from a Valencia, NM shelter where he was found as a stray, and hitched a ride on a transport back to Utah. He arrived very sick and lethargic. Took him to the vet within a couple days and learned he had pneumonia and bad ear infections. He was placed in isolation for a few weeks to get over his illness and regain his strength. Once he was able to get out and be a part of the family pack, hes been thriving ever since. Our little man was a fighter who wanted to live and now be part of the good life! Yahtzee has had a dental with 12 extractions. He has arthritis in his back legs and hips so will be on pain medications for the rest of his life. Due to this arthritis he should be in a home with very minimal steps or none at all. Yahtzee can totally be trusted in the home when his 2 legged people arent home. He is dog door trained. He loves his 4 legged siblings, male and female, small and large. He doesnt sleep on the couch or bed, he prefers a bed on the floor. His sight isnt 100% but he sees enough to get around. His hearing might be a little less than stellar as well. He is a very nervous little man, he will pace at times and his legs shake with nervousness. Yahtzee will play with chew toys on the floor every once in a while and he loves to tear up empty paper towel and toilet paper rolls. With his big floppy ears he comes to share after hes had a drink by dragging his ears across you, so cute, well okay, really kind of not that cute, but it goes with the territory. He will need regular grooming. This precious and sweet little man is pure as they come. Now its his time to find his forever family that will show him the unconditional love he deserves! He will surely melt your heart. Due to Yahtzees nervousness he needs to go to a home with no children, or at least older. He also needs a home with a fenced yard and no stairs, or very minimal steps due to his arthritis in his back legs and hips. Yahtzee is not a barker, very occasional yap. If you are interested in adopting a CAWS pet, please fill out an online application at http://caws.org/adoption-application

name: Iggy - Amazing, Amazing!
description:
Meet Iggy! He is incredible! He is deaf but that bothers him none! He knows 9+ signs, is super smart, loves tennis balls and with a proper intro to other dogs, can be so happy!

Iggy loves to play. He has waited forever to find a home and since he is new to us, we hope to find him a great home in the Pacific Northwest. Originating from Best Friends in Utah, we are so excited to have him here.

His local coach has worked with many deaf dogs, curiously most have white coats. They are the best.

He is a big snuggler, loves to play tug of war, chase balls and going for a walk, hike or run is all on his bucket list!

He is now updated on all shots, neutered and will be chipped. His adopt fee is $395.

We cover the medical to prepare the pet for adoption and the adopt donations go directly to cover those costs and range from $295-$495. Thank you for stepping up to save a life!

To expedite to meet with this dog, please go to our site at www.savinggreatanimals.org and fill out an application. We look at the first applications to arrive, so we hope to hear from you soon!

name: Ryder
description: Ryder is your guy! He is approximately 2 years old and a Golden Retriever/Border Collie/Heeler mix-best guess. He is a beautiful strawberry blond and has a long lean body with a docked tail. He loves being part of a pack and gets along well with other dogs. He was found as a stray from the Ute reservation in Cortez, NM, and is so glad he caught his freedom ride to Colorado. This smart goofy guy rides well in the car and hopes to become your favorite adventure buddy. He can be a little reserved at first, but once he becomes comfortable, he is affectionate and enjoys shadowing your every move. Ryder is housebroken and does well in his crate, although he prefers to be outside or free roam in the house. He is learning how to live in a house and once he masters his leash skills, he will make an awesome running buddy. Ryder is UTD on shots, neutered, and microchipped. He will do best with an active home, and someone that will be willing to continue his training. He would love a home with a companion dog, and older kids would suit him fine.Ryder is being fostered in Littleton. Want to meet Ryder and fall in love? Apply to adopt at rezdawgrescue.org

name: Forest
description:
If you are interested in adopting this dog, please download and complete an Adoption Questionnaire from our website and email US at hollyl@k-9lifesavers.org
You can learn about the adoption process and find a Word, PDF and ONLINE version of the questionnaire by visiting: http://www.k-9lifesavers.org/howtoadopt/.
Dog's Name: Forest
Estimated Breed : Husky Mix
Approximate Age: 2 years
Approximate Weight: approx. 65 lbs
Currently Living at: Boarding
Adoption Fee: $300
DOG'S DESCRIPTION
Forest is a very handsome husky mix with two beautiful different colored eyes! He came to us from rural VA where he was found as a stray. No one came to reclaim him so we scooped him up to give him his second chance! Forest gets along well with other dogs and loves attention from humans! He is a large dog who prefers to be a part of a pack and would prefer to go to a home with another canine buddy. He exhibits strong husky behaviors and would be better suited for somebody who has experience with the breed. He would be happiest in a home with a fenced-in yard.
Your new pet will require a refresher in house-training. K-9 Lifesavers strongly recommends all new adopters enroll their new pet into obedience training. This provides for an easier transition into a new home, ensures the dog remains well socialized, and helps form a bond between the dog and the new family.
Adoption fees cover basic vetting, spay/neuter surgery (for dogs over 6 months old), rabies, distemper/parvo vaccinations, treatment for worms, heartworm testing, monthly heartworm prevention and monthly flea/tick prevention (while the animal is in our care), and transport costs from high-kill shelter. Please note that on average, K-9 Lifesavers spend significantly more on each dog than their adoption fee. Adoption fee for HW positive dog also covers heartworm treatment at our partner vets.
Foster Program: Foster homes provide for the temporary care of a rescue until the dog is placed into a loving, forever home. For more information on becoming a foster parent, and our Foster Program, visit http://www.k-9lifesavers.org/foster/ or email our Foster Coordinator at foster@k-9lifesavers.org
Sponsor Me! Make a tax-deductible donation today by visiting us at http://www.k-9lifesavers.org/donate/ . Donations help us offset boarding costs and additional medical treatment for those dogs who need it. K-9 Lifesavers receives NO federal funding and survive with your generous support!
For more information on K-9 Lifesavers, or to view a complete listing of all our Adoptable Dogs, visit our website at www.k-9lifesavers.org.
Please \"like\" our Facebook Page for the most current events and new dogs.
Thank you for considering a rescue dog!

name: Betsy
description:
This dog is part of our shelter outreach program where we take dogs from overcrowded shelters in hopes of finding them a forever home here! We generally do not have much background info on them and cannot guarantee they are housebroken. They are all up to date on vaccines, spayed/neutered and microchipped.
Betsy (32lbs) and Frack (49lbs) came up from VA. They are part of a hoarding situation where they lived with dozens of dogs. This brother and sister pair have lived in the same 15x15 kennel for their entire lives. A rescue group in VA has worked with the owner for the past year trying to spay and neuter and remove dogs from her property. The owner loved the dogs but sadly things got out of control. The rescue group asked if we could help with these 2. Betsy and Frack are 8 years old and a bonded pair so need to go home together. They will need a fenced in yard and a home with love and patience. Betsy is the more nervous of the two. Our staff and volunteers are working hard with them to get them used to other people and different sounds and surroundings. They are making progress and seeking out attention. If you think you may have the right home for these 2, please stop in or call our facility. Fenced in yard required.
Kids 14+*Per JSAC policy, puppies and kittens under 6 months will not be adopted to families with children under the age of 6 years.

name: Yahtzee
description: Yahtzee is a 10 year 29 pound beautiful fawn color Cocker Spaniel. CAWS pulled Yahtzee from a Valencia, NM shelter where he was found as a stray, and hitched a ride on a transport back to Utah. He arrived very sick and lethargic. Took him to the vet within a couple days and learned he had pneumonia and bad ear infections. He was placed in isolation for a few weeks to get over his illness and regain his strength. Once he was able to get out and be a part of the family pack, hes been thriving ever since. Our little man was a fighter who wanted to live and now be part of the good life! Yahtzee has had a dental with 12 extractions. He has arthritis in his back legs and hips so will be on pain medications for the rest of his life. Due to this arthritis he should be in a home with very minimal steps or none at all. Yahtzee can totally be trusted in the home when his 2 legged people arent home. He is dog door trained. He loves his 4 legged siblings, male and female, small and large. He doesnt sleep on the couch or bed, he prefers a bed on the floor. His sight isnt 100% but he sees enough to get around. His hearing might be a little less than stellar as well. He is a very nervous little man, he will pace at times and his legs shake with nervousness. Yahtzee will play with chew toys on the floor every once in a while and he loves to tear up empty paper towel and toilet paper rolls. With his big floppy ears he comes to share after hes had a drink by dragging his ears across you, so cute, well okay, really kind of not that cute, but it goes with the territory. He will need regular grooming. This precious and sweet little man is pure as they come. Now its his time to find his forever family that will show him the unconditional love he deserves! He will surely melt your heart. Due to Yahtzees nervousness he needs to go to a home with no children, or at least older. He also needs a home with a fenced yard and no stairs, or very minimal steps due to his arthritis in his back legs and hips. Yahtzee is not a barker, very occasional yap. If you are interested in adopting a CAWS pet, please fill out an online application at http://caws.org/adoption-application

name: Luna
description:
This petite princess is Luna!  She is about  7-8 months old and weights 35 lbs.   She gets along great with other dogs, loves people, and is good with cats. She was rescued from a city shelter in Vicksburg, MS.  

Luna is housebroken and crate trained. She sees her crate as a safe place and likes to bring toys inside to play with. At night she brings a special toy or two up to bed to chew or cuddle with. She enjoys sleeping all curled up right next to her foster mom and will do best in a home where she can continue to enjoy this bonding experience.  

We donât know her past, but we donât think Luna had a chance to experience a carefree life as a puppy.  Her play consists of what is expected of an 8 month old with sporadic bursts of young puppy-like activity. Luna is focused, does well on car rides and loves a good belly rub. 

She is very smart and will thrive with experienced dog owners who will be able to take her on adventures that continue to work her body and mind.   

We do not provide DNA testing which is the only way to know with certainty which breeds are in her genetic background. Our best guess is that she is a Whippet mix with her long, slender build and markings. She may have White Shepherd in her family tree and Catahoula. We expect her to reach about 40-45 pounds as an adult, but we can not guarantee size at maturity. 

Highlights about Luna:
- Enjoys playing with other dogs  
- Is good with cats
- Housebroken
- Crate Trained  
- Friendly, Affectionate 
- Up-to-date on vaccines
- Super Smart!!
- Food motivated
- Well socialized

description:
Gracie #3 is an almost 2-year-old spayed black female lab. She weighs 44 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Gracie is a happy but shy girl, who loves adorably once she trusts you, but will take a bit of time and some caution to earn that trust. She absolutely loves other dogs, and has never met one she doesn't like. For this girl, the more dogs in her world, the better. If you are giving affection to another dog, her curiosity will get the better of her and she'll almost immediately come up to investigate. She can be a bit hand shy, even once she trusts you, so just needs humans that will go slow and understand to give her time. When she's in her element, she is silly, rolling on the grass, spinning around and zooming as fast as she can to play \"tag\" with the other dogs. And she's REALLY fast. She enjoys napping on the couch, and will allow herself to be a pillow for the other dogs. She also likes to sleep in bed with her humans and is incredibly silly in the mornings as she considers the bed a safe zone - she'll roll on her back and beg for belly rubs and play bitey-face. She especially loves when the other dogs join in the fun. She's excellent in the crate, and foster mom has spied her sleeping in the crate belly up while she's at work. Gracie prefers to eat alone, and will quickly eat her meals in her crate, or in a separate room, but is nervous eating in front of humans, unless it's people food that you are sharing with her (which she loves!). Her leash skills are pretty good, but she would prefer walking on quiet streets and not on a busy road. Gracie is a shy dog, and is always going to be a bit shy. She warms up to new people, but prefers them in small groups and not making a lot of noise, please. She's not the dog for you if you have rambunctious teenagers (or adults), throw parties often, or if you're looking for a dog to take everywhere with you. She started her life sheltered in a pen, and didn't get the socialization with humans she should have at an early age, so they make her a bit nervous. She's incredibly sweet and loving, and will reward you with her sweet, happy, silly self if you give her love, patience and understanding.

name: Kayla
description:
Kayla is an 8-year-old spayed chocolate female lab. She weighs 81 pounds but needs to lose about 5 pounds and is up to date on shots. This dog is approved for homes with children ages 10 and up.

Kayla is a happy chocolate girl who likes belly rubs and running in the yard. She has been a loving and attentive mommy to multiple litters of puppies and now she is ready to take her turn in the spotlight. Sheâs a friendly girl with lots of energy who would do best with a family that will give her plenty of playtime outside, long walks, and lots of love. Kayla is good with dogs, but not cats and approved for kids 10 and up. Kayla is from a rural area and has not been exposed to traffic, noise, or groups of people. If dogs are overwhelmed by their environment, they can exhibit behaviors like excessive barking. To avoid this, for now we are limiting placement to stand alone single-family homes or townhomes in a suburban neighborhood or rural area. As we learn more from the dog's time spent in foster, we will evaluate if placement can be expanded to include a more urban environment and send out an update. 

Foster family reports: Kayla has a vivacious, energetic personality. After spending much of her life outdoors, she is excited to be in her foster home. Her tail has not stopped wagging! She thinks she's a lap dog and would crawl in your lap with the slightest encouragement. She introduced herself to the resident lab with play bows and ran zoomies with him. She is friendly without being either dominant or submissive. Kayla had no problem navigating the hardwood floors. She can zoom up and down stairs. She likes watching TV, especially animal shows and Litter Robot advertisements, which bring her to her feet everytime. (Must be the cat!) She also enjoys watching squirrels outside. This former breeder girl had a litter quite recently and still has enlarged mammaries. She weighs 80 lbs but should weigh ~75. She shows interest in meeting children (approved age 10+). Kayla rode well in the car and walks nicely in an Easy Walk harness. She loved her first walk in the park. Although she came from a rural area, she does not seem bothered by traffic or loud noises. Kayla is food motivated, which should help with refreshing commands. Kayla is settling nicely into her foster home. She was a little over-amped when she first arrived but now she is able to settle in the house. She enjoys playing with the resident lab, and in fact, she is usually the initiator of play! She likes taking walks around the neighborhood, and we discovered that she is a retriever. Kayla did not appear to know her name or any commands, so we are working to teach her basic commands and leash skills. She walks pretty well with an EZ-Walk harness, doesn't pull, but will sniff a lot if you let her. She needs to be tethered in the car until she knows her commands or she will be in the driver's lap. She is not crated when we leave the house and she does not disturb anything. Kayla is super loving and affectionate. She has all the most desirable lab traits! She is a velcro dog to foster mom, but seems to do most of her lab leans on the men she meets. She has met the neighbors and their dogs and impressed them with her friendliness and beauty. Other dogs really like her, so she appears to share good vibes! We don't know yet whether she likes water. Her background continues to mystify us. She was photographed at intake living on a chain, but she also knows her way around a house, is interested in human food and would like to get up on the furniture (although not allowed by her current foster). Kayla is quite energetic for her age and will need regular walks and/or active time in the yard. Since she doesn't bark, navigates stairs easily and can be exercised on leash, Kayla is now approved for townhouses on a case-by-case basis.

name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

When we named Miss Nellie, we thought that she was on the verge of being a senior dog. Now that she is healthy and happy; we can confidently say that she has a long way to go before she is a senior. We now call her Scooter; which better describes her personality and her propensity to get frequent attacks of the Zoomies.

She came to us from a rural shelter in southwestern Virginia. She was malnourished, infested with intestinal parasites, and her fur was coming out in clumps. We were also concerned that she may be pregnant. During her wellness check, it was discovered she was indeed pregnant, but the vet felt something was wrong. An ultrasound was preformed and we found out her babies were not viable.  She needed emergency surgery.  If we had waited few more days; she may have not survived.  After a few weeks of recovery at her new foster home in South Carolina; the real Scooter showed herself.. Her coat is soft, full and beautiful. She loves to run around her wooded fenced property chasing away squirrels and any other critter bold enough to trespass.  Due to this, we think she would do best in a home without cats.  She likes going for leash walks and really loves to snuggle with her foster mom.  Scooter gets along with her big ACD foster brother, but is not very fond of other female dogs.  

Scooter is deaf, She may hear really low and high pitched loud sounds. For this reason, we feel a fenced yard is really important for her safety.  She is learning some sign language.  Like most ACD's Scooter is wary of new people until she gets to know them; then she quickly warms up for petting and treats.. She is a goofy, happy girl.  She is crate trained and likes to go for car rides. She has been a very good girl at all of her vet visits and with everyone she traveled with on her journey from Bristol, VA to Richmond, VA and onto Summerville, SC She is still learning about toys, squeaky ones are really fun.

We think Scooter is about  4yrs old, and 35 LBS, She is Heartworm negative, up to date on her vaccinations, crate trained, house trained, spayed, and being fostered near Summerville, SC

If you are interested in adopting Scooter, please visit the Adoption Process page on our website â http://carolinasrescue.com/Adoption_Process.html. You can download our Adoption Questionnaire there, then email it to us at adoptions@carolinasrescue.com. That will start the process.

name: Dood
description:
Thank you for your interest in dog who needs a new home. Adoption can be one of the most fulfilling experiences in your life and especially in the life of your new canine companion.

A note to those looking at CPR. We have no perfect dogs - but many of our dogs have proven to be perfect for a certain someone. Our job is to find those someone's. Our most successful adopters come to CPR not because they want a dog. They come to us because they want to give a dog a home. We urge all of our potential adopters not to fall in love with a picture. While we like to know what you like in looks, a dog is more than a pretty face. Our goal is to match you with the best possible pet for you and your home. We want to create furever families.

Our descriptions contain all that we know about this dog today. We'll update as more information is known.

Are you looking to adopt within the next 30 days? If so please visit our webpage at www.carolinapoodlerescue.org and complete the application. You'll find it in the menu on the left hand side. You'll also find a total listing of all our dogs available.

Just browsing but interested in poodles and poodle mixes? Please drop a note to applications@carolinapoodlerescue.org with your name, address and phone # and email. We'll add you to our mailing list.

thanks
the CPR Adoption team

Date into Rescue: 4/5/2019
Reason for being in rescue: VA shelter- allowed to run at large and picked up one too many times
Foster location: Dreamweaver Farms, Pacolet SC
Special Needs? Dood was deemed a dangerous animal in the state of Virginia. His previous owner would not keep him confined and he was allowed to roam at will. He is happy and gregarious and would run up to people and knock them down as a game. He's not shown any aggressive side to us at all but we all know how to tel him \"GET OFF\" and he's respecting that cue. He needs some training and someone with some common sense.
Weight: 99 lbs
Height: 26 in
Spayed/Neutered: Yes

Adoption Fee: $499

Fence needed? Without exception and it needs to be a solid, dependable fence and you need to plan to be in control of your dog. He's been failed by a human once before because of not understanding our dogs needs us to keep them safe and in places they can safely be, not roaming the streets.

What kind of home would be best for me? Dood's perfect owner will be someone with dog experience, who loves to take long, brisk walks and who would enjoy teaching, shaping and training their dog to be the excellent companion this dog has the potential to be. Dood is affectionate and friendly and longs for that companion that will be his partner, his friend and his guide through life instead of letting him run amuck.

What is my personality like? Dood is an even tempered and intelligent dog who has been allowed to run and roam and that got him on serious trouble. He was part of a pack with his sister Dette.

One of our temperament programs is to take our dogs off site for adventures. Dood is a perfect gentleman in the car just as he was in the trip from Virginia to South Carolina. He is attentive, likes to look out the window and enjoys seeing new places and learning new things.

How do I act when I first meet new people? Friendly. He's been known to bark at people but it's in a \"hi come on over and let's get to know each other\" way. But..as big as he is it is a deep bark and that can intimidate people.

Other tips and tidbits: Estimated Birthdate: 4/15/2015. Dood is a lot of dog with a lot of things going for him. He has been given a very bad rap and very nearly lost his life because his previous owner had no common sense. We are going to be extraordinarily picky about his next home to make sure it's his best home and his forever home.

Dood is NOT completely hypoallergenic. He does very lightly shed. We do not know his heritage but I am betting he is first generation so there is some shedding involved.

House trained? Dogs can be house trained if they are in the right environment and are allowed to follow a schedule as long as a physical reason doesn't keep them from being trained. A dog house trained in my home may not be in yours. We will help you teach your new dog this necessary skill and based on your schedule.

Please note - we do not ship dogs. If you are interested in adopting, please take a look at the distance between the foster home location and your location and make sure you are willing to make that trip. Most of our dogs are at our farm in Pacolet, South Carolina.

To apply, please visit our webpage at www.carolinapoodlerescue.org and visit the tab on the left that directions you to the online application.

Please note that when screening applications, we look at the entire home and then make suggestions based on what would be a good fit for your home. You are not being screened for a specific dog although we are looking to see what type of dog interests you - poodles or non poodles, color, age, etc. Others here may be a better fit for you. It is very difficult to get to know a living animal from a picture and a short description. Since we are constantly getting in new dogs, this may be a dog not in our listings yet. We want you to be very happy with your new companion and will make suggestions based on what you tell us about you.

Thank you for considering CPR.

name: Baby Jade
description:
Stare deep into those baby blues, and tell us it's not love at first sight!

Baby Jade is an absolutely stunning American Staffordshire Terrier puppy that had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. Baby Jade is currently in Houston, Texas and available for transport through our rescue partners. 

This little girl has been in foster care for about 3 months and has  trained quickly. She is smart, learns quickly and has grown to become confident dog with a playful nature. She has learned to walk on a leash, crate train and house train quickly. She is very food motivated and will require a home that will work with her on basic obedience and gives her guidance. Baby Jade can be a little stubborn and her favorite activities include stealing peaches off the trees and searching for pecans in the grass. She can be a little stubborn at times and tends to run off and explore on her own, while the other dogs play. She plays in a group daily with other dogs, both male and female, ranging from young pups to adults, and does great with all of them. She loves to wrestle and roughhouse, if the other dog will allow. When another dog sets boundaries with Baby Jade by barking, growling or correcting her with a bite to the neck, she will back down and go into puppy mode by running away. Baby Jade is dog friendly and great with kids.

She is about 50lbs now and still growing. She recently had a growth spurt and is in that awkward puppy stage where she has skinny body and long, lanky legs. Baby Jade will be a large dog when fully grown, from 80-90lbs, and has an incredibly sweet temperament. She is medium to high activity, and would be an amazing companion for runs, hikes or just a nice casual stroll around the park.

Baby Jade is at an age where she needs guidance and would thrive in an environment with another assertive and more confident dog. She does well with dominant female dogs and takes correction well, however may persist in roughhousing until her human steps in to correct her as she is all about playing. This girl is a tomboy and lives for mud puddles and water- don't let her good looks fool you into thinking she is a girly girl! She is also extremely vocal and \"sings\" when she is hungry, displeased or bored, so be prepared to always have someone talking to you and letting you know how she feels! 

Baby Jade has a high prey drive towards rodents, such as squirrels, rats and possum outdoors. We have not tested Baby Jade with cats, but she is very calm and submissive. She could likely be trained to accept cats, with strict reinforcement.

Background: 
Baby Jade had a rough start to life in the streets of Houston, Texas. She was found with a broken tail and infected, butchered ears from an amateur crop job at only 6 months old. She came to us as a stray, found by a Good Samaritan who saved her life after seeing a man beat and kick her on the street for approaching his dog while on a walk. He said she was vicious and tried to throw her into oncoming traffic. 

Vetting: Baby Jade has received the standard DHLPP vaccine, rabies vaccine and Bordatella vaccine. She is spayed, microchipped and heartworm negative. We recommend that all rescue dogs coming from Texas remain on heartworm preventative for 6 months after arriving in Washington, as a precaution.

Healthy dogs: As a rescue saving dogs from starvation, Neglect and Emaciation, RPR focus's on feeding each rescued animal the healthiest dog food made of Human Grade ingredients to help them recover from their stress and starvation. We share this with our adopters and encourage them to keep their new pet on the same foods for optimal health and a long life.

Adoption Fees

This covers transport from California to Washington, to the rescue facility, adoption and medical such as certain vaccines, worming, parasite, and flea/tick control, health certificate and wellness exam, microchip and any extra medical attention a dog may require such as dental, anal gland expression, emergency medical care. Also, we don't receive any grants so we rely solely on adoption fees and donations to fund all of our rescue efforts. About Rompin Paws Rescue

Rompin Paws Rescue is a licensed, non-profit organization working towards our 501C3, specializing in rescuing moms to be, moms with puppies, puppies without moms and other Death Row dogs. We are located in Western Washington State. Our passion is to bring people and pets together.

Come Meet Our Pets...
We have a home based operation on Acreage in Arlington and Our dogs are placed in foster homes around the greater Seattle/I-5 Corridor North to Arlington area where they receive socialization and training while they await adoption.

Our Adoption Process...
Since we have a small facility on gated acreage, we are unable to stay open to anyone who wishes to come visit. description:

He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

description: Domingo spent part of his life in a dog-training program in a prison. He is very smart, and knows over two dozen visual and verbal cues. name: Juliet
description:
COURTESY POST - Juliet is in need of a new home. She has been with her current family since she was adopted from a local shelter as a puppy. They are heartbroken to lose her, but feel that Juliet would be a happier dog with a different family/home situation. She is a beautiful and spunky 4 yr young 75 lb lab mix, spayed, current on all vaccines and no health issues and perfectly house trained. Juliet adores people and kids (because of her energy and strength she should be watched around small children). She is the biggest lover of people - loyal, affectionate, intelligent, highly trainable, protective, energetic, strong, sweet, in need of human love and interaction, good listener, senses emotion, loves to hang with her owners, needs daily exercise, needs routine, needs alpha management. She is a wonderful protector of home and family and will bark loudly and menacingly at strangers who approach the house until she officially meets them. She is anxious away from her owners and does not do well in kennels, she needs in-home boarding (at owner's home or in home of sitter.)

Juliet is an alpha dog and needs a firm and consistent hand which is not possible in her current situation. Juliet's ideal owner would be an experienced and alpha dog owner (single person, couple or family with children experienced with dogs) who could love and spend time with her, manage her firmly, and keep a routine for her. She does fine when home alone during the day as long as she knows her owners will return after work. She will do better with fewer handlers who can use the same training methods with her (e.g. we have too many handlers -- nanny, babysitters, housekeeper, dog walker, husband, wife, kids) Active owners - and with a yard - would be ideal.

Juliet cannot be with other dogs at this time - while she loves certain dogs that she knows, she has shown aggression with other dogs. She loves flirting with cats on walks, but it is unknown how she would do with a cat in the home. She shows aggression towards large dogs and needs active training before any further interaction with dogs. Juliet should not interact off leash with dogs until further training. Her current dog trainer located in Washington, DC has offered free training to the new owners.

All requests for information will be handled by Juliet's owner and should be directed to Katie at 202-258-2362 or email rehomingjuliet@gmail.com.
