name: Reilly Virginia
description:
Senior Dog Alert - Sweet, sweet senior

Reilly is a cocker girl we've rescued from West Virginia and she is as sweet as she is pretty - she is blind at this point in her life secondary to what we think is either cataracts or glaucoma - she will have an evaluation at a veterinary ophthalmologist when we get her to New England and are hopeful we can perhaps restore some sight to this girl.

Reilly was found on a porch in West Virginia - the gentleman couldn't get in his house as she was sleeping - he called the local animal control who came and picked her up - knowing our love of seniors we were asked if we'd take her - and the rest is history!!
Reilly gets along with other dogs at the shelter - she does get startled easily until she knows her surroundings but she does not show this in any aggressive fashion. When found she was covered in fleas and flea dirt - the staff at the shelter were able to get her groomed and she looks (and feels) so much better.

Our plan is for Reilly to come to New England the weekend of 9/27 - we are hopeful you will want to adopt er with the full knowledge of her eye condition however we will cover the evaluation with a veteran ophthalmologist - either one of the ones we partner with or if there's one you know of, we can certainly work with them if possible.

Reillly deserves a place to land, forever. She shouldn't need to ever roam around without a home.

For a dog as clever and driven as Chatter is (usually for food), we would love to see her put those mothering days behind her and be spoiled in her very own home. description:

Mr. Pricklepants enjoys nothing more than getting out and about in the yard where he can run to his heart's content.Â 

Mr. Pricklepants is a dog with a story to tell: he came to us from our rescue partner in West Virginia, where he had been a primarily outdoor dog before coming to their shelter. Mr. Pricklepants is truly an ideal companion for a family that wants a dog for nice long walks around the neighborhood, but who would equally be as comfortable watching a movie or Sunday night football. name: Winter Vale
description:
Welcome, Miss Winter Vale. Winter is approximately 2 years old and weighs about 60 lbs. 

BACKGROUND:  This pretty girl ended up in rescue after her person passed away suddenly leaving her with no one to take care of her. Understandably, Winter is a little lost and confused, but we are going to help this girl find her person again. Could that be you? We are not sure of her past life with her previous owner but we suspect that she may have been shaved at one time as her fur is starting to come back in as well.  

LIKES:  She loves to have her ears scratched, chase balls and, yes! Do zoomies when she is excited, even in the living room! She initially is excited on her walks and will pull on the leash. She is learning that pulling makes the walking stop and is making progress. She is decompressing & settling in the new environment. Winter is a great traveler in the car and loves to go where ever you may be headed. 

Winter is looking for someone who can spoil her and give her all the attention she needs. She enjoys attention & will throw paw to ask for it. She prefers to be the only dog in the home. 

If you are interested in adopting or fostering Winter, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Lilly
description:
Hi there! My name is Lilly.  I am 8 months old, weigh 28 pounds, and am full of happiness and fun. I came to Canine Humane Network all the way from West Virginia and I am hoping to find my fur-ever home here in Maryland! 

I am curious and love just about everything including children, kitties, other dogs, my Kong with peanut butter, chasing butterflies and squirrels...you get the picture - I am a happy-go-lucky girl! 

I donât even mind my crate and am house-trained.  I am very energetic, but I still like to be close to my foster parents, and can chill-out on the couch with them and my foster dog sisters. My foster mom is taking me on a lot of walks so I can  learn to walk with her like a grown-up dog. My favorite thing to do is run around in a fenced yard! 

WIll you please think about making me a part of your family fur-ever?  Ask about adopting me today!

Please note that puppies need to have human interaction every 3 hours. 
Adoption Fee is $350 with Spay/Neuter Contract. A separate $100 deposit will be collected but will be returned after we receive the spay/neuter certificate for your puppy at 6 months of age. 

Applications are required prior to meeting the puppy.  You can apply at: http://caninehumane.org/adoption-application/. If you have questions you can email chninquiries@caninehumane.org. Calling or emailing may delay your consideration without an application submitted.

name: Murry Murdoch da Tank!
description:
Murry Murdoch da Tank came to us from a shelter after his \"people\" left him in an overnight run. He was understandably confused but he seems to not be phased at all about his past life. Just a happy pup seeking a new life and home. Murry is ready to work for a treat and bond with his human.  

Murry is strong and all puppy. He seems to be missing basic manners that were never taught in his previous home. He acts more like a 3-month-old pup who likes to frolic and doesn't know his own strength. He is built like a tank & would love to learn how to pull a sled or go on a nice hike. He reminds us of the famous Balto. 

Typical puppy, he has energy to burn, but with regular exercise & mental stimulation, he is a happy good boy. Murry is eager to have a home, continue positive dog training and be loved. He walks nicely on a leash, will roll over for belly rubs and is ready to lean on you for some love. He knows sit makes good things happen & has so much potential. He is food motivated.

CHILDREN:  We are working with Murry to sit when meeting new people, but due to his strength & size, he has the potential to knock over small children. We believe a home with older kids is best. 

CRATES: Murry is not fond of crates; therefore, he will need a gated area for a den for his own space. We recommend a tall toddler gate & a fenced-in yard. He loves toys and will run around and play by himself by throwing them in the air, who doesn't like to play catch? 

OTHER DOGS:  He has done well meeting friendly female dogs so he may be able to live with another female that is around the same age.

name: Lakota Mato (Bear)
description:
Lakota is a 2-year-old boy born July 2017 who came to us from a shelter where his previous owners dumped him. He was purchased as a puppy and lived most of his life outside. He is still learning all the fun things life has to offer and good manners. He is a little unsure about things and how to behave. He is learning to trust humans again and we are providing consistency and patience so he can blossom. At two he still is mouthy and jumpy but we are working with him and already are seeing improvements. We have started working on Zen and he loves it. He enjoys companionship and is opening up nicely.  We are so glad Lakota is with the CHAAMP family!

Lakota would do best in a home with no young children. He did well when seeing other dogs on walks and we will continue to work with him and see how he does with a female companion. He is super smart and knows how to sit. He had us fooled in the beginning but he will sit now nicely when asked (a treat helps) and he will need continued positive training to be the best pup he can be.

name: Apollo the White Knight
description:
Apollo is a 2.5-year-old neutered loving boy. He weighs 75 lbs and is naturally slender. Unfortunately, due to male-male aggression, Apollo needs to be rehomed to a loving family. He would do well in a home where someone could spend most of the day with him. He is looking for someone experienced with large dogs or northern breeds. Typical male malamute characteristics. He has moments of zoomies and then would lay next to you and watch TV. Apollo is an expert digger and occasionally tries to dig inside and outside. Apollo doesnât realize his size and loves laying in your lap and taking up the entire bed. 

Apollo would prefer to be the only pet in the household but has been getting along with a similarly sized female. He could never live with another male due to male-male aggression nor be around another male dog unsupervised. Apollo does mark in the house, but most likely this is due to the presence of another large male sharing the house. He will wear a belly band but that does not deter his marking. During walks, Apollo avoids other dogs except for his two husky friends. He responds well to the dog walker and loves to give kisses. 

Apollo loves all toys. He always has a toy in his mouth and wants to play fetch or get pets while he chews them. He is a good sitter and will do almost anything for a treat. Himalayan dog treats and fresh beef bones are some of his favorite chew treats. 

While not too fond of many dogs, Apollo loves people and is always eager to say hi to everyone on walks. He has not lived with children but enjoys meeting them on walks. Not recommended for homes with small children due to his size and stature. 

If you are interested in adopting Apollo, please contact CHAAMP at CHAAMPapplication@gmail.com for an application. You may also complete an application online thru our web site, www.CHAAMP.org

CHAAMP accepts applications ONLY from Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Virginia, West Virginia, and Washington DC. The information on your application will help CHAAMP determine which of our dogs is a good match for you and your family, based upon your lifestyle, other pets, etc. A home visit is required prior to all adoptions. Many of our dogs are fostered in private homes and cannot be visited until you have been approved for adoption. 

ADOPTION FEES
~Adult dogs, the fee is $275.00  
~Older dogs (eight years old or over) the adoption fee is $100.00 
~Puppies between 6 months and 1 year are $350.00 
~Puppies under 6 months old are $375.00 

All dogs are micro chipped, spayed and neutered and up to date on vaccines. These fees help us cover these costs.  The rates are higher for puppies because they require more visits to the vet and shots. 

CHAAMP IS NOT A SHELTER. We are volunteers over a 7-state area dedicated to helping Malamutes in our rescue area. You can read more about Malamutes and about CHAAMP by visiting www.CHAAMP.org

name: Finn MacCool
description:
Born in 2017, Finn is a small pup who weighs around 55 lbs. Just a petite bundle of stunning WHITE fur with little slivers of chestnut on the top of his ears. He stays clean too. He can be shy & even fearful of some humans or just lean into you as he melts to the floor with his belly up for affection. Because he can be fearful of \"some\" people it's important to give him \"space\" and go slow with introductions. He has met older children and enjoyed their calm attention but to help him with his excitability he prefers a home with older children. He has blossomed with positive dog training (no force, no fear, no pain) and build his confidence while strengthening your bond. Finn is seeking his human soulmate. He is an amazing young boy & is waiting patiently for the right home.

OTHER DOGS: Currently, if we can't avoid a dog during our walk, then we keep a safe distance like on the other side of the street, in a calm voice tell him he is a good boy, watch, & we toss a treat in the air for him to catch. We allow Finn to watch the dog, but break his stare with something positive to change the experience. This also helps him refocus his energies to something delicious. With \"some\" dogs, this has worked well. There are still some dogs that he reacts to due to fear.  Finn tends to be intimidated by large dogs & can't help but want to chase small dogs, which is completely natural for Northern Breeds. He has met playful females and has done well with a slow introduction. He has also met some that made him fearful.  

INSIDE THE HOUSE:  Finn is calm inside the house as long as he gets a nice walk. We also give him a frozen toy filled with chicken broth & a couple of treats, which he loves to lick. Licking is very soothing to dogs & helps them stay busy. He enjoys chewing & licking toys. We always leave his crate open and he is kept in a gated area during the day, which is the kitchen as well as Finn's den. He is a very good boy & tries not to counter surf. He enjoys jumping on furniture & can learn which sofa is his spot.

BACKYARD FUN:  Finn enjoys your company while he runs around in the backyard. He enjoys keeping the garden free of critters, bugs, & eating fresh tomatoes off the vine. Thanks to Finn, the garden have survived! Finn hopes to have a fenced yard, so he can sniff and show you his zoomies, be your gardening assistant. He loves going outside & sprinting in happiness, especially in the winter!  He also loves to lay on his Kuranda dog bed under the shade after sipping water in between his own party in the backyard. He likes to play hide & go seek too. He also enjoys nuzzling his head in between your legs for affection in between his fun time. Just an amazing companion.   

Finn typically walks a mile 3 times a day. He sits nicely (with his paw up as if to say please hurry) for treats too. He has great potential & learns quickly too. The husky side of Finn is excitable. So it's important to help him practice calming down by asking for a sit, then a down, and then zen with long strokes on his back or a belly rub. He loves this & often melts into your side, then your feet with his belly up for love. In a new environment, it is important to remind him how to relax. He is a complete angel with his foster family, but they follow these guidelines earned his trust. He enjoys being with his foster family and is very affectionate. He loves to sleep on the bed & will initiate affection for a while, then goes to his side of the bed to sleep.  

TRAVEL COMPANION: Finn also travels well. He prefers to be seated close to his foster family. He is a family dog and loves with all his heart. 

TOYS & PLAY:  Finn likes squeaky tough toys (he destroys stuffed animals in seconds) and will trade his toy for a treat with no problem. He is quite playful & loves to smell & find things. He would do well-performing nose work. Finn enjoys being a \"good boy\" & loves working for a reward. It's important to provide with Finn a calm demeanor and go slow to help him blossom. Finn likes to play the \"find it\" game and he also likes to sit, wait, and catch a treat as you toss it in the air. He loves rotisserie chicken sandwiches, which he considers a high-value treat. We use it when counter conditioning scary things like dogs. 

SPACE: When introducing Finn to new things, we practice letting him go at his own pace and treating, repeat, etc. This has built his confidence. Trust is important for Finn. It is important to give him space and allow him to enter into your space when meeting him. Finn like most dogs does not like having his head pat by, especially strangers. 

We believe Finn is part Husky/Malamute, his Malamute side likes to keep his distance from other male dogs. His foster mom simply calls him and lets him sniff rotisserie chicken sandwich as she lures him to walk in a different direction (\"this way\"), he is rewarded with small bites. He responds nicely! He has so much potential. 

BACKGROUND:  Finn came to CHAAMP after living with a family on a farm with fur siblings. He was too interested in the chickens and the cats. He also wasn't getting along with the male dogs in the household. He was said to have high predatory behavior, which is normal for Northern Breeds. Finn can go from 0 to 70 in a blink of an eye due to excitement or if you go too fast and scare him. 

Finn's foster family has gone slow, provided structure, and practice positive dog training to help him make good choices. He is an amazing & affectionate young furry companion who loves his foster family & is seeking to fall in love with a special human.

name: Abby HAS BEEN ADOPTED!
description:
ABBY HAS BEEN ADOPTED!
The Ark of Hope Animal Rescue is a Christian organization that does not have a normal adoption fee. We do ask each adoptive family to consider what all we do to ready the animals for adoption. Surgeries, spays and neuters, medications, housing, bedding, blankets, electric, food, grooming, etc. We do not get any financial help from the local or state government as local shelters do. We depend on donations from the kindness of peopleâs hearts. For over 25 years it has worked for us.
âAbbyâ a beautiful Black German Shepherd, The Ark of Hope Animal Rescue âpulledâ this beautiful dog from a kill shelter in West Virginia. She was to be euthanized on Friday March 9th. We committed to take Abby so they held her over a day until we could get to her. She is only a puppy; born Aug. 31, 2016 she is almost 2 years old years old.  We had her vet checked and Rabies vaccinated. A week after she came to us we realized that she was pregnant. She has since given birth to her beautiful puppies and is now ready to be adopted herself, Abby will start to look for a family that will love her forever! Abby is housebroken, she listens very well, is very sweet and affectionate with men, women, and children. She is done with being tied outside; she is looking for a family that understands that she wants to be part of their family, which means that she doesnât want to live outside but inside their home with her new family. Could you be her new family? If you would to visit Abby, her puppies or any of the other dogs here at The Ark, go to arkofhoperescue.org. Under the filmstrip of pictures, click on âThe Adoption Procedure.â Scroll down to âDog Adoption Applicationâ click on it, fill it out and attach it to an email and send it to: arkofhoperescue@yahoo.com. You can also call Dianne at 301-478-3300.

Reese is good with cats, she lived with 5 of them. This girl walks great on a leash. She is Super Friendly and Sweet. name: Divot
description:
Divot is a sweet girl around 12 weeks old...she was rescued from a shelter in West Virginia. Her nose is a little funny, hence the name divot....our vet has said its just a birth defect. She's very sweet, loves everyone. She's about 20 lbs now so we think she'll be around 40 as an adult.

Email sheplover5@aol.com for an application to adopt. Please be within an hour of Spring City PA as we do require a home visit. Divot's adoption fee is $300 plus a $100 spay deposit. We will spay her at six months -no exceptions.

name: Rachel
description: Meet Rachel! Rachel is one of two beagle pups that have just been rescued from West Virginia. They are pint-sized pups that love to play and are roughly 9 weeks old. ~Please be within an hour of Spring City PA as we do require a home visit. Rachel's adoption fee is $400 which includes a$100 spay deposit. Email sheplover5@aol.com for more info.

name: Babish - Senior
description:
Babish is a 10-year-old hound mix who came to Pennsylvania from a West Virginia coal mine. She was born at that mine and was the only survivor of her litter. She is a lovingdog who craves human attention. Babish is very affectionate toward those she trusts.

Babish is housebroken and loves being outside. In an outside environment, she is tolerant of other dogs. Inside the house, she is cautious with other animals. She also needs time to warm up to people. She would need to go to an adult only home.

It's important for us to let everyone know about Babish's struggles.It is difficult for a dog as wary as Babish is, to find a good home. We know there is someone out there who will have the patience and understanding to let this girl become comfortable in her time.Babish has spent her entire life without a family or home. We know there is a forever home out there just for her. This girl is ready to live the good life.

You can apply to adopt Babish atwww.mostlymuttz.org/adoption-application/.

name: Rocky
description:
Rocky and his sisters Sharon and Serena are very close - we would love to find a home that would take at least two of them. Once they know you and trust you, they are wonderful but they are scared. They need to go to a home with a secure yard and patient owners.

FOSTER NEEDED ASAP!!!!!

10/28/18 - rocky is now a year old......still waiting for his forever home. He's sweet but shy with new people. Looking for a home that will give him a chance!!

Rocky is one of the six pups we took in from West Virginia. They were trapped and very scared pups.. They are sweet once you get to know them. We are looking for adopters or fosters who are willing to give them a chance. Rocky is about 20 lbs now and 4 months old. He needs someone to give him a chance. description:
These 3 girls are about 5 months old and came to us from the Kentucky West Virginia border. One of the girls is a low rider (Kardashians : Kim) and the other two have the graceful longer legs of a German shepherd. They are happy and fun loving and excited to meet their new family. They do well with other dogs And we anticipate that they will do fine with cats and children.

name: ROXY
description: Roxy is a healthy girl as affectionate and playful she's just not good around dogs, cats, or small children. She requires a secure fenced yard, and a family that is used to bully bully breeds. It's not a question of how nice you are dogs may be with this dog will attack your dog so no dogs at all. Otherwise she is well behaved and will make someone a great companion. She's located in Wilkes Barre Pennsylvania area. please make sure to include a phone number and the state you are in when you contact us, and please fill out an application at www.iongislandbulldogrescue.org

name: Elwood
description: Elwood is a bright-eyed Lab/hound mix who is full of energy and just raring to conquer the world. Born in 2012, Elwood came to Best Friends from a humane society in Wisconsin. As you might imagine, the hound in Elwood has blessed him with an awesome nose and he loves to play \"find it,\" while the Labrador in Elwood has provided him with a brain that's eager to learn. In fact, training is one of Elwood's favorite activities. He's already learned commands for sit, down, shake, place, wait and hand targeting! He's an amazing dog. Since Elwood was a pup, he has suffered from noise and storm phobias. This has decreased over time, but has not been eliminated. He also has PTSD from an unfortunate accident that happened at the humane society he was at previously. But when Elwood sees a familiar face, his tail begins to wag uncontrollably and his whole body fills with excitement. He just has to let people know he's happy! He also loves playing with other dogs has lived with a variety of sizes and breeds. Elwood's forever home will need a secure back yard, as his phobias have driven him to jump short fences and open latches in the past. He would do best with a dog savvy, patient person. If you can offer this guy the love and guidance he needs, he'll quickly become your biggest admirer. Will you give Elwood the forever home he's always wanted? Elwood has a generous sponsor who has offered to cover a portion of his adoption costs.

name: Willow
description:
Hi, my name is Willow.I am a 2 year old mini Australian Shepherd that was rescued from hoarding andabuse situation in Wisconsin. Because of my double merle breeding (color pattern),I am deaf and have limited vision in my lefteye. Don'tthink for one minute that stops me! I love to run, playand bark with the best of them.

My foster family has beenvery patient with me while I got used to being inside ahome. They showed me that humanscan be trusted and that they do love me. In return, I am showingthem my sweet personality. I love being part of the family and playingwith my foster brother and sister. They even let me help with a littlepuppy that visited!

If you are patient with me, I will give you lots of kisses andwiggle butts, showing youhow much I appreciate being treated so kind. OccasionallyI may be startledwithquick movements and shy away from strangers, but everyday is gettingeasier and easierfor me.

I have even learned a couple of sign language commands. That's how my foster family communicates with me.I am potty trained andalways go outside todo my business.

I willneed a fence at my new house. I would prefer another dogso they can show me how things work at your house. I am spayed and up-to-date on all vaccinations and prefer no children under age 10 years of age.My new family willneed to give memonthly preventatives for fleas, ticks andheartworms (no exceptions). If you're interested in giving me a loving home, you can apply here: https://www.speakstlouis.com/forms/adoption-application/

name: Teddy
description:
\"Hi, I'm Teddy!

Teddy is a mature (almost 10) Shih Tzu released from a commercial breeder in Wisconsin. He loves other dogs, a perfect lap dog who loves to snuggle. Teddy is good with children although still a little shy. Teddy is learning to be a dog. He is learning to walk on a leash. Currently he is not housebroken but we're working on it and he is catching on. He doesn't mind wearing belly bands.

Teddy would make a great companion dog for a quiet home, and also appreciates stretching out on the lawn , soaking in sunshine.

to fill out an online application.

name: XP Alphie Jo - Lafayette, NJ
description:
Alphie Jo was my best friend's dog (my aunt). Her wishes before she passed away was for him to live with her closest friend Linda in Pennsylvania. Our family made the arrangements for Alphie Jo to fly out from Wisconsin to PA 3 years ago. Linda was also my aunt's best friend, a dog lover like you've never met, and she owns a rescue as well.

Unfortunately Alphie Jo did not do so well living with her male dogs so she decided it was time to put him up for adoption through her rescue. He went in and out of two homes and was back at her rescue. I spent a lot of time in Wisconsin...taking care of my aunt and Alphie Jo. I formed a bond with him through a difficult time. As a dog lover, I couldn't bear another moment of hearing him \"being returned\". Last December I made the decision to take him to my home in Lafayette, NJ. He is still with me, and I wish it could always remain that way. But I have learned he cannot be around other pets no matter the size, species, or gender. He needs a home that fits him.

Alphie Jo is a 6-year-old English Coonhound - he is up to date on his shots. Here is more information about him:

-He cannot live with any other pets. He is unpredictable in that sense.
-He has been around children of all ages however we would feel more comfortable with him being with older, experienced children, if children at all.
-He is better suited in a country setting.
-He howls when he wants food, water, needs to go \"potty\

description:

name: Shiny
description:
Shiny is an approximately 4-6-year-old spayed Bull Breed mix. She came from a shelter in Wyoming, so we dont know anything about her prior history. She is an amazing girl with so many wonderful qualities. But, like all of us, she has some things about her that maybe arent brag-worthy. Well start with the things about Miss Shiny that are awesome. First off, she is a very sweet girl with loads of love to give. She LOVES people! She is a world-class snuggler and could spend the whole day curled up on her persons lap. She loves to burrow herself under blankets. That is her happy place. If you let her sleep underneath the covers, she will be one content little lady and will love you forever. She is very treats motivated and loves her food! Shes been living in her foster home for the past several months with multiple other dogs and has done great. As long as any other dogs shes around arent snappy or aggressive towards her, she makes friends with just about everyone. She is a goofball too. She can be extremely silly and funny and makes her foster family laugh all the time. Dont tell her we told anyone this (shed be so embarrassed), but she has a bit of a gas problem. She can be a motor butt at times, and its always good for a laugh. She loves to roll on the floor on her back and stare at you from upside down. Shes also very vocal when it comes to her disdain for things. When shes not happy, she does these funny grunts that communicate her dislike of a situation. 
None of us are perfect, and that goes for sweet Shiny too. She has a few things about her that need some work or is just things that make her who she is and probably will not change. While Shiny loves being around her dog buddies, that is where her ability to get along with other animals ends. She absolutely CANNOT be in a home with cats, rabbits, birds, guinea pigs, etc. She has far too high of a prey drive to be around small animals. She also is an extreme door darter. She bolts through any open door when given a chance. If its a door to outside the home, once shes out, she will run as fast and far as she can. She will mow over anyone to get out of an open door if she really wants to. Her foster family has been working with her on this issue for quite some time, but because her drive to bolt through doors is so high, they feel that it is something she will probably never really be fully trustworthy with. She, therefore, needs to be in a home without younger children and where doors are secured and opened only when she is safely put away, especially exterior doors where she is not given the opportunity to bolt and run, putting her safety at risk. She absolutely loves her walks and gets very excited to go. She has come a long way on her leash manners over the past few months, but she still needs some work. She doesnt travel great in a car at this point. She gets extremely excited in new situations, and a car ride is like her mind is on overload and she has a hard time not getting overstimulated in the car. Shes made progress, but she does still have a way to go as far as learning to ride calmly in a vehicle. Storms and fireworks are very scary for her. She doesnt understand the loud noises. She gets very stressed in these situations. She will need someone to be patient with her and help her feel as safe and secure when she feels the whole world is coming down. When she feels stressed at all, she has been known to take her stress and frustration out on pillows or dog beds. Shes very sensitive to any tension or anger in the home, and when she feels stressed out from any of these situations, she can be destructive. 
Shiny is an extremely sweet dog with so much potential. She will thrive in a home who can give her the guidance, love, patience, and security she needs and deserves.

If you think you would be good for our Shiny girl please send an email to Celestialzooutah@gmail.com. She is spayed, vaccinated, and microchipped, her adoption fee is $200.
